Fix panic on multi-byte UTF-8 characters in TUI text wrapping

Use unicode-width for display width calculations instead of byte length,
preventing panics when pasting text containing non-ASCII characters (e.g. █).

Fix TUI slowdown after losing terminal focus and fix 3 broken tests

Event loop processed only one event per render cycle. While backgrounded,
Tick events accumulated (~7/sec) in the channel. On resume, each stale
Tick required a full re-render, causing seconds of UI freeze.

Fix: drain all queued events before re-rendering, coalescing consecutive
Ticks. Enable crossterm FocusGained/FocusLost events. Fix plan_tool UUID
extraction off-by-2 and prompt_analyzer test assertions.

Fix UTF-8 panics, add message queue injection, add 23 tests

UTF-8 safety: safe truncation utility, fix http/doc_parser/qwen/onboarding
byte slicing, display-width input height estimation.

Message queue: inject user follow-ups between tool call iterations via
shared Arc<Mutex> callback (Claude Code-style mid-execution feedback).

Tests: truncate_str (6), render char boundary/wrap (15), message queue (2).

Streaming tool call fix — the root cause of tool calls failing on OpenRouter/Custom providers:

  1. Deserialization was broken: OpenAIToolCall had required id and type fields, but OpenAI streaming sends continuation chunks without them — causing every tool call chunk to fail parsing silently. Created a new
   StreamingToolCall struct with all optional fields + required index.
  2. No argument accumulation: OpenRouter/OpenAI stream tool call arguments as fragments across many SSE chunks (e.g. {'qu → ery': → 'hello'}). The old code expected complete JSON in a single chunk and skipped
  anything incomplete. Now arguments are accumulated in a HashMap<usize, ToolCallAccum> across chunks.
  3. Emit on completion: Tool calls are now emitted as ContentBlockStart events only when finish_reason: 'tool_calls' arrives (meaning the provider finished generating all tool calls), or on [DONE] as a fallback
  flush.

Streaming tool call fix — the root cause of tool calls failing on OpenRouter/Custom providers:

  1. Deserialization was broken: OpenAIToolCall had required id and type fields, but OpenAI streaming sends continuation chunks without them — causing every tool call chunk to fail parsing silently. Created a new
   StreamingToolCall struct with all optional fields + required index.
  2. No argument accumulation: OpenRouter/OpenAI stream tool call arguments as fragments across many SSE chunks (e.g. {'qu → ery': → 'hello'}). The old code expected complete JSON in a single chunk and skipped
  anything incomplete. Now arguments are accumulated in a HashMap<usize, ToolCallAccum> across chunks.
  3. Emit on completion: Tool calls are now emitted as ContentBlockStart events only when finish_reason: 'tool_calls' arrives (meaning the provider finished generating all tool calls), or on [DONE] as a fallback
  flush.

feat: add A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol support

Implement the A2A Protocol RC v1.0 specification for OpenCrabs,
enabling multi-agent communication and collaboration.

## What's included

- **A2A Protocol Types** (types.rs): Core data model — Task, Message,
  Part, Artifact, AgentCard, JSON-RPC 2.0 request/response types.

- **Agent Card** (agent_card.rs): Auto-generates .well-known/agent.json
  for agent discovery per A2A spec Section 8.

- **JSON-RPC Handler** (handler.rs): Dispatches message/send, tasks/get,
  and tasks/cancel operations with in-memory TaskStore.

- **Gateway Server** (server.rs): axum HTTP server serving Agent Card,
  JSON-RPC endpoint, and health check on the configured gateway port.

- **Multi-Agent Debate** (debate.rs): Multi-round discussion protocol
  with confidence-weighted consensus (inspired by ReConcile/ACL 2024).
  Supports knowledge context injection and structured critique rounds.

## Dependencies added

- axum 0.8 (HTTP server)
- tower-http 0.6 (CORS)
- tower 0.5 (dev, test utilities)

## Tests

22 unit + integration tests covering all modules.

fix: use provider pre-computed input tokens when stream usage reports zero

MiniMax (and similar providers) always return usage: {total_tokens: 0} in
the SSE stream, causing ctx to show the wrong token count (~14K instead of
the actual ~29K). The provider already computes an accurate
total_input_tokens = message_tokens + tool_schema_tokens (serialised
OpenAI JSON format) before the request. Now that value is used as the
fallback when the streaming usage reports 0, so tool_loop receives the
correct count directly via MessageDelta and the ctx display matches the
provider logs.

The tiktoken fallback in tool_loop is kept as a safety net for providers
that both report 0 AND don't have a pre-computed estimate available.

fix: SQLite WAL mode + larger pool to eliminate channel concurrency timeouts

Root cause: readers (Telegram, Discord) were blocked by writer lock held during
heavy TUI streaming (rapid message/token_count writes), causing 5s+ timeouts on
simple SELECT queries.

Changes to database pool config:
- journal_mode = WAL: readers and writers no longer block each other — the
  primary fix. A SELECT on sessions never queues behind an INSERT into messages.
- max_connections: 5 → 16: enough headroom for TUI + all channel handlers
  running simultaneously without pool exhaustion
- busy_timeout: 5000 → 30000 ms: graceful queuing when two writers briefly
  contend (e.g. two channels saving messages), instead of fast-fail SQLITE_BUSY
- synchronous = NORMAL: safe under WAL, ~3× faster writes than FULL default
- cache_size = 64 MB per connection: reduces disk I/O under heavy read workload

Zero user impact — WAL mode is transparent (adds .db-wal/.db-shm sidecar files
that SQLite manages automatically, existing databases upgrade on first open).

fix: WhatsApp sender identity — strip device suffix + inject contact context

1. Linked-device messages silently dropped
   sender_phone() returned "351933536442:34" for messages from WhatsApp

   This never matched the allowlist entry "351933536442", so all linked-
   device messages were logged as "non-allowed phone" and discarded.

   Owner messages pass through unchanged (they're already in direct context).
   Uses info.push_name (the contact's WhatsApp display name) when available.

fix: WhatsApp security — block owner→contact message processing

The old allowlist check only validated the sender phone. When the owner
sends a message to a contact (is_from_me=true), the sender IS the owner
so the check passed, causing the bot to process outgoing messages and
reply into contact chats.

Fix: also validate the recipient. Add recipient_phone() helper that
extracts the TO field from MessageInfo. Only process a message when:
- sender is the owner, AND
- recipient is the owner OR there is no recipient (group/broadcast)

This blocks: owner→contact messages (sender=owner, recipient=contact).
Self-DM still works: sender=owner, recipient=owner → passes both checks.

Covers self-DM use case only; no regressions for incoming messages from
allowed phones (sender check still blocks non-owners).

fix: WhatsApp handler regression with empty allowed_phones + connect tool fix

Two bugs introduced by the owner-only security check:

1. handler.rs: when allowed_phones is empty (unconfigured), owner_phone
   defaulted to "" causing is_from_owner to always be false — all messages
   blocked. Guard the check with !allowed.is_empty() to preserve previous
   open-mode behavior when no phones are configured.

2. whatsapp_connect.rs: the AI connect tool only used phones passed as
   tool input. If the AI called the tool without allowed_phones, the
   handler's allowed set was empty → hit bug #1. Now falls back to
   config channels.whatsapp.allowed_phones when tool input is empty.

fix: WhatsApp TTS — upload media before sending audio message

The previous implementation tried to send an AudioMessage with only
file_length set, which is invalid — WhatsApp requires media to be
uploaded to its servers first via client.upload(). Also corrected
field names (file_url→url, mime_type→mimetype) to match the
AudioMessage protobuf struct.

Now follows the same pattern as the library's own examples:
  1. synthesize_speech() → raw audio bytes
  2. client.upload(bytes, MediaType::Audio) → URL + crypto keys
  3. send AudioMessage with url/direct_path/media_key/file_enc_sha256/
     file_sha256/file_length populated

before sending it to the LLM for summarization. At >=90% usage, the
context was being truncated to 80% BEFORE compact_context ran, causing
the summarizer to produce generic/empty summaries with no real content.

LLM, and compact_context handles its own budget internally.

release: v0.2.55 -- compaction overhaul, usage ledger, macOS exit fix

Closes #29

Compaction system completely rewritten. Context is never truncated before
summarization. The full conversation reaches the LLM so it can produce a
real summary instead of a blank generic one. Compaction prompt expanded
to 10 sections: chronological analysis, code snippets, user preferences
with exact quotes, error log, recovery playbook (with gh CLI note),
and a personalized continuation message that references specific
conversation details. Manual /compact now calls the real compaction
pipeline. Compaction markers persist to the database so restarts load
only from the last compaction point forward. All 5 compaction paths
(manual, pre-loop, mid-loop before API call, mid-loop after tool
results, and emergency prompt-too-long) persist markers. TUI context
counter fixed to match what the agent actually sees after compaction.
/compact placeholder no longer shows as a user message in chat.
24 compaction tests.

New usage_ledger table tracks all token and cost usage permanently.
Deleting sessions no longer loses usage data. Migration backfills
from existing sessions automatically. TUI dialog, channel commands,
and /usage tool all read from the ledger now.

Replaced std::process::exit with libc::_exit to skip C atexit handlers
that trigger llama.cpp Metal GPU destructor crash on Apple Silicon.

Updated AGENTS.md brain template with new compaction behavior docs.

Existing users: update brain files after upgrading. The usage_ledger
migration runs automatically on first start. Always check brain file
templates for updates after each release.

Add daily release check notification

Spawns a background task on startup that checks GitHub for new
releases every 24 hours. When an update is available, shows a
temporary system message in chat prompting the user to /evolve.

Fix streaming usage parsing for MiniMax and OpenAI compatible providers

MiniMax and OpenAI send real usage in a final choices-empty chunk after
the finish_reason chunk. We emitted MessageStop on finish_reason and
never saw the real usage, falling back to tiktoken estimates.

Now defer MessageStop until the usage-only chunk arrives. Also guard
stop_reason from being overwritten by the deferred delta. Adds 5 unit
tests covering deferred vs inline usage patterns.

Fix context counter showing 243/200K when real usage was 19K

Calibration subtracted tool_count * 500 from input tokens to isolate
message-only count. With 38 tools that was 19,000 subtracted from
19,286 leaving 286, which propagated to the TUI via TokenCountUpdated
and ResponseComplete. Replace with actual serialized tool schema token
count. Combined with the streaming usage fix, the context counter now
reflects real API usage.

fix: remove fd-level stdout suppression that broke TUI on Linux

background model preload by 2s so it starts after the TUI enters
alternate screen. Any kalosm println goes to the alternate buffer
and is immediately overwritten by the next TUI render frame.

Also fixes test tolerance for dispatch error patterns.

fix: /stop now kills all in-flight agent calls instead of only the latest

store_cancel_token was silently overwriting the previous token when a new
message arrived on the same session, making old agent calls uncancellable.
This caused an infinite loop: each new message (including /stop) spawned
another concurrent agent, and cancellation only hit the newest one.

Now store_cancel_token cancels any existing token before storing the new one,
remove_cancel_token only cleans up already-cancelled tokens to avoid racing,
and a new AgentError::Cancelled variant suppresses noisy error messages when
the user explicitly stopped the operation.

Applied to all four channels: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp.

fix: streaming output token counter accumulated per-chunk in TUI instead of callback

The streaming_out AtomicU32 in the progress callback was reset to 0 on
every TokenCount event (between tool loop iterations), causing the
output token display to restart from "1 tok" after each tool call.

Moved accumulation to the TUI side (streaming_output_tokens += chunk)
where reset timing is controlled by send_message start. The callback
now sends per-chunk token counts instead of pre-accumulated totals.

fix: drop late tool/intermediate events after cancel to prevent unstacked display

arrive via the event queue. These created new tool group entries and
intermediate messages after the cancel handler had already finalized
the active group, leaving orphaned tool entries scattered in chat.

Added is_processing guard to these three event handlers so late events
after cancellation are silently dropped.

fix: pass --yolo to opencode CLI to prevent permission auto-rejection

and got auto-rejected (no TTY). The stream would end after step_finish,
causing 3 retries and an empty response. --yolo skips all permission
prompts, matching how claude CLI uses --dangerously-skip-permissions.

fix: TUI provider mismatch after restart — config is authoritative

fix: handle opencode CLI permission rejection gracefully

OpenCode CLI exits immediately when a tool call is rejected (permission
denied for paths like ~/Downloads). Previously this caused 2 retries
and a garbled empty response. Now:

- Set OPENCODE_PERMISSION env var to allow all permissions (including
  external_directory) so opencode runs non-interactively without
  rejecting tool calls
- Track tool rejection state in the stream reader as fallback
- When opencode exits after a rejection, emit a proper error message
  with MessageStop so the tool_loop doesn't retry uselessly

fix: restore opencode CLI tool call display in TUI

OpenCode tool_use events were sent as Ping (invisible) instead of
ContentBlock::ToolUse stream events. helpers.rs needs ToolUse blocks
to emit ToolStarted/ToolCompleted progress events that the TUI renders
as expandable tool call groups. Also set cli_handles_tools() = true so
the tool_loop doesn't try to re-execute opencode's internal tool calls.

fix: spawn opencode CLI at user home with --dir for full filesystem access

macOS TCC scopes file access per-process. Existing opencode sessions
locked tool execution to their original directory, blocking access to
~/Downloads/ etc. Now we always spawn at ~/ and pass --dir explicitly
so opencode's sandbox covers the full user home regardless of session.

fix: prevent duplicate assistant message for CLI providers

helpers.rs already flushes cli_unflushed_text as IntermediateText at
stream end. tool_loop.rs was emitting the same text again when
iteration > 0, causing the response to appear twice in the TUI.
Skip the second emission for CLI providers.

fix: Telegram intermediate texts vanishing between tool rounds

Root cause: the edit loop held a tokio::Mutex lock across multiple
Telegram API calls (send_message, edit_message, delete_message), each
taking hundreds of ms. During that time, the progress callback's
try_lock() silently dropped IntermediateText events, so intermediate
agent commentary between tool rounds was lost.

Fix: snapshot state under lock, release immediately, then do API work.
This keeps the lock held for microseconds instead of seconds, so
progress events are no longer dropped. Also drain any remaining
intermediate texts after the edit loop ends before sending the final
response.

always shows the bottom correctly. Long lines clip at pane edge.

fix: Telegram intermediate texts not sticking and wrong ordering

Root causes:

2. Edit loop processed tools before intermediates, breaking chronological
   order (text that appeared BEFORE a tool showed up AFTER it)
3. Streaming message not cleared on IntermediateText, causing stale text

Fixes:
- Switch streaming state to std::sync::Mutex — lock() always succeeds,
  no events ever dropped (all critical sections are microseconds, no
  await while holding lock)
- Replace separate tool_msgs/pending_intermediate processing with
  ordered DisplayItem queue that preserves chronological order
- Set recreate flag on IntermediateText so stale streaming message
  gets deleted

block. Final response only extracts text blocks AFTER the last

cancelled an in-flight call, those stale items were still delivered
alongside the new call's messages, causing duplicates.

processing the display queue. On cancellation, also cleans up any tool
messages the edit loop already sent during the call.

feat(self-healing): detect model degradation & auto-recover

Add response coherence check after model output parsing:
- is_response_coherent(): 4 heuristics (2+ triggers = garbage):
  1. High special-char ratio (>15% non-standard chars)
  2. No known English/code words (0 matches against 25 keywords)
  3. Unbalanced braces (>30% mismatch when count >2)
  4. Repeating char patterns (3-6 chars repeated 6+ times)
- count_known_words(): debug helper counting keyword matches

Wired into tool_loop.rs after text/tool extraction:
- If no valid tool calls AND text fails coherence:
  1. Log warning with char count + keyword match count
  2. Send SelfHealingAlert to progress callback (TUI/channels)
  3. Force hard truncate to 60% context
  4. Inject system message: 'your output contained broken
     syntax and garbled text — discard and start fresh'
  5. Discard garbled accumulated_text, continue loop

Catches the context-overflow degradation pattern: broken Rust
syntax, phantom variables, mixed-language fragments.

revert(self-healing): remove coherence check — caused more degradation than it fixed

The is_response_coherent() and count_known_words() heuristics were
too aggressive, flagging legitimate model output as garbage. This
triggered unnecessary context compaction loops that made models
produce worse output, creating a compounding failure cycle.

Removed both functions and all wiring from the tool loop.

feat(rate-limiting): add proactive pacing for OpenRouter :free models

Add a lock-free CAS-based rate limiter that enforces a minimum
interval between API requests. Attached automatically when the
configured model name ends with ':free' (≈ 20 req/min → 3s gap).

This is the first layer in our 4-layer rate-limit defense:
1. Proactive pacing → stay under the limit (new)
2. Exponential backoff → recover if we slip through
3. Retry-After header parsing → respect server instructions
4. Fallback provider switching → last resort

refactor(rate-limiter): share global static limiter across all OpenRouter :free provider instances

Previously each provider instance got its own RateLimiter, so a main
agent + 3 subagents could collectively hit ~53 req/min against a 20
req/min limit. Now OPENROUTER_FREE_LIMITER is a single LazyLock<Arc>
shared by every provider — orchestrator, subagents, and team members
all pace against ONE process-wide budget.

This is the difference between being merely resilient (catching 429s
after they happen) and genuinely robust (preventing them entirely).

fix(rate-limiter): treat last_granted=0 as sentinel so first call never waits

The original CAS logic compared PROCESS_START.elapsed() against
last_granted=0, which always showed elapsed < min_interval at
startup — so the first request incorrectly slept for the full gap.
Now last=0 is explicitly handled as "no previous grant" and always
returns immediately.

fix(qwen-cli): default missing stop_reason to EndTurn to stop response looping

Qwen CLI's `result` envelope frequently omits `stop_reason` entirely on
success. We were forwarding that missing value as `MessageDelta { stop_reason: None }`,
which the agent loop interprets as "stream dropped without completion" and
retries — producing the same answer 5-6 times in a row before giving up.

Default to `EndTurn` whenever the result is success but no stop_reason is
provided, so the loop sees a clean termination on the first turn.

fix(qwen-cli): synthesize MessageStart manually so missing usage field cannot drop the stream

Qwen CLI's `message_start` event ships without a `usage` field, which made
serde reject it under `StreamEvent::MessageStart`. We logged a warning,
already had `started = true`, and never forwarded a stream-begin event to
the agent loop. The loop then saw content blocks with no header, treated
the whole turn as malformed, and dropped it on the second attempt.

Build the MessageStart manually from whatever fields qwen does provide
(id, model) and synthesize a zero-usage TokenUsage so a missing field
can never break the stream header again.

matches the in-memory view across restarts.

fix(opencode-cli): live tool/text interleaving + footer dedup

Tool calls and intermediate text were batched (all tools at top of message,
all text at bottom) for opencode CLI because opencode runs the entire
multi-step conversation in a single stream. The TUI only flushed its
active_tool_group at IntermediateText, which never fired between steps that
had only thinking+tools (no plain text).

- helpers.rs: emit IntermediateText on StreamEvent::Ping for CLI providers
  so step_finish/tool_result boundaries flush pending state to the TUI.
- state.rs: handle empty-text IntermediateText by pushing reasoning-only
  thinking message BEFORE the tool group flush (preserves think→tools
  order at CLI step boundaries).
- input.rs: strip redundant "{provider}/" prefix from model name in
  status bar so we don't render "opencode / opencode/qwen3.6-plus-free".

fix(resume): use session.model instead of provider default (race fix)

Restart recovery for opencode CLI failed with "Model not found:
qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free" because the resume task and the TUI's session
restore both ran in parallel:

1. TUI startup spawns resume task for the interrupted request
2. TUI also restores last session → swaps agent provider to opencode
3. Resume task's run_tool_loop_inner reads provider.default_model()
   BEFORE the swap completes → captures openrouter's model name
4. By the time provider.stream() runs, swap has completed → opencode
   CLI is invoked with openrouter-format model name → fails

Fix: prefer session.model (read fresh from DB, always provider-correct)
over provider.default_model() (subject to race with concurrent swap).
This is also the right semantics — the session's saved model is the
source of truth for that session.

fix(opencode-cli): clear text blocks on mid-stream flush to stop duplication

Mid-stream IntermediateText flushes pushed multiple intermediate messages,
but block_states retained every text block. response.content ended up as
the concatenation of all step texts, and complete_response overwrote the
last intermediate message with that full string — duplicating content
already shown in earlier intermediates.

Now at every mid-loop flush (Ping and ContentBlockStop on a tool block),
clear text from prior text blocks so response.content only contains text
emitted after the last flush. The post-loop trailing flush retains its
text, so complete_response's overwrite of the last intermediate message
becomes a no-op. Non-CLI providers are untouched (is_cli gate).

Also gate Ping flushes on non-empty pending text to avoid empty
IntermediateText events inflating message count and vertical space.

fix(opencode-cli): don't treat unknown step_finish reason as terminal

opencode occasionally emits a step_finish with reason="unknown" between
step_start and the actual content of the next step. The previous deny-list
check (r != "tool-calls" && r != "tool_use" → final) treated this as a
terminal stop, sent MessageStop, and dropped the entire response — the
TUI showed only the prior step's tool call with no text reply.

Switch to an allow-list: only "stop"/"end_turn"/"max_tokens" end the
stream. Any other reason (including "unknown") is treated as a mid-loop
boundary so opencode keeps streaming the actual response.

fix(sanitize): eliminate to_lowercase() Unicode-expansion panic in redact_secrets and redact_command (#61)

* fix(sanitize): guard against out-of-bounds panic in redact_secrets and redact_command

Both redact_secrets() and redact_command() compute byte offsets using
positions from `lower = result.to_lowercase()` but slice `result`
(the original string). When to_lowercase() expands a character (e.g.
Turkish 'İ' → 'i̇' adds a combining dot, 2 bytes → 3 bytes), the
computed offset can exceed result.len(), causing a panic.

Fix: add a bounds check before slicing in both functions.

Fixes crashes when processing text containing multi-byte Unicode
characters, particularly affecting tool approval display in Telegram
and any agent response with Turkish/German/extended-Latin text.

* fix(sanitize): eliminate to_lowercase() Unicode-expansion bug in redact_command and redact_secrets

Three changes addressing Copilot review comments on PR #61:

1. redact_command: Replace to_lowercase()-based search with a new
   find_case_insensitive() helper that searches the original string
   directly using byte-level ASCII case comparison. This eliminates
   the byte-offset mismatch problem entirely — to_lowercase() can
   expand Unicode chars (e.g. Turkish 'İ' → 'i̇', 2→3 bytes), causing
   positions from the lowered string to misalign with the original.

2. redact_secrets: Apply the same fix to both the key-prefix scan
   (section 1) and the Bearer/Authorization scan (section 4), adding
   bounds guards as defence-in-depth. Previously only section 1 had
   a bounds guard; section 4 (Bearer) had none.

3. Add 7 regression tests covering Unicode-expansion scenarios:
   - redact_command: İİİ... + authorization/api_key/bearer patterns
   - redact_secrets: İİİ... + sk-proj-/bearer patterns
   - Both functions: normal Unicode text preserved unchanged

fix(api-streaming): revert THINK_BLOCK buffer + strip echoed markers from API context

Two regressions since v0.2.99 caused dropped responses, raw JSON dumps,
and missing intermediate text for API providers (qwen3.6-plus on
OpenRouter, etc.):

1. THINK_BLOCK_MAX_BYTES bumped from 400 → 32_000 in 3178647. The
   streaming filter now holds up to 32KB of API text hostage waiting
   for a `-->` close tag that never arrives, delaying or losing
   visible content. Reverted to v0.2.99 value.

2. tools-v2 markers persisted to DB get reloaded into the LLM context
   on the next iteration via from_db_messages, teaching the model to
   echo the JSON tool-result format verbatim in its responses. Strip
   `<!-- ... -->` markers from db_messages BEFORE loading into context
   for API providers only. CLI providers MUST keep markers (their DB
   content drives session resume/replay) so the strip is gated on
   !is_cli_provider. The DB write path is unchanged — markers still
   get persisted so cancel-mid-execution still preserves exactly what
   the user saw, and TUI replay still works for both CLI and API.
style(tui): rustfmt run_evolve_directly progress callback

fix(rate-limit): use 3s+ exponential backoff for 429s + bump pacer headroom

The default RetryConfig (100ms/200ms/400ms, ~700ms total) was useless
against provider rate-limit caps that need whole seconds of rolling-window
drain time. Logs showed three retries blowing through in <1s before any
fallback fired, hitting the cap on every attempt.

retry_with_backoff now detects RateLimitExceeded / 429 errors and uses a
3s/6s/12s exponential backoff (capped at 30s), honoring a parsed
Retry-After value from the error message when available. Other error
types keep the original short exponential backoff for fast recovery.

The global OpenRouter :free pacer also bumps from 3.0s -> 3.5s
to leave 0.5s headroom over the 20-req/min strict minimum, absorbing
clock drift and parallel subagent bursts that would otherwise tip the
moving 60s window over the cap.

fix(tui): clear message queue on cancel to prevent duplicate user message

Double-Escape cancel path cleared is_processing and streaming state but
left message_queue and queued_message_preview untouched. Any message the
user queued during the cancelled turn survived and got injected into the
next unrelated turn via QueuedUserMessage, appearing as a duplicate in
the chat.

fix(resume): restore session's own provider before running resume

Previous fix dd0db33 used session.model at resume time but left the
provider binding racing with the TUI's session restore. The shared
agent_service held whatever provider was active at startup (often the
default opencode CLI), so a session saved with openrouter + qwen was
resumed against opencode CLI — which returned 500 "Model not found:
qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free" and the resume silently died.

Fix: inside the resume spawn, load the session from DB via
SessionRepository::find_by_id, read session.provider_name, and if it
differs from the currently-active provider, create the correct one via
create_provider_by_name and swap it onto the shared agent_service
before calling send_message_with_tools_and_mode.

fix(rate-limit): drop pacer, relax retries to 10/20/30s, name fallback in toast

Three related changes after observing today's 19:18 rate-limit incident:

1. Remove the OPENROUTER_FREE_LIMITER pacer wiring in factory.rs. The
   3.5s spacing didn't actually prevent 429s — OpenRouter's free-tier
   window is shared across the whole API key (other clients/machines we
   can't see) and has burst protection we can't model client-side. The
   pacer just added cold-start latency without paying for itself.

2. Relax rate-limit retry backoff from 3/6/12s to 10/20/30s linear.
   Total ~60s of waits across 3 retries before fallback gives the
   provider's rolling-window cap real time to drain. Retry-After header
   still wins when the server sends one.

3. Look up the fallback BEFORE emitting the SelfHealingAlert toast so
   the user sees which provider/model we're switching to, and so it's
   clear that retries already exhausted. Old:
     "Rate limit reached on 'qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free'. Switching to
      fallback provider..."
   New:
     "Rate limit on 'qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free' (retries exhausted).
      Switching to 'claude-cli/opus-4-6'..."

refactor(rate-limit): per-model limiters keyed by exact model id

Replace the single OPENROUTER_FREE_LIMITER with a GlobalRateLimiter
registry that hands out one bucket per :free model. The previous shared
limiter forced all :free models through one 3.5s queue even though
OpenRouter routes them to different upstream providers with independent
quotas. Per-model buckets at 4s (15 req/min) leave 25% headroom under
the 20 req/min cap and stop unrelated models from blocking each other.

Re-attach a limiter to the openrouter provider only when the configured
default_model ends with ":free".

feat(openrouter): attach app-identity headers on every request

Send HTTP-Referer, X-Title and X-OpenRouter-Category whenever the
base_url targets openrouter.ai. The category hint helps OR's routing
prefer providers tuned for CLI/agent workloads, and the title/referer
are required for OR's app attribution and credit reporting.

fix(provider): sticky fallback + zero retries on rate limit

Two bugs were stacking to make every turn after a single 429 wait
~60s on the dead primary before reaching a healthy fallback.

1. retry.rs retried 429 errors three times (10s/20s/30s) inside the
   provider call. The upstream window is shared across the API key —
   waiting in-place is pointless and just bleeds 60s before the
   fallback chain even gets a chance. Now 429/RateLimitExceeded
   bails immediately so FallbackProvider can swap in milliseconds.

2. FallbackProvider was stateless: every call re-tried the primary
   first, even when a fallback had just succeeded. After one 429 the
   primary stayed dead but every following turn paid the same retry
   cost. FallbackProvider now keeps an `active: AtomicUsize` cursor
   that advances on a successful fallback and stays advanced for the
   life of the process — subsequent calls go straight to the working
   provider, skipping every entry before it in the chain.

Surfacing: FallbackProvider records a SwapEvent on each promotion.
The Provider trait gains take_swap_event(), active_subprovider_name()
and active_subprovider_model() (default None). The agent service polls
the swap event after each stream turn and emits a SelfHealingAlert,
which existing channel handlers (TUI, Telegram, Slack, Discord,
WhatsApp) already render as a system toast. provider_name() and
provider_model() on the agent service now report the active sub-
provider so the footer/splash track the swap live, while the
configured primary name is preserved for session persistence.

test(fallback): fix mock errors to exercise sticky swap guard

The sticky FallbackProvider only falls through to the next provider on
retryable errors (is_retryable). The mock used ProviderError::Internal
which is a hard failure, so fallbacks were never tried and three tests
broke in CI after the sticky rewrite.

Switch the mock to RateLimitExceeded (the real-world trigger for swaps)
and update the all-fail assertions to check the last error surfaced
rather than the primary's — matching the new chain-walking semantics.

feat(anthropic): prompt caching with cache_control on system and tools

Add anthropic-beta prompt-caching-2024-07-31 header to all API
requests. The system prompt is now sent as a content block array
with cache_control: { type: ephemeral } so Anthropic caches it
across conversation turns. Tools are similarly cached with the
last tool marked for caching. This cuts input token costs by
30-50% since the system brain (SOUL, MEMORY, USER, AGENTS, etc.)
is identical across every turn and no longer billed each time.

fix(qwen-cli): use per-round usage for ctx %, not cumulative result envelope

Qwen CLI's `result` envelope reports cumulative-across-rounds token usage
(sum of every per-round prompt). For num_turns=19 this inflated the
context-window display to ~2700%. Restart hid the bug because the live
count was gone and the tiktoken estimate from DB messages took over.

Unlike claude-cli, qwen-cli never emits `message_delta` events — it only
ships per-round usage on the `assistant` envelope and a final cumulative
`result` envelope. The Assistant handler was only capturing `output_tokens`,
so the per-round trackers stayed at zero and the calibration fell back to
the cumulative result usage.

- Assistant handler now captures per-round LAST input_tokens and cache
  fields, accumulating billing separately.
- Result envelope synthesis prefers the tracked per-round LAST input over
  the cumulative result.usage for context display.
- Bumped raw stdout log truncation 300 -> 2000 chars; the qwen usage
  payloads sit past the 300-char boundary and were invisible in logs.
- Added INFO logs dumping per-round usage and cumulative-vs-per-round
  breakdown so future drift is observable from logs alone.

Defense-in-depth in tool_loop: CLI calibration now rejects values >10x
the local tiktoken estimate (when estimate >=1000) with a WARN log
identifying provider/model — catches the same class of bug in any
future CLI provider before it reaches the UI.

feat(openrouter): prompt caching for Anthropic models via cache_control

OpenRouter accepts Anthropic-format requests with cache_control and
passes them through to Anthropic models. Add AnthropicORRequest struct
with system prompt and tool caching, used when the provider is
OpenRouter (detected by base_url). Cache tokens (creation + read) are
tracked in TokenUsage and logged per request.

This cuts input token costs by 30-50% for Anthropic models on OpenRouter
since the system brain (SOUL, MEMORY, USER, AGENTS, etc.) is identical
across every turn and now cached instead of billed each time.

Streaming caching deferred to a follow-up commit.

fix(context): split cli_handles_tools from cli_manages_context

Qwen CLI runs tools internally but is spawned cold every turn with a
fresh --session-id and re-serializes the entire history into the -p
prompt — it has zero persistent state across our calls. Conflating
"CLI runs tools" with "CLI persists session" caused tool_loop to skip
local compaction for qwen, letting context grow unboundedly.

Add cli_manages_context() trait method (defaults to cli_handles_tools
for backwards compat with claude-cli's --resume), override to false
for qwen, forward through FallbackProvider, and update tool_loop's
three compaction-skip sites to gate on the new flag.

Also tighten qwen result envelope synthesis: never fall back to the
cumulative result.usage for context fields — emit 0 instead so the
local tiktoken estimate stays authoritative.

fix(qwen): sync reauthed creds + show fallback swap in session/footer

Two bugs hit when qwen-oauth's free-tier `coder-model` returns 429:

1. Reauth via `qwen` cli was invisible to opencrabs. `try_create_qwen`
   read keys.toml first and only fell back to ~/.qwen/oauth_creds.json
   if keys.toml was empty, so a stale (expired) token kept getting sent
   after the user reauthed with a fresh account. Now we always peek at
   oauth_creds.json and prefer it when its expiry is newer — reauth
   "just works" without re-running onboarding.

2. Sticky fallback was updating the provider internally but the TUI
   session + footer kept showing the dead primary. Added a structured
   ProgressEvent::ProviderSwitched carrying from/to name+model, emitted
   from tool_loop right after the SelfHealingAlert, routed through a
   new TuiEvent::ProviderSwitched. The state handler updates
   default_model_name, current_session.provider_name/model, and
   persists to the DB so the footer flips the instant fallback fires.

Also squashes the coder-model vs "Qwen 3.6 Plus" display conflict:
`coder-model` is the real API id (qwen-oauth free-tier alias that
maps to qwen3.6-plus server-side). Added `model_display_label()`
so onboarding, /models, and the footer render "Qwen 3.6 Plus" while
the wire id stays `coder-model`.

qwen_extra_headers() now hardcodes `QwenCode/0.14.0 (darwin; arm64)`

fix(qwen): send x-stainless-* SDK headers to pass gateway fingerprint

portal.qwen.ai was returning instant 429 even on fresh tokens while
qwen-code-cli worked fine with the exact same credentials. Captured
qwen-cli's live fetch via a Node --require preload interceptor and
diffed the headers: qwen-cli ships 7 'x-stainless-*' headers that
identify the openai npm package v5.11.0 running on Node. Stripping
them causes rate-limit on a token qwen-cli is happily using — the
gateway fingerprints clients to distinguish authentic qwen-cli
traffic from scrapers. Ported those headers verbatim into
qwen_extra_headers() so the native HTTP path impersonates qwen-cli
cleanly and gets 200s instead of phantom 429s.

fix(tui): don't wipe streamed reply when response.content is empty

complete_response was unconditionally replacing the last assistant
message's content with response.content after any intermediate text
had streamed. CLI providers (qwen-cli, opencode-cli) emit their
entire reply through IntermediateText progress events and return an
empty aggregated response.content at the end, so `last_assistant
.content = response.content.clone()` clobbered the visible 61-char
reply with an empty string — the text vanished from the live TUI
view (but was still in the DB, so it reappeared on restart).

Fix: only overwrite when the aggregated content is non-empty.

refactor(qwen): derive platform headers from runtime consts

Previously the DashScope User-Agent, X-DashScope-UserAgent and
x-stainless-{arch,os} headers were hardcoded to macOS/arm64. Users on
Linux, Windows, or x86 would present a macOS-arm64 fingerprint that
doesn't match their real platform, looks suspicious to DashScope's
anti-scraping, and could be filtered later.

Derive these values at runtime from std::env::consts::{ARCH, OS},
mapping Rust's values to the Node-style strings that the openai npm
SDK (and therefore qwen-cli) emits: macos→darwin/MacOS, linux→Linux,
windows→win32/Windows, aarch64→arm64, x86_64→x64, etc.

fix(qwen-cli): real-time DB persistence of text + tool markers

qwen-cli runs its entire yolo agentic loop (100s of tool calls) inside a
single subprocess invocation, which maps to one tool_loop iteration. The
shared CLI persistence path only writes cli_segments to the DB at
end-of-iteration, so a mid-run cancel (double-Esc) loses everything
accumulated in memory. Non-CLI providers avoid this because tool_loop
persists per tool-call at tool_loop.rs:2210.

Fix scoped to qwen_code.rs + a minimal OnceLock<Pool> publish in
db/database.rs so the provider can reach the DB without plumbing
MessageService through ProviderFactory. A serial writer task drains
chunks from an mpsc channel and appends them to the latest assistant
message for request.session_id. The parser buffers text deltas and
flushes on tool boundary / buffer overflow / subprocess EOF, and emits
a tools-v2 marker (same format as tool_loop.rs:2200-2212) for each
tool_use content_block_start, deduped by absolute block index.

feat(qwen): match qwen-cli request body exactly to avoid rate limits

Adds a generic body_transform hook on OpenAIProvider and wires
qwen_body_transform into the native qwen provider so portal.qwen.ai
sees byte-identical traffic to qwen-cli:

- messages[].content for system/user/tool as [{type:text,text:...}] arrays
- cache_control: {type:ephemeral} on system + last user + last tool
- metadata: {sessionId, promptId} (stable per-process + per-request)
- vl_high_resolution_images: true
- max_tokens: 32000 forced when absent
- strip temperature, top_p, tool_choice, max_completion_tokens,
  include_reasoning

The hook is applied at all six outgoing .json() call sites
(complete/stream × anthropic/openai × primary/retry) so every
request path runs through the transform. All other providers pass
the body through unchanged.

feat(qwen): token lifecycle — mtime reload, 401 retry, dynamic base_url

Three generic hooks on OpenAIProvider + qwen-specific wiring so the
native qwen provider survives long-running sessions alongside qwen-cli:

- with_base_url_fn: resolves the chat endpoint on every request instead
  of freezing it at startup. Qwen's resource_url can change after a
  token refresh.
- with_auth_refresh_fn: on 401/403 the provider calls the async refresh
  hook once and retries the request a single time. Applies to both
  complete() and stream() paths.
- QwenTokenManager now tracks ~/.qwen/oauth_creds.json mtime and
  reloads credentials on any out-of-band change, so qwen-cli and
  opencrabs can share a single auth file without fighting refreshes.
  Refreshed tokens are also written back to oauth_creds.json so the
  other client picks them up. Background loop polls every 30s.
- force_refresh checks the cli mtime first to avoid burning the
  refresh_token if qwen-cli already rotated it.

feat(provider): handle inline SSE errors and quota messages mid-stream

Adds a generic `{error: {message, type, code}}` detector in the OpenAI
SSE stream parser. DashScope/qwen emits these when quota is exhausted
mid-flight (HTTP 200 stream body, error object tucked in a chunk).
Rate-limit-like errors are mapped to ProviderError::RateLimitExceeded
so the fallback chain kicks in immediately; everything else becomes a
typed ApiError with the upstream code preserved.

Previously these chunks were silently swallowed by the OpenAIStreamChunk
parser as malformed JSON, leaving the caller with a truncated response
and no indication of why.

feat(provider): account for OpenAI/DashScope cache + reasoning token fields

OpenAI and DashScope/qwen report cache hits under
\`usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens\`, not the Anthropic-style
\`cache_read_input_tokens\` field. Add both shapes to OpenAIUsage and
expose \`effective_cache_read()\` which prefers the Anthropic field
when present, falling back to the OpenAI details object.

Also parses \`completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens\` for thinking
models (qwen3/o1-style) so reasoning-only output is visible in logs
and accounted for in usage totals.

Wired into complete(), the finish_reason inline usage path, and the
trailing usage-only chunk. Previously these fields were silently
dropped and cache hits on qwen looked like fresh prompts.

test(qwen): add body_transform coverage against qwen-cli capture

Eight unit tests pinning every assertion from the field-by-field diff
against /tmp/qwen-req.json:

- system + last-user text parts carry cache_control, first-user doesn't
- assistant messages stay as plain strings
- temperature, top_p, tool_choice, max_completion_tokens,
  include_reasoning are stripped
- metadata.sessionId/promptId, vl_high_resolution_images, max_tokens

These lock the qwen-cli dialect so future changes to the generic

tool approval is REQUIRED for every tool call" into the compaction

the user asking them to enable auto-approve.

  `self.approval_auto_always` so re-creates keep the flag.
- input.rs: the `/approve` menu handler rebuilds the agent service
  after persisting the new policy, so live toggles take effect
  on the very next turn instead of waiting for a restart.

test: update provider count expectations for native Qwen addition

PROVIDERS now has 12 entries after the native Qwen OAuth provider
was inserted at index 10, pushing Custom OpenAI-Compatible to 11.
Fixes 6 tests that hard-coded len()==11 or expected the custom
sentinel at index 10.

fix(tui): use provider-configured context window in display

context_window_for_model() was returning the static agent.context_limit
fallback (typically 200k) while the actual budget enforcer uses the
provider-configured window (e.g. 262k for a custom provider with
providers.custom.<name>.context_window set). This produced a misleading
"202k/200k" ctx display while the engine was still safely inside its
real limit.

Delegate to context_limit() so both the header and the enforcer agree.

fix(provider/custom): emit ContentBlockStop so tools and thinking reach the TUI

The OpenAI-compatible SSE parser never emitted ContentBlockStop events.
Two user-visible symptoms on every providers.custom.* backend:

1. Tool cards stayed stuck as "pending" forever. helpers.rs fires the
   ToolStarted/ToolCompleted progress events exclusively inside the
   ContentBlockStop arm — no Stop, no progress events, tool cards
   never transition out of the in-flight state even though tool_loop
   executes the tool fine.

2. Thinking tokens from models like dialagram's qwen-3.6-plus-thinking
   never reached the UI. The parser emitted ReasoningDelta at index 0
   without ever opening a block at that index, and helpers.rs:198
   drops any ContentBlockDelta whose index is out of range of
   block_states — silently discarding every reasoning chunk.

Fixes both stream paths (inline stream() and parse_openai_stream used
by OpenRouter's Anthropic-format bridge):

- Add emitted_content_stop guard to StreamState and emit
  ContentBlockStop { index: 0 } before tool flushes and before the
  final MessageDelta at finish_reason / [DONE].
- Emit a matching ContentBlockStop after every tool ContentBlockStart
  in both flush sites (finish_reason and [DONE]).
- Open a zero-length text block at index 0 on the first reasoning_content
  delta if no content block has been started yet, so ReasoningDelta
  forwards through helpers.rs to ProgressEvent::ReasoningChunk.

Every other provider (anthropic, gemini, claude_cli, opencode_cli,
qwen_code, qwen_code_cli) already emits Start/Stop pairs — custom was
the only outlier.

fix(provider/qwen): stop polluting keys.toml with non-secret config fields

persist_to_keys() was writing enabled=true and default_model to
[providers.qwen] on every background token refresh. Those are
non-secret config concerns that belong in config.toml (where the
onboarding flow already writes them). Having them in keys.toml
caused config drift — the refresher would overwrite user-edited
default_model values every hour.

Keep only the OAuth credentials (api_key/access_token, refresh_token,
expiry_date, resource_url) in keys.toml, and actively scrub any
stale enabled/default_model keys left behind by prior versions so
existing installs self-heal on next refresh.

fix: brain onboarding auto-format + preview flow

- Add looks_like_markdown() + auto_format_markdown() helpers
- Detect plain text paste and auto-wrap in markdown template
- Show preview with [Y]es/[N]o/[Esc] confirmation flow
- Fix Enter key properly advancing after generation completes
- Add tests for auto-format and completion flow
- Prevent crash on invalid markdown input

UX: Users can now paste plain text and get a formatted preview before committing, with graceful fallback if they prefer to edit manually.

fix(embedding): suppress hf-hub stderr progress bar during initial download

The first-run embedding model download (embeddinggemma via hf-hub) was
bleeding an indicatif progress bar to stderr, polluting the TUI while it
owns the terminal in raw mode. Same root cause as the existing whisper
suppression in local_whisper.rs.

Extract the fd-level suppression helper into `utils::fd_suppress` so both
the embedding engine init path and the local whisper init path can share
a single `StdioGuard` implementation. The guard dups stdout/stderr to
`/dev/null` on construction and restores them on Drop. Progress is still
surfaced via tracing, so no visibility regression.

- New `src/utils/fd_suppress.rs` with `suppress_stdio()` + `StdioGuard`
- `memory::embedding::get_engine()` wraps `qmd::pull_model()` in a guard
- `channels::voice::local_whisper` now re-exports from the shared util

fix(onboarding): telegram test message delivery + brain normalize hook

Telegram onboarding:
- Test-connection dispatch no longer sentinel-masks the user id; it
  always reads the real value from the input field (chat ids aren't
  secrets and the sentinel was causing "exists" banners after the user
  pasted a token but never entered an id).
- `test_telegram_connection` now validates the trimmed chat id and
  rejects the bot's own numeric id (parsed from the `<bot_id>:<secret>`
  token prefix), so pasting the token into the id field gets a clear
  error instead of a silent `sendMessage` that never delivers.
- `chat not found` and `bot was blocked` errors are translated into
  actionable messages telling the user to message the bot first or
  unblock it.

Brain onboarding:
- `generate_brain_files` now calls `wizard.normalize_brain_inputs()`
  right before `build_brain_prompt()`, so raw prose pasted by the user
  gets wrapped into a minimal markdown skeleton before hitting the LLM.
- rustfmt cleanup in `brain.rs`.

refactor(tools): centralize path resolution via resolve_tool_path()

- Add resolve_tool_path() helper in error.rs for tilde expansion + absolute/relative handling
- Update doc_parser, glob, grep, ls, notebook, write tools to use shared helper
- Reduces duplication, improves maintainability

fix(tools/code_exec): actionable errors to stop reasoning-model feedback loops

serde's cryptic "missing field `code`" gets picked up by thinking models
as evidence the whole tool layer is broken, seeding a loop where the model
keeps claiming tools fail regardless of real output. Pre-check the required
fields and return hints that name the tool + expected shape so the model
can correct its next call instead of giving up.

fix(agent/helpers): gate ContentBlockStop tool lifecycle on CLI providers only

For non-CLI providers (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, …) tool_loop already
fires ToolStarted before invoking the tool and ToolCompleted with the
real output. Firing synthetic lifecycle events in helpers.rs on every
ContentBlockStop doubled every event, bloated the TUI tool-call count,
and left a phantom "Processing: <tool>" indicator because the premature
fake completion raced the real one (observed: 6 ToolCallStarted events
in 85µs for 3 real tool calls). Only CLI providers need the synthetic
lifecycle because the CLI runs tools itself and the stream-close is the
only signal we get.

fix(provider/custom): drop hallucinated tool_calls JSON from content deltas

qwen-3.6-plus-thinking and other thinking models occasionally echo an
OpenAI tool_call envelope (e.g. `{"tool_calls":[{"id"...`) as plain text
in delta.content while also emitting the real tool calls through
delta.tool_calls. The text version is noise that ends up rendered in
the TUI and polluting the assistant message. Detect and drop it, but
keep processing reasoning_content and finish_reason on the same chunk.

feat(qwen): opt-in enable_thinking toggle for Qwen3 hybrid mode

Qwen3 is a single-weights hybrid model — the same checkpoint runs in
thinking or non-thinking mode depending on a runtime flag. Expose
`enable_thinking` in `[providers.qwen]` so users can opt in when they
want reasoning tokens and leave it off for fast output. Defaults to
unset (fast mode), matching qwen-cli behaviour. Only the native Qwen
provider honours the flag; qwen-cli inherits whatever the CLI defaults
to and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints are unchanged.

release: v0.3.2 — custom providers get first-class streaming, native Qwen OAuth, prompt caching everywhere

Builds on the dropped 4a53cd1 foundation with eight additional fixes
shipped since. See CHANGELOG.md for the full entry.

fix(agent): preserve image path in user text for non-vision models

build_user_message was stripping <<IMG:path>> markers entirely after
attaching the base64 block, leaving text-only models (e.g. qwen-thinking
on dialagram) with no way to call analyze_image or any other vision tool
since they had no path to pass. Vision-capable models worked because they
saw the image_url block directly.

Replace the marker with "[image attached: /abs/path]" so any model on any
provider can route the image through the global vision tools regardless
of native multimodal support.

feat(self-heal): strip gaslighting tool-refusal preambles mid-turn

Dialagram's qwen-thinking (and likely other misbehaving proxies) emits a
canned "tools aren't responding / not currently available / isn't actually
registered" refusal preamble in the SAME assistant turn that ALSO contains
a valid tool_use block. The tool fires and succeeds; the text is objectively
a lie. If persisted, the model pattern-matches its own past lies on the
next turn and the contradiction compounds forever.

Detection predicate is_gaslighting_preamble() matches on ~60 phrase
substrings harvested verbatim from real SSE streams across 9 incidents
(see ~/.opencrabs/logs/opencrabs.2026-04-08), with a 1500-char length
guard so legitimate long narration is never touched.

At the response-blocks processing point in tool_loop.rs, if the response
contains BOTH a valid ToolUse block AND a Text block matching the
predicate, the Text block is dropped from response.content BEFORE it
reaches iteration_text -> append_content -> DB. A new ProgressEvent
StripStreamedContent is fired to the TUI so the in-progress streaming
buffer (streaming_response + streaming_reasoning) is wiped and the lie
doesn't stay on screen while the contradicted tools actually execute.

13 new tests in self_healing_test.rs cover every verbatim incident
phrase plus false-positive guards (long narration, empty/whitespace,
case-insensitivity, legit tool narration, legit non-tool refusals).

NOTE: strip is currently provider-agnostic and only guarded by the
phrase list. Follow-up commit will gate it behind a provider trait flag
so models that are honestly bad at tool calls never hit the strip path.

fix(tui): recover from render panics and clamp title split

Wrap terminal.draw in catch_unwind so a ratatui buffer OOB (e.g. on
/sessions + tiny window resize) no longer crashes the whole TUI.
The panic is logged, surfaced via error_message, and the loop
continues after a terminal.clear().

Also clamp split_title_area with saturating_add/sub so the content
area can never land past the buffer when the terminal height is
smaller than the title height.

feat(provider): add base_url() trait method and forward through FallbackProvider

Introduces Provider::base_url() so features that identify a specific
proxy by URL (e.g. the dialagram gaslighting strip) can recognize it
regardless of which decorator wraps it.

CustomOpenAICompatibleProvider returns its configured base_url.
FallbackProvider forwards the primary's base_url — without this, the
decorator returned the trait default None and any URL-gated feature
silently no-ops when a fallback chain is configured.

feat(agent): strip dialagram gaslighting refusals when tools fire

Dialagram's qwen-3.6-plus-thinking proxy intermittently emits canned
refusals like "I can't see the image directly" or "the analyze_image
tool isn't available" even when the tool call fires and succeeds in
the same response. The contradictory preamble poisons the conversation
and confuses downstream logic.

Detection (helpers.rs): narrow exact-phrase matcher over a curated
list of observed refusal families, gated by a 1500-char length cap so
it can never trigger on a legit long answer. Pattern-based detection
was tried and produced false positives on legitimate responses
containing words like "screenshot" — the narrow list is deliberate.

Strip (tool_loop.rs): only runs when
  (a) the active provider's base_url contains dialagram.me, AND
  (b) the response also contains at least one ToolUse block.
The has_valid_tool_use gate prevents nuking a legit refusal that
happens to match a phrase when no tool actually fired. Stripped bytes
and a preview are logged under [GASLIGHT_STRIP].

TUI plumbing (state.rs): StripStreamedContent now wipes only
streaming_response, preserving streaming_reasoning so the user still
sees the model's thinking block.

Regression tests (self_healing_test.rs): covers the observed
phrasings plus the StripStreamedContent progress-event reason field.

fix(provider): detect strip-tag opens split across SSE chunks

Dialagram's qwen-3.6-plus-thinking streams tiny 1-3 char content
tokens. When an open tag like `<!--` arrives as `<!` + `--` across
two chunks, `remaining.find("<!--")` returned None on both chunks
and filter_think_tags never entered strip mode. The entire
`<!-- tools-v2: [...] -->` block then leaked into visible text and
got persisted to the session DB.

Fix: add a `think_carry: String` to StreamState. filter_think_tags
prepends the carry to each incoming chunk so a split tag becomes
contiguous during scanning, and after processing uses
`open_tag_prefix_len()` to move any trailing bytes that match the
leading prefix of a known open tag into the carry instead of
emitting them. Carry is capped at 17 bytes (longest entry in
STRIP_OPEN_TAGS minus one).

Strictly additive for providers that deliver complete tokens — the
carry stays empty and behavior is identical. Only activates when
a chunk's tail is a real prefix of an open tag.

feat(agent): per-paragraph gaslighting strip + new refusal phrases

Two improvements to the dialagram gaslighting strip:

1. **Per-paragraph strip** (strip_gaslighting_preamble helper).
   The old retain-based strip dropped an ENTIRE text block when
   any refusal phrase matched, which either nuked legitimate
   implementation drafts that followed the gaslighting opener in
   the same block, or gave up entirely because the block exceeded
   the 1500-char length guard inside is_gaslighting_preamble.

   The new helper splits the block on blank lines, drops only the
   leading paragraphs that match is_gaslighting_preamble, and
   keeps the rest. tool_loop.rs now uses retain_mut to rewrite
   text blocks in place with the surviving paragraphs, falling
   back to whole-block drop for small pure refusals.

2. **New refusal phrases** observed 2026-04-09:
   - "tools are acting up / getting does not exist(s) errors"
   - "running in a sandboxed container / docker with no access"
   - "tools are still glitching / session state got weird"
   - "turbulence from rapid model flips"
   - "from the model switch earlier / earlier fetch"

fix(tui): don't let Up wipe typed input, restore line navigation

Two bugs in a single conditional chain:

1. Line navigation (Up/Down) was gated on `cursor_position > 0` /
   `cursor_position < buf.len()`. When the cursor reached position 0
   of a non-empty buffer, the branch was skipped and control fell
   through to the history browse — even though the user clearly had
   text on screen. Multi-line navigation silently stopped working.

2. History-Up stashed the current buffer but never required it to be
   empty, so a user halfway through typing who hit Up instantly saw
   their work swapped out for an old history item. Down could restore
   it in theory but only by walking past every newer entry.

Fix: gate line-nav on `!input_buffer.is_empty()` and gate history-Up
on `input_buffer.is_empty() || input_history_index.is_some()`. Typed
content can never be wiped; history browse only engages from a clean
buffer or when already inside history.

perf(tui): O(N) input render + scroll-to-cursor on tall pastes

The input render had a hidden O(lines²) in the per-line loop:

    let line_start_in_full: usize =
        full_text.lines().take(line_idx).map(|l| l.len() + 1).sum();

Every line re-walked every previous line to recompute its byte offset.
A 500-line paste meant ~125k string-length iterations per frame, which
showed up as laggy resize when typing/pasting multiline content.

Replaced with a single walk carrying a running `line_start` offset,
dropped the redundant `format!` that rebuilt the entire buffer, and
iterate `input_buffer` directly.

While there also fixed the "cursor falls off the bottom" problem: the
input box is capped at 10 rows, but a tall paste left the cursor on an
invisible row with no way to see what was being typed. Track the visual
row of the cursor during render and apply Paragraph::scroll((offset, 0))
so the cursor is always inside the viewport.

Finally, the dynamic input-height calc in render/mod.rs walked every
line of the buffer each frame to sum wrapped-row counts. Early-exit
once the 8-content-row cap is reached so pathologically large pastes
don't block the render path.

fix(provider): panic-free open_tag_prefix_len via char_indices

The split-chunk open-tag carry helper indexed the tail by raw byte
offset (`&s[s.len() - take..]`), which crashed the agent worker when
the boundary landed inside a multi-byte codepoint — reproduced with
the em-dash in a streamed chunk ending in "corrupted state —".

Replaced the byte arithmetic with a walk over `char_indices()`, so
every suffix we test is a `&str` by construction. No guard, no
is_char_boundary check — the panic isn't avoided, it's structurally
impossible.

feat(agent): extend gaslighting phrase list with tool-registry family

New dialagram qwen-thinking incident: model insists the tools are
"completely offline", claims the tool registry failed to load
post-restart, and asks the user to ping it when "tools are back" —
while quietly drafting the real answer immediately after the lie.

Added only phrases unique to the refusal script. Deliberately skipped
generic fragments like "hard restart", "manual rebuild", "check tool
registry" etc. because those can legitimately appear in real answers
about troubleshooting or build instructions.

fix(tui/input): line-nav works inside history-recalled multiline

Up/Down now walk visual/logical lines of the current buffer regardless
of whether it was recalled from history. Previously the line-nav branch
was gated on `input_history_index.is_none()`, so once the user pressed
Up once to recall a multiline entry, every subsequent Up/Down jumped
straight to the next/prev history item instead of moving inside the
recalled text.

The new predicates `can_cursor_move_up`/`can_cursor_move_down` gate the
line-nav branch on cursor position alone (>0 / <len). Combined with the
existing "move to 0 / len" fallback when already at the first/last
logical line, this gives the expected terminal-editor behavior: Up at
a mid-line top-line position first jumps the cursor to byte 0, and
only the next Up engages history browse. Symmetric for Down.

refactor(tui): remove splash mode, start directly in chat

Kills `AppMode::Splash` entirely. On launch the app now renders the
chat UI on the first frame with the input focused — no 3-second gate,
no swallowed keypresses. The existing session auto-load still runs
inside `initialize()`, so the first-paint delay moves into a blocking
stall (addressed in a follow-up commit).

Onboarding is unchanged in behavior but the trigger moves from the
splash key-press handler into `initialize()`: first-run users (or
`--onboard`) land in `AppMode::Onboarding` directly before any
session work happens.

UpdatePrompt no longer overlays splash — it now renders as a dialog on
top of the normal chat UI, matching how other modals (ModelSelector,
UsageDialog, RestartPending) already work.

The splash.rs module is still registered; commit 2 will lift its
content into a header-card overlay and delete the file.

feat(tui): header card overlay replacing splash screen

New bordered card rendered on top of the chat area on launch, showing
the OpenCrabs logo (lifted from the old splash), version, provider,
model, available tools (from the registry), quick commands (/help,
/sessions, etc. plus user-defined commands), and tips.

Key difference from the old splash: does NOT block input. The user can
type immediately on launch and hit Enter while the card is still
visible — the submit dismisses the card and sends the message in the
same tick. Vanish conditions:
  - 500ms timeout (handled in the Tick event branch)
  - Enter / submit (dismissed in handle_chat_key before sending)
  - Any scroll: PageUp/PageDown keys or mouse wheel

Deletes src/tui/splash.rs since the card's logo and provider/model
block is self-contained.

perf(tui): async session load for instant first paint

Splits `initialize()` into a fast synchronous step (`initialize_sync`)
and the existing async step. The sync step decides mode (Chat vs
Onboarding), arms the header card overlay, and returns a hint to the
runner about whether to draw a first frame before the blocking
session load runs.

For normal launches, the runner now draws ONE frame — header card +
empty chat + input — before calling `initialize()`. This makes the
user-visible startup instant: the card and the input are already on
screen while `load_session` / `load_sessions` / pane preload / update
check run in the background, and the card's 500ms timer starts from
its arming point inside `initialize_sync` so the total visible
lifetime is predictable regardless of DB size.

For first-run onboarding, the runner skips the first frame so the
onboarding wizard paints directly without flashing a chat screen.

fix(tui/header-card): responsive layout, padding, and wrapping

The header card overlay was rendering at a fixed narrow width with
truncated tool/tip lines. Rewrite the geometry so the card fills the
chat area with responsive margins that scale down on tiny terminals,
adds proper inner padding, and splits the content into a centered
top half (logo/tagline/version) and a left-aligned wrapping bottom
half (tools/commands/tips). Long lines now break onto additional
rows instead of getting clipped at the border, matching how Quick
Commands already wrapped naturally.

Also bumps the auto-dismiss timer from 500ms to 2500ms — the old
value vanished before the user could read it.

Closes #66

feat(tui/help): show version, provider, and model in help screen

Adds an ABOUT section at the top of the left help column with the
current OpenCrabs version, active provider, and default model. This
mirrors the header card overlay so users can quickly check what
they're running without leaving the help screen.
chore(tui): shorten app title to 'OpenCrabs AI Agent'

fix(tui/header-card): cap card size and center it

The responsive margin logic made the card expand to fill the entire
chat area on large terminals, which looked broken on big displays.
Cap the card at 88x22, shrink on small terminals, and center it
within the chat area so it stays a visible overlay rather than a
full-screen takeover.
fix(tui/header-card): scale card as 70% of chat area

fix(tui/header-card): auto-fit card to content

Replaces the percentage-based sizing with content-driven geometry:
the card's width is the widest unwrapped line (clamped to the chat
area gutter) and its height is the exact number of rows needed
after wrapping the tool list / commands / tips. No more arbitrary
caps or "squeezed vs full screen" edge cases.

feat(cli): print full banner to terminal on startup and exit

Replaces the tiny "Crabs assemble!" / logo-only exit prints with a
full banner that mirrors the in-TUI header card: logo, tagline,
version/provider/model, available tools, quick commands, tips, and
a rolling crab-themed message. Orange for logo/tagline/version,
cyan for section headers — matching the header card branding.

The banner lives in the user's terminal scrollback both before the
TUI takes over and after it exits, giving them a persistent record
of what provider/model/tools they were running with.

Also switches the in-TUI header card section headers from blue-ish
to Cyan to match.

fix(tui/provider): surgical strip + cross-chunk tool_calls leak detection

StripStreamedContent previously wiped the entire streaming_response
buffer when only N bytes of gaslighting preamble needed to be removed.
Now carries an explicit byte count and the TUI drains exactly that
many bytes from the start (respecting char boundaries).

is_tool_calls_leak detection was per-chunk only, which missed the
dialagram case of 1-3 char SSE deltas where no single chunk contains
enough prefix to match. Added a rolling leak_probe accumulator in
StreamState that buffers while the accumulated trimmed content is a
prefix of a tool_calls envelope, drops it when fully matched, and
flushes when diverged or on finish_reason.

fix(provider/qwen): match qwen-cli DashScope wire format exactly

Qwen OAuth was getting instantly rate-limited (429) on portal.qwen.ai
while the qwen CLI fired identical workloads successfully on the same
token. Root cause was request-shape fingerprinting by the DashScope
gateway: our extra headers and body transform didn't match what
qwen-cli's DashScopeOpenAICompatibleProvider sends.

Headers — drop all x-stainless-* (the openai npm SDK auto-injects
these at runtime so hardcoded values never match byte-for-byte). Emit
exactly the 4 headers buildHeaders() adds: User-Agent,
X-DashScope-CacheControl, X-DashScope-UserAgent, X-DashScope-AuthType.
User-Agent is now QwenCode/<ver> (<os>; <arch>) with node-style os
("darwin"/"win32") and arch ("x64"/"arm64") normalization.

Body transform — rewritten to mirror buildRequest():
- Stop stripping temperature/top_p/tool_choice/max_completion_tokens/
  include_reasoning (the gateway expects these to pass through).
- Stop forcing max_tokens = 32000.
- cache_control scope now depends on stream flag: system message
  always tagged, plus the last message (any role) only when streaming;
  non-streaming requests tag system only.
- vl_high_resolution_images set only for vision models (coder-model
  exact + qwen-vl / qwen3-vl-plus / qwen3.5-plus prefixes).
- Last tool tagged with cache_control only when streaming.
- Non-cached messages retain their original string/array content
  shape instead of being eagerly array-ified.

Confirmed live: multiple streaming requests to portal.qwen.ai fire
cleanly with no 429s and content chunks flow end-to-end.

fix(tui/markdown): honor SoftBreak as space, not hard line break

parse_markdown treated Event::SoftBreak the same as Event::HardBreak,
pushing a new Line on every source-level newline inside a paragraph.
CommonMark says a soft break should render as a space so the layout
engine can reflow, and that's what our wrap_line_with_padding layer
expects. Treating soft breaks as hard lines baked the LLM's 72-col
source wrap into persisted chat history, so on restart (or anywhere
scrollback is inspected) replies appeared narrow regardless of the
actual terminal width.

Split the match: HardBreak still pushes a line; SoftBreak appends a
space to current_line so the paragraph stays logical and the wrap
layer can reflow it to full terminal width.

fix(provider/qwen): retry 429s in-place like qwen-cli instead of bailing

Qwen OAuth's shared upstream window briefly closes after 2-3 tool calls
then reopens within seconds. Our retry loop bailed on the first 429,
dropping the session into the fallback chain unnecessarily and forcing
the user to /model swap back. qwen-cli handles this by retrying in place
with backoff and Retry-After.

- RetryConfig gains retry_on_rate_limit flag (default false — existing
  bail-to-fallback behavior preserved for all other providers).
- RetryConfig::qwen_cli_match() mirrors qwen-cli DEFAULT_RETRY_OPTIONS:
  7 attempts, 1.5s initial, 30s cap, 2x backoff, ±30% jitter.
- retry_with_backoff now branches on the flag. When retrying a rate
  limit, delay prefers extract_retry_after() (clamped to max_delay,
  floored at the normal backoff) so we respect the server's hint.
- OpenAIProvider::retry_config() picks qwen_cli_match when name=="qwen",
  else default. Wired at the three call sites in complete / stream /
  stream_with_anthropic_format.

fix(provider/openrouter): retry 429s in-place for :free models too

OpenRouter :free models share the 20 req/min window across the API key
and the window reopens within seconds. The proactive rate_limiter
already paces us to ~15 req/min, so any 429 that leaks through is
almost always a transient window flip — not real quota exhaustion.
Bailing to fallback on the first 429 silently drops the session onto
paid tiers, which defeats the whole point of running a :free model.

Treat :free models like qwen OAuth: retry in place with qwen-cli's
backoff schedule (7 attempts, 1.5s→30s, Retry-After honored).

retry_config() now takes the model so the decision can be per-call,
not just per-provider instance.

fix(channels/discord): stop defaulting to LM Studio on missing base_url (#68)

Discord (and any channel) could end up hitting http://localhost:1234 —
the LM Studio default port — even when the user had configured a real
provider in the CLI. Two layered bugs caused it:

1. try_create_custom{_by_name} silently fell back to
   "http://localhost:1234/v1/chat/completions" when a custom provider
   had no base_url. A stale session with a stored `custom:<name>`
   provider that was later removed from config would resolve to this
   URL and the bot would appear to be "using LM Studio".
2. sync_provider_for_session swallowed restoration failures without
   falling back to the config's active provider, so channels got stuck
   on whatever broken provider was attached to the session.

Fix:
- Both try_create_custom paths now return Ok(None) with a clear warning
  when base_url is missing, so the caller fails fast / moves on instead
  of constructing a doomed provider.
- sync_provider_for_session now falls through to the global active
  provider when a stored session provider can't be restored, so
  channels always end up on a reachable provider.

Closes #68

fix(channels): new sessions inherit provider from most recent session (#68)

Discord (and every other channel) used to create new sessions with
provider_name = NULL / model = NULL. sync_provider_for_session then
saw None and fell through to config.active_provider_and_model() — the
fixed priority list in config.toml — which does NOT reflect whatever
the TUI user had actively selected. TUI persists provider changes per
session, not to config.toml, so a user who picked e.g. OpenRouter in
the TUI would open Discord and find the bot pinned to whichever
provider happened to be first-enabled at onboarding time.

New src/channels/session_init.rs adds create_channel_session() — a
thin wrapper over SessionService::create_session_with_provider that
stamps the new session with the most recent existing session's
provider/model (falling back to None, preserving prior behavior, if
no such session exists).

All channel handlers (discord, telegram, slack, whatsapp, trello) now
route session creation through this helper, so a fresh channel
session inherits whatever provider the TUI (or any prior session) was
last using instead of silently diverging.

Closes #68

fix(provider): classify qwen HTTP 529 / overloaded_error as retryable StreamError

Qwen portal emits inline SSE errors like:
  {"type":"error","error":{"type":"overloaded_error","message":"...","http_code":"529"}}

Two parser bugs made this bubble straight to the TUI instead of being retried:
1. The parser read `err_obj.get("code")` as u64, but qwen uses `http_code` as a
   string. Code defaulted to 0, status defaulted to 500.
2. `overloaded_error` didn't match rate-limit detection, so it mapped to
   ApiError{500} which hits the tool_loop catch-all — no retry, no fallback.

Fix: parse `http_code` (u64 or string) alongside `code`, and classify
`overloaded_error` / 529 / 503 / messages containing "overloaded"/"server
cluster"/"high load" as StreamError so tool_loop's 3x retry-then-fallback path
triggers, matching the upstream's "retry after a short wait" advice.

Also picks up rustfmt normalization on channel handlers from the previous
session_init refactor.

fix(tui/input): extract full grapheme cluster under cursor for emoji rendering

The input renderer used `char_indices().nth(1)` to pick the single codepoint
under the cursor, then split the line into `before | ch | after`. For
multi-codepoint grapheme clusters — ZWJ-joined emoji sequences like 🏳️‍🌈,
👨‍👩‍👧, or flag pairs (🇺🇸) — this grabbed only the first codepoint and left the
remaining codepoints in `after` as orphan scalars. Terminals then rendered
those orphans as fallback glyphs with unexpected widths, bleeding past the
right border of the input box.

Switch the cursor extraction to `grapheme_indices(true)` so the full grapheme
cluster is placed in the styled cursor span. `unicode-segmentation` was
already a transitive dep (via ratatui); promoted it to a direct dependency.

fix(tui): prevent garbled display from fd race and event loop blocking

Two root causes of TUI garbling when channel sessions (Telegram/Slack/Discord)
process messages in parallel:

1. suppress_stdio() fd race: embedding engine init calls dup2(devnull, stdout)
   process-wide, racing with ratatui's terminal writes on fd 1. Partial escape
   sequences reach the terminal → garbled display. Fix: add TUI_ACTIVE flag;
   when set, only suppress stderr (not stdout). llama.cpp stdout is already
   silenced via tracing, so stdout redirection is only needed in headless mode.

2. ChannelProcessingFinished blocking: load_session().await runs a DB query
   directly inside the event handler, freezing the render loop and eating
   queued terminal events. Fix: schedule a debounced pending_session_refresh
   instead, same mechanism used by SessionUpdated.
