fix(tool/exa_search): support stateless MCP servers (missing session header)

Every exa_search call in the 2026-04-16/17 logs failed identically:

    [TOOL_EXEC] 💥 Tool 'exa_search' error: Tool execution error:
    Execution error: MCP server did not return session ID

5/5 failures = 100% rate per RSI feedback. The original init treated a
missing `Mcp-Session-Id` response header as a terminal error. But MCP
Streamable HTTP transport (rev 2025-03-26+) lets servers run in
**stateless** mode — each JSON-RPC request is standalone, the server
doesn't track sessions, and skips setting the header. EXA's hosted
endpoint at `mcp.exa.ai/mcp` apparently migrated to that mode.

init_mcp_session now returns Option<String>:
  - Some(id)  — session header present, keep and send the `initialized`
                notification as before.
  - None      — stateless mode, skip the notification (nothing to
                target), cache None so future calls don't re-initialize.

try_mcp_tool_call skips the Mcp-Session-Id header entirely in stateless
mode (sending an empty value would break some servers).

Any non-2xx init response still fails loudly with the server's status +
body (first 500 chars) so real breakages (500s, auth, protocol mismatch)
stay diagnosable instead of being swallowed behind a generic
"did not return session ID".

in on first call.

fix(tool/browser): detect dead CDP handler and relaunch instead of zombie (P1)

The 2026-04-19 09:49 "Navigation failed: channel closed" failure had
the underlying Chrome process already dead (OS kill / OOM / user
closed the window / socket break) but the BrowserManager still held a
cached Browser object. Next page.goto() hit the dead CDP channel and
failed. The manager never noticed the death — `ensure_browser`
early-returned on `inner.browser.is_some()`.

The CDP handler task we spawn in `ensure_browser` (lines 162-170) runs
`while let Some(event) = handler.next().await { ... }` until the socket
closes. When Chrome dies, the loop exits and the task finishes —
exactly the signal we need. Check `JoinHandle::is_finished()` in
`ensure_browser` and, if dead, tear down the stale Browser + pages
before running a fresh launch.

we now actually read it. Extracted the dead/alive decision as
`handler_is_dead(Option<&JoinHandle<()>>) -> bool` so it's pure and

fix(tool/browser): Drop impl aborts CDP handler + releases Browser (P3)

Previously, exiting opencrabs left the CDP handler task running as a
tokio zombie (it wouldn't re-spawn on next boot but its memory hung
around for the process lifetime) and the headed Chrome process could
remain visible with its CDP socket in a half-dead state. No Drop impl,
no signal handler, no explicit cleanup in main.rs.

Implement `Drop for ManagerInner` that runs when the last Arc clone
goes out of scope (natural app exit):
  - clears the page map
  - drops the Browser handle → Browser's own Drop closes the CDP
    connection → headless Chrome exits
  - aborts the handler JoinHandle so the tokio runtime doesn't wait
    on it during shutdown

Drop can't be async, so this is the synchronous subset. Full-graceful
(asking Chrome to close its windows first) would need a signal handler
in main.rs, out of scope for this commit.

fix(tool/browser): wait up to 10s for user's profile to unlock before falling back

profile lock before releasing it for additional instances. The old

fix(tool/browser_click): wait for network-idle after click instead of fixed 500ms sleep

Previously the click tool hardcoded a 500ms `tokio::time::sleep` after
every click to let the page settle. Two problems:

  - Too short for JS-driven pages: modern SPAs do hydration + AJAX
    chains that routinely run past 500ms, so the screenshot captured
    afterwards was often mid-load with skeleton placeholders.
  - Too long for simple toggles: clicking a checkbox or a disclosure
    button does no network I/O, so we burned 500ms for no reason.

Swap to `page.wait_for_network_almost_idle_with_timeout(3s)`. It
resolves as soon as ≤2 concurrent requests have been in flight for
500ms (the "almost idle" threshold), or the 3s cap elapses (silently —
a stuck page still falls through). Result: fast clicks are fast, slow
hydration gets the time it actually needs, stuck pages never hang
the turn.

No unit tests — chromiumoxide's wait_for_network_almost_idle drives
real CDP events from a running browser. Correctness is observable via
the existing click smoke tests users run through the TUI.

feat(tool/browser_find): new primitive for enumerating matches with stable selectors

Previously the agent had to roll its own element search by composing
browser_eval with hand-written JS like
`Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(...)).map(el => el.outerHTML)`,
parse the JSON result, then pass a hand-crafted selector into
browser_click. Three failure modes stacked:

  - JS syntax errors from imperfect string interpolation
  - non-unique selectors that matched a different element than intended
  - stale-reference races when the DOM mutated between the eval and
    the follow-up click

browser_find enumerates server-side, assigns each match a unique
`data-opencrabs-match="N"` attribute, and returns
`{selector, text, tag, visible}` per match with a selector
(`[data-opencrabs-match="N"]`) that survives DOM churn within the
turn. The follow-up click/type against that selector is deterministic.

Four modes:
  - css (default) — querySelectorAll
  - xpath — document.evaluate with ORDERED_NODE_SNAPSHOT
  - text — tree-walk with case-insensitive substring match on innerText
  - aria — [aria-label*="..." i]

Security boundary: user-supplied patterns are backslash- and
double-quote-escaped before interpolation into the JS string literal.
Raw double quotes would close the literal early and inject arbitrary
code into page context; raw backslashes would let subsequent chars
form escape sequences.

the match-object schema. No real browser required — the JS builder
is a pure `&str → String`.

release: v0.3.13 — Phantom detector expansion + channel dedup + browser reliability

29 commits since v0.3.12.

## Highlights

Phantom self-healing detector expanded with 28 new intent patterns.
The agent no longer drops requests after announcing investigative actions
("Let me hunt down...", "Now cherry-picking...") without calling tools.

Duplicate response elimination extended to Slack and WhatsApp, matching
the Telegram fix from v0.3.12. Slack image downloads now fall back
correctly when Slack returns HTML previews instead of raw bytes.

Browser tools received 10 reliability fixes plus a new browser_find
tool for stable element enumeration. wait_agent, exa_search, and
http_request all got targeted fixes.

## Self-healing

- 14 investigative intent phrases added (let me hunt/trace/track/look
  into/check into/find out/dig into + i'll variants).
- 14 "Now + gerund" patterns (now cherry-picking/updating/fixing/
  committing/pushing/merging/rebasing/deploying/building/testing/
  checking/applying/restarting).
- Regex-based gerund detection with sentence boundary requirement
  prevents false positives.
- Extracted has_investigative_intent() helper for testability.

## Channel dedup

- Slack: pre-send intermediate dedup + sanitized storage.
- Slack: image download fallback when url_private_download returns HTML.
- WhatsApp: pre-send intermediate dedup + sanitized storage.
- Discord: already clean (no intermediate sending).

## Browser tools

- NEW browser_find tool with CSS/XPath/text/aria modes.
- browser_click waits for network-idle instead of fixed sleep.
- browser_eval caps output at 50 KB.
- Per-session tab isolation, CDP handler lifecycle fixes.
- Stealth JS, dead CDP detection, SingletonLock sweep.
- macOS default browser detection via LSHandlers plist.

## Other fixes

- wait_agent resolves by prefix or label, lists actives on miss.
- exa_search supports stateless MCP servers.
- http_request sets default User-Agent to stop GitHub 403s.

## TUI

- Ctrl+O now works on first press for expand/collapse.
- History loading moved to scroll-up and PageUp instead of hijacking Ctrl+O.

## Test status

2,131 tests passing (+75 since v0.3.12).
7 new test files covering self-healing, browser, and tool fixes.

See CHANGELOG.md for the full list.

stdin = inherit, so they shared the TUI's controlling TTY. With
mouse capture enabled, every mouse move queues
`\e[<btn>;<x>;<y>M` bytes on that TTY. Any child that reads stdin
(pipes, `read`, bare `cat`, grep with no file args) consumed those
bytes and passed them through to its captured stdout, which became
tool output and leaked into the rendered TUI panel as raw escape
sequences after assistant messages.

The CLI providers (claude_cli, opencode_cli) already route stdin
through pipes or /dev/null. Apply the same to every tool spawn:

- bash.rs: normal `Command::new(shell).output()` path now pipes
  stdin from null (the sudo path already pipes stdin for the
  password write)
- dynamic/tool.rs: `sh -c` shell tools
- code_exec.rs: user-language interpreter runs
- evolve.rs: health_check_binary (`--version`) and the cargo-install
  spawn

Defensive — no tool has any reason to read from the TUI's keyboard.

fix(provider): unwrap proxy error envelopes and always log raw body

opencode.ai/zen wraps upstream failures as
  {"error":{"message":"Provider returned error","metadata":{
     "raw":"{\"error\":{\"message\":\"...real reason...\",\"type\":\"...\"}}",
     "provider_name":"Moonshot AI"}}}
so users saw only "Provider returned error" and had nothing to
diagnose. The real upstream message (e.g. Moonshot's
"thinking is enabled but reasoning_content is missing") was one
JSON-inside-JSON hop away.

- OpenAIError gains an optional `metadata` field and a new
  `OpenAIErrorMetadata` struct (raw + provider_name).
- unwrap_proxy_error walks the envelope, parses the stringified
  upstream payload, and returns (message, error_type) from the
  inner error. When a backend name is present it's prefixed like
  "[Moonshot AI] ..." so operators know which provider actually
  failed.
- handle_error now always logs the raw body at WARN regardless of
  parse outcome. The old non-OpenAI-only log left operators blind
  when the envelope parsed but hid the truth.
- Display for ApiError no longer prints empty "[]" when error_type
  is Some("").

fix(provider): retry transient proxy-passthrough 400s

HTTP 400 is non-retryable by default because it almost always
reflects a bad client payload. Proxies like opencode.ai break that
assumption: they return 400 with an empty `error_type` and a generic
message ("Provider returned error", "Upstream error", "Bad gateway")
when their upstream backend had a transient hiccup. Under the old
rule, one upstream flake → immediate fallback, so the user ping-
ponged onto a different model / subscription on every minor blip.

is_retryable now additionally retries HTTP 400 when:
- error_type is missing or empty (real client errors always carry
  a type like "invalid_request_error"), AND
- the message is empty or matches a known proxy-passthrough phrase

Default RetryConfig (max_attempts=3) now gives opencode.ai's
"Provider returned error" 400s three attempts with exponential
backoff before the fallback chain takes over. Real client 400s
(e.g. Moonshot's "thinking is enabled but reasoning_content is
missing") carry a non-empty error_type and correctly stay
non-retryable so we don't hammer the server with known-bad input.

fix(provider): echo Thinking blocks as reasoning_content for kimi/Moonshot

Moonshot kimi (direct and via opencode.ai/zen/go) 400s with
"thinking is enabled but reasoning_content is missing in assistant
tool call message at index N" when an assistant tool-call message
doesn't carry upstream reasoning. We were silently dropping every
Thinking content block in the OpenAI-compatible encoder, so kimi
failed on any multi-turn tool loop as soon as the first reasoning
block should have been replayed.

- OpenAIMessage gains an optional `reasoning_content` field,
  serialized only when set so providers that don't understand it
  (OpenAI, Anthropic, Zhipu, Minimax) see no change.
- The encoder collects text from ContentBlock::Thinking into a
  per-message buffer and emits it as `reasoning_content` on the
  assistant message (tool-call or plain).
- `needs_reasoning_content_for(base_url, model)` identifies the
  Moonshot-backed routes (direct moonshot.ai and
  opencode.ai+kimi). When we have no captured thinking text on a
  resumed turn, we inject an empty string so Moonshot's validator
  is satisfied instead of 400ing.
- Bumps visibility of OpenAIError*, unwrap_proxy_error, and
  is_transient_proxy_400 to pub(crate) so the tests in
  src/tests/provider_error_proxy_test.rs can exercise them.

Tests cover:
- opencode.ai envelope unwrap → [Moonshot AI] + real upstream msg
- non-JSON metadata.raw and no-metadata fallbacks
- Display no longer prints empty [] for Some("")
- retry budget applies to generic proxy 400s; bypass for real
  invalid_request_error / model_not_found
- needs_reasoning_content_for positive (opencode+kimi, moonshot)
  and negative (opencode+qwen, zhipu, minimax, openai) matches

fix(agent): thread real reasoning through context for kimi/Moonshot

The initial reasoning_content fix echoed a "[resumed]" placeholder
when no Thinking block was present on an assistant tool_call
message. It satisfied Moonshot's validator but discarded the actual
reasoning context from the conversation history — assistant turns
resumed from DB or mid-tool-loop were sent back with fake reasoning
instead of what the model originally produced.

Root cause: the LLMResponse stream returned `(response, reasoning)`
as a tuple. `response.content` held text + tool_uses but the
reasoning string was kept separate, used for UI / DB persistence,
then dropped before the assistant message was pushed to the agent
context. On resume from DB, `from_db_messages` only rebuilt
ContentBlock::Text from each row — the `thinking` column added in
14cbd51 was never read back.

Now:
- tool_loop.rs injects reasoning_text as a leading
  ContentBlock::Thinking on the assistant message it pushes to
  context each iteration (idempotent — skips if the response
  already carried one).
- from_db_messages reads the `thinking` column on assistant rows
  and prepends a ContentBlock::Thinking when non-empty. Rows with
  only thinking (no final text) are kept instead of skipped.
- The OpenAI-compatible encoder now serialises the real Thinking
  block text as `reasoning_content` on assistant tool_call
  messages. The `"[resumed]"` band-aid is gone; the last-resort
  fallback (" ") only fires for pre-14cbd51 DB rows where we can't
  reconstruct the reasoning.
- Removed the temporary [REQ_ENCODE] debug log.

Tests in src/tests/kimi_reasoning_test.rs cover:
- DB rehydration (user rows unaffected, empty/thinking-only rows
  handled, assistant rows gain a leading Thinking block)
- encoder emits reasoning_content verbatim from Thinking; fallback
  only fires for kimi/Moonshot when no Thinking present; non-kimi
  providers stay untouched when neither side has reasoning; real
  reasoning passes through to any provider that happens to carry
  a Thinking block.

fix(agent): tighten cloud-provider stream-handshake timeout to 30s

NVIDIA's `integrate.api.nvidia.com` was wedged on 2026-04-25 — TCP
accepted, headers never sent — and the previous blanket 90s
handshake timeout meant 3 retries × 90s = ~3 min before the
fallback chain fired. Logs at 16:14:25 → 16:18:56 walked the full
budget on a known-down upstream while the user waited.

The retry count itself is fine: 3 attempts with backoff is the
right knob for "the gateway might recover next time". The bug was
the per-attempt budget. Healthy cloud providers (OpenAI, Anthropic,
Zhipu, opencode.ai, NVIDIA NIM) return response headers in under
5s; 30s gives 6× headroom for real latency and only kicks in when
the gateway is genuinely wedged.

- Cloud HTTP (default for any URL that isn't local): 30s.
- Local HTTP (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / RFC1918 / *.local / [::1]):
  unchanged at 90s. Cold-loading a 35B gguf takes 30+ seconds —
  Unsloth log 2026-04-17 20:18 succeeded at +38s on retry 2.
- CLI providers: unchanged at 600s (subprocess + auth refresh).

Worst case before fallback drops from 270s → 90s for cloud, no
change for local, no change for CLI. Pulled the matrix out as
`handshake_timeout_for(cli, base_url)` so it's directly testable
without spinning up an async stream — 4 tests in
src/tests/handshake_timeout_test.rs cover every branch (CLI,
local IPv4/IPv6/RFC1918/.local, every cloud provider we support,
and the no-base_url case).

fix(rsi): window tool failure stats so stale alerts age out

Tool failure rates were aggregated over the entire feedback ledger
lifetime. A tool that broke once and was fixed reported "100%
failure rate" forever — until accumulated successes finally
exceeded accumulated failures. The 2026-04-25 RSI logs were full
of stale alerts:

  RSI opportunity: Tool 'exa_search' has 100% failure rate (5/5)
  RSI opportunity: Tool 'wait_agent' has 100% failure rate (6/6)

stateless mode, etc.). The RSI feedback table just had:
- 5 exa_search failures, all 2026-04-14 → 04-17, no successes
- 6 wait_agent failures, all 2026-04-17, no successes
…and `stats_by_dimension` aggregated forever, so any dimension
with no recent activity carried its old failures into every cycle.

since)`. Same SQL shape as the existing `stats_by_dimension` (kept
as a thin lifetime-aggregate wrapper for callers that genuinely

- tools with no events in the last week disappear from the report
- tools with REAL recent failures (browser_navigate, latest hit
  04-22) remain visible and actionable
- success rate is computed only from in-window events, so a tool

fix(telegram): key channel sessions by stable chat_id, not title

A "🦀 KRAB-INCEPTION 🦀" Telegram group was renamed to "🦀 HEY IOLO
BUILD 🦀" mid-conversation. The handler looked up by the new title
via `find_session_by_title`, missed, and created a brand-new session
row — orphaning a month of history (3020 messages, $258, 930M
tokens) and starting fresh under a duplicate id. Same bug fires
for any chat rename: title is user-mutable, chat_id is stable.

The fix embeds the stable Telegram chat_id as a `[chat:N]` suffix
on every new session title and looks up by that suffix on resolve.
Renames change the prefix (label) but the suffix stays put, so the
lookup keeps pointing at the same row.

Lookup chain in handler.rs:
  1. find_session_by_title_suffix("[chat:N]") — primary path,
     handles all post-fix sessions and any session ever migrated
     forward by step 2.
  2. find_session_by_title(legacy_format) — fallback for sessions
     created before this fix. On hit, the row's title is rewritten
     to the new "{label} [chat:N]" format so subsequent lookups
     go through path 1.
  3. Create a new session with the new format.

When path 1 hits but the stored label differs from the current
chat_title (rename happened since), the row's title is rewritten
to reflect the current label so /sessions etc. show what the user
actually sees.

New helper:
  - SessionRepository::find_by_title_suffix(suffix)
    — `WHERE title LIKE '%{suffix}' AND archived_at IS NULL
       ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1`
  - SessionService::find_session_by_title_suffix(suffix) wrapper

Tests in src/tests/session_chat_id_lookup_test.rs (8):

- finds it specifically when label changed but suffix didn't
- ORDER BY updated_at DESC picks the most recent on duplicate suffix
- archived sessions are excluded
- nonexistent suffix returns None
- suffix-as-substring (mid-title) does NOT match — anchored to end
- service layer delegates to the repo correctly
- service returns None for unknown suffix

fix(prompt): collapse $HOME → ~ in the system-prompt working_directory

The runtime info section of the system brain rendered the working
directory as the absolute path:

  Working directory: /Users/adolfousierstudio/srv/dart/heyiolo

Two problems with that:

1. Privacy/identity leak. Every request the agent fired out to any
   provider carried the local username (`/Users/adolfousierstudio`)
   as a literal token. That ends up in provider logs, prompt-cache
   keys, and any third-party proxy in the chain.

2. Cache-key drift across machines. The same agent run on a
   different developer's machine would emit a different prompt
   prefix purely from the username substitution, breaking
   prompt-cache reuse for cross-machine providers.

3. Token cost. `/Users/adolfousierstudio/srv/dart/heyiolo/...` is
   noticeably longer than `~/srv/dart/heyiolo/...` — every
   path-bearing line in the prompt pays the difference.

Adds `tools::error::collapse_home(&Path) -> String` as the inverse
of `expand_tilde`. Replaces a leading `$HOME` with `~`, falls back
to the original path string when no replacement applies. Wires it
into all three `RuntimeInfo` construction sites (cli/ui.rs,
cli/commands.rs ×2) so every system brain rendered today emits
`Working directory: ~/...`.

- collapses path directly under home
- collapses bare home → "~"

- passes through relative paths unchanged
- round-trips with expand_tilde
- collapsed string is strictly shorter than absolute for home paths

feat: persist recent file paths across sessions to anchor the agent

Logs from 2026-04-25/26 showed 73 path-not-found failures across two
days, with a single wrong guess (`heyiolo/lib/screens/...`) accounting
for 36% of them. The cluster ran inside one uncompacted session — so
the agent wasn't losing context, it was reaching for generic Flutter
conventions instead of the project's actual `lib/presentation/...`
layout. A prior session had already discovered the correct paths;
that knowledge died when the process exited.

Stores `(working_directory, path)` in a new `recent_paths` table on
every successful read/edit/write/ls/grep, both keys collapsed to
`~/...` form so they're stable across machines. At prompt-build time
the top 12 most-recent paths for the current project are appended to
the system brain as a "Recently accessed in this project" anchor,
filtered against the live messages so the section is silent during
normal uncompacted runs and only fires on cold starts or
post-compaction turns where the literals would otherwise be gone.

fix(tui): suppress URXVT-mode mouse fragments leaking into input buffer

EnableMouseCapture asks for both SGR (1006) and URXVT (1015) tracking
formats, and some terminals send motion events as URXVT (`\x1b[Cb;Cx;Cy M`)
even when SGR is also enabled. When crossterm consumes the leading ESC
byte as a bare KeyCode::Esc and the rest of the sequence arrives as
individual Key(Char) events, the URXVT format leaks: `[35;1;101M` lands
in the input buffer one char at a time, ratatui happily renders it,
and a fast mouse drag produces hundreds of these — the user sees a
wall of `[NN;NN;NNM` text and keyboard input lags behind the backlog.

The Apr 23 stdin-detach fix plugged the noisier subprocess-echoes-bytes
path; this is the residual leak it didn't cover.

`is_mouse_sequence_fragment` only knew about the SGR `[<…M` shape.
Extend it to also match URXVT's `[N;N;NM` shape, and broaden the
"bare `[` followed by mouse-alphabet" rule to include `;` and digits
so a sequence whose intermediate bytes were already suppressed can't

fix(rsi): make brain files append-only with backup-before-write

The 2026-04-26 RSI agent shrank ~/.opencrabs/TOOLS.md from 33 KB down
to a stub by passing the entire file as `old_content` to a
`self_improve` action="update", and did the same to MEMORY.md. Two
write paths could destroy a brain file in one call:

- self_improve action="update" — replacen(old, new, 1) with no size
  check; a huge old + tiny new effectively wipes the file.
- write_opencrabs_file operation="overwrite" / "replace" — same
  problem, plus overwrite has no read step at all.

Brain files are append-only by user policy. Removals are allowed
only when the bytes disappearing are duplicates that survive
elsewhere in the result.

New `brain_file_safety` chokepoint:

- Identifies the protected set (SOUL/USER/AGENTS/TOOLS/CODE/SECURITY/
  MEMORY/BOOT/IDENTITY .md), case-insensitive.
- `check_no_shrink` rejects writes that shorten a protected file
  unless the caller sets `dedup_intent=true` AND every non-blank line
  of the original still appears in the result. Sneaky deletions
  hidden behind dedup_intent get a tailored rejection message.
- `backup_before_write` snapshots the file to
  `<name>.YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMSS.bak` before any mutation.

Wired into both write paths. Both tools now expose `dedup_intent` in
their input schema so the agent has a discoverable, narrow escape
hatch instead of resorting to bulk replacements.

fix(prompt): anchor ~ to literal home and tell agent the shell expands tilde

Telegram (and any channel) regressed after 12344fa collapsed `$HOME → ~`
in the system prompt: with the literal username gone, the model started
inventing one when it needed an absolute path, typically the user's
first name from git config — `/Users/adolfo/...` instead of
`/Users/adolfousierstudio/...`. Every shell call to a sister project
failed because the path didn't exist.

Two short additions, both directly under the `Working directory:` line
in the runtime info block:

- `Home: <absolute home>` so the model has ground truth if it ever
  needs the expanded path.
- A one-line rule telling it not to substitute `/Users/<name>/...`
  itself — pass `~/...` verbatim and the shell expands it.

Wired into both render paths (build_system_brain and build_core_brain)
so neither code path can regress without breaking tests.

fix(bash): reject interactive commands up-front instead of looping

After the 2026-04-23 stdin-detach fix, interactive commands like
`git add -p` no longer hang or steal keystrokes — they exit silently
with code 0 on EOF, leaving the hunk preview text in stdout. The bash
tool reports ✅ success, the agent reads the prompt text, decides
"this would hang", explains to the user, then retries the same command
on the next turn. Free self-loop.

Adds `check_interactive_command` covering the families the agent
actually reaches for:

- git add -p / -i / --patch / --interactive
- git rebase -i / --interactive
- git commit with no message source (no -m, -am, --message, -F,
  --no-edit, etc.)
- editors: vim, vi, nvim, nano, emacs, pico, ed, joe, micro
- pagers: less, more, most, man
- TUI process viewers: top, htop, btop, atop, iotop
- bare REPLs: python, python3, node, irb, ghci, scala
  (allowed when -c / -e / a script path is present)
- DB clients: psql (no -c/-f), mysql (no -e), bare redis-cli
- interactive selectors: fzf, gum, tmux, screen

Each rejection includes a non-interactive alternative ("use git add
<path> or git apply", "use the edit_file tool", "use ps aux", etc.)
so the loop breaks on attempt 1 with a concrete next step.

Walks each segment of `&&` / `||` / `|` / `;` chains so
`cd foo && vim bar` is caught even though the leading `cd` is fine.
Skips leading `KEY=val` env-var assignments before checking the
command word.

Bash tool description also gets two short lines of guidance: stdin is
/dev/null (so interactive commands won't work — list given) and each
call is a fresh shell (so `cd` doesn't persist; chain with `&&` or
use `git -C <path>`).

fix(bash): short-circuit when the agent retries the exact same failing command

Layer 3 of the bash retry-loop guard. Layers 1 (interactive command
rejection) and 2 (tool description hints) catch most loops on attempt
1. Layer 3 is the catch-all for any other failure mode — exit-non-zero
commands, working-dir-not-found rejections, anything — by short-
circuiting a follow-up call with the exact same string.

Per-session ring buffer (capped at 5) of recent commands and their
outcomes lives in a process-wide OnceLock<RwLock<HashMap<Uuid, ...>>>.
Each bash call:
1. Working-dir check; record failure if missing.
2. NEW: check_recent_failure — if this exact command was just run and
   failed in the last 5 calls, return a strong "you already tried this"
   error that quotes the prior error snippet. Don't even spawn.
3. Layer 1 interactive-command pre-flight; record rejection on hit.
4. Run the command; record success or failure with first 300 chars of
   error output.

Move-to-front semantics: re-recording the same command bumps the
existing entry rather than stacking duplicates, so a flapping command
doesn't crowd legitimate other history out of the window.

Successful commands aren't held against retries — only failures
intercept follow-ups. Different sessions are isolated by Uuid key.

fix(agent): walk fallback chain on HTTP 402 (quota/payment exhausted)

The fallback trigger covered 401, 403, 429, and `InvalidApiKey` but
not 402. Provider returning `API error (402) [payment_required]:
Payment Required` propagated straight through to the user with no
warning, no fallback, no recovery — same failure mode the 2026-04-18
401-from-opencodeiolo regression hit before that case was wired up.

Treats 402 as fallback-eligible and tags it with its own classification
("payment_required" / "Quota/payment limit") so the SelfHealingAlert
distinguishes a billing exhaustion from a real auth failure or a
transient rate limit. The downstream walk-the-chain logic is unchanged.

fix(agent): per-session message queue + move inline tests under src/tests/

Two bugs fixed in one commit because they live in the same plumbing.

LEAK: pane A's queued user message was being injected into pane B's
turn. Root cause: App had two stores for queued messages — a per-
session HashMap used only for UI rendering, plus a process-wide
`Arc<Mutex<Option<String>>>` slot used by the agent inject path.
The MessageQueueCallback was nullary (`Fn() -> ...`) and just drained
the shared slot, so whichever agent loop hit a tool boundary first
won the message regardless of which session queued it.

Replaces both stores with one `Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<Uuid, Vec<String>>>>`.
Single source of truth: UI renders from it, the inject callback drains
from it. The callback signature gains a Uuid parameter — caller passes
its own session_id, lookup is keyed, cross-session reads are physically
impossible. std::sync (not tokio) Mutex because the lock is only held
across HashMap ops, never across an .await; the !Send guard makes
"hold across await" a compile error.

Wires through tool_loop.rs (2 call sites), helpers.rs::stream_complete,
the closure in cli/ui.rs, plus the App field, render paths, and every
write site in tui/app/.

fix(bash): isolate child TTY and prompt for SSH passwords via TUI

Two related TUI-corruption bugs are fixed by detaching every bash-tool
child from the controlling terminal before exec.

Setsid pre_exec hook
  Programs that bypass stdin and open /dev/tty directly (ssh password
  prompt, sudo getpass fallback, getpass-based readers) used to steal
  the user's TTY. The shell switched to no-echo mode, keystrokes (cursor
  keys -> "[[[[[[") got eaten by the child instead of the TUI, and the
  rendered chat filled with escape sequences until restart. setsid()
  in pre_exec puts the child in a fresh session with no controlling
  terminal, so any open("/dev/tty") returns ENXIO and the program
  either fails cleanly or falls back to a non-TTY auth path.

SSH password callback
  ssh/scp/sftp/rsync now go through a probe-then-prompt flow:
    1. Run with -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15 first. Key auth
       success path stays single-round-trip with no UI prompt.
    2. If the probe exits with a recognisable auth-failure stderr
       (Permission denied, password:, Host key verification failed,
       publickey,password, ...) and a callback is wired, request the
       password from the user.
    3. Retry the original command with SSH_ASKPASS pointing at a
       throwaway shell script that emits the password from a chmod-0600
       tempfile. Both files are NamedTempFile and clean up on Drop.
  The TUI dialog is a mirror of the existing sudo dialog, with a
  different title ("SSH password required") and prompt label ("Target:").
  Channels currently get None for the callback, which surfaces the
  raw probe stderr to the agent instead of bleeding into chat -- a
  channel-side approval-card flow can wire through the same callback
  type later.

Detection skips invocations that already opt out of password auth
(BatchMode=yes, PreferredAuthentications=publickey,
PasswordAuthentication=no) and ssh-keygen/ssh-keyscan/ssh-add.

Adds 10 unit tests for parse_ssh_invocation in
src/tests/bash_ssh_detection_test.rs covering plain ssh, scp/rsync,
identity flag, and all opt-out conditions.

feat(rsi): autonomous tool & command proposals via inbox

The autonomous RSI loop can now propose new dynamic tools (tools.toml)
and slash commands (commands.toml), the same way it already proposes
brain-file edits. Direct installation stays gated behind user review:
RSI writes proposals into ~/.opencrabs/rsi/proposed_*.toml; the
user-facing agent applies them on request.

Why split write from install
  A hallucinated paragraph in SOUL.md is recoverable. A hallucinated
  shell tool that runs at next invocation is not. The propose-then-
  apply split keeps RSI hands-off the live registries while still
  closing the autonomous-improvement loop: when the user says
  "show proposed" / "implement those", crab calls rsi_proposals and

fix(bash): POSIX single-quote askpass tempfile path

The SSH_ASKPASS shell script previously interpolated the password-file
path inside double quotes, which leaves $VAR / `cmd` / "" sequences
live to /bin/sh. tempfile names can't contain those characters today,
but the directory portion comes from $TMPDIR — a hostile $TMPDIR was
the only theoretical break-out vector for the askpass flow.

Switch to a POSIX single-quote escaper: wrap the path in `'…'` and
turn any embedded `'` into `'\''` (close, escaped quote, reopen).
Single-quoted strings in /bin/sh are 100% literal, so nothing inside
is ever expanded.

Adds 9 unit tests in src/tests/bash_posix_quote_test.rs covering plain
paths, embedded $/`/"/spaces/newlines, and single-quote escaping.

ci: add cargo-audit job for dependency CVE scanning

Catches RUSTSEC advisories on every push/PR. Uses taiki-e/install-action
for a prebuilt cargo-audit binary so the job runs in seconds without
compiling.

Cargo.lock is gitignored in this repo, so the job runs
`cargo generate-lockfile` first to give cargo-audit something to read.
A fresh resolve also picks up any patched compatible versions
automatically (e.g. rustls-webpki 0.103.13 lands without a manual bump).

One advisory is ignored: RUSTSEC-2024-0437 (protobuf 2.x uncontrolled
recursion, reached transitively via crabrace 0.1.0 → prometheus 0.13.4).
DOS-class only, no upstream fix without a major-version bump in the
prometheus chain we don't own. Reassess when crabrace drops prometheus
0.13.x.

refactor(skills): adopt SKILL.md layout with YAML frontmatter

Skills are moving to the de-facto format used by Claude Code, Anthropic's
managed agents, and OpenClaw: a directory per skill with a single
`SKILL.md` carrying YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) followed by
the prompt body.

The frontmatter is what makes a skill auto-discoverable by harnesses —
the `description` is read by the LLM to decide when to invoke the skill,
so it must be tight and trigger-rich.

Migrates the existing flat `cost-estimate-audit.prompt.md` to
`cost-estimate/SKILL.md`. Body unchanged; only adds the frontmatter
header and renames to drop the `-audit` suffix (the description already

Establishes the template for everything that follows.

feat(skills): add security-audit skill

Comprehensive, language-agnostic security & CVE audit. Detects the
project type from manifests (Cargo, npm/pnpm/yarn, pip-audit, govuln,
bundle-audit, composer audit, osv-scanner for Java/Dart/Swift, dotnet
list package --vulnerable, mix deps.audit, tfsec, trivy) and dispatches
to the appropriate scanner — no hardcoded assumption that the project
is Rust.

Eight stages:
  1. Project detection (manifest fingerprint → audit dispatch table)
  2. Dependency CVE scan (severity-graded, transitive vs direct)
  3. Static analysis on the diff — pattern catalogs across languages for
     SQL/command/path/template/XXE/LDAP injection, auth/authz,
     crypto/secrets, deserialization, web (XSS/CORS/CSRF/cookies/
     redirects), TLS bypass, SSRF (host-controlled only), memory safety
     (non-Rust), TOCTOU
  4. Subprocess hygiene sweep (argv vs sh -c, env scrub, setsid, fds)
  5. File permissions (0600 secrets, 0700 dirs, atomic tempfiles)
  6. Network surface (bind addr, TLS config, redirect cap, hardening
     headers)
  7. Container / infra (Dockerfile USER, compose privileged, k8s
     hostNetwork, terraform 0.0.0.0/0)
  8. Score 0-100 with per-dimension weights + HIGH/MEDIUM findings +
     items examined and cleared + what was NOT examined

Strict confidence floor (0.8) and an explicit exclusion list
(DOS / ReDoS / log spoofing / regex injection / memory safety in
memory-safe languages / lack-of-hardening / prompt injection) so the
output stays signal-rich.

Output is a markdown report with a per-dimension score table,
findings with file:line + exploit path + recommendation, and explicit
bounds disclosure.

feat(skills): embed built-in skills with user-dir overlay

New `src/brain/skills.rs` ships a tiny skill loader that mirrors the

  2. compile-time embedded built-in        ← include_str! from
                                              src/docs/reference/templates/skills/

fix(tui): responsive slash autocomplete dropdown + tighter skill descriptions

Two related bugs surfaced when /security-audit and /cost-estimate
landed with multi-paragraph trigger-keyword descriptions for LLM
auto-invoke:

  1) ratatui buffer panic on /
     The dropdown was anchored at `input_area.x + 1` but width was
     clamped at `input_area.width`. Skill descriptions inflated the
     content width past the soft cap, so the right edge tried to write
     at column `input_area.width` — out of bounds in a width-N buffer
     (valid indices 0..=N-1). Caught by the runner's panic recovery,
     so the app didn't crash, but the autocomplete frame was rolled
     back every keystroke after `/`.
  2) Descriptions clipped without ellipsis
     Even on the soft-cap path, the truncation budget assumed a
     10-char name column. `/security-audit` (15 chars) and
     `/cost-estimate` (14 chars) push the layout right, so the
     Paragraph widget hard-clipped the row mid-word before
     `truncate_to_chars` could add the ellipsis.

Renderer fix
  Extracted the sizing math into `dropdown_dimensions(name_col_chars,
  description_lengths, input_area_width, pad_x) -> (width, inner,
  desc_budget)` — a pure function unit-testable without a live App.
  Behaviour is now **responsive**: the dropdown grows to fit the
  longest row (name col + description), capped at `input_area.width
  - 1` so the right edge stays inside the frame. No fixed soft cap.
  Content shorter than the terminal renders verbatim; content wider
  than the terminal is truncated with `truncate_to_chars` and
  visibly ends in `…`.

  `name_col_chars` is computed from the actual longest visible name
  (with a 10-char floor for short-name aesthetics), so the
  description column lines up vertically and `desc_budget` accounts
  for the real layout — no more hidden hard-clip by Paragraph.

Skill descriptions
  Trimmed both shipped built-ins to one short sentence — the
  Claude-Code skill convention. The frontmatter `description` is
  what the LLM reads for auto-invoke discovery; verbose
  trigger-keyword paragraphs were both ugly in the slash menu and
  unnecessary for the LLM's call decision.

  /security-audit: "Run a comprehensive language-agnostic security &
                   CVE audit, scored 0-100"
  /cost-estimate:  "Estimate codebase cost-to-build, AI-assisted ROI,
                   and fair-market valuation"

12 new tests in src/tests/slash_autocomplete_dimensions_test.rs
covering: never overflows the frame right edge, narrow-terminal
clamp, zero-width robustness, responsive growth past the old 80-col
soft cap, truncation when content exceeds terminal, 40-col floor,
name-column alignment, and the `truncate_to_chars` helper
(passthrough, ellipsis, zero/one-char budgets, multi-byte unicode).

feat(mc): keyboard navigation + detail popup

Mission Control becomes fully interactive. Three keystroke layers:

    Shift-Tab / h      → cycle focused panel backward
    j / ↓              → next item in focused panel
    k / ↑              → previous item
    g / Home           → jump to first item
    G / End            → jump to last item
    Enter              → open the detail popup for the selected item
    Esc                → close MC, return to Chat

  Reserved for C12
    a / r              → apply / reject the selected proposal

spinning up a full `App`. The `handle_key` wrapper translates

fix(stream): TCP keepalive on all HTTP clients to detect silent drops

Without SO_KEEPALIVE, a silent network drop (network change, server crash,
NAT timeout) leaves the stream hanging until the 300s reqwest timeout
fires. With keepalive at 15s probes, the kernel detects the dead socket
in ~15-45s and reqwest surfaces an error so the retry chain in
tool_loop.rs can fall over to the next provider.

Applied to: anthropic, gemini, custom_openai_compatible (3 builders).

fix(stream): partial JSON repair so truncated tool args survive

When a stream is cut mid-tool-call, the accumulator holds raw JSON like

dropped the partial intent, so the tool got called with an empty object
or the call was lost entirely.

New `brain::provider::json_repair`:
  - Closes unterminated strings, balances unclosed brackets, drops
    trailing key-without-value, strips trailing commas
  - On unrecoverable input returns
    `{"_partial": "<raw>", "_repair_failed": true}` so the tool
    dispatch can surface a useful error rather than a silent {}

fix(claude-cli): run our compaction so ctx counter stops climbing past 200%

Claude CLI was reporting `484k/200k = 242%` in the user-input ctx meter
because OpenCrabs skipped its own context-budget compaction for any
provider where `cli_handles_tools()` is true.

That's wrong for Claude CLI specifically. Claude CLI:
- Handles **tools** internally (no re-execution by OpenCrabs) ✓
- Caches **prompts** internally (Anthropic billing) ✓
- Does NOT manage **the context we feed it via stdin** — we send the
  whole conversation each turn, so OpenCrabs owns context sizing.

Without compaction, tool-result messages (file reads, bash output,
grep dumps) accumulated across iterations and the local tiktoken
estimate climbed without bound. Each turn re-sent the bloated history,
costing real Anthropic tokens, and the ctx meter showed >100% with
no recovery — auto-compaction never fired because the gating flag
sent every CLI turn down the no-op branch.

Two fixes:

1. Override `cli_manages_context()` in claude_cli.rs to return `false`.
   The default `cli_handles_tools()` fallback is wrong for Claude CLI.
   qwen-code stays opted out (it does manage context via --resume).

2. The first compaction call site in tool_loop.rs (line 644) was
   gated on `is_cli_provider` instead of `cli_owns_context` like the
   other 3 sites. Switch to `cli_owns_context` for consistency so
   Claude CLI gets compaction at every trigger point.

Result: ctx meter reflects actual context sent (~22k for a healthy
session), auto-compaction fires at 65% / hard truncates at 90% as
designed, and Anthropic billing drops because we stop re-sending
post-compaction-needed messages every iteration.

fix(slack): close the duplicate-completion gap by sharing dedup map across paths

The slack handler had two distinct chat-post paths and they did not share
the content-dedup map. The intermediate-text progress callback posted
straight to Slack and tracked only timestamps; the final-response path
hashed the rendered text against `state.seen_responses` and posted on
miss. When the model emitted its full final answer in the last streaming
chunk before the tool loop terminated, the same content went out via
intermediate AND via final, with the final-path map empty (no
intermediate ever populated it) — so dedup never tripped. The
delete-intermediates-before-final cleanup at line 1418-1437 swallowed
its own errors with `let _ = chat_delete(...).await`, so when delete
silently failed both posts survived.

The fix:
- Capture `state` and `channel_id` into the progress callback closure.
- After a successful intermediate post, hash the rendered text and
  insert (channel_id:hash → real_ts) into `seen_responses`. The map now
  reflects what's actually visible in the channel, regardless of which
  path posted it.
- Final-path dedup: on hit, log and return. Drop the prior
  `chat_delete(old_ts)` call — the existing message IS the right
  content, deleting it would remove the only visible answer (and the
  delete was firing against the never-updated `SlackTs::new("0")`
  placeholder anyway).
- After the final post succeeds, stamp the real `ts` of the first
  posted chunk onto the seen_responses entry so the placeholder is
  no longer a lie.

Logs at 2026-05-05 10:44 confirm the diagnosis: one agent run, one
"deleting 1 intermediate messages before final response" entry, zero
"dropping duplicate response" entries, zero "failed to send reply"
entries — yet the screenshot shows two identical completion posts.
That's the intermediate-bypasses-dedup pattern this commit closes.

fix(provider): /models save now sources model from session provider, not global

Regression I introduced in 357693b2: `actual_model` was still being read
from `self.agent_service.provider_model()` — the GLOBAL agent service.
When the global was sitting on a sticky-fallback target (e.g. zhipu
after a previous failover), `provider_model()` returned that target's
default model (`glm-5.1`). The save flow then persisted
`session.model = "glm-5.1"` while pinning `session_providers[sid]` to
the freshly built dialagram provider, so every following turn shipped
`dialagram/glm-5.1` — a model dialagram doesn't serve. 3 retries, then
the fallback chain dragged it back to zhipu, exactly the cross-provider
mash-up the per-session-isolation fix was supposed to prevent.

The model has to come from the per-session provider, not the global
one. `provider_arc` is built fresh by `create_provider_by_name` (or
the global-fallback paths) right above, with the user's selected
default_model already written to disk before the rebuild — so
`provider_arc.default_model()` is the correct, session-local source.
Move the `actual_model` computation to AFTER `provider_arc` is built
and read it from there.

fix(session): enforce locked {provider, model} pair on every response write

The architectural rule has always been that a session's provider and
model are a locked pair — picked together, fail together, never mixed
across providers. The TUI's post-response writeback at
`messaging.rs:2137` violated that: it persisted `session.model` from
`response.model` while leaving `session.provider_name` untouched. The
gate was `session.model.is_none()` so it only fired for fresh sessions,
but when it did fire after a sticky-fallback turn (response.model was
the fallback's model, e.g. zhipu's `glm-5.1`), the row ended up with
provider_name pointing at the original (e.g. `dialagram`) and model
pointing at the fallback's catalogue. The next turn shipped
`dialagram/glm-5.1` — a pair that exists in no provider — failed three
retries, fell back to zhipu, and surfaced the cross-provider switch
banner the user just reported.

The fix is structural: AgentResponse now carries `provider_name`
alongside `model`, populated at every construction site
(messaging::send, tool_loop main path, both compaction sites) from the
per-session active provider name (`provider_name_for_session` resolves
sticky-fallback targets correctly). The TUI writeback drops the
`is_none()` gate and writes BOTH fields atomically when the pair has
changed since last persist. ProviderSwitched event handler still keeps
DB in sync independently; this is the second writer that closes the
same gap for code paths that may not fire ProviderSwitched (channel
turns, resume after restart, anything where progress events do not
reach the TUI event loop).

Audited every other site that touches `session.model =`:
- channels/commands.rs:865 already writes both atomically.
- state.rs ProviderSwitched handler writes both.
- state.rs sync_session_to_provider writes both.
- messaging.rs:283-292 (load_session canonical-rename) writes both.
- dialogs.rs /models save now writes both (e29e77e8).
The TUI post-response spawn was the last single-field writer.

fix(provider): persist sticky-fallback pair to DB independent of progress callback

Root cause of the dialagram/glm-5.1 (and similar) cross-pair the user
keeps hitting: every channel handler — Slack, Telegram, Discord,
WhatsApp — only matched ToolStarted / IntermediateText / SelfHealingAlert
on the progress callback and silently dropped ProviderSwitched on `_ =>
{}`. When a sticky fallback fired during a channel-driven turn:

  1. tool_loop.rs:1302 swapped session_providers[sid] to the fallback
     in memory (succeeded).
  2. tool_loop emitted ProgressEvent::ProviderSwitched via the channel's
     progress_cb (which had no arm for it — silently lost).
  3. DB row never updated. session_providers[sid] now disagrees with DB.
  4. Next channel turn's sync_provider_for_session reads the stale DB,
     forces session_providers[sid] back to the pre-fallback provider —
     "restoring" the original session into a state that contradicts
     what just succeeded.
  5. This loops every turn (e.g. opencode-qwen rate-limited → fallback
     to zhipu/glm-5.1 succeeds → DB unchanged → sync restores to
     opencode-qwen → next turn rate-limits again, repeat).
  6. Eventually some other path (TUI ProviderSwitched arm, response
     writeback) catches up out of order and writes glm-5.1 onto a
     session row whose provider_name is dialagram (or some other), and
     the next turn ships the cross-provider pair.

The fix is structural: stop relying on the progress callback as the
persistence channel for ProviderSwitched. Add `AgentService::persist_sticky_pair(session_id, name, model)` which writes both
fields atomically via SessionService (fire-and-forget tokio spawn) and
call it at every site that emits ProviderSwitched in tool_loop.rs:
  - 1403  rate-limit / auth fallback succeeded
  - 1656  stream-error fallback succeeded
  - 1883  5xx fallback succeeded
  - 1922  FallbackProvider's internal swap_event surfaced
The progress callback is now strictly UI-display: emitting (or dropping)
the event has zero effect on DB persistence.

Logs from 2026-05-05 10:34-11:30 on session 772d01e9 confirm the
diagnosis: many fallbacks fired during Slack turns, ZERO ProviderSwitched
log lines from state.rs:2531 in that window (Slack handler dropped them
all), session.provider_name oscillated between opencode-qwen and the
fallback target, and the cross-pair eventually surfaced on the user's
TUI as `dialagram/glm-5.1`.

revert: drop the 15s chunk watchdog (ded5d644) — it was killing healthy streams

The watchdog applied 15s post-first-chunk to every provider regardless of
kind. Pre-watchdog, the system was working smoothly: claude-cli ran for
hours through long tool sequences, and the only reason a stream got cut
was a real connection drop or the 1h idle timeout. After the watchdog,
any normal pause between chunks — claude-cli running cargo build, gh
pr create, or any internal tool that takes more than 15s of CPU — was
treated as a dropped connection. The subprocess got SIGKILL'd, three
retries fired off cold subprocesses that all hit the same fate, and the
fallback chain absorbed turns that had nothing wrong with them. Today's
14:31 incident on session 'slack' (TUI) was exactly this: 66 content
blocks of healthy streaming, then a tool pause, then "Stream chunk
watchdog timeout after 15s — no event received", SIGKILL, 3 retries
fail, fall over to dialagram for no good reason.

Faster connection-drop detection on remote HTTP wasn't worth the
collateral damage on CLI/local. The 90s remote / 1h CLI/local
stream_idle_timeout that existed before had no observed false negatives.
Restore that exact state — mechanical inverse of the ded5d644 diff.

fix(self-heal): catch "Now <file-op gerund>" phantoms (creating/writing/editing/...)

INTENT_PHRASES had the git/deploy gerunds (now committing / pushing /
cherry-picking / deploying / building / testing / checking / applying /
restarting) but missed the file-operation set (now creating / writing /
editing / adding / removing / deleting / reading / running / starting /
finishing / finalizing / installing / configuring / wiring / setting up).

Regression caught by the user at 14:47: a session emitted "Now creating
the new tests file for signin/invitation error messages." with zero
tool_use blocks. The relaxed phantom detector matched no intent phrase,
the iteration ended without re-prompt, and the request looked dropped.

Adds the missing gerunds to both the relaxed-path INTENT_PHRASES list
and the strict-path now_gerund_re regex (which only fires on a
sentence-boundary "now <verb>", so adding the verbs is safe — won't
match conversational "now" usage). Test exercises the exact phrase
from the screenshot plus four sibling shapes.

fix(rsi): escalate repeat violations of existing rules instead of skipping

The RSI agent prompt told the model to SKIP whenever a brain file already
covered a topic, even if fresh feedback showed the rule was being broken
again. That made RSI silent for ~2 days despite 5+ "check brain files
first" corrections in the May 5 02:48-02:52 sessions, because the rule
already existed in SOUL.md.

The strongest rules in SOUL.md carry inline counters
(`telegram_send: 7 violations`, `Git corrections from user: 2`). Those
counters are load-bearing: they tell the model the rule has bitten the
user multiple times, which is what makes the model take it seriously.
But nothing was bumping them — they're hand-edited, and RSI saw "rule
present" and skipped.

New decision branch in the workflow:

- File covers topic + FRESH repeat violation → action='update': bump the
  inline counter, append the new date/incident as evidence, tighten the
  wording.
- File covers topic + no fresh evidence → SKIP (unchanged).

Plus a "Repeat-Violation Escalation Pattern" section that names the
existing counter format as the gold standard and walks through the
read/locate-counter/update steps so the model has a concrete recipe.

Skipping a repeat-violation case because 'the rule already exists' was
the most common RSI failure mode. Now it's the trigger for escalation.

fix(telegram): strip <<IMG:path>> markers from intermediate text too

The final-response handler called extract_img_markers and sent the
image via send_photo, but the four intermediate-text sites
(handle_message edit-loop + post-stream, voice handler, DM handler)
never extracted the marker. When the LLM emitted <<IMG:/path>> mid-
stream, the marker leaked raw into the chat AND the prefixed
intermediate stopped string-matching the prior clean intermediate
carrying the same body, so the exact-equality dedup at
`sent_intermediates.iter().any(|prev| prev == &text)` whiffed and the
user got two copies of the same answer plus the visible marker token.

2026-05-05 18:45 incident: a "generate retro game cartridge box"
turn shipped one clean "There it is..." intermediate, then a second
intermediate prefixed with `<<IMG:/Users/.../opencrabs-retro-box.png>>`
followed by the same body, and finally the actual rendered photo
came in via send_photo — three messages where there should have
been one text + one image.

Sandwich `extract_img_markers` between `redact_secrets` and the
dedup at all four intermediate sites. The final-response handler
keeps its own extract call and remains the only path that calls
send_photo, so the image is still sent exactly once and the marker
is removed exactly once on every visible-text path.

fix(slack): strip <<IMG:path>> markers from intermediate text too

Same gap as the Telegram fix at 25501116: the final-response handler
called extract_img_markers and uploaded the image via files_upload,
but the IntermediateText branch posted the raw text verbatim. When
the LLM emitted the marker mid-stream the raw `<<IMG:/path>>` token
landed in the channel as a regular message, AND the prefixed
intermediate's content hash diverged from the prior clean
intermediate / the final post — defeating the seen_responses content
dedup (5a0e1133) that's supposed to skip the redundant final post.

Audit summary:
  - telegram: fixed at 25501116 (4 sites)
  - slack: fixed here (1 site)
  - whatsapp: already correct — extract_img_markers in chunked-send
    path (line 762) and final-response path (line 940)
  - discord: no IntermediateText handler, so no gap

revert: restore synchronous compaction (drops async spawn-then-swap from d98542d4)

Today's logs caught the catastrophic failure mode the async architecture
unlocked. Two events on the same session within 15 minutes:

  22:38:25 — Context at 397% (793690 tokens) — hard truncating to 80%
  22:38:27 — Hard truncation complete: 0 messages, 0 tokens (0%)
  22:53:27 — Context at 372% (744746 tokens) — hard truncating to 80%
  22:53:29 — Hard truncation complete: 0 messages, 0 tokens (0%)

Two bugs interacting:

1. enforce_context_budget at 90%+ called cancel_pending_compaction AND
   hard_truncate_to in the same step. Any in-flight async summary was
   thrown away; no [CONTEXT COMPACTION ...] marker was written to DB; the
   in-memory context dropped messages without leaving a recovered-brain
   anchor. The DB still held the entire pre-truncate history.

2. hard_truncate_to drops oldest messages until len() <= 2, then runs
   drop_leading_orphan_tool_results. If the surviving 2 messages were
   tool_result-only (common: the kept tail's preceding assistant got
   dropped), both were stripped → 0 messages. Next turn reloaded the
   same 793k-token history from DB → exploded again → truncated to 0
   again → loop, every time the user touched the session.

Synchronous compaction (the pre-d98542d4 behaviour) avoids the loop
because the turn waits for the summary to land BEFORE the request goes
out. The cost is a one-time pause when compaction triggers (~30-60s on
a slow model), accepted as a worthwhile trade for guaranteed history
preservation. The structural compute_compaction_summary /
apply_compaction_summary split from d98542d4 stays — only the
spawn-then-swap orchestration is removed:

  - enforce_context_budget at 65%+ now awaits compact_context inline
  - removed try_swap_pending_compaction, spawn_pending_compaction,
    cancel_pending_compaction
  - removed PendingCompaction struct + AgentService.pending_compactions
  - hard_truncate_to is kept but only fires as fallback when sync
    compaction itself errors (provider down, cancel, etc.) — not as
    a primary 90% guardrail
  - the four enforce_context_budget call sites in tool_loop.rs are
    untouched; they still get Option<String> back and persist the
    marker on Some

(Future improvement: re-introduce async with a NON-CANCELLING
overflow guard — block at 80%+ until the in-flight summary lands
instead of killing it. Out of scope here; the user wants the
working approach restored.)

fix(slack): scope dedup to one turn — global window dropped legit responses

My earlier slack-dedup commit (5a0e1133) put the content-hash lookup on
`HandlerState.seen_responses`, a global HashMap with a 5-minute eviction
window. That scope was wrong: any time the agent produced the same body
across separate user prompts within five minutes, the second turn's
final post was suppressed.

Logs from 2026-05-06 caught five distinct turns dropped on the same
content hash:

  01:18:27  skipping final post — hash=C0AEY3C2P9V:3476900567878811119
  01:32:09  skipping final post — hash=C0AEY3C2P9V:3476900567878811119
  01:39:57  skipping final post — hash=C0AEY3C2P9V:3476900567878811119
  01:40:26  skipping final post — hash=C0AEY3C2P9V:3476900567878811119
  01:41:45  skipping final post — hash=C0AEY3C2P9V:3476900567878811119

Compounding bug: the standalone "delete intermediates before final"
loop ran BEFORE the dedup check, so when the dedup did fire we ended
up with zero visible messages — intermediates deleted from the channel,
final skipped, user sees nothing.

The fix moves both concerns into one per-turn block inside the final-
response Ok arm:

  1. `sent_intermediate_ts` becomes `Vec<(SlackTs, content_hash)>` —
     each successful intermediate post records its slack ts AND the
     hash of the rendered body.
  2. At final-response time: hash the rendered final, partition the
     intermediate list into "matches the final" vs "doesn't match".
  3. Delete only the non-matching intermediates (those were partial
     stream chunks). If at least one matching intermediate exists,
     skip the final post entirely — the matching intermediate IS the
     answer. If none matches, post the final as usual.
  4. `state.seen_responses` field removed entirely (was the only
     writer; no other reader).

Telegram already uses a per-turn `sent_intermediates: Vec<String>`
on its `StreamingState` for the same purpose. Slack now matches that
shape.

fix(slack): empty-final guard — keep intermediates as the visible answer

Logs from 2026-05-06 01:53 caught the case my prior fix missed:

  01:53:11  user: "Good it willl take a while let it run, well done c"
  01:53:14  bot intermediate posted (echoed back as bot_id message)
  01:53:17  Slack: deleting 1 non-matching intermediate(s) before final response
  [no chat.postMessage of final, no error]
  user sees zero messages

Sequence: the model emitted its real reply as an IntermediateText event
during streaming, then `response.content` came back empty (the agent
loop completed with no additional text — common for short conversational
acknowledgements where the streamer delivered the whole answer).
`text_only.trim()` was empty after extract / strip / redact / mrkdwn.

The hash-match dedup compared hash("") (final) against the intermediate's
real hash → no match → intermediate classified "non-matching" → deleted.
Then the post loop iterated over empty text_only → all chunks empty →
zero chat.postMessage calls. Net: intermediate gone, nothing posted.

Guard: when text_only is empty/whitespace, return immediately without
touching intermediates. The intermediate(s) ARE the answer in that case.

fix(compaction): restore pre-d98542d4 enforce_context_budget logic

My bcfdce98 sync revert kept the OLD d98542d4 control-flow shape (single
attempt, no retries, hard-truncate as Err arm fallback). That shape, plus
the tokenizer-headroom mismatch on the summarizer, produced the cascade
the user kept hitting today: 90% → compact (400) → truncate to 80% →
compact (400 again, same input) → truncate (no-op, already at target) →
compact (400) → ... no marker ever lands, every reload re-explodes.

Restored the function to its byte-for-byte pre-d98542d4 shape — the
version that ran fine for months before the async refactor:

  Tier 2 (90%): hard_truncate to 80% FIRST, then fall through. Compaction
    below now sees a window-fitting input, so the summarizer doesn't
    reject and there's no failed-compaction-then-truncate cycle.

  Tier 1 (65%): up to 3 sync compact_context attempts. Most transient or
    tokenizer-edge 400s self-resolve on retry — single-shot was the
    regression. If the post-summary context is still over 65%, run one
    more pass with the tighter budget.

  Safety net: only if all 3 attempts totally failed AND context is still
    above 80%, hard_truncate to 80%. No marker persisted in that branch
    (LLM was unavailable, no summary to write).

The structural compute_compaction_summary / apply_compaction_summary
split from d98542d4 stays — that part of the refactor was clean. Only
the spawn-then-swap orchestration AND my flawed single-attempt retry
shape are gone.

2538 tests pass. Clippy + fmt clean.

fix(tool-loop): cap oversized tool_result bodies at 50 KB before context

Today's session 5ed9ff25 hit a runaway loop that wasn't a compaction bug
at all — `read_file` on opencrabs-retro-release.html returned 1,025,562
bytes (HTML with an embedded base64 PNG). That single tool_result
landed in context unmodified, ctx jumped 8k → 738k tokens (≈256k for
the one block), compaction summarizer rejected it (`400 Prompt exceeds
max length`), hard-truncate fell back, drop_leading_orphan_tool_results
stripped the surviving leading tool_results, and the in-memory message
list ended at 0. Then on the next turn the agent re-called the same
tool, repeated the cycle.

Added a single guard at the spot where `tool_results` is flushed into
context (`context.add_message(tool_result_msg)`). Each ToolResult block's
body is capped at 50 KB chars (~12k tokens, ~6% of a 200k window) with
a UTF-8-safe boundary, and the truncated tail carries an inline marker
telling the agent to re-call with offsets / grep / start_line / etc. for
the specific portion it needs. Generous enough that normal file reads
and bash outputs pass through untouched; tight enough that no single
tool result can blow up the budget.

Covers every tool that can return arbitrary-size content (read_file,
bash, grep, glob, http, doc_parser, etc.) — the cap fires regardless of
which tool produced the oversized output. Compaction logic untouched.

The structural complexity of the ToolResult enum match means the cap
only runs in this hot path; other ToolResult constructions (small,
known sizes — error stubs, "no approval mechanism", etc.) are not
affected.

2538 tests pass. Clippy + fmt clean.

fix(slack): strip <!-- tools-v2: --> from intermediate text too

Slack final-response handler runs `strip_llm_artifacts` on `text_only`,
which removes the inline `<!-- tools-v2: [JSON] -->` accounting comments
that the agent embeds alongside its prose. The intermediate-text branch
in the progress callback was never updated to match — only
`extract_img_markers` and `markdown_to_mrkdwn` ran, so any v2 marker
emitted mid-stream landed in the channel verbatim. The user caught it
in a multi-bash-step turn where one tool's wrapper rendered as raw
HTML-comment text in Slack instead of as a normal tool block.

Same shape gap as 601b8a74 (the IMG-marker fix); a different artifact
type slipped through. Telegram's intermediate paths already call
`strip_llm_artifacts`; Slack now matches.

Single-line addition before the existing extract_img_markers call.

release: v0.3.17 — provider stickiness, streaming resilience, context isolation, channel cleanup

44 commits since v0.3.16. This release fixes the most critical pain points:
provider switching that did not stick, streaming drops that corrupted tool
calls, Claude CLI context leaking past 200%, and channel messages showing
LLM metadata brackets in the TUI.

PROVIDER SWITCHING (7 commits)
Sticky fallbacks now actually stick. The stream error path was dropping
the restore guard without nulling original, so Drop always reverted to
primary. Both stream error and 5xx paths were missing ProviderSwitched
events. The handler updated DB but not session_providers Arc, causing
stale footers on pane switch. save_provider invalidation nuked ALL
sessions matching a provider name instead of just the current one.
Per-session swap now persists in DB and memory, live-fetched models are
honored, /models save sources from session provider not global, and the
locked {provider, model} pair is enforced on every response write.
Fallback pairs are persisted to DB independent of progress callbacks.
Health-aware startup (FallbackProvider::new_with_health) advances the
active index on creation if primary has 2+ consecutive failures, so
sticky fallbacks survive restarts.

STREAMING RESILIENCE (4 commits)
TCP keepalive (15s) added to Anthropic, Gemini, and all custom
OpenAI-compatible HTTP clients. Detects silent TCP drops at OS level in
~15-45s instead of waiting for the 300s idle timeout. New json_repair
module closes unterminated strings, balances brackets, strips trailing
commas, and drops trailing keys-without-value. Wired into 5 drop sites
across OpenAI-compatible providers and the ContentBlockStop finalizer.
Unrecoverable input returns a {_partial, _repair_failed} envelope instead
of crashing the turn. New RetryAttempt progress event emitted on
stream-drop retries, shown as TUI system messages so users see transient
recovery in progress. One 15s chunk watchdog attempt was reverted after
it killed healthy streams with long thinking blocks.

CONTEXT MANAGEMENT (6 commits)
Claude CLI context leak plugged: cli_manages_context() defaulted to
cli_handles_tools(), silently opting out of compaction. Context grew
unbounded (484k/200k = 242%). Override returns false so OpenCrabs owns
compaction for Claude CLI sessions. Compaction restored to synchronous
(reverted async spawn-then-swap race condition). Pre-regression
enforce_context_budget logic recovered. Oversized tool_result bodies
capped at 50 KB before entering context. Per-session context window
isolation prevents cross-session contamination.

CHANNELS (6 commits)
All channel handlers (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Trello) now
persist clean display text to DB and TUI instead of LLM metadata brackets.
Each handler builds appropriate display: bare text for owner DMs,
"Sender: text" for groups and non-owner messages. Slack got 5 rounds of
fixes: duplicate-completion gap closed by sharing dedup map, intermediate
text cleaned of <<IMG:path>> and image markers, dedup scoped to one
turn instead of global window, empty-final guard keeps intermediates as
visible answer.

SELF-HEAL + RSI (4 commits)
Phantom detectors extracted into their own module. Expanded to catch
"Now <file-op gerund>" phantoms (creating/writing/editing) and
build/deploy intent + past-tense completion claims. RSI now escalates
repeat violations of existing rules by bumping a violation counter
instead of deduping them away. Rules that keep getting broken get louder.

FEATURES (4 commits)
OpenRouter response caching for zero cost on identical requests.
4 safe built-in skills added (opencli, browser-cdp, a2a-gateway,
dynamic-tools) with SKILLS section in help screen and splash integration.
Thinking content now persisted to DB on both ResponseComplete and
IntermediateText events. Approval policy read from config at runtime
on every tool request instead of cached at startup.

OTHER FIXES (6 commits)
Scroll offset capped and first-render inflation explosion prevented.
Streaming scroll compensation removed entirely (was inflating offset by
1000+ lines during thinking model streaming). Exit/start splash updated
with skills section and corrected /models command. Brain directory path
exposed in core prompt context index. Session working directory now
survives crash recovery. TOOLS.md and CODE.md moved from core to
contextual brain files. Session IDs no longer dumped in assert messages
(CodeQL #62, CWE-312).

Full changelog: https://github.com/adolfousier/opencrabs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#0317---2026-05-06

fix(slack): close intermediate-vs-final dedup race + post-completion sweep

Slack was posting the same body twice when an IntermediateText spawn was
still in-flight at stream-end: stream emits IntermediateText -> spawn fires
chat_post_message (~hundreds of ms) -> stream ends ~immediately -> final
handler reads `sent_intermediate_ts` while it's still empty -> classifies
the in-flight intermediate as not-yet-posted -> posts the same body a
second time. Confirmed in logs: two `chat.postMessage` events from the bot
ms apart, no `Slack: skipping final post` line because the read happened
pre-push.

Two complementary fixes:

1. Track every IntermediateText `tokio::spawn` JoinHandle in a sync Vec;
   before reading the dedup list, drain + await all handles so every
   `(ts, hash)` push has landed.

2. Post-completion sweep: after the final post lands, drain handles a

fix(stream): surface underlying error reason on TUI when fallback fires

the maintainer when users report) saw a generic "Stream error" with no

   3 retries: Request timed out after 30s. Switching to fallback
   provider..."

fix(stream): no provider fallback for truncation continuations

When a response ended with `finish_reason=stop` but mid-sentence, the
truncation-mid-sentence detector asked the model to continue once on the
SAME provider. If that continuation request hit 3 retries' worth of
errors, the existing fallback path advanced to a different provider,
which produced visibly garbled output: the original provider had been
emitting one format (e.g. qwen vertical-label rows) and the fallback
continued in another (e.g. glm pipe-table syntax) — pulldown-cmark
can't reconcile the seam, so the user sees a Frankenstein response.

Observed on 2026-05-07T16:31 with dialagram/qwen-3.6-max-preview-thinking
falling through to zhipu/glm-5.1 mid-table on a continuation. Format
drift is deterministic given the input — retrying on the fallback
produces the same garbled output, so cross-provider fallback for
continuations is strictly bad.

New per-iteration flag `current_iter_is_truncation_continue` is set
right before `continue;` from the truncation branch and snapshot+reset
at the top of each loop iteration. When the stream-error path runs and
the flag is true, abort the continuation (return the last error) instead
of advancing through the fallback chain. The user sees the visibly cut-
off response and can re-prompt — better than a Frankenstein answer.

fix(tui): hard-break between pipe-rows when not recognised as a table

CommonMark renders a single newline inside a paragraph as a soft break,
which we render as a space so wide terminals can reflow LLM output that
was wrapped at 72 cols. That's correct for prose but produces a wall of
text when an LLM emits pipe-table syntax without a `|---|---|` header
separator — pulldown-cmark falls back to treating each row as a
paragraph line, the soft breaks collapse to spaces, and rows like

  | 11 | a | b |
  | 12 | c | d |

render as

  | 11 | a | b | | 12 | c | d |

Observed when a stream-error fallback transitioned from a vertical-label
format (qwen) to pipe-table format (glm-5.1) mid-table — the fallback
emitted body rows without restarting the table header, so pulldown-cmark
never recognised it as a table.

In the SoftBreak handler, peek at the last span of `current_line`: if
its trimmed content ends with `|`, push a hard break instead of a
space. Heuristic, but `|` at line boundaries is almost always table
syntax — false positives would require legit prose ending one line and
starting the next with `|`, which is vanishingly rare. All 9 existing
markdown tests pass unchanged.

fix(browser): wait for network idle after navigate, not just CDP load event

`page.wait_for_navigation()` resolves on the CDP `load` event — which
fires before paint and before any JS hydration completes. Screenshots
and clicks issued right after would land on a blank/half-rendered page,
producing the "stuck on initial window" symptom: the auto-screenshot
captured a blank pixel buffer, the model couldn't see the actual UI,
and subsequent click/type calls missed elements that hadn't rendered
yet.

Replace with `wait_for_network_almost_idle_with_timeout(3s)` — same
helper that click.rs:87 already uses successfully. Network-idle
correlates well with "page is interactable" for both static SSR and
JS-hydrated SPAs. 3s timeout caps worst case for slow pages.

fix(browser): pre-flight CDP health check before screenshot

`page.screenshot()` was being called without verifying the underlying
page was responsive. If the CDP connection had dropped (handler task
exited, browser crashed, tab closed externally) the screenshot call
would either hang or return a generic "Screenshot failed: {e}" with no
signal whether the page itself was dead or the capture failed.

Adds a `page.url()` round-trip first — cheap CDP call, fails fast if
the connection is broken. Specific error message tells the user the
page is unresponsive and suggests `browser_navigate` to reset or
`browser_close` to clean up. Differentiates dead-page from
screenshot-failure so the agent can recover instead of getting stuck.

fix(browser): log instead of silently dropping errors in navigate

Three sites in `browser_navigate` swallowed errors via `let _ = ` or
`.ok().flatten().unwrap_or_default()` — invisible failures with no
trail in logs, making "browser got stuck" investigations harder than
they should be.

  proceed anyway, but the log line proves the wait fired and what it

release: v0.3.18 — Codex CLI provider, repo-audit skill, browser resilience, security fixes

32 commits since v0.3.17. This release adds a new built-in provider
(Codex CLI), a language-agnostic repo-audit skill, fixes browser CDP
stability issues, plugs a Gemini API key leak flagged by CodeQL, and
cleans up slash command parsing for file paths.

NEW PROVIDER (8 commits)
Codex CLI integrated as a built-in subprocess provider. User authenticates
once via `codex` CLI; OpenCrabs piggybacks on cached credentials with zero
API key handling. Non-interactive mode via `codex exec --json` with JSONL
streaming. Models: GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.3-Codex. Wired into `/models`
picker, `/onboard` wizard, factory registry, and config (`[providers.codex_cli]`).

SKILLS (2 commits)
Repo-audit skill added: language-agnostic repository health checks via
5-phase pipeline (language detection, native tool execution, git metrics,
language-specific AST analysis, scoring + recommendations). Covers Rust,
JS/TS, Python, Go with per-language metrics for error handling, dependencies,
naming conventions, module structure, and god-file detection.

BROWSER (4 commits)
New `browser_close` tool to free CDP sessions and prevent stale page reuse
across actions. Network idle wait added after navigate (was only waiting for
CDP `load` event, missing async fetches). CDP manager lock now dropped before
screenshot await to unblock concurrent browser operations. Pre-flight CDP
health check added before capture to prevent failures on stale connections.
Navigate errors now logged at WARN instead of silently dropped.

CRON (3 commits)
Generic `deliver_api_key` field added to cron jobs for HTTP webhook Bearer
token auth configurable per-job. Replaces hardcoded provider-specific auth
in `deliver_http`. New `deliver_api_key` column on `cron_jobs` table
(migration 21). Agentverse-specific URL hack reverted from scheduler.

SECURITY (1 commit)
Gemini API key leaked in URL query string in `analyze_video` (CodeQL #64,
HIGH severity). Key passed as `?key=...` in two call sites (resumable upload
init + file-state polling). Moved to `x-goog-api-key` header, matching
`analyze_image` and `generate_image`.

FIXES (5 commits)
File paths starting with `/` no longer treated as slash command typos.
Added `looks_like_file_path()` helper gating both TUI and channel handlers.
Cloud handshake timeout bumped 30s to 60s for slow routing proxies like
dialagram (legitimately 20-45s). Truncation continuations no longer trigger
provider fallback. Fallback error reason now surfaced on TUI instead of
swallowed. Pipe-delimited rows get hard-breaks when not recognized as tables.

REFACTORS (4 commits)
Extracted `truncation.rs` (mid-sentence continuation path), `feedback.rs`
(ledger writes), and `compaction.rs` (context budget enforcement) from
service module. Replaced magic provider indices with `index_of_provider()`
helper across TUI and onboarding.
