fix(cron): validate provider/model pair before dispatch and use session-scoped swap

Cron execute_job had two bugs:
1. No validation of effective_model against the provider's supported_models.
   A reversed cron config (model=zhipu, provider=glm-5.1) reached the tool
   loop and produced RSI entries like dialagram/zhipu where a provider name
   leaked into the model slot. Now creates the provider early, checks the
   model against supported_models(), and skips the job with a loud error
   if the pair is invalid.

2. Used agent.swap_provider() (global swap via *self.provider.write())
   instead of agent.swap_provider_for_session(). All cron jobs share a
   single session, so concurrent jobs with different providers stepped on
   each other. Now uses session-scoped swap.

fix(rsi): record post-remap provider/model pair in feedback dimension

Three record_provider_feedback sites in tool_loop.rs recorded
provider_model_dim using the requested model_name before helpers.rs
silently remapped mismatched pairs. With a reversed cron config, this
produced impossible RSI entries like dialagram/zhipu (provider name in
model slot). Now resolves the actual model by checking the provider's
supported_models() at each recording site, matching the same logic
helpers.rs uses before the HTTP call.

fix(file-picker): skip VCS metadata dirs so big .git doesn't starve the cap

`@` recursive walk had `.hidden(false)` to surface user dotfiles like
`.env`, but that also meant `.git/` was fully traversed. On repos where
`.git/` holds thousands of pack/ref files, the 5000-result cap was
exhausted inside `.git/` before sibling source dirs (enumerated later
in filesystem order) were reached, so legitimate files silently never
appeared in `@` results regardless of query. Add an explicit
filter_entry skipping `.git`/`.hg`/`.svn`, and raise the cap to 20k.

fix(provider): catch bare top-level tool-call array leaking to TUI

qwen-3.6-max-preview-thinking double-emits: the full
`[{"id":"call_...","type":"function","function":{...}}]` array goes
out as delta.content while the real tool call still arrives via
delta.tool_calls. Logs 2026-05-16 ~20:16 show the model streaming
`\n\n[` then `\n  {\n    "id": "call_1", "type": "function",...` as
content chunks immediately before the structured chunk lands. The
existing leak guards only recognised `<tool_call>`, `<function=`,
`tool_call:`, and the `{"tool_calls":...}` / `{"tool_call":...}`
envelope shapes — a bare top-level array has none of those, so the
JSON copy survived to the TUI as raw text.

Generalised the balanced extractor to accept `[…]` openers in addition
to `{…}`; all existing callers pre-validate `{` so this is additive.

Added a three-state classifier (Full / Prefix / None) that walks
`[ ws* { ws* "id" ws* : ws* "call_` tolerant of arbitrary JSON
whitespace between structural tokens. Anchored on the `"call_"` ID
prefix because OpenAI-style tool-call IDs almost universally use it —
this keeps false positives on code blocks showing `[{"id":1,...}]`
near zero.

Wired the classifier into three places:
  - Stream-time leak probe: bare-array Full match flips leak_active so
    the whole turn's remaining content is dropped (mirrors the existing
    `{"tool_calls"` envelope branch). Probe cap raised 64→128 to fit
    pretty-printed envelope prefixes.
  - extract_text_tool_calls: new Pass 1.5 walks each `"id":"call_`
    anchor back up to 64 bytes to find the wrapping `[`, runs balanced
    JSON, parses items via the existing parse_tool_call_value helper.
  - finish_reason fallback: has_markers_in_accum gains the
    `"id":"call_` signal so any leak the streaming filter missed gets
    swept on terminal chunks.

Rebuild loop now sorts strip_ranges before splicing — the bare-array
pass can insert ranges out of order with respect to the Claude-style
and main-loop passes.

Ten new tests in qwen_tool_extractor_test cover: balanced extractor
accepting arrays, full classifier state machine, compact + verbatim
pretty-printed log shape + multi-call + stringified-args extraction,
and false-positive guards (non-call_ IDs, prose mentions of
`"id":"call_xyz"`). 34/34 green, full lib suite 2583/2583, clippy
clean with -D warnings.

fix(heal): abort turn on stuck `Let me…` intent loops without retry

dialagram/qwen-3.6-max-preview-thinking (and similar small-model setups
on custom OpenAI-compatible providers) regularly emits the same
intent-narration line three to nine times in one streamed response,
zero tool calls. The existing phantom detector caught each batch but
spent the full retry budget reproducing more of the same — user saw 4+
`Let me fetch issue #81…` paragraphs before the loop finally broke.

Add a stricter signal `is_stuck_in_intent_loop` that fires when the
iteration text has 3+ line-start intent phrases (`Let me X`, `I'll X`,
`Let's X`, optionally prefixed by `Now`, `OK,`, `Sure,`, etc.). When it
fires, the tool loop:

  - skips the retry-and-nudge path entirely (nudges don't recover this
    pattern; the model is stuck)
  - records `phantom_intent_loop` provider feedback
  - emits a `SelfHealingAlert` naming the repetition count
  - replaces `iteration_text` with a user-visible abort notice so the
    final assistant message reflects the self-heal rather than yet
    another `Let me X` line

The regex requires line-start matches (interjections like `OK,` /
`Sure,` allowed before the opener) so intent phrases embedded mid-
paragraph in normal prose don't false-fire. Both ASCII `'` and curly
`’` apostrophes accepted because markdown round-trips swap them.

`Now <verb>` alone is intentionally not counted — too many false
positives (`Now is the time`). `Now let me X` / `Now I'll X` do count.

Seven new tests in self_healing_test cover the verbatim log shape
(2026-05-16, 5+ `Let me fetch` paragraphs), threshold boundary (2 is
fine, 3 trips), mixed openers, curly-apostrophe round-trip, embedded
intent in prose (no trip), single-intent list items (no trip), and
plain prose (no trip). 83/83 self-healing tests green, full lib suite
2590/2590, clippy clean with -D warnings.

fix(heal): replace phantom-exhaustion text with abort notice instead of leaking

The standard phantom branch in the tool loop only fires while
`phantom_retries_used < MAX_PHANTOM_RETRIES`. Once the budget is spent,
any further phantom response slips past the gate and falls through to
the loop's break path — landing as the turn's "final" assistant message
and getting persisted/displayed verbatim. On dialagram/qwen-3.6-max-
preview-thinking that means after three retries the user still sees a
fresh `Pushed.` / `Committed as abc123.` claim with zero tool calls
behind it.

Add a second guard right after the existing phantom block: if retries
are at or above the cap AND the current iteration is still phantom,
record `phantom_retry_exhausted` provider feedback, emit a
`SelfHealingAlert`, and rewrite `iteration_text` to a self-heal abort
notice. The loop then proceeds to break normally, but the persisted
message reads:

  [self-heal] Aborted after 3 retry attempts — the model kept
  describing actions but never executed a tool call. Try a different
  model, rephrase the prompt, or check that the provider exposes the
  function schemas correctly.

Complements the Phase 1 early-abort (3+ intent line-starts in one
iteration): Phase 1 covers single-batch spinning, this one covers the
slower drift where each retry produces a fresh-but-still-phantom turn.
Together they ensure leaked intent narration never reaches the TUI as
the model's final answer.

fix(usage): strip `.gguf` file extension before quant-pattern matching

`-ud-iq4_xs` but the actual stored name had a trailing `.gguf` file
extension (this is the raw llama.cpp filename); none of the patterns
matched and the name fell through untouched, so the dashboard treated

fix(tui): clamp slash + emoji popup height to fit short terminals

Users on default macOS Terminal, Ghostty, and old Windows Terminal
(all default to 80×24) reported the TUI completely locking with a
blank screen after pressing `/` — only Ctrl+C escaped. Alacritty
users escaped because their default window was tall enough that the
dropdown still fit.

Root cause: the slash autocomplete sized its Rect as
`count + 4` rows with no height clamp. The built-in SLASH_COMMANDS
list (21) + auto-registered skills + user commands easily produced a
30+ row popup. On a 24-row terminal that's an oversized Rect, ratatui
panics writing past the buffer, the render `catch_unwind` clears the
screen, the next frame renders the same popup and panics again — an
infinite blank-screen loop the user can't get out of. The earlier
`7e2cc92` panic-capture commit even called this exact class out
("Reproduced by hitting /models with the terminal resized to 120x23")
but the slash dropdown was never given the same clamp.

returning `Option<DropdownFit>`:

- `None` when there's literally no room (rows_above_input < chrome+1
  or list is empty) — caller skips rendering, no panic.
- `Some(DropdownFit { height, visible_items, scroll_offset })` where
  height is clamped to `rows_above_input`, visible_items reflects how
  many fit after chrome, and scroll_offset is computed so the
  selected row stays inside the visible window.

fix(mc): show cron jobs again — tolerate BLOB-typed prompt rows

Mission Control's Schedule panel was rendering "No scheduled jobs."
despite 7 rows existing in `cron_jobs`. Root cause: 4 of the 7 rows
had `prompt` stored with SQLite storage class **BLOB** rather than
TEXT. SQLite's flexible typing happily accepted byte-buffer inserts
into the `TEXT NOT NULL` column (legacy sqlx-era binding glitch from
before the rusqlite migration in `220d9a3c`), and rusqlite's strict
`row.get::<String, _>("prompt")` failed on those rows with:

    Invalid column type Blob at index: 4, name: prompt

`CronJobRepository::list_all` then returned Err, `schedule_service`
swallowed it as an empty list with only "Failed to list cron jobs"
in the warn log (the underlying chain was masked by `{e}` not `{e:#}`)
— and the panel went blank. `opencrabs cron list` had the same
failure but exited code 1 with zero stderr because main.rs never
printed the error from `cli::run()`.

Three layers fixed:

1. **Defensive reader.** New `text_or_blob_col` helper in
   `db/models.rs` reads either Text or Blob storage class and UTF-8
   decodes. Used for `cron_jobs.prompt`, `.name`, `.cron_expr`,
   `.timezone`, `.thinking` in `CronJob::from_row` — any string column
   that could plausibly have been bound as bytes.

2. **Data heal.** New migration
   `20260517000001_cron_jobs_text_recast.sql` runs `CAST(col AS TEXT)`
   on every cron_jobs text column where `typeof(col) = 'blob'`. CAST
   is a no-op on existing TEXT values; on next TUI startup the 4
   stuck rows get recast in place.

3. **Diagnostic surface.** `schedule_service::list` now logs the full
   anyhow chain via `{e:#}`, `CronJobRepository::list_all` decodes
   rows one at a time and attaches the failing row's `id` to the
   error, and `main.rs` prints the error chain to stderr on CLI
   failure. Together these change "1 panel silently empties + 1 CLI
   exits 1 with no output" into "warn log names the row, CLI prints
   the chain" — the exact diagnostic pipeline that let me catch this
   in under 10 minutes once it surfaced.

in `cron_test.rs` seeds an in-memory pool with one BLOB-prompt row
and one TEXT-prompt row, sanity-checks the `typeof()` matches the
real bug, and verifies `list_all` returns both as proper Strings.

fix(heal): stop injecting phantom text into context

The phantom retry path added the model's phantom narration as an
assistant message, then added a correction nudge as user message.
Each retry added 2 messages to context. After 3+ retries, context
grew with phantom+correction pairs that confused the model, causing
it to hallucinate new phantom responses from the correction feedback
itself.

Now only the correction nudge is added — the model doesn't need to
see its own phantom text, just the correction.

fix(heal): skip persisting phantom iterations to DB

`4db7b717` ("stop injecting phantom text into context") stopped the
IN-MEMORY `ConversationContext` pollution during a single turn loop —
but the per-iteration `append_content` call at
`tool_loop.rs:2589-2600` still wrote phantom text to the
`messages.content` column on every iteration, unconditionally.

That meant the assistant DB row for one turn ended up holding the
original phantom + the retry's fresh phantom + the retry-after-that
phantom + the final answer, all concatenated. On the next turn (or on
session reload — Telegram is the worst case because sessions are long-
lived) `messages_from_last_compaction` reloaded the row, the phantom
narrations entered LLM context as legitimate assistant history, and
the model hallucinated more phantoms by extrapolating from its own
corrections. Discussion #86 / gist 85cfdc26 showed 34 such entries
piled into one session.

Fix: detect phantom right before the iteration-level persist and skip
the `append_content` (and the `accumulated_text` push) when the
iteration narrates without any tool_use blocks. The eventual
successful iteration persists normally because by then
`iteration_text` is no longer phantom; the stuck-intent-loop and
cap-exhaustion branches further down install a `[self-heal] Aborted —…`
replacement into `iteration_text` and now do an explicit
`append_content` so the abort notice survives session reload (the
break path itself doesn't persist — only emits `IntermediateText` for
the TUI).

Nudges are unaffected: they were already added only to in-memory
`context` (`Message::user(nudge)`), never to the DB row, so they don't
pile up across turns.

fix(rsi): dedup cycle output by hashing assembled opportunities

The RSI engine emitted `ImprovementOpportunity` notifications inline
while building each opportunity (tool failures, user corrections,
provider errors) and then unconditionally spawned the autonomous
improvement agent. The existing "skip if total feedback count
unchanged" gate at `rsi.rs:521-526` only caught zero-new-event cycles
— a single new event re-ran the full cycle and re-printed the same
top-50 corrections + top-20 errors blob to the TUI.

Transcript 2026-05-18 shows cycle #426 dumping byte-identical recent-
corrections / recent-errors output to cycle #425, then the autonomous
agent wrote "Cycle #426 — Converged. No improvements applied. /
Telemetry identical to cycle #425" — exactly the case worth skipping.

New flow at the end of opportunity collection:

  1. Build the `opportunities: Vec<String>` (same code as before, just
     no longer emits notifications inline).
  2. Hash the joined descriptions with SHA-256
     (`hash_opportunities`, sentinel-joined so adjacent entries can't
     collapse into one merged-content entry).
  3. Compare against the persisted hash at
     `~/.opencrabs/rsi/last_opportunities_hash`.
  4. On match: skip every `ImprovementOpportunity` send AND the agent
     spawn, surface one compact `AgentCycleComplete { summary:
     "Converged — N opportunity/opportunities identical to previous
     cycle; no agent run." }`. Empty-and-duplicate stays silent.
  5. On miss: emit each opportunity, then run the agent as before.
  6. Persist the new hash regardless so the first real cycle records
     a baseline.

Mitigation (the "don't miss anything" half of the user ask): the hash
covers the full description bodies, including the per-event
`session=…, time=…, text=…` lines. Any reorder, any new event in the
top-N slice, any whitespace change re-enables the full emission path.
The 1h cycle interval bounds the worst-case "miss" to a single cycle
even if hashing turned out too aggressive.

`tracing::info!("RSI opportunity: …")` log lines above each emission
are untouched, so log-file diagnostics stay full-fat regardless of
the TUI gating.

Six new tests in `rsi_test::hash_opportunities`:
  - identical lists → same hash
  - count change → different hash
  - top-5 reorder → different hash (the mitigation contract)
  - adjacent-entries vs merged-content → different hash (sentinel-join
    integrity)
  - empty list → stable deterministic hash
  - one-char whitespace delta → different hash

fix(dialogs): custom-provider model selection now persists + syncs live list

Two related bugs in the `/models` dialog save path for custom
providers, both surfaced 2026-05-18 when the user picked
`qwen-3.7-max-preview-thinking` from the dialagram live list and
the status bar reverted to `qwen-3.6-max-preview-thinking` after
save.

1. **Selected model wasn't read.** The save path branched on
   `provider_idx >= CUSTOM_PROVIDER_IDX` and used
   `self.ps.custom_model.clone()` — a text field that's only
   populated when models AREN'T fetched (free-text fallback).
   The list-picker branch at `focused_field == 3` only mutates
   `selected_model` and `model_filter` as the user navigates;
   `custom_model` stays at whatever was loaded from config when
   the dialog opened. So pressing Enter on a fresh live-list
   entry silently dropped the new choice and re-persisted the
   stale text. Fix: when `self.ps.models` is non-empty, resolve
   the model via the filtered list + `selected_model` index
   (same pattern the built-in branch already uses); fall back to
   the text only for the free-text path.

2. **Live `models` list never persisted.** The merged
   `ProviderConfig` write at `dialogs.rs:1189` always copied
   `existing.models.clone()` from the previous config, ignoring
   the live `self.ps.models` populated by the `/models` endpoint
   when the dialog opened. New models appeared in the picker but
   never reached disk; retired models stayed forever. Fix: use
   the live list when non-empty (replaces + dedupes the saved
   list against the endpoint's current view); fall back to
   `existing.models` only when the live fetch was empty
   (offline / endpoint down / free-text custom).

Net behaviour after both fixes: picking any model from a custom
provider's live list now persists that exact name as
`default_model` AND syncs the surrounding `models` array to
match the endpoint's current catalogue. Built-in providers are
unaffected — they don't store a `models` field in config and
their picker branch was already correct.

fix(telegram): pipe-separate model callback so custom-provider colons survive parse

The `/models` inline-keyboard buttons generated callback data as
`model:<provider_name>:<model>`, which works for built-ins
(`model:openai:gpt-5-nano` → split_once(':') → `(openai, gpt-5-nano)`)
but quietly breaks for custom providers: their `provider_name` is
literally `custom:<slug>` (e.g. `custom:dialagram`), so the payload
became `model:custom:dialagram:qwen-3.7-max-preview-thinking` and
the parser's `split_once(':')` ate the wrong colon. Result on the
2026-05-18T23:39 callback for dialagram:

  sync_provider_for_session[…]: session wants
  custom/dialagram:qwen-3.7-max-preview-thinking, agent currently on
  dialagram/qwen-3.7-max-preview-thinking — attempting restore

— provider got persisted as `"custom"` and model as
`"dialagram:qwen-3.7-max-preview-thinking"` (the dialagram: prefix
glued onto the model name). At wire time, `create_provider_by_name`
fell back to the in-memory agent (dialagram was already there) and
the request still hit qwen-3.7, but a fresh restart or any
sync-from-stored-metadata path would have rebuilt the wrong provider.

OpenRouter has the symmetric problem on the other side — models like
`qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free` carry a trailing `:free` suffix, so even
`rsplit_once(':')` would mis-split there. The actual fix needs an
unambiguous separator.

Swap `:` for `|` between provider_name and model. Generator + parser
move in lock-step:

  generator: format!("model:{}|{}", resp.provider_name, m)
  parser:    rest.split_once('|')

Now `model:custom:dialagram|qwen-3.7-max-preview-thinking` splits as
`("custom:dialagram", "qwen-3.7-max-preview-thinking")` and the
OpenRouter case `model:openrouter|qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free` keeps the
`:free` suffix intact. Telegram callback_data byte limit (64) is
unaffected — the new separator is the same length.

Buttons are session-lived (regenerated each `/models` invocation) so
there's no migration risk for stale callback payloads. In-memory
session metadata corrected on the next selection; DB sessions table
had no rows with the broken shape (transient state only).

fix(context): strip compaction banner from LLM context so models don't echo it

User reported 2026-05-18T22:51 Telegram session (qwen-3.7-max-preview-
thinking, session 1e35bab0): the model emitted a `[[CONTEXT COMPACTION
— …]]` banner followed by a structured "CONTEXT SUMMARY" block
(Chronological Analysis / Files Modified / User Preferences) as its
visible response to a `continue crab` message. The double-bracket form
made it clear this was the MODEL hallucinating the format — not our
code returning the summary directly. But the imitation only happens
because the real marker lives verbatim in DB as a user-role message,
and `messages_from_last_compaction` loads it into LLM context every
turn. Chatty models then copy the template into their own output.

Fix: extract `AgentService::strip_compaction_banner` and run it in the
DB→LLM-context conversion loop alongside the existing
`strip_llm_artifacts` pass. Removes the banner LINE
(`[CONTEXT COMPACTION — …]\n\n`) but keeps the summary body that
follows, so the model still has the task snapshot it needs to continue
work. The banner-detection scan in `messages_from_last_compaction`
runs against the raw DB rows BEFORE this strip, so the load-point
lookup is unaffected.

Strip is a strict no-op when:
- the message doesn't start with the canonical `[CONTEXT COMPACTION`
  prefix (only OUR marker is stripped; the model's `[[...]]` imitation
  flowing through other paths is left alone),
- the marker line lacks the expected `\n\n` blank-line separator
  (defensive against malformed historical persists — we don't want to
  swallow real content past a single `\n`).

CLI-provider sessions skip the whole strip block (they manage their
own server-side history) so this change is no-op for them.

Four new tests in `compaction_test::banner_strip`:
- banner prefix stripped, summary body retained
- no banner → unchanged
- malformed banner without `\n\n` → unchanged
- model's double-bracket imitation NOT touched (only OUR canonical
  single-bracket form is stripped)

fix(compaction): wire ProgressEvent::Compacting so channels show activity

User reported 2026-05-19: long Telegram session (heyiolo) hit
auto-compaction at ~65% context, the agent silently stalled for 30s
while `compact_context` ran, and Telegram showed no typing indicator
or intermediate message during the whole window. Looked like the
request was dropped — it wasn't, just no visible signal until the
post-compaction iteration produced its first streaming chunk.

`ProgressEvent::Compacting` was defined in types.rs but never emitted
and the only handler (`cli/ui.rs:522`) was `return`. Wire it up
end-to-end:

  - **Emit** in `enforce_context_budget` right before the LLM
    `compact_context` call fires (Tier 1, the slow path). Tier 2
    hard-truncation is sync + fast so no event there.
  - **TUI** (`cli/ui.rs`): convert to `TuiEvent::SystemMessage` —
    "🗜️ Compacting context — this may take 30-60s on long sessions".
    Renders as a system row in the chat, scoped to the originating
    session via the existing `SystemMessage` plumbing.
  - **Telegram** (`channels/telegram/handler.rs`): push a one-shot
    `DisplayItem::Intermediate` with the same text. The intermediate
    flush also triggers `send_chat_action(Typing)` via the existing
    intermediate-text path so the user sees Telegram's native typing
    indicator alongside the message.
  - **Discord / Slack / WhatsApp**: send a one-shot post with the
    same text via each channel's existing async-spawn pattern.

Summary body still stays internal — only the FACT that compaction is
running is surfaced. Models can't echo this event (it's a channel-
side rendering, not an LLM context entry).

fix(self-heal): gate phantom on turn-level tool execution and add sticky fallback on exhaust

The phantom detector previously fired on the final text-only iteration
of a turn even when earlier iterations had successfully executed tool
calls. A clean wrap-up like "Pushed (abc123). Favicon replaced, deploy
complete." matched the past-tense action claim heuristic and was
replaced with a self-heal abort notice — a false positive on a turn
that had already completed correctly.

Track `tools_executed_this_turn` in the tool loop and skip every
phantom branch once any tool has run. Bump MAX_PHANTOM_RETRIES from 3
to 5 to give the model more room to recover from a rough start. When
the cap finally exhausts on a turn with zero tool activity, force a
sticky fallback to the next provider in the chain (via the existing
`force_next_fallback` API) and continue with a fresh retry budget
instead of aborting outright. The fallback pair is persisted via
`persist_sticky_pair` so reconnects and reloads land on the working
provider.

Regression test pins the false-positive case: provider emits a
ContentBlock::ToolUse on iter 1, then "Pushed (abc123)…" on iter 2 —
the final response must preserve the wrap-up and never contain a
`[self-heal] Aborted` notice.

fix(compaction): refresh typing indicator on channels without banner text

Auto-compaction produces zero streaming chunks for 10-60s. On
Telegram the existing 4s typing-pinger loop in handle_message stays
alive throughout, but a long compaction window can drift past a ping
gap and look momentarily frozen. On Discord there is no continuous
pinger at all — the channel goes truly silent until the next chunk.
Channels with no typing API (Slack, WhatsApp) have always been silent
during compaction and remain so.

Emit `ProgressEvent::Compacting` from `enforce_context_budget` right
before the slow `compact_context` LLM call. Channel handlers consume

intermediate text, no system message:

  `send_chat_action(Typing)` to reset the 4s window so users see the
  dots resume the moment compaction starts.
- Discord: spawn a bounded loop that calls `broadcast_typing` every
  8s for up to 90s (Discord typing pings last ~10s). The loop runs
  fire-and-forget; if compaction finishes earlier, real streaming
  chunks resume the indicator naturally and the leftover pings are
  harmless.
- TUI: kept as `return` (spinner already covers it).
- Slack / WhatsApp: no handler — `_ => {}` already drops the event.

including the TUI. Compaction stays transparent as before; only the

  - Discord DMs: resolver uses `"Discord: DM <name> (<author_id>)"`;

source of truth — `find_session_by_title*` returns the most recently
touched row, so the freshly-created /new session naturally wins the
next lookup. No in-memory chat→session reverse map needed.

fix(self-heal): never abort, always retry or fallback

The stuck-intent-loop branch added in e186fea3 (unauthorized agent commit
under user's git config) hard-aborted on the FIRST detection of 3+
intent line-starts in a single iteration. Zero self-heal attempts ran
before the abort fired, and the cap-exhaustion branch later in the
same path also ended in an abort once retries ran out. Both wrote
"[self-heal] Aborted …" into the assistant message and broke the turn,
stranding the user with no result even when the model had already done
the real work earlier in the same turn.

Rework so the self-heal pipeline NEVER aborts:

1. Stuck-intent-loop: still flagged as a strong signal, but no longer
   triggers an early break. If we've already burned half the retry
   budget on this provider, fast-escalate to a sticky fallback
   immediately (the current provider has demonstrated it can't reach
   its tool-call channel for this prompt). Otherwise fall through to
   the regular nudge-and-retry path. The fast-escalate also kicks in
   the moment a non-stuck phantom hits MAX_PHANTOM_RETRIES on this
   provider, so the swap path is unified.

2. Cap exhaustion: drop the "[self-heal] Aborted" string and the
   abort SelfHealingAlert. Instead reset phantom_retries_used to 0
   and inject a hard system nudge ("STOP narrating, call the tool
   NOW via the structured tool-call API"), then `continue`. The loop
   keeps trying. The user presses Stop if they truly want out.

3. Counter reset on every successful tool execution. Previously the
   counter accumulated for the whole turn, so a single late phantom
   burst after good work pushed us straight over the cap. Now a real
   tool run wipes the counter, making it "consecutive phantoms since
   the last real tool", which is the meaningful signal. Applied at
   both `[TOOL_EXEC] ✅` sites (approval-required path and direct path).

Result: the screenshot scenario (10 successful tool calls then 6
intent-only lines in a single iteration) now sees counter=0 entering
the phantom path, gets a nudge, retries, and either recovers on this
provider or sticky-swaps to the next. No "Aborted" string ever
reaches the user.

feat(tools/dynamic): per-param coerce_empty_to / coerce_null_to for tools.toml (closes #95)

Dynamic tools (HTTP + shell executors) had no per-parameter shape
control: empty arrays landed as `[]`, nulls as `null`, with no way to
distinguish "omit" vs "send empty" vs "reject" across the call paths
(typical concern for MCP/fastmcp targets that strict-validate the
body).

Adds two optional fields to `ParamDef`:

  coerce_empty_to  empty array / empty object / empty string handler
  coerce_null_to   JSON-null handler

Each accepts one of `keep` (default), `omit`, `null`, `error`. Defaults
preserve existing behaviour for every `tools.toml` already on disk.

The new `coerce_params` step runs right after `extract_params` so both
executors get the same rules:

  - keep    pass through unchanged
  - omit    drop the key from the params map
  - null    replace with JSON `null`
  - error   reject the call before exec, surface the param + shape
            in the error message back to the agent

Shell template renderer gains mustache-style conditional sections:
`{{#name}}…{{/name}}` renders the body when the key is still present
after coercion, and collapses the whole block when it was omitted. So
`run {{#ids}}--ids {{ids}}{{/ids}}` cleanly drops the `--ids` flag
instead of leaving a dangling `--ids ` in the command. The HTTP path
needs no template-side change — omitted keys just disappear from the
URL/header substitution map.

Touched callers (existing struct literals): `tool_manage.rs` and the
inline test fixtures in `dynamic/tool.rs` + `dynamic/loader.rs` now
spell out `coerce_empty_to: Default::default()` / `coerce_null_to:
Default::default()`.

fix(gemini): strip additionalProperties from tool schemas before send (closes #99)

Gemini's `function_declarations[].parameters` validator accepts only a
narrow subset of OpenAPI 3 and rejects `additionalProperties` with a
400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. Built-in tools that declare dynamic dict fields
(`http` for headers/query, `tool_manage` for headers, etc.) ship
`additionalProperties` in their JSON schemas because every other
provider accepts it. The result: any agent session using Gemini —
TUI, Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, cron, daemon — failed every
turn that tried to use those tools, with the exact error reported in
the issue.

Add `sanitize_schema_for_gemini(value)`: walks a `serde_json::Value`
recursively and removes any `additionalProperties` key from every
object node. Apply at both Gemini schema embed sites:

  - `build_request_body` — the per-turn function_declarations array.
  - `cache_content` — the cached-tools path used by the
    cached-content optimization.

Other Gemini-incompatible JSON-Schema keys (`$ref`, `oneOf`, etc.) are
left alone; expand the strip list if real-world usage surfaces them.

7 new tests in `gemini_schema_sanitize_test.rs` cover:
  - top-level `additionalProperties` stripped
  - nested in `properties[*]` stripped
  - nested inside `items.*` (array element schemas) stripped
  - schemas without `additionalProperties` are returned unchanged
  - non-object root values (bool/string/number/null) pass through
  - deeply nested object trees recurse correctly
  - smoke test against the real `http` tool schema shape

fix(tui/models): refresh per-provider fields after saving a new custom provider

After saving a new custom provider in the /models dialog, the cursor
moved to the new entry's alphabetical slot but the per-provider input
fields (base_url, custom_name, custom_model, context_window,
editing_custom_key) kept showing whatever the user had just typed.
Visually: the cursor stood on a different row than the fields next to
it referenced.

Two failure modes from this:

  - The Base URL line displayed the wrong value for whichever
    existing row the cursor next landed on, making it look like the
    other provider's URL had been overwritten (it hadn't — config on
    disk stays correct as long as no further save happens in this
    state).
  - If the user then pressed Save without first navigating away with
    Up/Down (which IS the only existing path that triggered the
    field-reload), `save_provider` would write base_url to whichever
    section `self.ps.custom_name` still pointed at — namely the new
    entry. Existing rows still safe, but cross-row confusion was
    real and the next-save danger was a foot-gun.

  - Extract the field-reload logic (lines 312-335 of
    `handle_model_selector_key`) into a `reload_model_selector_custom_fields`
    helper on the App.
  - Call the helper from the existing Up/Down navigation path (no
    behavioural change there).
  - ALSO call it from the post-save reposition path right after
    `selected_provider = CUSTOM_INSTANCES_START + pos`, so the
    cursor and the displayed fields stay in lockstep.

fix(self-heal): 5-nudge budget for reasoning-only turns + sticky fallback so empty replies never silently drop

The empty-reasoning self-heal used a one-shot bool (`empty_reasoning_retry_used`).
After it fired once it was never reset within the turn, so when a thinking model
emitted reasoning-only TWICE in a row (e.g. alibaba-qwen `qwen-latest-series-
invite-beta-v34` on a hostile prompt), the second iteration skipped the nudge,
fell through to `final_response = Some(response); break`, and returned an empty
response. The TUI showed the "nudging for response" alert and then nothing —
looked exactly like a dropped request.

Now:
- Counter `empty_reasoning_retries` with `EMPTY_REASONING_MAX_NUDGES = 5`.
- Each nudge sharpens the system instruction (rounds 4–5 explicitly warn about
  the upcoming fallback).
- When the budget is exhausted, walk `self.fallback_providers`: swap to each
  candidate, retry the request, check whether the candidate's response contains
  visible text. First one that does sticks (`persist_sticky_pair`) and its
  response replaces the empty one for this turn — the user gets a real reply
  and the next user message lands on the recovered provider.
- If no fallback is configured OR every candidate also returns empty, emit a
  final `SelfHealingAlert` so the user sees a "switch model manually" message
  instead of an empty hang.

feat(ctx-counter): per-provider tokenizer calibration so the footer doesn't jump on first turn

`brain::tokenizer::count_tokens` uses cl100k_base, which overcounts
Qwen-family models by ~2.4×. On a fresh /new session the footer would
start at the local cl100k estimate of system_brain + tool_schemas
(~24k/200k for the current setup) and then drop to ~10k/200k as soon as
the first real `response.usage.input_tokens` from
alibaba-qwen/qwen-latest-series-invite-beta-v34 arrived. Users (and the
LLM) read this as a glitch.

New `brain::token_calibration` module keeps a per-provider ratio in
`~/.opencrabs/token_calibration.json`. On every API turn that reports
real `usage.input_tokens`, the tool loop records
`(local_estimate, real_input_tokens)` for the active provider and
updates the ratio via an EMA (alpha=0.3, MIN_OBSERVATION_TOKENS=500,
ratio clamped to [0.10, 5.00]). `AgentService::base_context_tokens()`
applies the ratio when displaying; the raw cl100k count stays as the
budget denominator so compaction still trips a hair early (safe
overestimate).

Net result: first turn of a calibrated provider lands close to the real
value (~10k for Qwen instead of ~24k), the footer no longer "drops" on
the first hi, and the calibration self-tunes across sessions.

feat(ctx-counter): uncalibrated providers show 0/max instead of the misleading raw cl100k estimate

session against a provider with no calibration data shows 0k/200k, and
every subsequent /new on that provider shows the calibrated estimate
from the start. Previous commit ea7d8e18 still fell back to the raw
cl100k_base count when no ratio existed, which reproduced the exact
"footer drops from 24k to 10k after first hi" complaint we set out to
fix — just on the first ever session per provider.

- `token_calibration::calibrate` now returns `Option<u32>`: `Some` only
  when a ratio exists, `None` for fresh providers.
- `base_context_tokens()` returns `0` when uncalibrated. Footer renders
  0/max until the first turn observation lands, at which point the
  calibration ratio is recorded AND the displayed value flips to the
  real `usage.input_tokens` from the response.

fix(rsi): reject raw failure-event logs in brain files (closes #111)

@leshchenko1979 reported TOOLS.md accumulating ~30 sections shaped like
`### Bash Exit Code 127 — Recurring (6 failures since 2026-05-17)` with
bodies enumerating timestamps and session IDs. The brain file had become
a failure-event audit log instead of operational guidance. Root cause:
the RSI agent prompt told it to write to TOOLS.md when `tool_failure`
events recurred but didn't draw a sharp enough line between "the rule
derived from those failures" (belongs there) and "the raw log of when
they happened" (does not). The Repeat-Violation Escalation Pattern made
this worse by encouraging inline counters, which the agent then
escalated to full incident lists.

Two-layer fix:

1. `RSI_AGENT_PROMPT` in `brain/rsi.rs` — the TOOLS.md guidance now
   spells out the rule-vs-log distinction with explicit good and bad
   header examples, and reinforces that incident counters belong on a
   single inline `Violations: N` line inside the rule body, not in the
   section header or as a list of dates/sessions.
2. `self_improve` tool in `brain/tools/self_improve.rs` — defense in
   depth. New `looks_like_failure_log` heuristic scans the proposed
   `content` for section headers matching `(N failures: ...)` or
   `Recurring ... failures` patterns; both `apply` and `update` actions
   reject those with a message pointing back at issue #111.

The user's main TOOLS.md is already clean (grep -c 'failures:' returns
0). The reporter's profile-specific copy stays as-is — it's their own
agent's brain file. This change prevents new bloat from accumulating in
any profile going forward.

feat(browser_click): accept text= and xpath= selectors in addition to CSS

Before: browser_click only accepted CSS selectors. When the agent passed
a Playwright-style `text=Peinture` it hit CDP `find_element` which only
speaks CSS and bounced with `Error -32000: DOM Error while querying`.
Logs from this morning show the agent then ran 25+ wasted iterations
flailing through navigate/wait/screenshot before finally falling back to
browser_find.

Click now branches on a selector prefix:
- `text=Label` → in-page JS walks visible elements and clicks the first
  whose innerText (case-insensitive) contains the substring. Scrolls
  into view first.
- `xpath=//...` → in-page JS evaluates the XPath and clicks the first
  visible match.
- Anything else → existing CSS path via page.find_element.

When the text path finds nothing, the error explicitly tells the agent
how to recover with browser_find. Tool description updated to document
all three shapes so the agent picks the right one up front.

feat(browser_click): inline recovery hint when CSS selector misses

The CSS fallback path's error was just "Element 'X' not found: <CDP err>"
with no suggestion of what to try next. The agent then spent 5+
iterations guessing alternate CSS variations before discovering
browser_find on its own.

Now the error appends:
- If the selector looks like prose (contains spaces or pipes), suggest
  `text=...` directly.
- Otherwise, suggest browser_find with mode=text/aria/role and the
  `[data-opencrabs-match="N"]` workflow.

Turns "5 wasted iters guessing" into "1 retry with the right tool".

fix(tool_loop): only warn on empty input when the tool actually requires fields

The empty-input ERROR fired for every tool called with {} regardless of
whether the schema declared any required fields. browser_screenshot's
selector parameter is optional — calling it with {} is valid and the
tool runs fine — but the loop still logged
"[TOOL_EXEC] ⚠️ Tool 'browser_screenshot' received empty input — tool
call will fail" four times per browser session in this morning's logs,
making real failures hard to find.

Now consult the tool's input_schema.required array: ERROR only when
required is non-empty, DEBUG otherwise.

feat(self-heal): semantic loop detection for browser screenshot-spam

Exact-loop detection only trips when the same tool+args repeat. The
navigate→wait→screenshot rotation uses three different tools, slipping
through every check. Logs from 2026-05-23 09:04 show 32+ iterations of
this rotation in a single turn before the agent gave up in French.

New heuristic runs after the per-iteration exact-loop check: if the last
8 iterations contain `browser_screenshot` 4+ times AND zero
progress-making interactions (`browser_click`, `browser_type`,
`browser_eval`), inject a one-shot user nudge:
- Tells the agent it has enough screenshots and must interact.
- Lists the three productive actions (click, type, navigate) with the
  new text=/xpath=/CSS selector shapes for click.
- Routes the agent to `browser_find` when it can't find what to click.

`browser_screenshot_loop_nudged: bool` resets per turn so a stuck cycle
gets exactly one nudge. The exact-loop break still fires if the agent
ignores the nudge and keeps spamming the same tool+args.

feat(browser_screenshot): reject no-op repeats when the page hasn't changed

feat(browser_navigate): short-circuit same-URL re-navigation

made between calls. The tool already returns title + final_url, so the
output didn't lack info — the agent just wasn't reacting to "already

equivalent to the requested one (trailing slash and fragment ignored,

feat(voicebox_stt): 2s liveness probe before multipart POST so dead voicebox fails fast

When the voicebox process is down (port refused, no DNS, hung), the
existing transcribe path would block on the multipart upload for the
full request timeout (~30s) before bubbling the error. That blocks
voice messages on Telegram and burns user time with no signal.

Now: send a 2s GET to the base URL first. Any HTTP response (2xx/3xx/
4xx/5xx) counts as alive — the server is reachable even if root 404s.
Only connection-level failures (refused, timeout, DNS) cause the probe
to fail. When the probe fails, transcribe returns immediately with
`Voicebox STT unreachable (liveness probe failed): ...` which the
upstream STT dispatcher will catch and use to route to the next
provider in the chain (commit C in this series).

- stt_liveness_probe_fails_fast_when_voicebox_down — asserts <5s

chat verbatim — opaque to the user, and the message hides the actual
fix (rebuild voicebox with `--collect-data <pkg>` + a
`hooks/hook-lazy_loader.py` setting `hiddenimports = ['lazy_loader']`).

`translate_voicebox_error()` runs on every 5xx body:
- Detects the `Cannot load imports from non-existent stub` + `__init__.pyi`
  fingerprint that lazy_loader produces when PyInstaller strips the
  runtime stubs.
- Extracts the top-level Python package name from the path
  (`/_MEI<rand>/librosa/core/__init__.pyi` → `librosa`) so the
  message names the exact `--collect-data` arg the rebuild needs.
- Wraps the actionable rebuild instruction around the original detail
  (preserved at the end for debugging).
- Unknown error shapes pass through unchanged.

feat(voice): STT fallback chain — user-configured provider order with auto-failover

When the primary STT provider failed (voicebox unreachable, OpenAI 429,
Groq rate-limited, etc.) the dispatcher returned the error verbatim and
the voice note was lost. Users wanted the same sticky-fallback ergonomics
the completion-side already has: codify "if my local voicebox is down,
try Groq, then OpenAI" once and let the system route around outages
automatically.

New `[providers.stt].fallback_chain` config field, e.g.:

    [providers.stt]
    fallback_chain = ["groq", "openai_compatible", "local"]

Accepts these labels (case-insensitive, with aliases): `voicebox`,
`openai_compatible` / `openai-compatible` / `openai`, `groq`,
`local` / `whisper` / `local_whisper`. Unknown labels are silently
dropped so a typo doesn't break the chain.

Dispatcher behaviour:
1. Resolve the primary from current config flags (voicebox first if
   enabled, then openai-compatible, groq, local — unchanged precedence).
2. Build the fallback list: user chain when non-empty, otherwise the
   default priority order. Primary is always excluded from its own
   fallback list. Unconfigured providers (missing API key, no base_url)
   are filtered out before the chain runs — no point routing to a
   provider that will fail immediately.
3. Try each candidate in order. Audio bytes are cloned between attempts
   so each provider gets a fresh copy.
4. First success wins; the recovery is logged with the attempt chain
   so the user can see what saved them.
5. Full-chain failure returns a composite error citing every provider
   and its specific failure reason — much more actionable than the
   single-line error before.

`SttProviderKind` enum + `resolve_fallback_chain` helper are
`pub(crate)` so the new test module can exercise the resolution logic
without spinning up actual STT backends.

fix(custom_openai_compatible): extract dict-by-call-id tool call shape

Regression hit 2026-05-24 on qwen-3.7-max-preview (@adolfousier
Telegram screenshots): the model started emitting tool calls as a
top-level object KEYED BY CALL ID instead of using the structured
tool_calls API or any of the existing text-fallback shapes:

  {"call_5f8d9c7b4a3e2f1c8d6e5b9a": {"name": "read_file",
                                     "arguments": {"path": "..."}}}

The existing extractor handled <tool_call>, tool_call:, "tool_calls":
[...], bare arrays of [{"id":"call_...","type":"function",...}],
Claude-style <bash><command>...</command></bash>, etc. — but NOT the
dict-by-id shape. So these calls leaked into delta.content text, never
dispatched, and Telegram rendered the JSON as a markdown code block
(often inside a ```json fence emitted by the same model).

New Pass 1.6:
- Cheap signal: `"call_` + (`"name"` OR `"function"`) somewhere in text.
- Anchor on every `"call_` occurrence; require it to be the FIRST key
  of an object (walk back past whitespace, must hit `{`). Skips prose
  mentions like `the "call_id" field`.
- Balance-extract the wrapping object, parse as JSON, iterate top-level
  keys matching `^call_`, route each value through the existing
  `parse_tool_call_value` helper (so it picks up name/args nested under
  `function` too).
- Strip the matched object range so it doesn't get re-rendered as text.

Five new tests covering:
- Single call (the exact screenshot shape)
- Multiple call_<id> keys in one object
- Wrapped inside ```json fence (Telegram's most common rendering path)
- Prose mention of "call_id" is not extracted
- function-envelope-nested form inside the dict-by-id shape

All 39 extractor tests green (34 existing + 5 new).

fix(ctx-counter): real-time data only, rip out the calibration system (closes #119)

The calibration system shipped on 2026-05-24 (ea7d8e18, 12249c40)
tried to predict the initial /new footer by learning a per-provider
`real_input_tokens / local_cl100k_estimate` ratio. It was the wrong
approach from the start — opencrabs already has REAL data on every
turn from `response.usage.input_tokens`, no need to predict.

It also shipped with a double-count bug: `local_estimate` was computed
as `context.token_count + base_context_tokens_raw()`, but
`context.token_count` already includes the system_brain (added by
`AgentContext::with_system_brain` at context.rs:58) and
`base_context_tokens_raw()` counts it again. For the ops profile
(brain ~100K, tools ~14K) that produced a local_estimate of ~214K vs
a real API value of ~47K, learning a ratio of 0.22 — way too small.
Issue #119 screenshot: footer showed 19K on /new, then jumped to 47K
on the first real reply. Calibration made the jump WORSE, not better.

This commit:
- Deletes `src/brain/token_calibration.rs` entirely.
- Removes the `pub mod token_calibration` line from `brain/mod.rs`.
- Replaces `base_context_tokens()` with `pub fn base_context_tokens(&self) -> u32 { 0 }`.
  /new now shows `0/max` until the first turn lands.
- Removes the `record_observation` call from the tool loop. The
  per-call branch that handles `response.usage.input_tokens > 0` now
  just returns the provider's value verbatim.

Net behaviour: footer reads exactly what the provider tells us, every
time. No predictions, no learned ratios, no drift.

`base_context_tokens_raw()` is kept for the few internal call sites
that still need a local floor estimate when a provider reports zero
input_tokens (CLI providers, streaming-without-usage paths). Those
are budget-side, not display-side.

fix(auto-title): fire on the FIRST turn + retry when the LLM call fails (closes #118, closes #120)

Two related Telegram regressions reported by @leshchenko1979:

  #118 — Sessions are not autorenamed in Telegram.
  #120 — New session is not that new in Telegram (all 10 visible
         sessions in /sessions had the identical default title
         "Telegram: DM Алексей (133526395) [chat:133526395]",
         distinguishable only by timestamp).

Same root cause from two angles:

(a) The auto-title trigger required `db_message_count >= 1`, where
    `db_message_count` was taken BEFORE the current user message gets
    stored. So on a fresh /new session the first turn saw count=0 and
    auto-title was skipped. Many users only send one message per
    /new — the reporter clearly does — so auto-title never ran and
    every session sat with its channel-generated default title
    forever, indistinguishable in the /sessions list.

(b) `mark_auto_title_attempted` was called BEFORE the title-generation
    LLM call (correctly, to prevent race conditions if the user fires
    a second message while the title is in flight). But if the LLM
    call failed (provider down, 5xx, timeout), the flag stayed true
    permanently. No retry path. Session stuck with default title.

Fix:

- Drop the `db_message_count >= 1` guard. The current `user_message`
  is in scope; we don't need DB history to title from it. Trigger
  becomes `!user_message.trim().is_empty() && !auto_title_attempted
  && is_default_or_empty(title)`. Fires on turn 1.

- Add `SessionService::reset_auto_title_attempted` (mirror of
  `mark_auto_title_attempted`, sets the column back to 0).

- Background task's Err arm now logs WARN (not DEBUG) and calls
  `reset_auto_title_attempted` so the next user message can retry.
  Same recovery on the "LLM returned an unusable empty title" path.

- Removed the now-unused `db_message_count` capture.

Behaviour after this commit:
- /new + first message → auto-title fires once, in the background.
  On success: session renamed (default prefix preserved if it
  existed). On failure: flag reset, next message retries.
- Multiple concurrent messages on a single session: only the first
  one fires the spawn (flag prevents the rest).
- 28 auto_title tests stay green.

fix(profile): seed brain-file templates on `profile create` so new profiles aren't blank

Audit triggered by @leshchenko1979's `ops` profile breakdown on #119
revealed that `create_profile` only built `profiles/<name>/`,
`memory/`, and `logs/` — no brain files at all. Users running
`opencrabs profile create <name>` got an empty brain dir and the
agent ran with no SOUL.md / TOOLS.md / SECURITY.md / etc. until the
user manually copied templates over or re-ran the onboarding wizard
with the profile active.

RSI's `sync_templates` doesn't fill the gap either: it explicitly
skips files that don't exist locally (`rsi_sync.rs:299`) by design
— it never CREATES brain files, only updates existing ones. So an
empty profile stayed empty forever.

Fix: new `seed_brain_templates(&profile_dir)` helper writes the same
8 templates the onboarding wizard's `seed_templates` path materializes
(SOUL, IDENTITY, USER, AGENTS, TOOLS, MEMORY, CODE, SECURITY). Called
from `create_profile` right after the directory skeleton is set up.
- Skips files that already exist in the target dir (safe to call from
  recovery paths in commit 2).
- Failures are logged WARN but don't abort profile creation —
  registration still proceeds so the profile is usable; the user can
  manually seed later if needed.

Templates are inlined via `include_str!` rather than importing the
TUI's `TEMPLATE_FILES` list (`config` must not depend on `tui`). Both
modules reference the same files under `src/docs/reference/templates/`,
so they stay in lockstep.

fix(rsi_sync): re-seed brain templates when a profile dir is mostly empty

Companion to 70bbc35c. That commit fixed the forward path
(`profile create` now seeds templates). This one fixes the recovery
path for profiles created BEFORE that fix — they got a blank brain
dir and `sync_templates` was a no-op on them because it explicitly
skips files that don't exist locally (rsi_sync.rs:299), by design.

New helper `seed_missing_templates_if_blank(&home)` runs at the top
of `sync_templates`:
- Counts how many of the 8 core brain templates (SOUL, IDENTITY,
  USER, AGENTS, TOOLS, MEMORY, CODE, SECURITY) are missing from
  `home`.
- If more than half are missing, calls
  `crate::config::profile::seed_brain_templates(&home)` to materialize
  them from the bundled template strings.

The half-missing threshold is the heuristic that distinguishes "blank
profile that needs rescue" from "healthy install where the user
intentionally removed one or two files". A brand-new empty profile
will have all 8 missing → re-seeds; a healthy install with 7 of 8
files (e.g. user deleted USER.md) won't trigger the seeder.

`seed_brain_templates` itself never overwrites existing files
(commit 1's defensive behaviour), so this is safe to run on every
sync — it's a no-op when files are present.

test(profile): cover brain-template seeding on create_profile + the no-overwrite contract

Locks in the behaviour added by 70bbc35c. Until now `profile_test.rs`

fix(auto-title): handle thinking-only responses from reasoning models + add real e2e test (closes #121)

@leshchenko1979 reported on #121 that v0.3.28 STILL did not auto-rename
Telegram sessions. Multiple "fixes" had shipped (#114, #118, #120) and
each one looked correct on code review, but none of them tested the
end-to-end flow. They tested `is_default_channel_title`, `clean_auto_title`,
prefix/suffix extractors — pure helpers. Nothing exercised the actual
spawn → LLM → DB write path.

Wrote that test first. It passed against a normal mock provider, which
narrowed the bug to a specific response shape. Wrote a second mock that
returns ONLY a `ContentBlock::Thinking` (no Text) — the shape
`qwen-3.7-max-preview-thinking` produces for short prompts. That test
failed with empty title. Root cause found.

`extract_text_from_response` only reads `ContentBlock::Text`. When the
title-generation `complete()` call returned Thinking-only, the extracted
string was empty, `clean_auto_title("")` returned empty, the spawn
hit the empty branch (which 9b083078 made reset the attempt flag for
retry). Next user message: same provider, same Thinking-only response,
same empty title, same reset. Infinite no-op. Title never landed in DB,
session stuck on default channel-generated name forever.

Fix:

- New `extract_title_candidate(response)` helper in `types.rs`:
  tries Text blocks first (existing behaviour), falls back to
  Thinking blocks. From a Thinking block, plucks the last quoted
  phrase (the model's settled candidate) or the last short sentence.
  `pluck_title_from_thinking` is the private heuristic.

- `tool_loop.rs` spawn now calls `extract_title_candidate` instead
  of `extract_text_from_response` + `clean_auto_title` separately.

- New `auto_title_e2e_test`: a single `#[tokio::test]` that drives
  both phases (Text-block response, then Thinking-only response)
  through `send_message_with_tools_and_mode` (the same entry point
  Telegram uses), polls the DB for the rewritten title, and asserts
  channel prefix + [chat:ID] suffix are preserved. Both phases share
  one tokio runtime because `Database::GLOBAL_POOL` is a OnceLock
  whose first-test setter would poison a sibling test's pool ref.

fix(db): use MEMORY journal + max_size=1 for in-memory test pool

CI release-mode runs of `auto_title_e2e_test::auto_title_end_to_end_
covers_all_scenarios` were panicking with `Database("Failed to create
message")`. With the error chain surfaced the underlying cause was
`Error code 262: database table is locked: sessions` — SQLite's
SQLITE_LOCKED on the shared in-memory cache.

Two compounding problems on the in-memory test pool:
1. WAL journal mode is a no-op for `:memory:` (no file to journal to)
   but with `cache=shared` it triggers spurious table-lock failures
   under concurrent writers in release mode.
2. `max_size = 5` made deadpool hand out distinct connections that
   then fought for shared-cache table locks. The auto_title flow
   spawns a background title task which races the main turn's session
   touch — reliable failure in release, flaky in debug.

Fix:
- Split `apply_pragmas` so in-memory connections get
  `journal_mode=MEMORY`, `synchronous=OFF`, `foreign_keys=ON` (file
  pools keep WAL/NORMAL).
- Cap the in-memory pool to a single serialized connection. No
  cross-connection lock contention, every interact() runs in order,
  debug and release behave identically. Each Database still gets a
  unique URI so parallel tests stay isolated.

auto_title_e2e` → 1 passed; full release suite 2945 passed / 0 failed.

needs a connection — under the new single-conn pool this is a

fix(custom_openai_compatible): extract bare-args bash tool calls (qwen-3.7-max-thinking)

2026-05-27 regression on qwen-3.7-max-thinking via the dialagram provider:
the model emitted orphaned bash arguments as bare JSON objects directly in
delta.content with no call_id wrapper, no `name` field, and no XML tag.
Shape from the user's TUI screenshot:

  {"command": "cd ~/srv/rs/opencrabs && cat src/rtk/tracker.rs | head -150"}
  {"command": "cd ~/srv/rs/opencrabs && cat src/rtk/mod.rs | head -200"}
  ... (5 blobs total in one assistant turn)

All five passed straight through the early-return signal check in
extract_text_tool_calls (none of the existing markers matched), rendered as
visible JSON in chat, and the calls never dispatched. Self-heal could not
detect the pattern either since it relies on the same extractor signals.

Same root-cause family as the 2026-05-24 dict-by-call-id leak fixed in
fd6b180c (qwen-3.7-max-preview), different wrapper. Both stem from qwen
variants choosing to emit tool args as content instead of through the
structured tool_calls API. The fix mirrors Pass 1.6's structure with
stricter guards because bare-args has no unique signature like `"call_`:

- New signal `has_bare_command_args` triggers on `{"command":` anchored
  forms (with whitespace tolerance for `{ "command":` and `{"command" :`).
- Pass 1.7 runs LAST so it can check the accumulated strip_ranges and
  skip any `"command"` anchor already inside a wrapper the other passes
  captured. Without this, nested `{"arguments":{"command":"..."}}`
  inside a structured envelope would synthesize a duplicate call.
- Anchor walks back past whitespace to find `{`. If the byte before the
  `{` is `:` and the byte before THAT colon is `"`, the object is the
  value of a JSON key (nested envelope we are deliberately ignoring per
  the openai_nested_function_name_without_wrapper test contract). Prose
  colons (preceded by letters/digits) still allow extraction.
- Strict schema match: all keys must be in bash's schema
  (`command`, `working_dir`, `timeout_secs`), and `command` must be a
  string. Rules out prose like `{"command": "show example", "note": "x"}`
  and avoids synthesizing on non-bash tools.
- On match: synthesize a bash tool call and add the object's byte range
  to strip_ranges so the JSON disappears from visible content.

feat(qwen): add looks_like_qwen_target detector for auto-cache enablement

New pub helper `looks_like_qwen_target(base_url, model)` returns true
when a custom provider points at a known Qwen / Alibaba endpoint
(dashscope, aliyun, aliyuncs, dialagram) OR when the model name starts
with `qwen` (strict prefix, case-insensitive).

Detection is the foundation for auto-enabling Alibaba's ephemeral
cache_control markers on custom providers — no user config required.
Wire-up lands in the next commit; this one just ships the predicate +
exhaustive unit tests so the matching policy is locked in before any
production code paths consume it.

Match policy is deliberately conservative:
- Strict `qwen` prefix only — `tongyi-*` and `q3-*` aliases do NOT
  match. Users running those through a custom provider can rename
  their model entry. Better to miss a few aliases than to inject
  markers on a non-qwen backend.
- URL substring match across the four known hosts. Adding more would
  broaden the auto-detect surface; better to start tight and expand
  on signal from real-world reports.

Adding `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` to a non-qwen backend is
benign — OpenAI / Gemini / Groq / DeepSeek silently ignore unknown
JSON fields per the chat-completions spec. Worst case is ~30 bytes
of wasted JSON per request.

explicit non-match list (openai, anthropic, gemini, deepseek, kimi).

custom provider pointed at a known Qwen / Alibaba endpoint (or running a
`qwen-*` model) auto-applies the same `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}`
markers the built-in qwen provider has used since v0.3.x. No config flag,
no opt-in. Users on dialagram, dashscope, aliyun, etc. get ~90% input
token savings on cache hits with zero friction.

New helpers in factory.rs:
- `auto_qwen_cache_transform(base_url)` — body transform that reads the
  `model` field per-request and applies `qwen_body_transform` only when
  `looks_like_qwen_target(base_url, model)` returns true. No-op
  otherwise. Per-request check is necessary because a single custom
  provider may route to multiple models.
- `chain_body_transforms(a, b)` — left-to-right composition so the
  existing `local_thinking_body_transform` (for local llama.cpp/MLX/etc
  servers) composes cleanly with the new cache transform when both
  apply.

Both transforms are no-ops on non-matching requests, so the wire bytes
sent to non-Qwen backends are unchanged.

Before: channels::commands::format_providers filtered the picker to
providers that already had an API key in keys.toml. OpenCode-API,

fix(onboarding): only Enter on the last step commits in quick-jump mode

2026-05-28 bug: a user ran /onboard:provider to inspect models, hit
Enter on the API key field to fetch the model list, then hit Escape to
back out. Their active provider switched silently from dialagram to
openrouter, ~30 config keys were rewritten, and config.toml was
mutated without any visible confirmation prompt.

Root cause: AuthField::Model and AuthField::CustomContextWindow both
called `self.next_step()` on Tab and Down (in addition to Enter).
`next_step()` in quick-jump mode sets `quick_jump_done = true` which on
the next event tick triggers `WizardAction::QuickJumpDone` → which
calls `wizard.apply_config()` → which disables every provider, enables
the selected one, writes default_model + base_url, and rebuilds the
agent service. One unintended Tab while the user was navigating the
model list silently rewrote half the config.

Fix: only Enter commits on the LAST step of each flow.
  - AuthField::Model (built-in providers, last step): Enter commits,
    Tab is now a no-op, BackTab still navigates back to ApiKey.
  - AuthField::CustomContextWindow (custom providers, last step):
    Enter commits, Tab and Down are now no-ops, BackTab/Up still
    navigates back to CustomModel.

Escape behaviour unchanged — already returns WizardAction::Cancel in
quick-jump mode, never commits. The current Escape policy now matches
user expectations: if they didn't explicitly press Enter on the last
step, nothing was written.

8 unit tests in src/tests/onboarding_no_silent_commit_test.rs lock
the policy in:
  - Enter on Model + on CustomContextWindow: commits (positive case)
  - Tab on Model + on CustomContextWindow: no commit
  - Down on Model + on CustomContextWindow: no commit
  - BackTab on Model: no commit
  - Escape on Model in quick_jump: Cancel, never commits

fix(sanitize): strip orphan close tags (</tool_result> etc.) leaking to TUI

2026-05-28 user report: TUI rendered `</tool_result>` lines between
paragraphs of normal prose, e.g.

  </tool_result>
  Now let me verify it compiles and runs clean through clippy:
  </tool_result>
  Clean build, zero warnings. Here's what landed:

Root cause: `strip_xml_tool_calls` only matched MATCHED PAIRS
(`<tool_call>...</tool_call>`). Models routinely emit standalone close
tags because:
  - The opener was already eaten by an earlier extraction pass
  - The model hallucinates close tags without ever opening them
  - The wrapper was a different shape (e.g. `<qwen:tool_call>`) and
    only its content got stripped

The matched-pair regex left the orphan close on the floor where it
rendered as visible chat text.

Changes:
- Extend `TOOL_CALL_BLOCK_RE` to also match `<tool_result>...</tool_result>`,
  `<qwen:tool_call>...</qwen:tool_call>`, `<function_calls>...</function_calls>`
  (these were missing from the matched-pair list too)
- New `ORPHAN_CLOSE_RE`: matches a standalone close tag alone on its
  line (with optional surrounding whitespace) for tool_result,
  tool_call, tool_code, tool_use, invoke, function_calls,
  qwen:tool_call, minimax:tool_call, StartToolCall, parameter, result
- New `INLINE_ORPHAN_CLOSE_RE`: trailing close tag at end of line, for
  the rarer "prose ending with </tag>" shape
- `strip_llm_artifacts` now runs the orphan pass unconditionally
  whenever any orphan-close tag is present, not gated on
  `has_xml_tool_block` (which only fires for matched pairs)

Strict policy preserved: mid-sentence prose mentions like
`"we fixed the </tool_result> bug"` survive because the orphan regex
requires `(?im)^...$` line-boundary anchoring.

- Verbatim user report (two `</tool_result>` orphans between prose)
- Per-tag-name coverage (tool_call, invoke, function_calls,
  qwen:tool_call, tool_use)
- Negative: mid-sentence prose mention survives
- Negative: plain prose round-trips unchanged
- Regression guard: matched pairs still strip correctly with the
  unconditional orphan pass enabled

fix(tui): tok/s footer counts only active streaming time + persists last rate

2026-05-28 user report: the footer's `tok/s` field showed wrong numbers
that decayed as turns dragged on. Root cause: the live rate was
computed as `streaming_output_tokens / processing_started_at.elapsed()`
which counted ALL idle time — tool execution waits, approval prompts,
between-stream network round-trips, compaction delays. A 200 tok/s
burst would visibly decay to "8 tok/s" after a 30-second bash command.

User's spec: count only time when actually outputting tokens (thinking,
completion, tool-call args). Persist the last finalized rate after a
turn ends so the footer keeps showing it until the next turn produces
its first token.

New `StreamingTpsTracker` in `tui::app::state`:
- `advance(now)` — call on every StreamingOutputTokens event.
  Opens a window on first call, extends it on consecutive calls
  within 1.0s of the previous, closes-and-reopens on longer gaps
  (so tool exec / wait time is excluded from the active denominator).
- `active_secs_now(now)` — total active seconds so far this turn.
  Measured between window_start and the LAST token event, never
  extended toward `now` — idle ticks past the last token don't
  inflate the rate.
- `finalize(total_tokens)` — called from complete_response. Stashes
  `total_tokens / active_secs` into `last_tps` and zeroes the
  accumulator. A turn with zero tokens or zero active secs leaves
  the prior `last_tps` untouched (preserves the visible value).
- `last_tps: Option<f64>` — finalized rate from the most recent
  non-empty turn. Persists across idle until the next finalize.

Footer render in `tui::render::input`:
- Live: `streaming_output_tokens / active_secs_now()` during the
  current turn once tokens start arriving.
- Persisted: `last_tps()` when no live turn is active.
- Empty: only when neither has ever been computed.

- Fresh tracker / first advance edge cases
- Consecutive advances extend the same window
- Gap > 1.0s closes the prior window, idle excluded from total
- Three windows separated by gaps each count individually
- Finalize stashes rate + resets accumulator
- Empty turn / zero-active-secs don't clobber prior last_tps
- Idle ticks past last token don't inflate the in-flight window

fix(tui): count reasoning chunks toward live tok/s footer

2026-05-29 user report: a 38-second reasoning-heavy turn on
qwen-3.7-max-thinking showed "65 tok / 3 tok/s" in the footer while
the screen filled with thousands of tokens of visible thinking
content. Only the final ~65 tokens of completion text (the
"Got the full picture..." line) were counted.

Root cause: cli/ui.rs::progress dispatch emitted
TuiEvent::StreamingOutputTokens only on ProgressEvent::StreamingChunk
(final completion text). ProgressEvent::ReasoningChunk just forwarded
to TuiEvent::ReasoningChunk without counting tokens. All of the
model's thinking output went silent on the meter even though the
tracker accumulator was correctly measuring active streaming time.

Fix: mirror the StreamingChunk handler in the ReasoningChunk arm.
Count tokens via the same tiktoken path, send StreamingOutputTokens
before forwarding the ReasoningChunk event. Both completion text AND
thinking now feed the accumulator — matches user's explicit spec:
"should count only when its outputting tokens like thinking or
completion or tool calls whatever".

Tool-call argument tokens still aren't measurable per-chunk (they're
collected internally and emitted as complete ToolCall events at
end-of-stream, so there's no per-delta event to count). That's
acceptable: tool args are usually a small fraction of total output
tokens and the meter remains a model-speed indicator rather than a
strict accountant.
