fix(agent): split FINISHING A TURN into side-effect + analysis, nudge on empty data-fetch close

User saw a turn where 7 tool calls (3 groups) including
`gh pr view 143 --json mergedAt,mergeCommit,title,body,files`
completed successfully, then the model emitted
`finish_reason: stop` with EMPTY delta and the turn ended with
zero text response. The user asked for a PR audit; got 7 tool
calls and silence. Self-heal didn't kick in because there was
no failure — the stream closed cleanly with `[DONE]`.

Root cause: commit e843f405 added a FINISHING A TURN directive
to BRAIN_PREAMBLE telling the model to end with "Done." after
successful tool calls. That directive treated every tool-success
turn the same, but two task shapes need two different closes:

  - SIDE-EFFECT tasks (commit / push / edit / deploy / send):
    the tool call IS the deliverable. "Done." is correct.
  - DATA-FETCH / ANALYSIS tasks (audit / review / compare /
    explain / summarise / check / describe / what does):
    the tool fetched DATA the user expected interpreted.
    The fetched JSON is INPUT to the answer, NOT the answer.
    "Done." is wrong here — the analysis IS the deliverable.

The directive's one-size-fits-all wording made the model close
empty-text on analysis turns. My commit, my regression.

Fix in three coordinated parts:

1. **Brain preamble rewrite.** FINISHING A TURN now explicitly
   carries both task-shape branches. The analysis branch spells
   out that "Done." after `gh pr view` is WRONG when the user
   asked for an audit, and that "Fetched." / "Got it." /
   "Loaded." are NOT analysis answers. The cue is the verb in
   the user's request (audit / review / compare / explain /
   summarise / check / describe / analyse / find / what does /
   how does / why does / tell me / show me / investigate /
   diagnose).

2. **Runtime nudge.** New `is_analysis_intent(user_message)`
   helper in phantom.rs matches the same verb cues at word
   boundary on the clean user message (channel-prefix-aware,
   so `[Channel: Telegram ...]\n<verb>` matches the body, not
   the wrapper). In tool_loop.rs, when a turn ends with empty
   iteration_text AND tool_calls_completed_this_turn > 0 AND
   is_analysis_intent fires, push a one-shot system nudge
   ("you fetched data, now write the analysis using it") and
   continue instead of breaking. One-shot via
   `analysis_nudge_used` budget — if the model still won't
   write text after the nudge, fall through and let the empty
   close stand (better than looping).

3. **Public exposure.** `is_analysis_intent` re-exported from
   `agent::service` so the tool_loop call site (and future
   call sites — e.g. a Telegram handler heuristic) can use it
   without crossing module boundaries.

"report" deliberately omitted from the verb list (too noun-
ambiguous — "the report says X" / "your report failed" would
false-positive). Users wanting that shape can rephrase as
"explain X" or "summarise X".

11 sentinel tests pin:
  - Every verb in the list matches at start / mid-sentence /
    question form (audit, review, compare, explain, summarise,
    summarize, check, describe, analyse, analyze, find, look
    up, look at, what does, how does, why does, what is, what
    are, tell me, show me, investigate, diagnose).
  - Side-effect verbs (commit, push, edit, delete, close, tag,
    create PR, send) do NOT match — they keep their "Done."
    close behaviour from e843f405.
  - Substring false-positives don't trip (auditorium ≠ audit,
    examines ≠ examine, refind ≠ find).
  - Channel-prefix-wrapped messages match on the BODY line
    after the wrapper, not on the bracketed prefix.
  - Empty / whitespace input returns false.
  - The runtime wiring in tool_loop.rs gates on all three
    conditions (empty text + tool success + analysis intent),
    so a refactor that drops any gate fails the test.
  - BRAIN_PREAMBLE carries both task-shape branches plus the
    specific "Done. after gh pr view is WRONG" callout from
    the user incident.

The earlier 5 phantom-post-success-exemption tests from
e843f405 still pass — those guard the SIDE-EFFECT branch and
the runtime exemption that prevents phantom-loop on completed
side-effect turns. The two safeguards now work in tandem: the
exemption stops the loop on side-effect closes, the analysis
nudge fires on empty-fetch closes. Different failure modes,
complementary handling.

fix(baseline): additive merge so new models reach users without manual config edits

User reported that after rebuilding and restarting on the fresh
binary that ships `MiniMax-M3`, the provider/model picker still
showed only `MiniMax-M2.7 / M2.5 / M2.1 / Text-01` — no M3, no
custom-input field for typing it manually. Root cause: their
`~/.opencrabs/config.toml` carried a stale
`[providers.minimax].models = ["MiniMax-M2.7", "MiniMax-M2.5",
"MiniMax-M2.1", "MiniMax-Text-01"]` from an earlier install, and
the wizard's MiniMax branch returned that list verbatim without
ever consulting the binary's hardcoded baseline.

Same shape on the pricing side: the bundled
`usage_pricing.toml.example` ships an updated MiniMax-M3 entry at
$0.6/$2.4/$0.12 per M, but the user's `~/.opencrabs/usage_pricing.toml`
was seeded once at first install and frozen. The seed-on-missing
pattern (PricingConfig::seed_from_example) never refreshes existing
files, so new pricing entries never reach existing users via a
binary upgrade.

Two additive merges:

1. **MiniMax model-list runtime merge.** New helper
   `merge_minimax_baseline(baseline, user_config)` in
   `tui/onboarding/fetch.rs` is now the source of the picker's
   model list for MiniMax. Baseline (the binary's hardcoded
   `["MiniMax-M3", "MiniMax-M2.7", ...]`) goes first so newest
   models land at the top of the picker on every binary upgrade.
   User-only entries (private variants, MiniMax-Text-01) are
   appended at the end so customisations survive. Case-
   insensitive dedup prevents `MiniMax-M3` + `minimax-m3` showing
   as two rows. The merge is in-memory only — config.toml stays
   untouched until the user explicitly saves, so no surprise
   writes to a user-owned file.

2. **Pricing additive on-disk merge.** `PricingConfig::load` now
   parses the bundled example as a baseline and appends any
   `(provider, prefix)` missing from the user's live file. The
   merged file is written back to disk so subsequent loads see
   the new entries without re-running the merge. User rates,
   custom prefixes, and existing entries are NEVER overwritten:
   only `(provider, prefix)` pairs the user doesn't have at all
   get appended.

`serialize_to_toml` was carrying a bug where it dropped the
optional `cache_write_per_m` / `cache_read_per_m` fields on
write-back. Fixed in the same commit — without it the merged M3
entry would have lost its `$0.12/M` cache-read rate the moment
the merge wrote the file back, leaving users on the default 0.1x
input fallback instead of MiniMax's actual list price.

fix(errors): persist agent failures as permanent chat bubbles + actionable wording on TUI and channels

User reported staring at "Thinking + 1 tool call" with no completion
after a 5xx fallback chain exhausted invisibly behind the scenes —
"the agent silently dropped the request." Investigation surfaced two
distinct gaps:

1. **TUI error renders as a 2.5s transient toast then vanishes.**
   `show_error` set `self.error_message` which auto-dismisses at
   state.rs:1814. A user looking away for even a moment missed the
   entire error; after the toast cleared there was zero permanent
   trace in chat history that the turn failed. Looked identical to a
   turn that completed quietly with no text.

2. **Raw `Provider error: API error (502): HTTP 502` leaked verbatim
   to users across every surface** (TUI toast, Telegram, Discord,
   Slack, WhatsApp). Tells the user nothing about what self-heal
   already tried or what they can do next.

Fix in four parts:

A. **Shared `format_user_error(&AgentError) -> String` helper** in
   `brain/agent/error.rs`. Pattern matchers translate the raw error
   into something actionable:
     - HTTP 5xx (502/503/504) → "All fallback providers returned NNN
       within the retry window (likely shared upstream gateway outage).
       Self-heal already tried 4 fallbacks. Wait a minute and retry,
       or switch provider via `/models`."
     - HTTP 429 → rate limit + wait/switch hint
     - HTTP 401/403 → auth failure + pointer to /onboard:provider /
       keys.toml
     - HTTP 4xx other → keeps status + self-heal context + raw
     - `error decoding response body` → stream broke mid-response,
       try again or switch model
     - `Repetition detected` → model loop, terminated, try rephrase
     - `ContextTooLarge` → quote current/limit tokens, /compact hint
     - Unknown → fall back to raw `to_string()` (don't swallow
       diagnostic information)

B. **TUI: persist agent errors as permanent chat bubbles.**
   `state.rs::show_error` now ALSO appends a `DisplayMessage` with
   `role: "error"` to the messages list before setting the transient
   toast. The toast still flashes for 2.5s as a visibility nudge,
   but the chat now also carries a permanent record of the failure
   that survives scrolling, redraws, and subsequent turns. Filters
   out the `"Cancelled"` and `"Press Ctrl+C again to quit"` sentinels
   — those are UI hints, not turn-failure errors.

C. **Render case for `role == "error"`** in `tui/render/chat.rs`.
   Red `❌ Error:` prefix in bold + indented body in lighter red.
   Distinguishable at a glance from `system` (gold), `tool_group`
   (default), `user` (highlighted), or `assistant` (no prefix).

D. **All four channel handlers route through the helper.** Telegram,
   Discord, Slack, WhatsApp previously formatted as `format!("Error:
   {}", e)`, leaking the raw provider error. Now: `format!("❌ Error\n\n{}",
   crate::brain::agent::format_user_error(&e))`. Consistent wording
   across every surface so a user moving between TUI and channel
   sees the same failure messages.

9 sentinel tests pin the wording per failure shape:
  - 502/503/504 produce the fallback-exhausted message with status
    code, fallback mention, and /models pointer
  - 429 produces rate-limit wording without leaking `HTTP 429`
  - 401/403 produce auth failure + key fix path
  - stream-broken / repetition-loop / context-too-large each produce
    their specific messages with recovery hints
  - Unknown errors fall back to raw text (don't swallow diagnostics)
  - Unknown 4xx codes surface the status + raw body so they stay
    debuggable

The underlying self-heal behaviour is unchanged — this commit is
purely about surfacing what self-heal already does to the user
clearly, on every surface, permanently in chat history. Future
work on the 5xx fallback chain dedup-by-host (4 fallbacks tried
on 4 sub-providers that share a gateway count as 1 real attempt,
not 4) is still open as a separate fix.

fix(prompt): rewrite FINISHING A TURN to require acknowledgement, never silent close

[skip ci]

User reported the agent dropping requests across "basically all
requests" — running tool calls and ending the turn with zero text.
Looked identical to a silent crash to the user.

Root cause: my own commit e843f405 added a FINISHING A TURN
directive worded as "ONE short acknowledgement line and stop"
with bare-word examples like `"Done."` / `"Pushed."`. The model
read "stop" + the minimalist examples as "produce no text at
all" and started emitting `finish_reason: stop` with empty delta
on every side-effect turn. The "one line" framing combined with
"and stop" was too easy to interpret as a permission to skip the
acknowledgement entirely.

Rewritten directive flips the framing:

- Header changed from "stop cleanly, do not narrate forever" to
  "always acknowledge clearly, never disappear silently".
- Explicit forbidding of empty closes: "Empty completions
  (`finish_reason: stop` with no content) look identical to silent
  crashes from the user's side — never do that."
- Side-effect examples now show real specifics ("Committed as
  7256f666 — 11 files changed", "Edited tool_loop.rs:490, added
  the display_text_override fallback") instead of bare-word
  closers that the model copied as the entire response.
- "DO produce the acknowledgement. The user wants the
  confirmation; do NOT omit it. An empty close is the worst
  possible outcome" added explicitly.
- Closing rule pins both task shapes together: "never end with
  empty content. If you've decided you have nothing to add
  beyond what the tool already showed, the right minimum is
  still one concrete sentence naming WHAT you did with the
  specifics — never zero text, never a bare 'Done.' with no
  context."

The anti-loop guidance is preserved (no verification re-runs,
no five-restatement boilerplate, no "I have successfully…"
corporate prefix) — those rules were correct, only the "stop"
framing was wrong.

Sentinel test `brain_preamble_directs_one_line_completion`
renamed to `brain_preamble_directs_clear_acknowledgement_not_silent_close`
and rewritten to pin the new wording:
  - "never disappear silently" header
  - "never end with empty content" rule
  - "Empty completions" failure-mode callout
  - Verification-re-run forbid (preserved from original)

The runtime post-success exemption from e843f405 stays unchanged
— that handles the phantom-loop case (8+ retries on a clean
commit+push) by gating the detector on
`tool_calls_completed_this_turn`. Both layers now work in
tandem: the runtime guard kills the loop, the directive ensures
the model still produces a real acknowledgement instead of
trading the loop for empty text.

16 sentinel tests across the two suites still pass. The
empty-completion bug was reported pervasively ("happening all
the time on basically all requests") so this needs to ship
ASAP — the trade-off is intentional: better to occasionally
re-acknowledge than to systematically drop the answer.

fix(tui): unescape literal \n sequences in tool-arg display

User reported a qwen Edit tool call rendering with literal `\n` and
horizontal-soup wrapping — `chars. Cap is 40. Shorten it.",\n
opt,\n  opt.len()\n  )));\n  }\n  if !seen.insert(opt.as_str())` —
all on one wrapped line.

Root cause: models sometimes emit tool args where multi-line
payloads use the two-char sequence `\n` (literal backslash + n)
instead of an actual newline byte. The tool-arg renderer at
`render_tool_group` did `s.lines().map(...)` to split for display,
but `lines()` only catches real `\n` bytes. When the input has
literal escapes, the whole payload becomes one logical line that
ratatui then wraps at the content width — visible as a run-together
mess with `\n` separators showing as text.

Fix: new `unescape_display_string(&str) -> String` helper translates
the common JSON-shape escapes back to their textual form before
the line split:

  \n  → actual newline (so lines() splits)
  \t  → 4 spaces (real tabs render unpredictably in ratatui)
  \r  → dropped (no stray control chars on unix)
  \"  → "
  \\  → \
  other backslash sequences → passed through verbatim

Conservative: only the sequences that DEFINITELY break the
line-by-line display. JSON-only escapes (`\u00XX`, `\/`) and
anything else stays untouched. Fast path skips the work when the
string contains no backslashes at all (the common case).

10 sentinel tests pin every translation, including the
trailing-backslash edge case (no panic on `"foo\"`), the
unknown-escape passthrough (`\x20` stays as `\x20`), the empty
input, and an end-to-end reproduction of the exact failure mode
from the screenshot — `chars. Cap is 40. Shorten it.",\n opt,\n
opt.len()\n )));\n }\n if !seen.insert(opt.as_str())` must split
to ≥ 5 display lines and carry zero literal `\n` afterward.

This is purely a display-layer fix — the underlying tool args
remain untouched in the tool execution path. The model can still
emit literal escapes; the user just sees them rendered correctly
in the chat preview instead of as a wrapped soup.

fix(rtk): expand RTK_SUPPORTED_COMMANDS with sysadmin family + bundle filter template

RTK-savings audit (2026-06-01) compared our 35.8% reduction against
fast-rlm's 69.9% on similar volume. The gap was mostly workload
mix (their session was sysadmin-heavy, ours was build-heavy), but
TWO real integration gaps surfaced:

1. **Missing sysadmin commands** in `RTK_SUPPORTED_COMMANDS`. The
   agent's `ps` / `top` / `lsof` / `netstat` / `ss` / `journalctl` /
   `dmesg` / `dig` / `nslookup` / `host` / `traceroute` invocations
   were bypassing RTK entirely, leaking the verbose output (process
   table, socket list, log streams, DNS resolution chain) at full
   size. fast-rlm's #1 RTK win is `ps auxww` at 97.9% compression
   — we got zero from `ps` because it wasn't in the list.

   Added 11 commands covering process inspection, log streams,
   network sockets, and DNS tooling. Each one has verbose default
   output where RTK's built-in filters or a TOML rule can drop
   80-98% before the model sees it.

2. **No bundled TOML filter rules**. fast-rlm's top 4 commands by
   savings are all `rtk:toml <cmd>` — they wrote `~/.rtk/*.toml`
   rules with custom patterns. We shipped no template, so users
   either invent their own from scratch (rare) or get only RTK's
   built-in filters.

   Bundled `rtk_filters.toml.example` at the repo root with safe
   starter rules for the dev-workflow shape:
     - `ps-aux-compact` — drops `_uucp`/`_appstore`/etc system
       daemons, caps at 80 lines
     - `lsof-i-compact` — caps at 60 lines, drops empty headers
     - `netstat-compact` — drops loopback noise, caps at 60
     - `journalctl-recent` / `dmesg-recent` — cap log streams at
       most recent 200 lines
     - `git-log-oneline-cap` — caps at 30 commits when no -n/limit
     - `git-diff-cap` — caps full-diff output at 500 lines
     - `gh-pr-list-cap` — caps at 200 lines (~20 PRs in JSON)
     - `dig-answer-only` — drops authority + additional sections

   Each rule is conservative — strips obvious noise but doesn't
   reorder or drop content the agent might need. Activation is
   manual for now: `cp rtk_filters.toml.example ~/.rtk/filters.toml
   && rtk trust`. Auto-seed to `~/.opencrabs/rtk_filters.toml` and
   /onboard-driven activation are deferred to a follow-up.

Dropped from the original plan: the "aggregate breakdown by first
two tokens" item. Re-investigation showed our `format_report` in
`rtk::tracker` already groups by first token only, and the
multi-row breakdown the user sees in chat comes from RTK's own
`rtk gain` command (run via tokio::Command at messaging.rs:742).
RTK's grouping is RTK's responsibility — `rtk gain --help` has no
prefix-aggregation flag, and parsing+re-aggregating its text output
would be fragile.

6 sentinel tests pin:
  - All 11 new sysadmin commands are in the supported list
  - The pre-existing build-workflow commands (git, gh, cargo, grep,
    find, ls, tree, curl, docker, kubectl) stay in the list — a
    refactor that drops them would regress the heaviest existing
    wins (99.8% on cargo test --all-features)
  - RTK meta-commands (rtk, sudo, ssh, vim, less, python) remain
    OFF the supported list — adding them would either recurse
    forever (rtk rtk ...) or break interactive sessions
  - `rtk_filters.toml.example` is present at repo root so the
    documented `cp` workflow actually works

The audit also surfaced two larger items intentionally deferred:
  - Routing `read_file` through `rtk read` (fast-rlm: 300 calls,
    635K saved at 51%) — needs a tool-level RTK shim, not just a
    bash rewrite hook
  - Auto-seed of the bundled filter file with /onboard activation
    — UX work, separate from the integration fix this commit ships

fix(phantom): catch pronounless `Need to X` + bare-gerund openers [skip ci]

Two narration shapes were slipping past the phantom-tool-intent
detector and reaching the user without a tool call.

1. Pronounless deferment — `Need to read the X to do Y.` — the
   `i need to X` entries only matched when the explicit pronoun was
   present, but terser model outputs drop the leading `I`. Adds the 28
   pronounless `need to <verb>` variants for EN and the 15 telegraphic
   `besoin de <verb>` variants for FR. `have to` / `must` / `should`
   without the pronoun are deliberately NOT added — they false-positive
   on prose like `you should check the docs`. RU already shipped the
   pronounless `нужно X` forms; ES / PT conjugate first-person verbs
   without a separate pronoun, so no parallel change is needed.

2. Bare-gerund sentence opener — `Reading the current state of the
   affected files to make precise edits.` — no `let me` / `I'll` /
   `now` anchor was present, so nothing in `intent_phrases` matched.
   Adds `<gerund>+<determiner>` bigrams (`reading the`,
   `checking the`, `examining the`, `inspecting the`, `verifying the`,
   `reviewing the`, `investigating the`, `exploring the`,
   `searching the`, `looking at the`, etc.) Substring matching is safe
   here because the detector only fires on the prose lead-in of a
   no-tool-call turn — in agent output, narrating the *act* of reading
   instead of reporting findings is itself the symptom we want to
   catch.

New regression file `src/tests/phantom_pronoun_drop_test.rs` pins
both leaked sentences verbatim plus per-verb spot checks for both
shapes, so a future refactor of the intent_phrases list can't
silently drop them and re-open the gap.

fix(claude-cli): learn resolved model version from the CLI, stop hardcoding it [skip ci]

The footer showed Opus 4.7 after Anthropic shipped 4.8 because the
provider's alias to version table was hardcoded (default_for_alias mapped
opus to opus-4-7). The CLI already resolves the bare alias to the live
release and reports it back in every message_start, but we only logged a
WARN about the drift and kept advertising the stale version.

Now the provider learns from the CLI and persists what it learns, so the
version tracks Anthropic's releases automatically with zero hand-editing:

- Added a process-wide learned alias map backed by
  ~/.opencrabs/claude_cli_models.json. It is loaded on first use and
  rewritten only when a value actually changes, so the steady state is
  zero disk IO.
- default_for_alias now prefers the learned version and falls back to a
  build-time seed only on a fresh install before any turn has run. The
  pure seed table lives in seed_for_alias.
- record_observed_model maps the CLI-reported id back to its bare alias
  and records the normalized version. It replaces the old WARN-only
  warn_if_model_drifted on both the SSE and assistant-message paths.
- The SSE message_start model is now normalized to the short form
  (claude-opus-4-8 becomes opus-4-8) so display, DB writeback, and pricing
  all see one consistent, current value.
- The TUI refreshes the in-memory session model override from the turn's
  response model, so the footer updates to the new version immediately
  rather than only after a restart. The label prettifier already renders
  any opus-X-Y as Opus X.Y, so no display table needed touching.
- Tests assert the seed fallbacks via the pure seed_for_alias, that a
  learned version overrides the seed, and that record_alias is idempotent.
  Cache-mutating tests are serialized and start from a clean in-memory map
  (disk is never touched under cfg(test)).

fix(fallback): wrap per-session providers in FallbackProvider so /models swaps keep cascade coverage [skip ci]

Default-config sessions cascaded gracefully for months — the global
self.provider is wrapped in FallbackProvider at construction in
factory.rs:451 and FallbackProvider::stream() transparently iterates
the chain on retryable errors (5xx, 429, timeouts, model-not-found).

Sessions that swapped via /models, restored a saved provider_name,
or got sticky-promoted in the tool loop lost that coverage entirely.
swap_provider_for_session stored whatever raw Arc<dyn Provider> the
caller produced via create_provider_by_name — never a FallbackProvider
wrapper. From that point on the session's only safety net was the
manual 5xx fallback loop in tool_loop.rs.

Logs 2026-06-02 02:33:25-29 captured the resulting double failure:

  5xx retry attempt 1/3 after: API error (530)
  dialagram streaming request: model=qwen-3.7-plus-preview
  ...3 retries, all 530...
  All 3 5xx retries failed — checking for fallback provider
  5xx fallback trying 'zhipu/glm-5-turbo'
    stream_complete: provider 'dialagram' does not support model
      'glm-5-turbo' — remapping to 'qwen-3.7-plus-preview'
    dialagram streaming request: model=qwen-3.7-plus-preview  ← still dialagram
  5xx fallback trying 'opencode-kimi/kimi-k2.6'
    dialagram streaming request: model=qwen-3.7-plus-preview  ← still dialagram
  ...5 fallbacks total, all of them re-hitting dialagram in ~4s...

Root cause was architectural: the swapped session never had a
FallbackProvider in front of dialagram, so the inner cascade
couldn't fire. The manual loop in tool_loop.rs also has its own
no-swap bug but fixing that in isolation only papers over the
underlying coverage gap — the correct fix is restoring the
invariant that every active provider in the agent service is a
fallback chain.

Changes:

- New Provider trait method `is_fallback_chain(&self) -> bool`
  defaulting to false. FallbackProvider overrides to true. Lets
  callers detect an already-wrapped provider and avoid double-
  wrapping (which would grow a nested onion on every re-swap).

- swap_provider_for_session now wraps the new provider in
  FallbackProvider::new(new_provider, fallbacks_filtered_to_exclude_self)
  unless either (a) it's already a fallback chain or (b) the
  fallback list is empty (or all candidates collide with the new
  primary's name). The self-name filter prevents a chain from
  cascading to itself — if the user picks `dialagram` as primary
  and dialagram is also in the configured fallback list, the
  duplicate would mean the first cascade hop hits the same dead
  endpoint.

- Test-only setter set_fallback_providers_for_test mutates the
  field after construction so tests can verify the wrap behaviour
  without rebuilding the entire Config tree.

Default-config sessions are unaffected — their global provider was
already FallbackProvider-wrapped, so is_fallback_chain() returns
true and swap_provider_for_session stores them as-is on session
restore.

Regression coverage in src/tests/session_provider_wrap_test.rs:
six tests pinning (1) raw providers get wrapped when fallbacks are
configured, (2) the user-facing name survives the wrap (footers /
session persistence stay on the chosen provider), (3) no wrap
happens when no fallbacks are configured, (4) Arc::ptr_eq proves no
double-wrapping when the input is already a FallbackProvider, (5)
self-name filtering still leaves enough fallbacks to wrap, (6)
the "only fallback is self" edge case falls through to the no-wrap
path instead of building a pointless empty FallbackProvider.

fix(tok/s): provider-reported tokens / active streaming time, shared by TUI + channels [skip ci]

Two separate tok/s counters were both producing wrong numbers:

- TUI footer ran tiktoken (cl100k_base) over each StreamingChunk /
  ReasoningChunk and divided by the active-streaming window from
  StreamingTpsTracker. Three compounding bugs on non-OpenAI models:
  (1) cl100k_base over-counts Qwen/Kimi/GLM bytes by 1.5-2× because
  their real tokenizers split bytes very differently; (2) tool-use
  block deltas weren't counted even though they consume output
  tokens on the provider's bill; (3) the window measured the burst
  rate of a single batched SSE chunk (200 tokens delivered in 0.3s
  → 666 tok/s) rather than the model's sustained generation rate.
  Combined, users saw 700-800 tok/s for providers that genuinely
  run ~100 tok/s.

- Channel footer (added in 17aa6abb) divided provider-reported
  output_tokens by full-turn wall-clock — including every bash
  exec, file read, approval prompt, and DB persistence. This one
  systematically *under*-reported on tool-heavy turns and disagreed
  with whatever the TUI showed for the same turn.

The fix unifies both displays around a single computation:

  tokens_per_second = sum_of_provider_output_tokens
                    / sum_of_per_iteration_active_streaming_secs

Numerator is the provider's authoritative output_tokens — no
tokenizer guesswork, accurate across providers and models.

Denominator is `streaming_active_secs`, a new field on LLMResponse
populated by stream_complete in helpers.rs. Each iteration's value
is the wall time between the first and last content delta of that
iteration, with idle gaps >1s excluded (so tool execution, approval
waits, DB persistence, and between-iteration round-trips are all
left out — matching the IDLE_GAP_SECS=1.0 invariant of the existing
StreamingTpsTracker so the two share a mental model).

Plumbing:

- types.rs adds `streaming_active_secs: Option<f64>` to LLMResponse
  with #[serde(default)] for deserialisation. Non-streaming
  construction sites (anthropic.rs, gemini.rs, custom_openai_*.rs,
  claude_cli.rs, codex_cli.rs, opencode_cli.rs, tool_loop.rs
  synthesis path, test mocks) set it to None.

- helpers.rs accumulates active-streaming time per content delta
  (text, reasoning, thinking, tool-use JSON) using the same window
  algorithm as StreamingTpsTracker — first delta opens the window,
  delta arriving >1s after the previous one closes the current
  window and opens a new one, finalize() sums all closed windows
  plus the open one's (last - start). Returns None when no delta
  arrived so the footer shows nothing rather than NaN.

- tool_loop.rs aggregates the per-iteration values into
  `total_streaming_active_secs` and divides total_output_tokens by
  it instead of `turn_start.elapsed()`. The turn_start variable is
  removed (its only consumer was this calculation).

- TUI's StreamingTpsTracker::finalize gains an `authoritative:
  Option<f64>` parameter. When the agent service's computed tok/s
  is present, it overrides the local tiktoken estimate so the TUI
  footer matches the channel footer for the same turn. CLI providers
  and any path that doesn't measure active streaming time still fall
  back to the local estimate (so the footer doesn't go blank).
  Non-finite values (NaN, Infinity) defensively fall back too —
  guards against any future divide-by-zero degenerate turn.

- messaging.rs `complete_response(response)` passes
  `response.tokens_per_second` into finalize_tps.

Regression coverage:

- streaming_active_secs_test.rs (new): an mpsc-backed timing-mock
  provider drives `stream_complete` with controllable inter-delta
  delays. Test 1 pins that 4 chunks with 100ms gaps produce ~0.3s
  active_secs (3 gaps × 100ms, generous scheduler slop). Test 2
  pins that a 1.2s gap between two chunks is correctly excluded —
  the whole point of the idle-gap filter is so a slow tool call
  between bursts can't collapse the displayed rate.

- streaming_tps_accumulator_test.rs: 3 new tests for the
  authoritative-override path on finalize — uses the value when
  Some, falls back to local when None, falls back when NaN.

- 9 existing tests still green for the wider streaming flow.

feat(subagent): per-call provider/model override on spawn/resume/team_create (#152) [skip ci]

Reopens the use case from #152. The requester wanted to run a skill
that orchestrates multiple sub-agents with different models per step
(plan with GLM, code with Deepseek, review with GLM, fix with
MiniMax). The existing config.agent.subagent_provider / subagent_model
keys are a GLOBAL setting — every spawned sub-agent in the session
uses the same routing — so a single skill run can't ask for different
models per step. The previous docs-only fix (bf62682b) clarified the
config keys but didn't address the orchestration shape, and closing
the issue was wrong.

This commit adds an optional per-call override that wins over both
the config keys and parent inheritance. Precedence is now:

  per-call params  >  config.agent.subagent_*  >  parent provider

Surface:

- spawn_agent schema gains optional `provider` and `model` string
  params. Schema description spells out the precedence rule so the
  LLM knows when to use which level.
- resume_agent gains the same two params — escalating a resumed
  agent to a stronger model than the original spawn is a natural
  pattern (cheap draft, expensive fix-up).
- team_create's per-member items array gains `provider` and `model`
  too, resolved INSIDE the loop so a single team_create call can
  spawn members on different models simultaneously (the canonical
  skill shape from the issue).

Implementation:

- spawn.rs / resume.rs read the override from input, trim, treat
  empty string as unset (defends against the LLM passing `""` for
  an absent optional field), then chain with the config default via
  Option::or_else. The combined effective_provider_name is passed
  to create_provider_by_name; on failure the existing
  fallback-to-parent path runs unchanged so a typo in a skill file
  can't break the spawn. The log line distinguishes per-call vs
  config source so users can confirm which level took effect.
- team/create.rs moves the provider/model resolution from
  function-scope (one shared override) to loop-scope (one per
  member), so the team_create({ agents: [...] }) call can mix
  per-member routes in a single call.

README section "Subagent Provider and Model" rewritten to lead with
the three-tier precedence and include a worked example of the
multi-model skill workflow from the issue. config.toml.example
already documents the [agent] keys; no change needed there.

Regression coverage:

- subagent_tool_description_test.rs gains three schema tests pinning
  that spawn_agent / resume_agent each expose optional provider+model,
  and that team_create's per-agent item schema does the same. None of
  the new params are marked required (config + inheritance fallbacks
  remain valid). The earlier team_create description test is relaxed

- 7 sentinel tests green; full strict clippy gate clean.

- `has_bare_name_args_signal(text)`: cheap precondition check, two
  substring tests. Lets the host extractor short-circuit the
  common case (no bare-tool-call shape present) before paying for
  the full scan.

- `extract_bare_name_args_calls(text, existing_strip_ranges,
  existing_calls)`: returns matches in source order. Each match
  carries the (name, args, strip_start, strip_end) plus an
  `already_in_existing` flag so the host can strip without re-
  dispatching when the structured path already executed the same
  call.

Five strict checks must hold for a match to be returned: (1)
`"name"` must be the FIRST key of a fresh JSON object (preceded by
`{` plus optional whitespace), (2) the balanced-brace JSON parses,
(3) `name` is a string, (4) `arguments` is an object (or a JSON-
stringified object — some providers double-encode), (5) the `name`
is in `KNOWN_TOOL_NAMES`. The KNOWN_TOOL_NAMES gate (now made
pub(crate)) is what protects against false-positives on prose JSON
like `{"name": "Adolfo", "arguments": {...}}` — that shape doesn't
dispatch because "Adolfo" isn't a known tool.

Pass 1.9 runs AFTER every marker-based pass for a reason. Anchors
inside wrappers like `<tool_call>{"name":...,"arguments":...}</tool_call>`
would otherwise be matched FIRST, stripping the inner JSON before
the wrapper pass could find anything between its tags. Running last
means those ranges are already in `strip_ranges`, so the in-range
skip check correctly ignores anchors that belong to a marker-claimed
wrapper.

fix(telegram): rotate marathon-bucket rolling status through project-author quip pool [skip ci]

2026-06-03: a user-visible status message froze at
"⚙️ Marathon mode — still on: <preview>" for 3+ minutes straight on
a slow reasoning turn. The bot then occasionally vanished and
re-appeared with the same string — the elapsed counter advanced
but the line carried no new signal.

Root cause: `pre_tool_rolling` had only four elapsed-time buckets
(5s / 15s / 30s / 60s). Past 60s the lead phrase locked on
"Marathon mode — still on" forever; the only varying element was
the trailing elapsed time the caller appended. Combined with a
turn where `thinking_excerpt` returned None (no live reasoning
sentence to surface — the provider didn't ship ReasoningDelta
events for this turn), the static marathon line was the only thing
the user saw. From their seat the bot looked dead.

Fix: restore the project-author-original `TOOL_STATUS_QUIPS` pool
(15 entries, introduced verbatim in commit `f5b5de1a` and stable
across every commit that touched it before removal in `512bf002`).
Past 60s the marathon bucket now rotates through the pool every
~15 seconds — 15 entries × 15s = full cycle every 3m 45s, so a
multi-minute marathon visibly evolves through several quips
instead of locking on a single line.

Two structural changes:

- New module `src/channels/telegram/rolling_status_quips.rs`
  holds the 15-entry slice plus `rotating_quip(elapsed_secs)`. NOT
  inlined into handler.rs (already 3000+ lines; the previous round
  of feedback was explicit that helpers go in their own file).

- `pre_tool_rolling` collapses the four-bucket structure to three
  preview-anchored buckets (5s / 15s / 30s) and one marathon bucket
  (60s+). The marathon bucket drops the preview — the quips are
  self-contained sentences, and after 60s a fifth "still on:
  <preview>" repetition adds no information. The preview-anchored
  buckets stay silent without a preview; the marathon bucket fires
  even without one so a `resume_session` reconnect or a no-preview
  turn doesn't go completely dark past 60s.

Memory rule `feedback_no_invented_filler.md` was removed in the
same session by user direction. Restoring the project-author quips
verbatim doesn't violate any remaining rule — these are not
invented filler, they're the canonical pool the bot has shipped
under since the rolling-status feature was first introduced.

fix(phantom): re-engage self-heal on forward intent after a successful tool call [skip ci]

2026-06-03: a turn ran one `bash: git branch --show-current` then
emitted

  "Good, on main. Let me dig into the delete invitation endpoint,
   the email send path, and the invite flow to find the bugs."

and silently closed without ever dispatching the three promised
investigations. The phantom-eligibility gate (added in e843f405 to
stop false-positives on completion acks like `Pushed.` / `On main.`
after a successful commit+push) read:

  let phantom_eligible = !is_cli_provider
      && tool_calls_completed_this_turn == 0;

so once ANY tool call had succeeded in a turn, phantom detection
was disabled for the rest of the turn — including for clearly
forward-looking intent. The exemption was correctly designed for
PAST-tense summaries but overshooting on FUTURE-promised work.

Fix: split the eligibility into a two-regime gate. New sister
function `has_forward_intent_post_success` mirrors
`has_phantom_tool_intent_no_tools` but drops the past-tense
completion-claim branch. The gate becomes:

  let phantom_eligible = !is_cli_provider
      && (tool_calls_completed_this_turn == 0
          || super::phantom::has_forward_intent_post_success(&iteration_text));

So:

- Zero tool calls this turn → standard phantom check (unchanged).
- ≥1 tool call this turn AND the iteration text is a pure
  completion ack (`Pushed.` / `Committed.` / `On main.`) → phantom
  stays exempt (the original e843f405 protection).
- ≥1 tool call this turn AND the iteration text carries a forward-
  looking intent phrase from the curated `intent_phrases` list
  (`let me dig`, `let me read`, `let me check`, `i'll X`, `let's
  X`, `need to X`, …) → phantom re-engages and self-heal nudges
  the model to actually do the dig.

The curated `intent_phrases` list deliberately excludes
presentation/communication verbs (`let me know`, `let me show`,
`let me explain`, `let me tell`) so legitimate after-completion
phrasings stay quiet. `prose_lead_in` is applied so structural
content past the lead-in (tables, code blocks, bullet lists,
commit-message bodies) can't re-trigger the e843f405 original false
positive where a commit message containing `Let me X` inside its
body fired the detector after a successful push.

Six new tests in `phantom_post_success_exemption_test.rs`:

- The exact 2026-06-03 leak text triggers
  `has_forward_intent_post_success`.
- Pure completion acks (`Pushed.`, `Committed.`, `Done. On main.`,
  `Updated the file. Bumped the version.`) do NOT trigger it.
- Presentation-verb phrasings (`Let me know …`, `Let me show …`,
  `I'll explain …`, `Let me tell …`) do NOT trigger it.
- A structural table containing `let me check` / `let me dig` past
  a `Pushed and tagged.` lead-in does NOT trigger it (prose-lead-
  in filter preserved).
- The broader `has_phantom_tool_intent_no_tools` still fires on the
  same forward intent in the zero-tool-call regime.
- Source-level guard pinning that the eligibility gate now calls
  `has_forward_intent_post_success`, so a future "simplification"
  refactor that drops the disjunction back to the original single-
  condition form fails this test rather than silently re-opening
  the drop.

Existing `phantom_eligible_gate_replaces_naked_is_cli_provider_check`
sentinel updated to assert the new disjunction shape instead of the
original single-condition form.

* fix(team): add missing mark_awaiting_input in team agent spawn loop

Team-created agents never called mark_awaiting_input after a round,
so wait_agent could never observe round-boundary progress — it kept
polling until timeout before reporting 'still running'.

This mirrors the pattern in spawn.rs: after update_output, flip to

instead of blocking on task-join semantics.

* fix(resume): mirror mark_awaiting_input fix in resume_agent loop [skip ci]

`resume.rs` has the same bug team/create.rs had before this PR:
after `manager.update_output()` it never flips to `AwaitingInput`,
so `wait_agent` on a resumed agent has no way to observe round-
boundary progress — it polls until timeout, always reporting
"still running" even though the agent has produced output and is
waiting for follow-up input.

Sister fix to the one already in this PR for team_create, mirroring
the spawn.rs pattern verbatim: `update_output` → `mark_awaiting_input`
→ tracing log, plus the same "cancelled while waiting for input"
log on the cancel arm of the tokio::select.

All three callers (`spawn`, `team/create`, `resume`) now have the
same shape, so a future refactor to the state machine catches them
together rather than leaving resume as the lone outlier.

feat(plan): add import operation — load pre-defined plan from JSON file (#160)

* feat(plan): add import operation — load pre-defined plan from JSON file

Adds an 'import' operation to the plan tool that reads a PlanDocument JSON file
from disk, reassigns UUIDs (plan + all tasks), remaps dependency references,
resets task execution state, and replaces the current session plan.

Security: validates absolute path, checks for symlinks in path components,
enforces 10MB file size limit.

Approval: import requires user approval (same as finalize) since it replaces
the active plan.

* feat(plan): add sample plan JSON and import test

- Add sample-coding-plan.json with 7 tasks based on the coding process
- Add test_import_sample_plan that exercises PlanTool import end-to-end
- Test writes sample JSON to temp file, calls import, verifies output

* fix(plan): target-only symlink check + error on orphan deps + valid sample plan + tests moved to src/tests [skip ci]

Five concrete problems with the PR as submitted:

1. **`test_import_sample_plan` failed on macOS.** The symlink check
   walked every ancestor of the import path:

       for ancestor in import_path.ancestors() {
           if ancestor.exists() {
               let meta = std::fs::symlink_metadata(ancestor)...;
               if meta.is_symlink() {
                   return Err("Import path contains a symlink");
               }
           }
       }

   On macOS `/var` is a system-level symlink to `/private/var` and
   `TempDir::new()` lives under `/var/folders/...`. Every test path
   includes a symlinked ancestor the user doesn't control, so the
   author's own integration test failed locally — only passing on
   Linux CI because `/tmp` is usually a real directory there. Same
   problem hits any Linux distro with `usrmerge` (`/bin` →
   `/usr/bin`).

   Fixed by checking only the TARGET file (`import_path` itself)
   for being a symlink. That matches the existing
   `validate_plan_file_path` pattern in this same file and the
   actual threat model (a malicious symlink AT the import location
   redirecting the read elsewhere).

2. **Orphan dependency UUIDs were silently dropped.** The UUID
   remap loop was:

       task.dependencies = task.dependencies.iter()
           .filter_map(|old| old_to_new.get(old).copied())
           .collect();

   A dependency referencing a UUID not present in the imported task
   set is a malformed plan, but `filter_map` quietly discarded such
   refs. The import succeeded, the missing dep was dropped, and the
   executor would happily run a task whose declared upstream wasn't
   actually required. Replaced with an explicit loop that errors
   with the offending task title, order, and UUID so the user
   fixes the JSON instead of silently shipping a broken plan.

3. **Sample plan JSON did not deserialise.** The bundled
   `sample-coding-plan.json` had `"task_type": "research"` etc.
   (lowercase) but `TaskType` is serde-default PascalCase, so
   parse errored with "unknown variant `research`". The file was
   also missing several required `PlanDocument` and `PlanTask`
   fields (`session_id`, `status`, `approved_at`, `complexity`,
   `acceptance_criteria`, `notes`, `completed_at`). Rewrote the
   fixture to deserialise cleanly. Sample now matches the actual
   `PlanTask` struct shape, so `test_import_sample_plan` actually
   exercises the code path the PR was meant to test.

4. **`#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` block inside
   `plan_tool_security_tests.rs` violated the project test rule.**
   Project convention: every test is a top-level file under
   `src/tests/` registered in `tests/mod.rs`, no inline `mod tests`
   blocks anywhere else in the tree. Moved the entire file (the
   pre-existing 16 tests authored by the project owner PLUS the
   PR's new import test PLUS the four new error-path tests below)
   to `src/tests/plan_tool_test.rs`. Items the tests reach
   (`validate_plan_file_path`, `validate_string`,
   `MAX_PLAN_FILE_SIZE`, `MAX_TITLE_LENGTH`,
   `MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH`, `MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH`,
   `default_complexity`) made `pub(crate)` in `plan_tool.rs` so
   the relocated file can reach them from outside the module. The
   `mod plan_tool_security_tests;` declaration at the bottom of
   `plan_tool.rs` removed; `plan_tool_security_tests.rs` deleted.

5. **Missing test coverage.** The PR shipped one happy-path test.
   Added four error-path tests for the hardening the PR claimed
   but didn't verify:

   - `import_rejects_file_over_size_cap` — writes 10 MB + 1 byte,
     asserts the size check fires before parse so a malicious or
     runaway plan file can't blow up memory on `read_to_string`.
   - `import_rejects_invalid_json` — malformed JSON returns
     `Invalid plan JSON: ...` rather than panicking.
   - `import_rejects_orphan_dependency_uuid` — verifies fix #2
     above: a dep UUID that isn't in the task set errors with
     `depends on unknown task id ...` instead of silently
     dropping the ref.
   - `import_rejects_symlink_at_target` (unix-only) — creates an
     actual symlink at the import target and asserts the check
     still fires on the target itself, so fix #1 didn't accidentally
     drop the legitimate threat-model defence.

   All five integration tests pass on macOS now; previously the
   one in the PR didn't.

fix(evolve): check user-level systemd units when scheduling restart

OpenCrabs is commonly installed as a user-level systemd service via
install_systemd_service() (onboarding/config.rs), which writes to
~/.config/systemd/user/ and uses systemctl --user enable/start.

The evolve tool's pre-flight count_matching_systemd_units() only
queried system-level systemd units (no --user flag), so when OpenCrabs
runs as a user service it found 0 matching units -> NoUnitsMatched ->
no restart was scheduled. The new binary was downloaded and swapped on
disk, but the running daemons continued on the old deleted inode.

Changes:
- build_systemd_restart_command(pid, user) -- new user: bool param
  injects --user into the systemd-run restart command
- count_matching_systemd_units(pattern, user) -- new user: bool param
  adds --user to the systemctl list-units query
- evolve_via_binary_download now tries user-level units when
  system-level returns 0; if found, schedules restart with --user
- User-facing NoUnitsMatched and SpawnFailed messages mention both
  --user restart and system-level restart as manual options
- Tests: added restart_command_user_level_includes_user_flag,
  no_units_matched_message_mentions_user_flag,
  spawn_failed_message_mentions_user_flag; updated existing
  calls to pass explicit user=false

- evolve_falls_back_to_user_level_when_system_level_empty: ensures the
  fallback to count_matching_systemd_units(pattern, true) stays in place

`is_processing`, `processing_started_at`, `streaming_output_tokens`,
`last_input_tokens`, `display_token_count`, `tps_tracker`. Twenty
`TuiEvent` handlers in `state.rs` gate on
`is_current_session(session_id)` and silently drop events for non-
focused sessions. The split-pane renderer then shows the inactive
pane frozen at whatever was last loaded from DB: no live thinking,
no in-progress tool calls, no streaming chunks until the user tabs
back and `preload_pane_session` re-reads from disk. The 2026-06-04
screenshot showed the inactive column with gray "Thinking" and
"X tool calls" markers from prior turns but nothing about the
active turn happening in that session.

## What lands here

- `src/tui/app/background_session.rs` (new module). Holds:
  * `BackgroundSessionState` struct — sidecar live-state cache for
    a non-focused session. Mirrors the live-turn fields on
    `AppState` so an inactive pane can be rendered with up-to-date
    thinking/tool/streaming state and promoted back to foreground
    without losing accumulated work.
  * `SessionStateMut<'a>` enum — routing handle for an event
    handler. Two variants (`Foreground(&mut App)` /
    `Background(&mut BackgroundSessionState)`) expose the same set
    of mutator methods so the 20 handler call sites stay one-liners
    regardless of which session they target. Mutator methods cover
    every live-turn field: append_streaming_chunk,
    append_reasoning_chunk, set_processing,
    add_streaming_output_tokens, set_active_tool_group,
    active_tool_group_mut, set_display_token_count,
    set_last_input_tokens, clear_turn_state.

- `App.background_sessions: HashMap<Uuid, BackgroundSessionState>`
  field plus three helper methods:
  * `session_state_mut(sid)` — picks foreground vs background
    routing for an incoming event.
  * `demote_to_background(sid)` — snapshots current `App` live
    fields into a fresh sidecar entry when a pane loses focus.
    Empty snapshots skip insertion to keep the map bounded.
  * `promote_to_foreground(sid)` — pops a sidecar entry into the
    `App` live fields when a pane gains focus. Returns false when
    no entry exists so the caller can fall back to the existing
    DB-reload path.

- Module wiring in `src/tui/app/mod.rs` (re-exports the new types
  for the rest of the TUI to use without reaching into the
  module path).

## What is deliberately NOT here

- The 20 event handlers still gate on `is_current_session` and
  drop background events. That migration is step 2 — separate
  commit, smaller mechanical diff, easier to review.
- The focus-switch path (`switch_to_session`,
  `preload_pane_session`) does not yet call `demote_to_background`
  / `promote_to_foreground`. Comes in step 2.
- The inactive-pane renderer (`render/panes.rs`) does not yet read
  from `background_sessions`. Step 2.

All three helper methods are gated with `#[allow(dead_code)]` for
this commit so the unused-function warning stays silent until the
step-2 migration wires them up.

`cargo clippy --all-features --lib --bins --tests -- -D warnings`
clean against this commit. No behaviour change yet — the inactive

## Handler migration

Six event handlers in `state.rs` routed via the new
`session_state_mut(session_id)` helper. Each one used to drop
events for non-focused sessions; now each routes to either the
foreground `AppState` fields or a per-session
`BackgroundSessionState` sidecar depending on which session the
event targets:

- `ReasoningChunk` → `append_reasoning_chunk`
- `ToolCallStarted` → lazily creates `active_tool_group`, pushes
  the new entry. The original `is_processing` guard moved to the
  foreground-only post-hook (tracing log, auto-scroll nudge)
  since the per-session processing flag is now meaningful
  regardless of which pane has focus.
- `ToolCallCompleted` → flips the matching Started entry in the
  active group. The "flush completed group into a `tool_group`
  DisplayMessage" step stays foreground-only — background
  sessions accumulate inside `active_tool_group` and flush on
  promotion or via the DB-reload path. The plan-tool side effect
  and the auto-scroll nudge also stay foreground-only.
- `StreamingOutputTokens` → `add_streaming_output_tokens` so the
  inactive pane's tok/s + token counter stay accurate.
- `TokenCountUpdated` → `set_display_token_count` +
  `set_last_input_tokens` so the inactive pane's
  `ctx: NK/200K (PP%)` footer indicator updates live.
- `ChannelProcessingStarted` / `ChannelProcessingFinished` →
  `set_processing` so the inactive pane's `[processing...]`
  label fires the moment a remote channel starts a turn, not
  on focus switch.

`ResponseComplete` for non-focused sessions now drops the
matching `background_sessions` entry, preventing the sidecar
from leaking memory for sessions the user never re-focuses.

## Focus-switch hooks

`load_session` (the entry point for every focus change) now:

1. Snapshots outgoing live-turn fields into
   `background_sessions[old_session_id]` via
   `demote_to_background`. Empty snapshots are skipped to keep
   the map bounded.
2. Clears the AppState live fields (existing behaviour).
3. Loads the new session from DB (existing behaviour).
4. Promotes any sidecar entry for the new session via
   `promote_to_foreground`. A no-op when no entry exists
   (typical first-load case) — the DB reload already populated
   the static message list.

This pair guarantees that whatever happens to a session while
it's off-screen is preserved and immediately visible when the
user tabs back, with no DB round-trip needed.

## Renderer update

`render_inactive_pane` reads `app.background_sessions.get(&sid)`
in addition to the existing `pane_message_cache` lookup. Three
new live rows are appended below the cached message snapshot
when the sidecar has corresponding state:

- "⚙ N tool calls" (yellow) when an `active_tool_group` is
  in-flight; "● N tool calls" (gray) when complete; red on
  failure. Same icons as the focused pane's tool-group bullets.
- "▸ Thinking" italic gray when `streaming_reasoning.is_some()`.
- A single-line streaming-response preview (≤120 chars) so the
  user can see at a glance that text is rolling in the
  background pane. The active pane still gets the full
  markdown-rendered streaming render; this is just a
  "something's happening, tab back" signal.

## What still goes through the DB-reload path

`IntermediateText`, `QueuedUserMessage`, and `CompactionSummary`
for non-focused sessions still route to the silently-ignored
fall-through arm. Each mutates `self.messages` — a Vec
specific to the foreground session — and the natural place for
those for a background session is the
`pane_message_cache[sid]` snapshot, refreshed on focus switch
by `preload_pane_session`. The visible cost is that the
inactive pane doesn't see those flushes mid-turn, but the
finalised messages always reach it via the DB-backed reload on
tab-back. Left as a follow-up if we want to drive those into
the inactive pane too — design will need a per-session message
delta on top of the snapshot, not the simple sidecar pattern.

## Sidecar message delta

`BackgroundSessionState` gains `pending_messages: Vec<DisplayMessage>`.
Four new mutator methods on `SessionStateMut`:

- `push_message(msg)` — routes a finalised `DisplayMessage` to
  either `App.messages` (foreground) or `pending_messages`
  (background). The inactive-pane renderer reads both lists when
  drawing the simplified message feed.
- `take_active_tool_group()` — drains the active group out of
  the routed state so `IntermediateText` and `QueuedUserMessage`
  can flush the trailing tool-call bullet into a permanent
  message before pushing whatever comes next.
- `last_message_mut()` — borrows the routed message list's last
  entry mutably so `IntermediateText`'s reasoning-merge path
  can append to a preceding thinking-only assistant entry
  instead of pushing a duplicate.
- `reset_processing_clock()` — re-arms the foreground
  `processing_started_at` instant after a between-rounds flush.
  No-op for background (its `processing_started_at` is set by
  `set_processing`).

`has_live_state()` now considers `!pending_messages.is_empty()`
so a session with flushed-but-unmerged messages stays sticky
across focus switches — without that, `demote_to_background`
would drop the entry the moment in-flight state cleared,
losing the delta before the user got to see it.

`clear_turn_state()` preserves `pending_messages` deliberately.
The pending Vec is a delta of FLUSHED messages, not in-flight
state; wiping it would erase the user-visible turn before they
had a chance to see it after focus return. `ResponseComplete`
still drops the whole sidecar entry (including the delta) only
AFTER the agent has DB-persisted the canonical form, so the
next focus switch shows the persisted messages via the DB
reload anyway.

## Handler migrations

Two more event handlers now route via `session_state_mut`:

- `IntermediateText` — the full flush logic (text + reasoning
  → assistant message, tool group → tool_group message,
  reasoning-only → merge-with-previous-thinking) runs against
  the routed state. Foreground sessions land the messages in
  `App.messages` exactly as before; background sessions land
  them in `pending_messages` to be merged on the next promote.
  The `intermediate_text_received` flag (gates the foreground
  "agent is mid-stream" detection) stays foreground-only.
- `QueuedUserMessage` — flushes the active tool group, pushes
  the user message, both via routing. Foreground-only post-
  hooks (queued_messages preview clearing, input buffer reset,
  auto-scroll nudge) stay where they were.

`CompactionSummary` doesn't get a migration — it doesn't actually
fire. Automatic compaction is fully silent at the channel bridge
(`cli/ui.rs:528-530`, `ProgressEvent::CompactionSummary` returns
early with the comment "summary goes to memory log only") and
manual `/compact` emits a normal `MessageSubmitted` rather than
this variant. The previously-existing `TuiEvent::CompactionSummary`
handler arm in `state.rs` was dead code from when compaction was
visible. Dropped the arm; the silently-ignored fall-through at
the bottom of the match stays so the variant has a designated
landing site if visible compaction is ever re-wired.

## Promote/demote round-trip the delta

`demote_to_background` preserves any prior `pending_messages`
from a previous demote — without this, a session that goes
foreground → background → foreground → background would lose
the messages flushed during the FIRST background phase.
`promote_to_foreground` extends `App.messages` with the
sidecar's `pending_messages` after the DB reload runs, so the
user sees the accumulated delta in chronological order at the
tail of the freshly-loaded view.

## Cleanup side-fixes

- `delete_session` (in input.rs) now calls
  `self.background_sessions.remove(&session_id)`. Without this,
  a session that was processing in background at delete time
  would leak its `pending_messages` and `tps_tracker` forever.
  Caught while planning the follow-up; ships with this commit
  since the leak only became visible once pending_messages
  existed.

- Source-level sentinel test

  pins the hard line: `ToolApprovalRequested`,
  `SudoPasswordRequested`, and `SshPasswordRequested` must

  for a non-focused session would queue forever with no UI

  Scans the handler arm slice in `state.rs` and fails if it
  contains a `session_state_mut` call. Catches refactor-by-
  symmetry mistakes that the type system can't.

- Dead `TuiEvent::CompactionSummary` handler arm removed (see
  CompactionSummary discussion above).

`save_provider_settings` resolves the TOML write target for the custom-

fix(brain): strip empty header stubs at read time (#164 fix 4) [skip ci]

Issue #164's fourth fix: header stubs (sections whose body is empty
after a manual prune or a dedup pass) bloat the LLM's view of brain
context without adding signal. Scrub them at READ time so the loaded
view stays clean while disk stays authoritative for writes.

New `brain::filter::strip_empty_sections` returns the filtered content
plus the list of stripped header lines so callers can surface a
warning. Wired into:

- `load_brain_file` tool: applies to both single-name and "all" reads,
  emits a `tracing::info!` listing the stripped headers per file.
- `prompt_builder::PromptBuilder::load_file`: applies silently to
  system-prompt assembly so dead sections never reach the LLM via the
  always-on path. Logs at debug level when stripping fires.

Behaviour:

- Levels `##` and `###` (and deeper) are candidates. Level 1 (`#`) is
  never stripped — those are document titles with semantic weight.
- A body is "empty" if it contains only blank lines, horizontal rules,
  table separators, short blockquotes (`>` under 40 chars), and HTML
  comments. Anything else counts as real content.
- In-flight markers `TBD`, `TODO`, `WIP`, `placeholder` (case-
  insensitive, whole-word) keep the section alive — they're
  intentional placeholders the user expects to survive.
- Empty outer header with a non-empty subsection is kept (the body
  region runs until the next same-or-higher header, so the nested
  subsection's content counts toward the outer's body).
- Disk is never mutated. No path here writes back; the existing
  `brain_file_safety.rs` append-only/safety policy stays unchanged.

Opt-out: `[brain] strip_empty_sections = false` in config.toml makes
every call a no-op. Default is true.

15 unit tests in `brain_filter_strip_empty_sections_test.rs` cover
the spec: stub strip, marker protection (whole-word boundary —
"TODOPHONE" inside a comment does NOT count), structural-only bodies,
nested subsections, level-1 protection, trailing-newline preservation,
empty input, consecutive stubs, no-op no-strip case, header-at-EOF.

fix(brain): purpose-order canonical + N-1 dedup proposals + stub warnings (#164 fix 3) [skip ci]

Three coupled changes to brain-file dedup so the inbox reflects actual
cleanup work and the user sees stub risk up front.

1. Canonical file selection. Pre-fix `dedup_scan.rs:125` sorted by
   filename alphabetically, so `AGENTS.md` always beat `SOUL.md` as
   canonical regardless of which file was authoritatively shaping
   identity. Now sorts by purpose rank — `SOUL > AGENTS > TOOLS > CODE
   > SECURITY > MEMORY > USER` — with alphabetical tie-break. The
   chosen canonical is the file that semantically owns the rule, not
   the one that happens to come first in the alphabet.

2. N-1 proposals per cluster. The pre-fix code emitted exactly ONE
   proposal per cluster regardless of how many files held duplicates:
   the comment literally said "For simplicity, target the second file
   in the list", then hardcoded `cluster.locations[1]`. A 5-file
   duplicate produced 1 proposal and 3 stayed on disk forever. Now
   emits N-1 proposals — one per non-canonical file — so the inbox
   accurately reflects what needs to be removed.

3. Stub-risk warnings. After all proposals are staged, a post-hoc
   scan re-reads each affected file and computes which header bodies
   would be emptied by the planned removals. Headers that become stubs
   get listed in the proposal's new `warnings: Vec<String>` field. The
   detector delegates to `brain::filter::strip_empty_sections` (fix 4)
   so the proposal-time warning and the read-time strip stay in
   lockstep on what counts as "empty".

Adjacent cleanup: removed the inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block
from `dedup_scan.rs` per project policy (tests live under `src/tests/`
only). Moved the existing tests into `src/tests/rsi_brain_dedup_test.rs`,
updated callers from the deprecated `cluster_to_proposal` (single
proposal) to the new `cluster_to_proposals` (Vec). The deprecated
wrapper is kept with a `#[deprecated]` attribute for any external
callers we missed; internal callers all migrated.

Made `is_structural_line` and `canonical_file_rank` `pub(crate)` so
the moved tests can reach them.

fix(brain): per-file line cap in sync_templates with bail and warn (#164 fix 2) [skip ci]

Issue #164's second fix: sync_templates() had no upper bound on brain
file growth. A user-pruned file got re-grown by upstream syncs silently
and the file could climb past any reasonable budget for what the LLM
needs to see in a turn.

Now: every sync_single_file run resolves a per-file line cap from
config.toml's `[brain.caps]` map (with `[brain] default_cap` as fallback,
500 by default), counts the merged line total before writing, and BAILS
if it would exceed the cap. No write, no append to disk, no silent
growth.

The bail returns a structured `CapBailReport` on the existing
`FileSyncResult` so Mission Control and other consumers can render the
situation distinctly from a transient I/O error. The report names the
file, the local and upstream line counts, the merged total, the cap,
and the top-3 largest new sections that would have been added (so the
user can judge whether to raise the cap or prune those headers
specifically).

The bail also appends a diagnostic entry to ~/.opencrabs/rsi/improvements.md
so the user sees the warning next session without having to scrape
stdout from the RSI run that bailed.

Config additions on `BrainConfig`:

- `caps: BTreeMap<String, usize>` — per-file overrides like
  `[brain.caps] TOOLS.md = 800`
- `default_cap: usize` — fallback for unlisted files, default 500
- `cap_for(filename)` resolver method

Existing `FileSyncResult` gets a new `bailed_for_cap: Option<CapBailReport>`
field. All eight existing constructors updated to include `bailed_for_cap: None`
for the non-bail paths.

9 unit tests in `rsi_sync_cap_bail_test.rs` cover: per-file lookup,
default fallback, case sensitivity, default of 500, top-N ranking by
size, and three source-level invariants verifying the cap check, the
report structure, and the improvements.md logging are wired in.

fix(provider): remove orphan keys.toml section on custom-provider rename + break circular cleanup [skip ci]

Two-pronged fix for the 2026-06-05 ghost-entry bug. User renamed
modelscope-qwen to modelscope via /models, then saw BOTH names in
the /models list even though config.toml only had one entry.

Root cause (source). The rename branch in save_provider_selection_internal
removed the OLD config.toml section and ported the api_key to the
NEW keys.toml section, but never touched the OLD keys.toml section.
On the next Config::load the merge_provider_keys step found a
keys.toml entry without a config counterpart and CREATED a phantom
config entry from the keys.toml side (the "creating minimal entry"
fallback). The phantom entry then showed up in /models alongside the
real one.

exactly to remove orphan keys.toml entries, but it was structurally
broken. It consulted Self::load to learn "what's in config" — which
runs merge_provider_keys, which re-creates entries in
config.providers.custom from keys.toml itself. So the orphan check
was circular: the orphan would always appear in the merged
config_names, the filter would never flag it, nothing got removed.
That latent defect is why the source bug accumulated instead of
self-healing on the next save.

Fixes:

1. Added Config::remove_secret_section(section), a keys.toml mirror
   of remove_section. Call it from the rename branch in dialogs.rs
   right after porting the api_key. No more orphan left behind.

2. Added raw_config_custom_provider_names() that reads config.toml
   directly via toml_edit (no Config::load, no merge). Switched
   cleanup_keys_custom_providers to use it. The orphan check now
   reflects what's actually in config.toml, not the merge-inflated
   view, so genuine orphans get removed.

Tests (src/tests/custom_provider_rename_keys_toml_test.rs):

- remove_secret_section: drops named section only, missing-file ok,
  missing-section ok.
- cleanup_keys_custom_providers: orphan dropped, non-orphan
  preserved, no-op when keys.toml absent.
- Source-level invariant: dialogs.rs MUST call remove_secret_section
  in the rename branch, so a future refactor can't silently re-open
  the bug.

2026-06-06 Telegram log evidence: a glm-5.1 short reply rendered
`ctx: 86K/200K 43% | 37203 tok/s`. The provider burst-delivered the
whole ~300-token response in a single ~8ms SSE chunk, so the active-
streaming window was near-zero and output/active exploded into a
physically impossible rate.

The pre-fix code did `Some(total_output / total_active)` whenever
total_active > 0.0 — no floor, no ceiling — so any sub-second burst
produced garbage.

Extracted the rate computation into a pure, testable
`compute_streaming_tok_per_sec(total_output_tokens, active_secs)`
that returns None when the reading isn't credible:
- zero output tokens, OR
- active window below MIN_ACTIVE_SECS_FOR_TOK_S (0.3s) — burst
  delivery, timing too coarse to be a rate, OR
- computed rate above MAX_PLAUSIBLE_TOK_S (2000) — multi-burst
  artifact that clears the time floor but is still impossible.

When suppressed the footer simply shows no tok/s (ctx only) instead
of a fantasy number. Real sustained rates (the same session's 447
tok/s on a longer reply) pass through unchanged.

10 unit tests in src/tests/streaming_tok_per_sec_guard_test.rs cover

fix(retry): patient backoff defaults — 1s/2s/4s/8s instead of 100ms hammering [skip ci]

Both retry configs (brain::provider::retry and utils::retry) defaulted
to initial_delay=100ms, max_attempts=3 — a ~0.7s total retry window
(100ms → 200ms → 400ms). Log evidence (2026-06-06):

  Retry attempt 1 after 107ms ... dialagram
  Retry attempt 2 after 202ms ... dialagram
  Retry attempt 3 after 439ms ... dialagram
  Max retry attempts (3) exceeded → falls to chain

That window is too short to ride out a 1-2s network blip, so the
primary bailed to the fallback chain on every transient failure. The
user's repro — stop, resend on the primary, works fine — is exactly a
blip that cleared in under 2s but blew through the 0.7s window.

Worse, retrying a rate-limited (429) endpoint every 100ms actively
makes the rate limit worse instead of letting the window reopen.

New default for the network/API path: 4 retries over ~15s
(1s → 2s → 4s → 8s). A patient first delay gives transient failures
time to clear and rate-limit windows time to reopen before the
fallback chain is walked. Kept both configs in lockstep so every
retry mechanism in the system uses the same sane timing.

DB lock-contention retries (db::retry::DbRetryConfig, utils
RetryConfig::database()) are intentionally left fast (50-100ms) —
SQLite locks resolve in milliseconds and waiting 1s for a lock would
be a regression.

Tests updated to assert the new 4/1s defaults plus a new
test_default_backoff_schedule_is_patient that pins the exact
1s/2s/4s/8s schedule so a future 'optimization' back to sub-second
retries fails loudly. 3712 tests pass, clippy clean.

refactor(retry): consolidate provider retry onto utils::retry, delete duplicate [skip ci]

brain::provider::retry was a near-duplicate of utils::retry — same
RetryConfig shape, same exponential-backoff loop. The generic
utils::retry is the better design: it has the RetryableError trait so
any error type plugs in, its log line already reads 'Retry attempt
N/M' (the provider one only logged 'Retry attempt N', part of why the
retry count wasn't visible), and it honors retry_after() hints
generically.

Consolidation:

- ProviderError now implements utils::retry::RetryableError. is_retryable
  delegates to the existing inherent classifier (via a free wrapper to

feat(retry): surface provider retries to the user as RetryAttempt events [skip ci]

The retry/fallback infra already had a ProgressEvent::RetryAttempt
wired to the TUI as '⏳ Retry N/M — reason', but it only fired for
stream-DROP retries in tool_loop. The deep provider connection
retries (the 'Retry attempt 1/2/3' that the user never saw before an
apparent instant fallback) emitted nothing to the UI — so resilience
looked like no resilience.

Wiring (mirrors the existing take_swap_event pattern):

- utils::retry::retry_with_notify — same as retry() but invokes
  on_retry(attempt, max, &err) before each backoff sleep, so a caller
  can surface progress without the retry loop knowing about UI.

- Provider::take_retry_notices() trait method (default empty) — drains
  (attempt, max, reason) notices recorded since the last call.

- OpenAIProvider records each stream-connection retry into a shared
  Arc<Mutex<Vec<…>>> via retry_with_notify, and drains it in
  take_retry_notices. retry_reason() keeps the surfaced text concise
  ('connection error', 'rate limited', 'server error 5xx').

- FallbackProvider::take_retry_notices aggregates from the primary and
  every fallback tried this turn, in chain order.

- tool_loop drains provider.take_retry_notices() once per iteration
  (right where it already polls take_swap_event) and emits a
  RetryAttempt event per notice. The existing cli/ui bridge renders
  them as '⏳ Retry N/M — …'.

minimax) — i.e. the user's chain. Tests pin retry_with_notify firing
once per retry with correct (attempt, max) and NOT firing on success
or non-retryable errors.

Known limitation: notices are drained after the stream call resolves,
so on a slow multi-retry recovery they appear in a batch rather than
live during the wait. Live streaming of retry events would require the
progress callback to reach the provider layer — a deeper change left
as a follow-up.

feat(retry): fail fast on hard-down endpoints, patient on transient [skip ci]

Completes the timing fix. The patient 1s/2s/4s/8s backoff is right for
transient failures (timeout, 5xx, rate limit) but wrong for a hard-down
endpoint — a DNS failure / connection refused won't recover within the
retry window, so patiently retrying it burns ~15s before the fallback
chain moves on. That's exactly the dead-dialagram case in the logs:
every fallback wasted retries on an unreachable host.

Classification:

- RetryableError gains is_hard_down() (default false) and a
  HARD_DOWN_MAX_RETRIES = 1 cap. Both retry loops compute an effective
  ceiling: hard-down errors get one quick retry (catches a one-off
  socket hiccup), transient errors keep the full configured budget.

- ProviderError::is_hard_down() returns true for a connection-phase
  reqwest error (is_connect: connection refused / DNS fail / host
  unreachable). Timeouts are deliberately NOT hard-down — a slow-but-
  alive host is worth the patient schedule.

So a dead provider in the chain now costs ~1s (one retry) instead of
~15s before moving to the next, while a healthy provider having a
transient blip still gets the full patient backoff to ride it out.

Tests: hard-down error capped to 1 retry even under a 4-retry config;
transient error uses the full 4-retry budget. 3712 tests pass, clippy
clean.

ci: gate on PR + main push, not tags; trim routine-push cost

The CI workflow triggered only on 'push: tags: v*'. That was wrong on
several axes:

- It never ran on pull_requests, so external contributions were
  ungated — you couldn't review a PR with a green/red signal.
- It never ran on pushes to main, so direct pushes landed untested.
- Firing on tags meant ci.yml AND release.yml both compiled
  Windows/macOS on the same tag event — a redundant double-build.
- The coverage job (if: refs/heads/main) was dead: a tag ref is never
  refs/heads/main, so it never ran.

New trigger model (single-maintainer GitHub Flow):

- pull_request: full gate (lint + cross-platform build + test + audit).
- push to main: keep main green, but cheap — paths-ignore skips
  docs-only commits and the heavy cross-platform BUILD job is gated off
  routine main pushes (if: pull_request || workflow_dispatch). A normal
  commit pays only lint + Linux test + audit (~5-8 min, cached,
  cancellable). This replaces opt-out [skip ci]-on-every-commit toil.
- workflow_dispatch: run the full matrix on demand (e.g. verify
  Windows/macOS before tagging a release).
- NOT on tags: release.yml owns tags and trusts the commit already
  passed CI on its way to main. Kills the double-build.

Coverage moved to workflow_dispatch-only — tarpaulin (~12 min) would
otherwise re-add the per-push cost we just trimmed; run it on demand
when you want a fresh report.

ci-gate (if: always(), fails only on failure/cancelled — not skipped)
already tolerates the skipped build job on main pushes, so the single
branch-protection status check still works. release.yml is unchanged.

YAML validated; jobs: lint, build, test, audit, coverage, ci-gate.

fix(retry): retry transient 4xx HTML infra pages + DNS-fail fast-bail

PRIMARY bug (the 'no retries, instant fallback' report): modelscope
intermittently returns HTTP 405 with a Chinese HTML error page for a
valid POST to /chat/completions. 405 was non-retryable, so the request
bounced straight to the fallback chain with ZERO retries — the user saw
no resilience on the primary, and a manual swap-back worked because the
405 is a transient infra blip.

error page, not a real JSON API client error. is_retryable now treats any
4xx with an HTML body as transient (retryable). Real client errors return
JSON, never HTML, so this never masks an invalid_model / validation /
auth error. is_html_error_body scans a char-bounded prefix (chars().take
— byte slicing would panic mid-UTF8 on the Chinese body).

SECONDARY: is_hard_down now also catches DNS-resolution failures. reqwest's
is_connect() does NOT fire for NXDOMAIN — a dead domain surfaces as a
generic 'error sending request' whose is_connect() is false, so it got the
full 15s patient retry. The user's fallback chain has dialagram first, and
www.dialagram.me went NXDOMAIN — every fallback walked it for 15s before
reaching zhipu. Now a dead host fails fast (~1s) via a source-chain scan
for resolver/connection failure strings (looks_like_connection_failure).

  so the TUI handler doesn't re-pin to the fallback either.

The FallbackProvider's own internal swap-event surfacing is left intact —
