[skip ci] fix(#179): resolve restart failure after /evolve

The bug: after auto-update via /evolve, restarting the agent crashed with
'exec() failed: No such file or directory (os error 2)'.

Root cause: SelfUpdater::auto_detect() unconditionally cloned the source
tree into ~/.opencrabs/source/ even for pre-built binaries, then set
binary_path to source/target/release/opencrabs which was NEVER BUILT.
When /evolve or restart tried to exec() into that path, it failed.

Fix (3 changes in src/brain/self_update.rs):

1. auto_detect() rewritten for pre-built binaries:
   - Walks up from current_exe looking for Cargo.toml (unchanged)
   - If no Cargo.toml found (pre-built binary), uses current_exe as
     binary_path instead of a never-built target/release path
   - Source dir is recorded but NOT cloned eagerly
   - The evolve tool already replaced the binary at current_exe in-place,
     so restart just exec's it back

2. New ensure_source_tree() method (lazy clone):
   - Only called by build_streaming() when /rebuild is invoked
   - If Cargo.toml exists at project_root: git pull --ff-only
   - If not: git clone --depth 1 into ~/.opencrabs/source/
   - Errors surface cleanly to the caller

3. build_streaming() updated:
   - Calls ensure_source_tree() before cargo build
   - After successful build, checks if <project_root>/target/release/opencrabs
     exists and returns that; falls back to self.binary_path otherwise
   - This handles both build-from-source (returns target/) and the
     rare case where binary_path is already correct

Result: /evolve, /rebuild, and auto-restart all share the same approach.
The binary path always points at a real file on disk.

Closes #179

fix(restart): /rebuild restarts the binary it built, not the stale exe (#179)

Follow-up to dab44db0. That fix made auto_detect() use current_exe() for
a pre-built install (correct for /evolve, which replaces the exe in
place). But /rebuild on a pre-built install builds into
~/.opencrabs/source/target/release/opencrabs — a DIFFERENT path from the
running exe. The RestartReady handler ignored the build path (masked
`_status`) and re-derived via auto_detect(), so /rebuild compiled the
new binary then restarted into the OLD exe.

RestartReady now carries the binary to exec:
- ProgressEvent::RestartReady / TuiEvent::RestartReady gain
  binary_path: Option<PathBuf>.
- /rebuild (tool + TUI command) passes Some(built_path); the TUI command
  also stopped discarding build_streaming's returned path (was Ok(_)).
- /evolve passes None — the handler resolves current_exe() (it replaced
  the exe in place).
- The handler uses binary_path when Some (SelfUpdater::restart_into),
  else falls back to auto_detect; the previously-masked status is now
  logged, not dropped on the floor.
- SelfUpdater::restart_into(path, sid) added; restart() delegates to it.

auto_detect()'s path logic is factored into a pure resolve_paths(exe,
source_dir) so it's testable without the real current_exe(). 3 tests:
pre-built install resolves to the running exe (NOT an unbuilt target/
path — the #179 regression), source tree resolves to target/release,
and a nested deps/ exe walks up to the Cargo.toml. 3750 pass, clippy
clean.

feat(rebuild): run /rebuild in the background via a one-shot cron job

/rebuild blocked the session (and the agent turn, for the tool) for the
minutes a release build takes. Now it's backgrounded through the cron
system, per design:

- schedule_background_rebuild(pool, session_id, deliver_to) queues a
  reserved one-shot cron job (__opencrabs_rebuild__) carrying the
  originating session id, and returns immediately. Re-scheduling replaces
  the prior job so two builds never stack.
- The scheduler special-cases the reserved job: instead of an agent
  prompt it deletes the job first (one-shot, no 60s-tick re-trigger),
  builds from source, and on success exec-restarts into the freshly-built
  binary (using restart_into from the #179 fix, so it loads the BUILT
  binary, not the stale exe), resuming the session. On failure it
  delivers the error and stops.
- Because the scheduler runs in-process, exec() replaces the whole
  process (TUI included) — no need to route a reload signal through the
  TUI event loop.
- /rebuild tool + TUI command now just schedule and report 'reload when
  ready'; the build no longer blocks. RebuildTool's now-dead progress
  field + import removed (not masked).

Behavior chosen with the user: cron schedules the build, the main
process reloads, auto-reload immediately on success.

Test: scheduling queues exactly one resumable one-shot job and

[skip ci] fix(#182): isolate cron jobs to the profile they were created in

Cron jobs could execute under the wrong profile's brain/config/tools. A job
created in a named profile (e.g. ops) could be picked up and run with the
default profile's environment: execute_job() calls Config::load(), which keys
off the process-global active profile, not the profile the job belongs to.
This surfaces when profiles share a DB (config.toml carries an explicit
database.path, and migrate_profile copies *.toml between profiles), so one
process sees another profile's cron_jobs rows.

The active profile is a process-global OnceLock that drives Config::load(), the
brain loader, and the DB path, and cannot change at runtime. So a job can only
ever run with the active profile's environment. Rather than silently run it
under the wrong one, the scheduler now refuses jobs that don't belong to the
active profile.

Changes:
- Migration 20260608000001 adds a nullable profile_name column to cron_jobs.
- CronJob gains profile_name. CronJob::new() stamps the active profile, storing
  the literal "default" for the base profile so the match is exact. Legacy
  rows stay NULL.
- schedule_background_rebuild() stamps the active profile so the one-shot
  rebuild job still runs in-process.
- Scheduler tick() skips any job whose stamped profile does not match the
  active profile, BEFORE is_due / last_run updates, so a foreign job's schedule
  is never advanced out from under its owning process. A NULL stamp (legacy)
  always runs: origin is unknown and the per-profile DB already isolates it, so
  blocking would break existing jobs.
- New predicate job_runs_in_active_profile(job_profile, active) encodes the
  rule and is unit-tested in src/tests/cron_profile_isolation_test.rs.
- Repository insert writes profile_name; from_row reads it.
- Bumped Database::MIGRATION_COUNT 25 -> 26 and added profile_name to the

ProviderSwitched event mid-turn to stop the fallback re-pinning the

  cannot drop, because nothing in the fallback/emit/stream path changed.
- A /models switch (TUI dialog + channel) calls mark_manual_switch,
  which captures the (epoch, provider, model) pin.
- run_tool_loop_inner snapshots the epoch at turn start; AFTER the
  response is built (finalize_manual_switch), if the epoch changed the
  user switched mid-turn, so the pinned pair is re-applied atomically
  (swap_provider_for_session sets provider+model together — no desync)
  and persisted to the session DB row.

fix(#182): run cron jobs under their own profile, not the process profile

The first pass at #182 skipped any job whose stamped profile did not match
the running process. That was backwards: in a shared-database setup a job
created in a non-default profile would be seen by the default process and
then silently never run. Skipping is not isolation, it is a silent drop.

This reworks it to the contributor's option 2: run each job under the
profile it was created in.

How it works:
- New scoped profile-home override in config::profile. with_profile_home()
  sets a thread-local home that resolve_profile_home() consults BEFORE the
  process-global active profile OnceLock. It is only ever set across a
  synchronous span (config + brain load), never held across an await, and a
  drop guard clears it even on panic, so it cannot leak between async tasks.
- home_for_profile() resolves a profile name to its home dir without reading
  the OnceLock (default/None to the base dir, named to profiles/<name>).
- The scheduler resolves a (Config, AgentService) per job. Jobs in the active
  profile (and legacy unstamped jobs) use the existing factory agent, the
  common path, unchanged. A job stamped with a different profile gets its own
  config + brain materialized from that profile's home, its provider built
  from that profile's keys, and its working dir set to that profile's home.
  The shared DB pool is reused, that pool is why the foreign job is visible.
- Tools are shared from the factory registry: dispatch is profile-agnostic
  and the per-call config we pass drives profile-specific behaviour.
- Removed the skip predicate and the tick() skip branch.

Scope/limit: the materialized config, brain, provider, and working dir are
correct for the foreign job. A tool that re-resolves the profile home at
runtime (e.g. a memory write) still uses the process profile, since the
override is synchronous-only. That is an edge case for cron and a separate
follow-up if needed.

Tests: src/tests/cron_profile_isolation_test.rs now covers home_for_profile
mapping and the scoped override (applies inside the closure, cleared after).

fix(#182): task-local profile scope for full cron job execution

The previous commit used a thread-local for the profile home override,
which only covered the initial config/brain load. Any tool call during
agent execution (memory writes, config reads, brain file ops, key lookups)
reverted to the process profile because the thread-local was cleared
before the first .await.

Now using tokio::task_local! scoped to the spawned task. The profile home
persists across every .await inside the entire job execution, so all 25+
opencrabs_home() call sites inside tools resolve to the job's profile.
The scope dies with the task, no leak to sibling jobs.

- with_profile_home_async(): wraps the full execute_job future
- resolve_profile_home() checks task-local before OnceLock
- with_profile_home() uses sync_scope for initial materialization
- Removed RefCell/thread_local, now purely task-local

fix(telegram): model picker hung on 'loading' for long model names

Selecting a custom provider with long model names (e.g. modelscope's
'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B') in the Telegram /models
picker spun on 'loading' forever and never showed the model list, while
short-name providers (dialagram) worked fine.

Root cause: the model buttons encoded 'model:<provider>|<full-name>' as
callback_data. Telegram caps callback_data at 64 BYTES, and
'model:custom:modelscope|deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B' is
65. Telegram rejects the ENTIRE inline keyboard (BUTTON_DATA_INVALID)
when any button overflows, and the edit_message_text call that attaches
the keyboard was 'let _ =' — the 400 was swallowed, so no buttons ever
rendered and the message never updated. dialagram's names are short, so
its keyboard stayed under the limit.

Fix: model_button_callback_data() keeps the literal form when it fits
(short names, backward compatible) and falls back to a compact index
'model:<provider>|#<i>' when it would overflow. The handler resolves the
index back to the model name via model_at_index(), which reads the same
config list the picker rendered (no live fetch). Tests pin the 64-byte
guarantee, the literal-form fallback, and the index round-trip.

fix(#183): give the agent its version in Runtime Info so it stops hallucinating

The #183 /doctor fix surfaced the version on demand, but the root
complaint was 'asking the Crab its version is futile — they
hallucinate.' That happened because the system prompt carried no
ground truth: the Runtime Info block listed Model/Provider/working
directory/OS/Timestamp but never the version.

Add the compile-time CARGO_PKG_VERSION (the running binary's real
version, so it tracks across evolve/rebuild) to both Runtime Info

'what version are you?' is answerable from context, not just via
/doctor. Test pins the version line in both paths.

fix(retry): patient backoff for DNS/connection errors — stop fast-failing flaky providers

Remove the 'hard-down' fast-fail entirely. It capped DNS-resolution and
connection-refused errors at a single retry on the premise that 'a dead
host won't come back within the retry window.' That premise is wrong for
flaky-but-recovering providers: dialagram answers ~98.8% within 24h, so
its DNS/connection failures are usually brief blips that the patient
window (1+2+4+8s) would ride out. Fast-failing them after one retry
abandoned the user's chosen provider for a transient hiccup and bumped
the request onto a fallback unnecessarily — the 'it switched my model
when falling back' behavior.

Now every retryable error (DNS/connection included) gets the full
patient backoff. A genuinely dead host is still bounded — not by giving
up on the first request, but by the fallback chain (serves the request)
plus the sticky-fallback threshold (after 4 consecutive primary failures
the session pins to the fallback, so a dead primary isn't re-hit every
request).

Removed: HARD_DOWN_MAX_RETRIES, RetryableError::is_hard_down,
effective_max_attempts, ProviderError's is_hard_down impl, and the
now-orphaned looks_like_connection_failure. Tests updated to pin that
all retryable errors use the full budget.

fix(rsi): dedup before appending to brain files — stop the append→dedup→append loop

RSI re-proposes the SAME improvements every cycle ('Add retry logic to
bash tool', 'Add conciseness guideline'), because a tool's failure rate
doesn't drop just because the guideline was already written. The
self_improve 'apply' action appended that content blindly each cycle, so
brain files grew with 12-14 duplicate blocks until the dedup-scan cleaned
them up — an endless append→dedup→append loop (visible in Mission
Control: the same proposals repeating hourly, dedup proposals chasing
them).

Route 'apply' through filter_duplicate_append() — the same paragraph-level
dedup write_opencrabs_file already uses:
- all-duplicate content → skip the write entirely, return a 'already
  present, do not re-apply' result (and don't log a fresh 'Applied'
  entry), so RSI converges instead of churning
- partially-new content → append only the genuinely-new paragraphs

This is deterministic: no matter how often RSI re-proposes, it physically
can't create a duplicate. Tests pin both the skip and the partial-append
via a throwaway profile home.

Also isolates three pre-existing apply tests (apply_writes_to_rsi_
improvements, apply_valid_brain_file, apply_without_rationale) onto a
throwaway profile home. They wrote to the real ~/.opencrabs and relied on
apply always appending; with dedup they were order-dependent against the
shared home (and had been quietly polluting the user's real brain files).

fix(errors): surface the real cause in TUI warnings instead of 'connection error'

The retry notice and the 'Switched to …' fallback alert both rendered
HTTP failures as a flat 'connection error' / 'error sending request for
url (…)', throwing away the actual cause. reqwest carries the real
reason (DNS lookup failure, connection refused, TLS, timeout) in its
error source chain — it just wasn't being read.

Add user_facing_reason()/describe_reqwest_error(): walk the source chain
to the deepest OS/resolver cause, classify it into a concise phrase, and
append the host. So instead of 'dialagram connection error' the TUI now
shows 'DNS lookup failed (www.dialagram.me)'. Wired into retry_reason
(the ⏳ Retry line) and the fallback promote reason (the 🔧 Switched-to
alert).

fix(context): never inject the feedback/performance digest into the LLM context

The feedback digest (tool failure rates, recent failures) was appended
to the system prompt at three sites (TUI chat, cmd_run, agent-
interactive). It's a maintenance WARNING — it belongs in
~/.opencrabs/rsi/digest.md (written by write_startup_digest), not in the
conversation the model sees. Injecting it put unrelated stats into every

fix(ctx): reject over-reported provider usage so a lying endpoint can't inflate the counter

A fresh session (1 message, ~65 chars) showed ctx 28,775 tokens. The
counter was right to trust the provider's reported input_tokens — but
the provider lied. The zhipu 'coding' endpoint (glm-5.1) over-reports a
FLAT ~20k on every call regardless of content size: the gap between our
local tiktoken estimate and its reported input was a constant ~20,300
across requests from 8k to 30k (additive, not a tokenizer ratio — an
8.4k request came back as 28.8k). The user was billed for the phantom
tokens.

The non-CLI calibration trusted input_tokens unconditionally (only a
drift>5000 check), unlike the CLI path which already guards against
cumulative/inflated provider numbers. Add is_implausible_token_report():
when a provider reports >2× the real content size (system + messages +
tool schemas), keep the local estimate and log a warning instead of
calibrating the ctx counter (and cost) up to the inflated number.
tiktoken vs any real tokenizer agree within ~2×, so 2× is a safe
ceiling. Tests pin the observed over-report, legitimate tokenizer
differences, tool-schema overhead, and the tiny-request floor.

feat(tools): lazy tool-schema loading via tool_search discovery (flag-gated)

set + a tool_search discovery tool, and let the agent activate EXTENDED
tools on demand (the same pattern as load_brain_file for brain files).

feat(cron): multi-profile daemon (#182) - one process covers all profiles

The daemon now discovers every profile under ~/.opencrabs/profiles/ at
startup and runs a cron scheduler for each, in one process. Before, you
had to run a separate daemon per profile.

How it works:
- cmd_daemon lists all profiles. The active profile is still run in full
  by cmd_chat_inner (which spawns its own scheduler). Every OTHER profile
  gets a lightweight cron-only scheduler via spawn_cron_scheduler_for_profile.
- That helper builds the profile's DB, provider, brain and channel factory
  INSIDE a with_profile_home_async scope, then drives the scheduler loop
  there so its setup and jobs resolve to the right profile home.
- CronScheduler.spawn() is split into run() (loops in the current task, no
  internal spawn) plus a thin spawn() wrapper. The daemon drives run()
  inside the scope; the active-profile call site is unchanged.

Profile correctness:
- Added profile::current_profile_name(), backed by a new task-local set
  alongside the home override. Job stamping (CronJob::new, background
  rebuild) now uses it, so a job created while running under a foreign
  profile is attributed to that profile, not the process global.
- resolve_job_agent compares the job against current_profile_name() so a
  scoped job reuses its in-scope factory/config.
- Per-job scoping still keys off the process global active_profile(),
  which is correct: the spawned execution task does not inherit the
  scheduler's task-local, so it must scope whenever the job's profile
  differs from the process global.

fix(logging): reliable daemon file logs + correct logs status/view/cleanup (#190)

Primary — daemon log file freezes ~5s after start with the process alive:
the file appender was wrapped in tracing_appender::non_blocking, whose worker
thread (worker.rs) does `Err(_) => {}` on an IO error and keeps draining the
channel — so once a write fails, every subsequent line is silently dropped and
the file freezes with no fd and no surfaced error. It also drops events when its
bounded buffer fills under load. Write the rolling daily appender SYNCHRONOUSLY
instead: each event is attempted on the calling thread, write errors reach
tracing-subscriber's stderr fallback instead of vanishing, and a transient
failure can't permanently wedge the writer. Debug file logging is opt-in (-d),
so the synchronous IO cost is an acceptable trade for logs that actually work.
LoggerGuard is now a marker (no worker guard to keep alive).

Secondary — logs status/view/cleanup all broken: the rolling files are named
`opencrabs.YYYY-MM-DD` (no .log extension), but every reader filtered on
`path.extension() == "log"` (the date is the 'extension', never 'log'), so
they matched zero files — status reported 0, view found nothing, cleanup never
pruned. cmd_logs also looked under the process CWD instead of ~/.opencrabs/logs,
so a daemon always saw an empty dir. Added log_dir() + is_log_file() +
DEFAULT_LOG_PREFIX as the single source of truth; writer (main) and all readers
now resolve the same path and matcher.

Test: logging_log_files_test covers the filename matcher and documents why the
old extension check missed every file.

fix(logging): self-healing daily file writer — recover from a lost fd mid-run (#190)

Follow-up to the synchronous-logging fix. Writing the rolling appender directly
removed the non_blocking worker that silently dropped events on IO error, but
tracing_appender's rolling appender only reopens the file on date rollover — so
if its fd goes bad mid-day (file removed by an out-of-band logrotate, fd closed
externally) every later write hits the same dead handle and the log stays frozen
until restart, which matches the issue's 'no fd open' symptom.

ResilientFileWriter wraps the rolling appender (reusing its UTC date handling +
rotation) and, on any write error, rebuilds it so the very next event reopens
the file. Synchronous + Mutex-serialized, no background thread. LoggerGuard
stays a marker; init_debug_logging uses ResilientFileWriter as the fmt writer.

writes a readable opencrabs.<date> file that is_log_file() recognizes.

fix(usage): cache-efficiency % was inflated by NULL cache columns

The Cache Efficiency card read ~87% when the real hit rate was ~53%. The
denominator query summed `input_tokens + cache_creation_tokens + cache_read_tokens`
per row, but non-caching requests store NULL (not 0) in the cache columns, so
`input + NULL + NULL` is NULL and SUM() drops that whole row — removing those
rows' input tokens from the total. With ~2500 non-cached rows (~175M input
tokens) falling out, the denominator shrank from 449.7M to 274.4M and the
fraction (cached / total) ballooned. Numerator was always correct.

Fix: COALESCE every column to 0 individually inside the SUM. Extracted the
aggregation columns to CACHE_STATS_SELECT_COLS so the regression test runs the
exact production SQL against rows with NULL cache columns.

Real data: 237.3M cached / 449.7M total = 52.8% (was shown as 86.5%).

fix(usage): cache efficiency measures caching-capable requests only (metric B)

Filter to caching-capable rows explicitly (cache_read OR cache_creation IS NOT
NULL); a cache MISS (value 0, not NULL) stays in the denominator and correctly

cache field still counts. Extracted CACHE_CAPABLE_WHERE so the regression test
runs the exact production filter.

fix(self-heal): phantom intent detection works across all languages, not just the detected one

The no-tools phantom self-heal gated intent-phrase matching on detect_language(),
which only routes Cyrillic and accented-Latin text reliably. Accent-free non-English
narration (e.g. an "I'm about to use <tool>" plan with no marker char) fell through
to English and slipped past, so the self-heal never fired for it.

Scan intent phrases across every language at once: they are multi-word and carry
language-distinctive tokens, so the union is collision-free. Single-word action_verbs
stay gated to the detected language, where cross-language collision is real. Applied
to all three intent gates (no-tools, post-success forward intent, investigative).

Also add the strongest forward-commitment shape that English was missing
("I'm going to <verb>") and fill the use/write/run verb gaps in es/fr/pt/ru.

fix(telegram): don't react to a peer bot's half-streamed message in groups

Bots that stream their reply by editing one message progressively (the same
mechanism we use) arrive as a first frame via a message update, then a run of
edited_message updates. The dispatcher only handled message updates, so we
processed the first frame — a half-written message ending mid-sentence — and the
model would conclude it was cut off and disengage, never seeing the final text
because every subsequent edit was dropped.

Hold a bot's text message in a group until its edit stream settles (no further
edit for a few seconds), then dispatch the final text. Each edit resets the
settle timer via a generation counter so the latest frame wins and the pending
map self-cleans. Add a filter_edited_message branch: while a message is still
pending it refreshes the timer; once already processed it reconciles stored
history (new ChannelMessageRepository::update_content) so group context reflects
the final text without reprocessing. Humans, DMs, and non-text messages are
unaffected and still process immediately.

fix(telegram): tune peer-bot settle window to 2s for snappier bot-to-bot

Wait for the peer's stream to go quiet for ~2s rather than 4s, then process.
That still clears the ~1.5s edit cadence so we never act on a partial, while
starting our turn promptly after the other agent finishes.

test(telegram): cover ChannelMessageRepository::update_content reconcile path

Assert an edit rewrites the stored frame in place (no duplicate row) and that

fix(evolve): restart the real binary path, not a post-swap "(deleted)" path

On a standalone (no-systemd) pre-built install, /evolve unlinks the running
binary then renames the new one into place. Afterward Linux reports
/proc/self/exe as "<path> (deleted)", and current_exe() returns that literal
string. Two failures followed: the restart exec'd a non-existent "… (deleted)"
target (ENOENT), and a retry captured that same path and wrote the next
downloaded binary to a real file literally named "opencrabs (deleted)".

Resolve the running binary through a new running_binary_path() that strips the
" (deleted)" marker, and use it in both auto_detect() and evolve's capture
site. evolve also now hands the RestartReady handler the exact path it wrote the
new binary to (captured before the swap) instead of None, so the handler never
re-derives the path post-swap.

fix(providers): default the Xiaomi section so keyless works without a config block

Xiaomi is keyless during the free collab window (the proxy supplies the key),
but try_create_xiaomi returned Ok(None) when config.toml had no
[providers.xiaomi] section — so a config predating the provider, or a fresh
evolve that never appended the section, showed Xiaomi as keyless-available in
the picker yet dead-ended with 'No models available', and default_model()
reported the MISSING_MODEL sentinel.

Materialize the canonical keyless section (enabled, default_model mimo-v2.5-pro,
the mimo-* list, proxy base_url, no key) via a serde field default so a missing
section deserializes to a working provider — single source of truth in
xiaomi_provider_defaults(), reused as a belt-and-suspenders fallback in the
factory for any programmatically-built Config. The keyless time-gate stays in
the factory, so the synthesized section is harmless after the cutoff. The serde
default is deserialization-only, so Default::default() keeps xiaomi None and the
blast radius stays small.

fix(self-heal): catch brief 'Running checks now.' work announcements as phantom

A turn whose only visible text was a short present-continuous work announcement
("Running checks now." — 19 bytes) with zero tool calls slipped past the
no-tools phantom detector: it early-returned at the len() < 20 floor before ever
examining the text, so the self-heal never fired and the turn dropped.

Add a per-language work_announcement_re, checked before the length floor: a
leading action gerund (or, for fr/ru, present-tense verb) plus a required
imminence marker (now / ahora / agora / maintenant / сейчас / … / : ). The
marker requirement keeps ordinary sentences that merely open with a gerund
("Reading the file is straightforward.") from matching. Scanned across all
languages like the intent phrases, and capped at 80 chars so a paragraph can't
qualify.

fix(providers): parse tool calls wrapped in <tool_call_list> (mimo-v2.5-pro)

mimo-v2.5-pro sometimes leaks its tool call into content as
<tool_call_list>{"tool_call_id":"…","tool_name":"…","tool_input":{…}}</tool_call_list>
instead of using the structured tool_calls field. None of the text-extractor
signals matched it — "tool_call_id" doesn't contain the literal "tool_call" —
so the whole block shipped to visible content and the call never dispatched.

Add a pass that scans <tool_call_list>…</tool_call_list> blocks (single object,
newline-separated, or JSON array; closing tag optional) and dispatches each
call, and teach parse_tool_call_value the tool_input arguments alias. The
phantom self-heal still covers the cases where the same shape lands in
reasoning_content rather than content.

fix(self-heal): catch work announcements that lead a multi-sentence turn

The v1 work_announcement_re required the announcement to be the whole line and
the helper capped the lead at 80 chars, so when mimo led with the announcement
then kept talking — "Running fmt, clippy, tests now. Then fetching fresh
commits.\n\nClippy clean. Tests next." — it slipped past and the turn dropped
again.

Anchor each per-language regex to the message start (drop multiline), match the
opening sentence, and require the imminence marker (now / ahora / agora /
maintenant / сейчас / … / trailing :) at a sentence boundary — so a turn that
leads with the announcement and continues still matches, while "now" used as a
mid-sentence adverb ("Running it now takes a minute.") does not. Drop the
80-char lead cap.

feat(mimo): remind mimo models to emit structured tool calls, not prose

fix(evolve): strip all stacked (deleted) markers from the running exe path

A binary evolved while already running from a deleted inode stacks the marker
(opencrabs (deleted) (deleted) was seen on a VPS after repeated pre-fix

fix(service): honest systemctl errors + system unit for root installs

Two bugs in 'opencrabs service' on Linux:

1. False success. Every systemctl call used .status()?, which only propagates a
   spawn failure, not a non-zero exit. So when 'systemctl --user' failed with
   'Failed to connect to bus' (the usual case on a headless VPS with no user
   D-Bus session), the command still printed the green success line. Now every
   call goes through run_systemctl(), which checks the exit status, surfaces
   systemctl's stderr, and returns the error.

2. No working path on a VPS. A user unit needs a per-user systemd + bus that an
   SSH session lacks; sudo made it worse (root has no user bus, 'No medium
   found'). When run as root we now install a SYSTEM unit (/etc/systemd/system,
   plain systemctl, enable --now so it boots), running the daemon as the
   invoking SUDO_USER so it reads that user's ~/.opencrabs. When a user-scope op
   fails we print actionable guidance (enable-linger, or sudo install).

build_systemd_unit is a pure helper with unit tests for the system vs user
shape.

fix(service): honest exit-status checks for onboarding installer and launchctl

The onboarding daemon installer and the macOS launchctl branches had the same
bug as the CLI service command: .output()/.status() was checked only for a spawn

feat(rtk): auto-download the RTK binary on first use when missing

When RTK is not bundled or on PATH, OpenCrabs now downloads the pinned RTK

configured_context_window(), which only the OpenAI-compatible impl overrode.

fix(hot-reload): detect atomic-save config edits + refresh ctx-budget footer

The config watcher watched config.toml/keys.toml/commands.toml as individual
files. Editors and our own toml_edit writes save atomically (write temp, rename
over target), which changes the file's inode — a file-level watch stays bound to
the deleted inode and silently misses every later edit. That's why config/keys
edits (e.g. Telegram respond_to all->mention) didn't hot-reload and needed a
full restart, on the daemon and the TUI alike.

Watch the ~/.opencrabs directory instead and filter events by filename to the
three config files (the dir also holds the churning SQLite DB). Renames now
survive, so config, keys, commands, and the config-gated tool re-register all
reload reliably with no restart.

Also refresh the TUI context-budget footer on reload: context_max_tokens was
cached once at construction. Recompute it in the ConfigReloaded handler, and
send that event AFTER the provider swap completes so it reads the new window.
A changed providers.<name>.context_window now updates the footer immediately.

fix(daemon): systemd unit uses Restart=always so the daemon self-recovers

The Linux service unit used Restart=on-failure, which does not restart on a
clean exit (exit 0) — and the headless daemon exits 0 whenever its shutdown
future completes. So a restart that ended the process left the daemon dead with
no recovery, and the user had no idea how to bring it back. The macOS
LaunchAgent already uses KeepAlive=true (restarts on any exit); switch systemd
to Restart=always to match, so the daemon always comes back (except an explicit
systemctl stop).

docs(readme): daemon troubleshooting note for restart policy + hot-reload

Document that older service installs may still carry Restart=on-failure and can
be refreshed by re-running 'service install', and that config/keys/commands/
tools hot-reload so editing config never needs a daemon restart.

fix(zhipu): merge config.toml models into the GLM model picker

z.ai's /api/paas/v4/models is entitlement-gated and returns only the models the
key can access, so a brand-new GLM (e.g. a new glm-*) that the account hasn't
been granted, or that lives on the other endpoint_type, never appears — and
zhipu had no fallback (only MiniMax did). Merge the user's
[providers.zhipu].models from config.toml with the fetched list (first-wins
dedup) so a model can be pinned by exact id even when /models omits it.

fix(vision): native Xiaomi vision_model + Gemini fallback for resilience

Two gaps left analyze_image dead for the keyless Xiaomi promo:
1. Xiaomi shipped no vision_model, so active_provider_vision returned None and
   vision fell through to the Gemini path — which the keyless user has no key
   for, so analyze_image ended up unregistered. MiMo v2.5 is multimodal, so set
   vision_model = mimo-v2.5-pro in the defaults and example; analyze_image now
   routes to Xiaomi's own model via ProviderVisionTool, no Gemini needed.
2. No fallback: if the provider's vision endpoint fails (model/proxy rejects

fix(brain): normalize timestamps in paragraph_exists() to catch repeated incident entries

The RSI cycle accumulates violation-log entries in brain files (issue #197).
Each entry has a unique date/session ID, so the 70% line overlap check in
paragraph_exists() lets every new entry through as 'new content'.

Added normalize_incident_line() that strips ADDED/REPEAT date prefixes,
(session <hex>) fragments, standalone ISO dates, and (confirmed ...) suffixes
before comparison. The normalized overlap check runs as a 4th strategy after
exact substring, header match, and raw line overlap.

This means the same rule appended with different timestamps is now caught
as a duplicate and filtered out.

fix(brain): extend looks_like_failure_log() to catch plain-text incident entries

The existing guard (issue #111) only checks section headers (#/###) for
failure-count patterns. RSI was appending plain-text paragraphs like
'ADDED 2026-06-11 (session ba623fd1): Another quoting error...' that
walked right past the header-only check.

Now catches lines starting with ADDED/REPEAT that also contain 'session '
and digits. These are raw incident logs, not derived rules.

fix(brain): cap evidence entries in RSI prompt to prevent brain-file bloat

Issue #197: the RSI prompt told the model to 'Append the new date/session
as evidence' with no cap. Each new entry has a unique timestamp so dedup
guards let it through, causing indefinite accumulation (16+ entries in
the reported SOUL.md, 15KB of bloat).

Now caps at 2 evidence entries per rule, then uses an inline counter
'Violations: N, last: YYYY-MM-DD'. Full history stays in feedback ledger.

docs: document context_window override + the edit-or-ask config workflow

context_window was undocumented. Add a comprehensive README section: how auto
compaction works (transparent, 65% soft / 90% hard, percentage-based so it
scales), the 200k default as the battle-tested sweet spot for cloud models
(latest large non-flash models handle bigger windows robustly; locals want
~128k; the cost of >200k is just tokens), the per-provider override working on
every provider, and that both vision_model and context_window can be changed by

write_config, with config_manager reload as a fallback if hot-reload misses a

feat(telegram): markdown rich-message front-end (AST + parser + HTML fallback)

First slice of Telegram rich-message support. A small, single-purpose module
tree under channels/telegram/rich/ parses markdown into a wire-independent AST
(headings, paragraphs, nested/ordered/task lists, GFM tables with alignment,
code, blockquotes, inline + block math) and renders it to Telegram HTML.

The AST is deliberately independent of Telegram's InputRichMessage schema so
the parser and its tests don't churn when the rich-first serializer lands; the
same AST will drive both the rich path (sendRichMessage) and this HTML
fallback.

Wired conservatively: markdown_to_telegram_html now routes only table-
containing messages through the AST renderer (they previously rendered as raw
`| pipes |`); every other message keeps the existing line-based path, so the
sibling render assertions are untouched. 14 new tests; all 224 telegram tests
green.

Files: ast (types), inline/table/list/parse (front-end), render_html
(fallback), mod (entry points called only when needed).

fix(tui): project identifier badge uses brand orange, not yellow

The {.project} badge in the sessions list was rendered in Color::Yellow,
off the app palette. Match the orange (Rgb 215,100,20) used for the other
accents in this view.

fix(tui): show project badge in real time after assigning a session

Assigning a session to a project updated the database but not the in-memory
sessions list, so the {.project} badge only appeared after leaving and
re-entering the list (which reloads from the DB). Update the in-memory
session's project_id on a successful assign so the badge populates immediately.

feat(tui): per-project badge colours in the sessions list

Map each project to a stable colour from an on-brand palette (orange, amber,
cyan, teal, blue, light blue, soft white, pale blue-white) by project id, so
projects are distinguishable at a glance while staying within the app's
orange/cyan/white/blue family. Same project always renders the same colour.

feat(telegram): route task-list messages through the rich AST too

Extend the fallback routing from tables-only to a prefers_rich_render predicate
that also fires on `- [ ]` / `- [x]` task lists. The legacy line-based path
rendered those as literal `- [ ]` text; the AST renders them as ☐/☑. Ordinary
prose and plain bullet lists stay on the legacy path, so the sibling render
assertions are untouched.

feat(telegram): native sendRichMessage path for proactive sends

InputRichMessage takes the message as a `markdown` string that Telegram parses
server-side into rich blocks (tables, headings, nested lists, math) — so there
is no block JSON to construct. Added a small raw-API client (teloxide 0.17 has
no binding) that POSTs sendRichMessage with the model's markdown verbatim.

Wired rich-first into the telegram_send tool's `send` action: try the native
rich render, fall back to the prior plain-text send on any failure so a rich-API
hiccup never drops a message. Default-on, no config toggle.

The streaming reply path (edit-in-place + footer + chunking) is a larger,
separate integration and is left for a follow-up, ideally with the
sendRichMessageDraft / editMessageText rich_message schema.

feat(telegram): convert the final streamed reply to rich on completion

Streaming stays exactly as-is — intermediate edits remain HTML, token by token,
with the footer and 4096 chunking untouched. Only the final "done" edit of a
single-chunk streamed reply converts the message to native rich via
editMessageText's rich_message param: the raw model markdown (plus the plain
ctx footer) is handed to Telegram to render as tables/headings/lists/math.

On ANY failure the existing HTML edit runs unchanged, so the high-traffic
streaming path carries zero regression. Adds editMessageText rich support to
the raw-API client and factors the ok/error response handling into a shared
helper.

feat(telegram): gate native rich on real structure, not plain prose

Add has_rich_structure (table / ATX heading / list item / fenced code / block
math) and gate both native rich paths on it: the proactive telegram_send and
the final streamed-reply edit only go rich when the message actually carries
block structure. Plain prose — even with inline **bold**/`code` or an incidental
`*`/`#` — stays on the existing plain/HTML path so Telegram's markdown parser
never reinterprets stray characters.

Kept separate from prefers_rich_render (which still gates the HTML-fallback
routing) so broadening the native gate doesn't disturb the sibling render tests.

docs(readme): document Telegram native rich message formatting

Add a Messaging Integrations subsection covering the Bot API 10.1 rich
rendering: structured markdown (tables, headings, lists, task lists, code,
math) renders natively in Telegram, automatic with no toggle, on both the
final streamed reply and proactive sends, with silent HTML fallback and
plain prose left untouched.

fix(telegram): don't italicize intra-word underscores in the rich renderer

`custom_openai_compatible` was rendering as "customopenaicompatible" because
the inline parser treated `_openai_` as italic and ate the underscores. Require
underscore emphasis to sit at a word boundary on both sides (CommonMark's rule
for exactly this case), so snake_case identifiers stay literal while real
`use _this_ word` emphasis still works.

fix(telegram): restore blank-line spacing between blocks in the rich renderer

Routing a table-containing message through the AST renderer collapsed the prose
to single newlines, so paragraphs, headings, and lists ran together with no
breathing room. Separate block-level elements with a blank line (keeping list
items single-spaced) so the paragraph spacing from the source markdown survives.

fix(telegram): attempt native rich for replies of any length, not just single-chunk

The rich conversion was wired only into the single-chunk edit branch, so long
replies — exactly the ones with tables — took the multi-chunk delete+send path
and never tried sendRichMessage, landing on the ugly <pre> HTML fallback.

Lift the rich attempt above the chunk branching: a structured reply is now
delivered as a native rich message regardless of length (edit the streamed
placeholder if present, else send fresh), and only on failure does it fall
through to HTML chunking. The proactive telegram_send tool likewise sends
structured text whole through rich (chunking only the plain fallback) so a
table is never split across chunks.

perf(config): demote per-load config-load logging from info/debug to trace

merge_provider_keys logged one INFO line per custom provider (plus a summary)
on every Config::load(), and the load path logged several DEBUG lines each
time. With config loaded very frequently, this alone produced gigabytes of
near-identical log lines per day (the INFO ones fired even without -d). Move
all nine per-load config-load statements to trace so they're silent at info
and debug; they're still available when explicitly tracing config issues.

fix(telegram): never collapse allowed_users — union with config, don't overwrite

Onboarding apply_config wrote telegram allowed_users from a single input field
(loaded from allowed_users.first()), and the telegram_connect tool wrote it
straight from tool input — both a wholesale REPLACE. So a re-apply or a partial
reconnect silently collapsed the allowlist to one entry, locking out everyone
else with no human action.

Both now read the existing allowed_users from config.toml (the source of truth)
and union the new id(s) in, never dropping authorized users. The owner/first-id
handling is unchanged.

fix(config): snapshot last_good when config changes and parses, not once per process

last_good was saved exactly once per process — on the first successful LLM
response (a process-lifetime AtomicBool) — so a long-running daemon's snapshot
went stale for months, and a restart could overwrite a good snapshot with an
already-broken config (an LLM call succeeding says nothing about config
validity).

Move the snapshot into the config watcher's reload path: when config.toml
actually changes and parses cleanly (debounced, once per edit), copy it to
last_good. Recovery now always has the latest valid config.

perf(config): in-memory current-config mirror, refreshed by the watcher

config.toml was read + parsed + key-merged from disk on every request (~50x per
turn). Add a process-wide mirror: Config::current() returns a cheap Arc clone of
an in-memory copy that the config watcher refreshes the instant config.toml
changes (and that startup seeds). config.toml stays the source of truth and the
watcher is the only writer, so the mirror is never stale and never a drifting
shadow — it satisfies "load only when changed" with zero disk IO on the hot path.

Reserve disk-reading Config::load() for startup, the watcher, and write-then-
reread. Migrated the per-turn / per-message hot readers first: prompt_builder
(system-prompt build), load_brain_file, rsi_sync, trello idle timeout, and the
provider-swap paths in the telegram/discord/slack agents. Remaining read-only
load sites can be swept to current() incrementally.

feat(telegram): render structured intermediate messages as native rich too

Native rich was only on the final reply, but streamed responses are delivered
as intermediate messages (the final edit is often empty) — so real summaries
kept rendering as <pre>. Add send_rich_markdown_id (returns the new message id
for tracking) and a try_send_intermediate_rich helper, then wire it into all
five intermediate-delivery paths in the handler: a structured intermediate
(table / heading / list / math) is sent via sendRichMessage and tracked by id;
no structure or a rich rejection falls through to the existing HTML chunking.
Dedup/tracking key stays the raw text, consistent with the HTML path.

feat(prompt): instruct the model to format responses with headings, tables, fenced code

Add a RESPONSE FORMATTING section to the system brain: use headings for
sections, Markdown tables for tabular/status/comparison data instead of one
bullet per field, bullets only for true short lists, and fenced blocks for
code/commands. This steers the model toward the structure that now renders as
native rich blocks on Telegram (and degrades gracefully elsewhere), and away
from walls of single-bullet lines.

fix(service): probe unit file scope instead of relying on euid (#200)

cmd_service used running_as_root() for Start/Stop/Restart/Status/
Uninstall to decide system vs user systemctl scope. This fails when
the binary is run as root but units were installed as user-level
(systemctl restart opencrabs.service → unit not found).

Add unit_scope() which checks which path the unit file actually
exists at (/etc/systemd/system vs ~/.config/systemd/user) and falls
back to running_as_root() when neither exists (fresh install).

Install keeps using running_as_root() since that decides where to
write a new unit.

test(service): relocate unit-scope tests to src/tests, isolate with tempfile

Move the service-scope tests added with #200 out of the inline
`#[cfg(all(test, target_os = "linux"))] mod tests` in cli/commands.rs into
src/tests/service_scope_test.rs (our standard test location), gated on Linux
and registered in tests/mod.rs. Bumps `running_as_root` and `unit_scope_probe`
to pub(crate) as the test seam. Replaces the original shared temp dir keyed by
process id (which races under cargo's parallel runner) with a fresh
`tempfile::tempdir()` per test. Same seven cases, same assertions.

fix(service): resolve the invoking user's home under sudo for unit-scope probe

unit_scope() probed dirs::home_dir()/.config/systemd/user to detect a user-scope
unit, but under sudo that resolves to root's home (/root), not the invoking
user's — so a user-level unit was missed and operations wrongly fell back to
system scope (the exact root-binary + user-units case #200 targets). Resolve the
user's home from SUDO_USER (/home/<user>), matching the convention install
already writes into the unit's Environment=HOME=. Falls back to dirs::home_dir()
when not under sudo. Pure resolver user_home_from() is split out and tested.

fix(provider): handle orphan think close tags in streaming and non-streaming paths

Some models (Mimo, Qwen) occasionally skip the opening think tag and
emit only the closing tag. Previously, the close tag was treated as
literal text and all preceding content leaked as visible display output.

Streaming path (filter_think_tags): when inside_think is false and no
open tag is found, scan for orphan close tags. Text before the orphan
close is routed to the reasoning buffer; the close tag is consumed and
processing continues with any remaining display text. The generic HTML
comment closer is excluded from orphan detection as too generic.

Non-streaming path (strip_think_blocks): after stripping all
properly-paired think blocks, scan for orphan close tags and strip
everything before them.

Both functions promoted to pub(crate) for testability.

fix(provider): exclude bare `-->` orphan close by value, not index

The cherry-picked orphan-think fix skipped index 2 of STRIP_CLOSE_TAGS to keep
the generic `-->` from triggering orphan routing — but `-->` is also a candidate
inside the index-1 list, so prose like "a --> b" still got routed to reasoning.
Skip `-->` (and empty strings) by value across all lists in both filter_think_tags
(streaming) and strip_think_blocks (non-streaming), so `</think>` and
`<!-- /reasoning -->` still trigger orphan routing while bare arrows don't.

Also fix a typo in the relocated test: orphan_close_empty_before fed `<think>`
(an open tag) where its own comment says "close tag at the very start"; the
intended `</think>` now exercises the orphan-close-at-position-0 path it claims.

fix(telegram): send fresh rich message instead of editing the placeholder into rich

Native rich never actually rendered in the bot flow: the final reply edited the
streamed HTML placeholder into a rich message via editMessageText, and editing a
normal message into a rich one glitches the client — overlapping renders during
the transition, and a stale pre-edit (HTML) version after a refresh / chat
switch. Only a fresh sendRichMessage renders clean (as the manual DM test
showed).

Deliver the final structured reply as a fresh sendRichMessage and delete the
streamed placeholder only after it succeeds (so a failure leaves the placeholder
for the HTML fallback). Removes the now-unused edit_rich_markdown. Intermediates
and proactive sends were already fresh sends, so every rich path is now fresh —
no edit-to-rich anywhere.

fix(telegram): wire native rich into resume_session final delivery too

resume_session (the resumed-turn delivery path) had no rich path at all — its
final reply always went out as HTML, so any structured reply delivered through
a resumed turn stayed old-format while handle_message went rich. Add the same
fresh-send rich delivery (send a fresh sendRichMessage, delete the placeholder
on success, fall back to the existing HTML edit otherwise), so both delivery
paths render structured replies as native rich consistently.

feat(telegram): gate native rich behind channels.telegram.rich_messages, default off

Native rich messages are unreadable on Telegram Web and older clients — those
show a "not supported, update Telegram" placeholder and the rich API has no text
fallback. Defaulting rich on meant a real chunk of users got an unreadable
message. Make it opt-in: a new channels.telegram.rich_messages flag (default
false) gates every native sendRichMessage path (the two final-delivery paths,
the intermediate helper, and proactive telegram_send) via should_send_native_rich,
which checks the flag (through the zero-disk config mirror) AND has_rich_structure.

Off by default, the universal HTML rendering is used — which works on every
client and was already improved (aligned tables, ☐/☑ task items, proper
spacing). On, structured replies render as native rich. Documents the flag in
config.toml.example and corrects the README (which claimed no-toggle/always-on).

feat(telegram): responsive table rendering for the HTML path — cards for wide tables

The HTML fallback (used by default, and on Web/old clients) rendered every table
as a fixed-width <pre> monospace grid, which overflows the narrow Telegram/Web
view on wide tables (horizontal scroll, cramped) — the TUI fits because it sizes
columns to the terminal; Telegram can't.

Render responsively: keep the compact aligned <pre> grid for tables that fit a
phone (<= 40 cols), but switch wider tables to a layout that can't overflow — a
`key: value` list for 2-column tables (header dropped, columns self-labelling),
and one card per row (bold title + "Header: value" lines) for 3+ columns. Cards
preserve inline formatting since they aren't inside <pre>. Small tables look
exactly as before; wide ones now fit any screen.

fix(tui): keep in-progress input when a queued message enters mid-turn

When a queued message was injected during a streaming response, the
foreground post-hook cleared input_buffer, wiping whatever the user had
started typing for their next message — and arrow-up could not recover
it. Drop only the queue entry now; leave input_buffer untouched.

Also guard the arrow-up dequeue-for-edit so it only fires on an empty
input, so recalling a queued message never clobbers live typing.

fix(tui): bind Ctrl+W / Ctrl+Backspace to word-delete for terminals without Option-as-Meta

Alt+Backspace only reaches us when the terminal sends Option as Meta
(ESC + DEL). Terminals that don't (Warp's default) never produce the
ALT modifier, so word-delete silently did nothing there. Accept Ctrl+W
(readline word-erase, a literal byte every terminal sends) and
Ctrl+Backspace as cross-terminal fallbacks.

feat(tools): add pdf_to_images for rendering PDF pages the text path can't show

A PDF with plenty of text but embedded figures/screenshots takes the
text-extraction path on ingest, so the images never reach a vision
model and the agent can't see them. Add a pdf_to_images tool that
renders requested pages (page_range/pages) to PNG and returns the page
paths; the agent then views each with analyze_image one at a time, the
same pattern the scanned-PDF flow already uses. Also append a hint to
the text-path ingest output so the agent knows the renderer exists when
the user asks about something visual.

fix(tools): register pdf_to_images in the interactive TUI path too

The tool was registered in both non-interactive run paths but not in the
TUI session setup, so it was missing from interactive chat — the main
surface where users share PDFs.

fix(pdf): preserve scanned PDFs on render failure instead of deleting them

A scanned/image PDF with no extractable text went to the vision-render
path, which passed the shared tmp/files/ dir as the render output dir.
When no renderer was available, render_pdf_pages' cleanup wiped that
whole directory — deleting the PDF just saved (and other sessions'
files). The failure path then returned no path at all, so the agent
ran blind `find` and never located the file.

Render into a dedicated {pdf}_pages/ subdir so cleanup can't reach the
saved PDF, and on failure keep the PDF and inject its real path with
guidance (pdf_to_images / parse_document). Renderer-missing error now
gives the poppler install commands.

feat(install): install poppler alongside the binary for PDF rendering

Scanned/image PDFs are rendered to page images via poppler (pdftoppm).
The one-line installer now installs it best-effort across brew/apt/dnf/
pacman/apk, and the README documents it as a dependency with per-OS
install commands.

fix(tui): download whispercrabs to ~/.local/bin, not the brain dir

The brain dir (~/.opencrabs) is for agent state, not executables.
New whispercrabs downloads now go to ~/.local/bin (platform data dir
on Windows). An existing copy already in the brain dir is reused in
place — not moved or deleted.

feat(tui): detect shell-escaped and PDF/doc drag-dropped paths

Terminals shell-escape dropped paths (spaces become \\ ), so a dragged
screenshot like 'Screenshot 1.png' failed Path::exists() and silently
never attached. Resolve the real path (raw, then unquoted, then
POSIX-unescaped) before checking existence, storing the real path so
analyze_image can read it. Also detect .pdf/.docx/etc. drag-dropped
paths and surface the path + a parse_document/pdf_to_images hint
instead of inlining binary bytes.

fix(tools): bounce read_file on binary media to the right vision/parse tool

Reading an image/video/document as text yields garbage, and the agent
would loop on read_file for a dropped screenshot instead of viewing it.
read_file now detects binary media by extension and returns a redirect:
images -> analyze_image, video -> analyze_video, PDFs/docs ->
parse_document (and pdf_to_images for scanned PDF pages).

fix(browser): React-safe browser_type — replace value + dispatch input/change

The focused-element path did document.activeElement.value += text: it
APPENDED to placeholder/stale text (the 'placeholder + credentials'
garbage) and assigned .value directly, which framework-controlled
inputs (React/Vue/Svelte, NextAuth) ignore — their value tracker never
sees the change, so a later submit reads an empty field and the form
never submits.

Now both the selector and focused paths resolve the element, REPLACE
the value via the native HTMLInputElement/TextAreaElement value setter
(so the framework's tracker registers it), and dispatch bubbling input
and change events so onChange fires. Values are JSON-encoded into the
script so quotes/backslashes/newlines can't break it. contenteditable
is handled too.

feat(agent): detect reasoning repetition loops

Add rolling-window repetition detection for reasoning/thinking content
during streaming, matching the existing text-repetition guard but with
larger thresholds tuned for legitimate deep reasoning:

- REASONING_REPEAT_WINDOW: 4096 bytes (vs 2048 for text)
- REASONING_REPEAT_MIN_MATCH: 300 bytes (vs 200 for text)

the stream is terminated with StopReason::EndTurn and a warning is
logged. This prevents runaway thinking loops where the model rewrites
the same reasoning paragraph indefinitely without producing output.

fix(config): auto-repair broken config.toml and never poison last-good

A malformed config.toml (e.g. an array left unterminated by a hand edit)
made the entire file fail to parse, which took down config loading. The
approval check then had no config and defaulted to "ask" — flipping
auto-always (yolo) users into tool-approval prompts.

Two compounding defects fixed:

- The config watcher called Config::load() (which already recovers from
  last-good, so it returns Ok even when config.toml is broken) and then
  raw-copied the broken file over config.last_good.toml. A single bad edit
  poisoned BOTH the live config and its snapshot at once, leaving recovery
  nothing valid to fall back to. The watcher now skips the snapshot when the
  load was a recovery, and save_last_good_config refuses to snapshot a
  config that does not parse.

- On a parse failure, Config::load now first attempts a mechanical repair of
  the broken file (close unterminated arrays), gated on the result
  re-parsing as valid TOML. The fix is saved back to disk with the broken
  original backed up to <file>.autofix.bak. If it can't be safely repaired,
  it falls back to last-known-good. Repair logic and file IO live in
  config/repair.rs, keeping types.rs to a thin call.

fix(evolve): retry health-check spawn on transient ETXTBSY/ENOENT

evolve writes the downloaded binary to a temp path and immediately execs it
with `--version` for the pre-swap health check. A binary written moments ago
can briefly fail to exec even though it is valid: ETXTBSY (os 26 — the kernel
still treats it as open for write) or a transient ENOENT (os 2) before the
write settles. This broke evolve on a VPS — one run failed to spawn with os 2,
the next with os 26, both on the same 79MB binary.

Retry the health-check spawn up to 5 times with backoff when the spawn fails
with os error 2 or 26, instead of treating the first transient miss as a real
failure and rolling back.

fix(logging): demote per-SSE-chunk [STREAM_RAW] logs from debug to trace

The raw-SSE-chunk log fired once per streamed chunk at debug level, so in
debug mode (the only mode that writes log files) every response flooded the
log with hundreds of [STREAM_RAW] lines — the "infinite stream logs" a user
saw in ~/.opencrabs/logs. Per-chunk raw dumps are trace-level firehose detail,
not debug; move both lines to trace so they're opt-in for deep diagnostics.

fix(evolve): single-flight + process-unique temp to stop concurrent-evolve race

Server logs showed the real cause of the "health check failed to spawn"
rollback: TWO evolves ran at the same instant — a manual `evolve` and the
background auto-updater — both downloading to the same /root/opencrabs.evolve_tmp
and exec'ing it together. One hit ETXTBSY (sibling still writing), the other
ENOENT (sibling deleted the temp on its own failure). A later solo run then
swapped the binary fine, which is why it was "already on latest" after restart.

- Single-flight: a real (non-check-only) evolve takes an in-process guard;
  a second concurrent run bails immediately instead of racing. check_only
  stays exempt (read-only).
- Process-unique temp name (evolve_tmp.<pid>) so two separate processes can't
  collide on one file either.

Together with the spawn retry, this removes the collision rather than just
retrying through it. Local commit for a future release — NOT part of v0.3.44.

fix(mission-control): detail popup now fits content instead of fixed 70% height

The popup was hardcoded to 70% of screen height regardless of content,
leaving massive empty space below short entries.

Now estimates content height by counting visual lines (accounting for
soft-wrapping), then uses min(content_height, 70%) as the popup size.
Popup stays centered vertically in the available area.

fix(glob): bound the walk — symlink-safe, off-executor, capped, with timeout

terminates), has no entry or time bound, and ran synchronously on the async
executor. With zero matches it traversed the entire tree before returning.

- ignore::WalkBuilder with follow_links(false) — the symlink loop is the most
  likely cause of a multi-minute hang.
- Run it in spawn_blocking with a 30s timeout so it can never wedge the agent.
- Cap at 500k scanned entries; report truncation.
- Prune node_modules / .git / target / .cache.
- Keep gitignore DISABLED and descend into dotdirs so files under ~/.opencrabs
  (whose .gitignore is `*`) are still found; still filter hidden FILES unless
  include_hidden, matching the old behaviour.

missing target. Local commit for a future release.

fix(voice): prevent Voicebox TTS timeout on long text

## Problem
Voicebox TTS (Kokoro engine) had a hard 120s timeout. Text over ~4000 chars
timed out and fell back to Piper, causing audible gaps and inconsistent audio
quality. Voicebox also received raw markdown (code fences, headers, URLs)
while only Piper used clean_for_tts.

## Changes

### Dynamic timeout (voicebox_tts.rs)
Timeout now scales with text length: 60ms per char, clamped to 120s-600s.
A 5000-char response gets ~300s instead of the old hard 120s cap.

### Text chunking + markdown cleaning (service.rs)
- clean_for_tts applied to ALL TTS providers, not just Piper
- Text > 1500 chars split at sentence boundaries (. ! ? newline)
- Each chunk synthesized independently, audio bytes concatenated
- 10 new tests for chunking/splitting logic

## Files
- src/channels/voice/voicebox_tts.rs — dynamic timeout, removed unused constant
- src/channels/voice/service.rs — shared clean_for_tts, chunking, concat, tests

fix(evolve): sweep stale transient restart units before scheduling

Each scheduled restart creates a transient opencrabs-evolve-<pid> unit.
We can't pass --collect to systemd-run (unsupported on systemd < v240,
RHEL 7 / CentOS 7), so finished units linger and failed restarts pile up
in the failed state without bound. Run 'systemctl reset-failed
opencrabs-evolve-*.service' (portable to every targeted systemd version)
right before scheduling a fresh restart, so spent units never accumulate.

fix(channels): TUI takes priority over a running daemon for channel locks

A background instance (e.g. an 'opencrabs daemon' auto-started by systemd
on boot) holds the per-credential token lock, so when the user opens the
TUI its acquire_token_lock is denied and the interactive session silently
gets no Telegram — the channel was already set up, but the user has to
'reconnect' to wrest the getUpdates poll back.

On TUI startup (interactive only, never headless), shut down any other
live same-profile instance holding channel locks before reconciling
channels: stop its systemd unit so Restart=always can't resurrect it,
SIGTERM the PID for a bare terminal daemon, escalate to SIGKILL if it
ignores SIGTERM, then take the locks and show a banner. The daemon stays
down until the user starts it again.

State the rule that only one runs per profile and the TUI takes priority,

feat(cron): honor timezone, validate schedule with next-run feedback, document format

Three fixes for the cron format the agent kept tripping on:

- Timezone was stored but ignored: is_due/next_run_after computed purely in
  UTC, so a job set to '9am America/New_York' fired at 9am UTC. Add chrono-tz
  and a shared schedule_util that interprets the expression in the job's zone
  (DST-aware) and converts back to UTC. The tool and CLI now reject an unknown
  timezone instead of silently falling back.

- No confirmation feedback: creating a job now echoes the next few run times
  in the job's timezone so the agent (and user) can verify intent before
  treating it as done. A wrong day-of-week parses fine but the next-run list
  exposes it.

- Format undocumented: day-of-week is 1-7 = Sun-Sat (1=Sunday, 0 invalid) and
  there are no @daily macros, both common mistakes. Document in README (with a
  format table), AGENTS.md, the tool param description, and the invalid-cron
  error message; steer toward day names (Mon-Fri).

Also route cron Telegram delivery through the same renderer as interactive
replies: honor channels.telegram.rich_messages (native rich message when on +
structured), otherwise our markdown-to-HTML parser with ParseMode HTML and
4096-char chunking, instead of the fragile legacy parse_mode=Markdown.

feat(cron): wire Discord and Slack result delivery

Cron jobs could only deliver to Telegram; Discord and Slack just logged

- Slack: chat.postMessage with 'Bearer <token>'; text renders mrkdwn,

fix(preempt): never run instance preemption against the real workspace from tests

Critical regression from today's TUI-priority work: the non-ignored test
no_foreign_instance_means_no_preemption called the real
preempt_other_profile_instances(), which scans ~/.opencrabs/locks/ and sends
SIGTERM/SIGKILL to every live same-profile instance it finds. Running the
test suite (e.g. the agent invoking 'cargo test' from inside the TUI) thus
KILLED the user's running instances with no panic or crash report (plain
SIGKILL).

Split the killing core into preempt_instances_in(lock_dir, stop_services),
parameterized by the lock directory and whether to stop systemd services.
The public preempt_other_profile_instances() is the only caller that targets
the real ~/.opencrabs/locks/ and real services, and it is invoked solely from
TUI startup. Tests now drive preempt_instances_in against a TempDir with
service-stopping disabled, so they can never touch the real workspace or
signal a real process. Added coverage for empty-dir, dead-PID, and
other-profile cases; the live-kill test spawns and signals only its own
child in a temp dir.

fix(brain): rebuild system brain from disk when brain files change (#213)

The system brain was assembled once at startup and cached as a static
string (`AgentService.default_system_brain`, `ChannelFactory.shared_brain`),
so edits to brain files via manual edit, `write_opencrabs_file`, or
`self_improve` stayed invisible until the process restarted. The on-demand
`load_brain_file` tool already read fresh from disk; only the system-prompt
path was frozen.

Fix: a `BrainRebuild` handle rebuilds the brain from disk on the next turn
whenever a brain file's mtime advances, and otherwise returns the cached
render byte-for-byte so the provider prompt cache stays warm when nothing
changed (verified prompt caching is active via cache_read/creation tokens).

- `BrainLoader::brain_files_mtime` — cheap `*.md` dir stat, no content reads.
- `BrainRebuild` (Arc-backed, cheap clone) seeded with the startup brain;
  `render()` is mtime-gated. `AgentService::live_system_brain` is the single
  source of truth for the prompt sent each turn.
- Wired at both per-turn injection sites (context.rs, tool_loop.rs), the TUI
  agent service, and channel agents (factory carries runtime_info so the
  rebuilt brain keeps its model/provider/working-dir lines).
- `/models` provider rebuilds carry the handle (and its warm cache) forward
  so they don't revert to a static brain.
- config.toml and keys.toml are unaffected; token-estimate floors keep using
  the startup seed (cosmetic only).

fix(tools): JIT-activate an extended tool when called by name (#214)

With `lazy_tools` on, only CORE tools plus those discovered via `tool_search`
ship in the system prompt, but `registry.execute()` runs ANY registered tool
by name. So a model that calls an extended tool directly (no prior
`tool_search`) is guessing params with no schema in context, the call fails on
bad params, and nothing ever promotes the tool, so the next turn guesses blind
again. A permanent gap, hit hardest on fat-param tools like `telegram_send`.

Fix: `execute()` activates a non-core tool for the session right after name
resolution and BEFORE validation, so even a failed first call surfaces the real
schema on the next request and the model self-corrects instead of looping.
No-op for CORE tools; harmless when `lazy_tools` is off (the active set is never
consulted). Single choke point covers both the approval and direct exec paths.

Tests: an extended tool that fails validation is still in the session active
set afterward (activation precedes validation); a core-named tool is never
added.

fix(rsi): don't count pre-execution misses against tool success rate (#214)

A tool called blind (no schema in context) that fails on bad params, or a
hallucinated name that never resolves, was recorded as `tool_failure`, the same
event used for genuine runtime failures. Since `stats_by_dimension("tool_")`
computes success rate over every `tool_%` event, these pre-execution misses
dragged down the reliability of tools that never actually ran and failed.

Fix: classify the two pre-execution error cases (`NotFound`, `InvalidInput`)
via `ToolError::is_pre_execution_miss()` and record them as `discovery_miss`
instead. That event is NOT `tool_`-prefixed, so it falls outside the
success-rate numerator AND denominator, while staying visible in the event-type
breakdown and queryable for "what is the model guessing blind" analysis.
Genuine failures (tool ran and errored, or returned success=false) stay
`tool_failure`. Applied at both `Err(e)` arms in the tool loop.

This complements the JIT activation: most blind calls now succeed from turn 2,
and the rare first-call miss no longer pollutes the stats.

Tests: `is_pre_execution_miss` covers each variant; a ledger test proves a
`discovery_miss` keeps a tool at 100% while the same event as `tool_failure`
would halve it.

docs(brain): require a tool_search reminder when naming extended tools (#214)

Brain templates named extended tools (`analyze_image`, `message`) as if
directly callable, which invites the exact blind call #214 fixes: the model
calls them with no schema in context and wastes the first attempt.

- TOOLS.md: state the authoring convention. Whenever a brain file names a
  specific extended tool, pair the mention with a `tool_search` reminder.
- AGENTS.md: apply it to the image/voice handling notes (`analyze_image`,

The JIT activation recovers a blind call on the next turn, so this is the
belt-and-suspenders half: avoid the wasted round-trip in the first place.

fix(brain): move extended-tool tool_search guidance to preamble + RSI (#214)

The #214 brain-file convention was put in the TOOLS.md/AGENTS.md templates,
but templates are seeded copy-if-absent (profile.rs:366), so the edit only
reaches brand-new profiles. Every existing user already has their own brain
files and would never see it on upgrade. Wrong surface for a rule that must
reach everyone.

Relocate it to the two compiled-in surfaces that DO reach every user:

- Preamble (`BRAIN_PREAMBLE`): the runtime rule. CORE tools carry their schema
  by default; every other tool's schema is absent until `tool_search`, so
  calling a non-core tool by name from memory guesses params blind and the
  first call likely fails validation. Now stated explicitly on the existing
  PROACTIVE TOOL DISCOVERY line. Pushed into every brain build, so it lands
  for all users regardless of their customized brain files.
- RSI prompt (`RSI_AGENT_PROMPT`): the authoring rule. `self_improve` writes
  brain files autonomously, so when it authors a rule naming a non-core tool
  it must pair the mention with a tool_search reminder (without restating the
  global rule the preamble already carries).
- Revert the template edits: the guidance now lives where it propagates, and
  duplicating it in the seed-once templates would only drift.

fix(telegram): isolate sessions per forum topic (#215)

#130 fixed the reply ADDRESS (replies land in the right forum topic), but
session resolution still keyed on `chat_id` alone, so every topic in a
supergroup shared one session and context bled across topics. This scopes the
CONVERSATION to the topic.

- `session_resolve`: `chat_id_suffix` / `build_session_title` take an
  `Option<i32>` topic. A real topic becomes `[chat:<id>:topic:<tid>]`; base
  chats stay `[chat:<id>]`. A base title never ends with `:topic:<n>]` and a
  topic title never ends with the bare `[chat:<id>]`, so the
  `find_session_by_title_suffix` `LIKE '%suffix'` lookups never cross-resolve.
- `topic_session_id` gates on `is_topic_message`, so only genuine forum topics
  isolate. DMs, non-forum groups, the General topic, and plain reply-threads
  resolve to `None` and keep the exact pre-topic behaviour.
- `TelegramState.chat_sessions` now keys on `(chat_id, Option<i32>)`;
  `register_session_chat` / `chat_session` thread the topic. The forward
  `session_chats` map (approval routing) stays topic-agnostic.
- Handler ingest, `/new`, and the callback/`/sessions`-switch paths all pass
  the resolved topic. The legacy (pre-suffix) fallback is skipped for topic
  messages so a topic never adopts and rewrites the old shared row.
- Incoming-line log now includes `topic_id`.

Existing supergroups get a one-time split: the current `[chat:<id>]` row
stays the base/General session, and each non-general topic spins a fresh
session on its next message.

Tests: suffix/title topic format, `is_topic_message` gating, composite-map
isolation, and a DB test proving base and topic suffixes never cross-resolve.

fix(cron): double-fire on first tick when near cron boundary (#224)

When a job's first-ever tick landed within 60s of a cron boundary, the
scheduler fired twice. Root cause: tick() computed next_run_after(job, now)
instead of next_run_after(job, boundary). For a new job at 10:59:44 with
boundary 11:00:00, this set next_run_at to 11:00:00 (same boundary). The
next tick at 11:00:44 saw 11:00:00 <= 11:00:44 and fired again.

Fix: derive the anchor from job.next_run_at (existing scheduled) or
re-derive the boundary from the cron expression (first-run path), so
next_run_after always resolves to the NEXT boundary, not the current one.

feat(brain): add /goal command with autonomous LLM-judged goal loop

Implements a Claude Code /goal inspired system where the agent works
toward a user-defined goal autonomously, evaluated by an LLM judge
after each turn.

## Architecture

- `src/brain/goal/` — self-contained module (types, judge, manager)
  - `types.rs` — GoalVerdict, JudgeDecision, GoalDecision enums
  - `judge.rs` — LLM judge with structured JSON verdict parsing
  - `manager.rs` — GoalManager with full CRUD + evaluate_after_turn
  - `mod.rs` — re-exports

- `src/migrations/20260626000001_add_goal_state.sql` — goal_state table
- `src/db/models.rs` — GoalState model with from_row/new

## How it works

1. User (or agent via tool) calls `/goal <description>`
2. Goal state persisted to DB with turn budget (default 20)
3. After each tool-loop iteration, if a goal is active:
   - Judge LLM evaluates last response vs goal
   - CONTINUE: injects continuation prompt, re-enters loop
   - DONE: marks goal completed, breaks normally
   - Budget exhausted: pauses goal
4. Fail-open: judge errors continue the loop rather than abort
5. Max 3 consecutive parse failures before auto-pause

## Slash command

`/goal <text>` — set new goal
`/goal status` — show current goal
`/goal pause` / `/goal resume` — control execution
`/goal clear` — remove goal

fix(tools): surface tools.toml parse errors instead of dropping every tool (#235)

DynamicToolLoader::read_config used `toml::from_str().unwrap_or_default()`,
so a single TOML error (e.g. a duplicate key) silently collapsed the whole
file to an empty config — all dynamic tools vanished with no log, the only
trace being "Reloaded 0 dynamic tool(s)". Worse, the mutating paths read the
same way, so an add/remove on an unparseable file would overwrite it from an
empty config and destroy every tool on disk.

read_config now returns a Result: a MISSING file is still an empty config
(fresh setup), but a parse/read error is logged at ERROR and returned as
Err. Callers handle it deliberately:

- load() degrades to zero tools (a bad file must never crash startup) and
  relies on the logged ERROR.
- reload() returns Err and bails BEFORE unregistering anything, so a bad
  edit can't strip the live registry down to zero.
- add_tool/remove_tool/set_enabled propagate the Err, refusing to overwrite
  a valid-but-unparseable file — the data-loss path is closed.
- tool_manage 'list' and 'reload' now report the parse error to the user
  (with a hint that a duplicate key drops the entire file) instead of
  showing an empty list or "Reloaded 0".
