fix(telegram): include replied-to author identity in reply context

Reply context identified the replied-to author by bare first name only, so
the agent lost the @username and numeric user ID and could not tell exactly
who was being replied to (or disambiguate users in a group).

Extract format_reply_sender and render a human as "{name}{handle}, ID {id}"
— the same shape already used to identify the current sender — while the bot
still collapses to "assistant". The label flows through format_reply_context
unchanged.

fix(telegram): recover the EXACT replied-to message by id, not the latest

Field logs showed a user replying to an older bot message got the bot's
NEWEST reply injected as reply context instead — the recovery fell back to
"the most recent assistant message" because Telegram delivers rich bot
messages with empty text, leaving the handler nothing to match on. It only
ever worked when replying to the bot's latest message.

Persist every bot reply's Telegram message_id and look the replied-to
message up by id:

- capture the final reply bubble's message_id across all delivery paths
  (sendRichMessage via send_rich_markdown_id, in-place edit, chunked send);
- store it as platform_message_id on the channel_messages row — for DMs too
  (lookup-only; DM conversation context still comes from session messages);
- add ChannelMessageRepository::content_by_platform_message_id;
- in reply recovery, resolve the exact message by reply.id first, keeping the
  old last-assistant-message heuristic only as a fallback for messages sent
  before id capture.

test(telegram): pin exact replied-to message lookup by platform id

content_by_platform_message_id returns the message matching the given
Telegram id even when a newer bot message exists, and None on an unknown id
(so the caller falls back to its heuristic).

fix(telegram): stop fabricating reply context when content is unretrievable

Field logs showed the real failure mode: when the exact-id lookup missed
(message sent before id capture, or a cron message that stores no id), the
recovery fell back to "the most recent bot message" and injected it as
[Replying to assistant: "..."]. The model then confidently described that
stale, mismatched message as the reply target — every "yeah I can see it"
was a hallucination built on the wrong content.

Remove the guess. When we genuinely cannot read the replied-to bot message,
emit an explicit marker (resolve_reply_context) telling the agent the content
is unavailable and to NOT guess, summarize, or describe it — ask the user to
quote it instead. Honest "I can't see it" beats a confident wrong answer.

fix(cron): persist delivered Telegram message id for reply recovery

Cron-delivered messages were sent straight via the Bot API and never stored,
so replying to a cron message (e.g. a stats report) found no content — the
reply handler then guessed the wrong message and the model fabricated around
it. This is the path behind the field reports of "it lied about seeing my
cron message".

deliver_telegram now captures the delivered message's Telegram id (from
sendRichMessage, or the sendMessage response for the HTML path) and records
it in channel_messages keyed by platform_message_id, threading the pool down
from execute_job. A later reply to that message is then recovered exactly by
id instead of falling back to a wrong guess.

feat(rsi): keep recoverable tool failures out of the success-rate denominator (#236)

The RSI banned working built-in tools because environmental/recoverable
outcomes were logged as plain tool_failure and dragged success rates down —
e.g. hashline_edit's stale-hash "file may have changed" errors (recovered by
re-reading) gave it a 9% rate, which the RSI escalated to "blanket DO NOT USE".

New brain::feedback_policy module classifies a failed call as recoverable when
it is environmental or user-driven (hashline stale-hash, channel-send not
connected, follow_up_question cancelled/timed-out). record_tool_feedback now
logs those under a non-tool_ event ("recoverable_failure") so they stay
queryable but never count against the tool's success rate — mirroring how
discovery_miss is already excluded. Genuine defects still record as
tool_failure. Policy lives in its own small module; the call site stays thin.

feat(rsi): refuse self_improve rules that ban built-in tools (#236)

The RSI escalated hashline_edit to a "blanket DO NOT USE" directive in the
brain files. Banning a built-in removes capability rather than fixing
anything — their failures are environmental/recoverable, not defects.

Add catalog::is_protected_builtin (core set + channel/browser/runtime
built-ins) and a self_improve_guards module whose bans_builtin_tool guard
rejects content that prohibits a protected tool. It is precise about the
ban's object: "do not use hashline_edit" / "DO NOT USE it" under a
### hashline_edit heading are rejected, while routing guidance ("prefer
edit_file over hashline_edit for large files") and command rules ("never use
git add -A") pass. Wired into both self_improve write paths (apply + update)
alongside the existing failure-log guard. Logic lives in its own module; the
call sites stay one-liners.

fix(channels): restart dead channel agents on reconcile (fixes #239)

reconcile_* keyed "running" off handles.contains_key(name), which never
checks whether the agent task is still alive. When a channel agent crashes
or exits, its JoinHandle lingers in the map, so an enabled channel was
treated as running and never restarted. For WhatsApp this wedged pairing:
the dead agent left a stale handle, every later enabled=true reconcile was a
no-op, no fresh agent ran, and the pairing QR never reappeared (UI stuck on
"Starting WhatsApp connection...").

Add a pure, testable channel_action(should_run, alive) -> Start|Stop|Noop and
a handle_alive() liveness check (handle.is_finished()), and route all five
reconcile paths (telegram/whatsapp/discord/slack/trello) through them. A dead
or never-started agent now yields Start, so it (re)starts; start overwrites
the stale handle. Unit tests cover the decision matrix.

Same root cause as the first-time-onboard no-QR report (#240): a never-started
agent (no handle) now also yields Start on enable. The first-time QR path
still needs live verification for a possible subscribe-before-emit race, so
#240 stays open.

fix(whatsapp): show pairing QR on connect and force fresh re-pair on reset (fixes #240)

Two timing bugs left the onboarding QR blank. The agent emits a QR, but:

1. The QR broadcast had no replay, so a connect that subscribed AFTER the
   agent already emitted saw nothing until the next ~20s refresh (the "press
   Enter twice" symptom). WhatsAppState now stores the last QR and the connect
   flow replays it to a fresh subscriber immediately.

2. Reset wiped session.db on disk but the live agent kept its in-memory auth
   and was never restarted, so it never re-paired and no fresh QR appeared.
   WhatsAppState gains a restart request; reconcile_whatsapp honors it by
   aborting the live agent so it restarts against the wiped session, dropping
   old auth at runtime. The connect/reset handler sets the request (and clears
   the stale QR) before re-enabling.

Tests cover QR replay (latest wins) and the restart request (set, clears stale
QR, consumed once).

fix(whatsapp): authorize the paired owner, confirm via agent, lock QR after connect (fixes #245)

After pairing, the owner got no response, there was no real confirmation, and
the QR reappeared. Three causes, three fixes:

- No response: the owner filter compared the sender to config allowed_phones[0]
  (and read it from a HashSet non-deterministically), so any mismatch with the
  real paired number dropped the owner's own messages. Replaced with a pure,
  number-agnostic wa_should_respond: open mode when no allow list; the paired
  account messaging its own self-chat (is_from_me && sender == chat) is always
  the owner; an explicitly allow-listed contact is also accepted. A config or
  paired-number mismatch can no longer lock the owner out.
- Owner identity: on PairSuccess the real paired number (PairSuccess.id) is
  pinned to channels.whatsapp.bot_owner and appended to allowed_phones if
  absent, so the person who scanned is the authoritative owner.
- No confirmation: on connect the bot now runs a real agent turn in the
  persistent WhatsApp session and sends the reply into the owner self-chat;
  a failure broadcasts an error so onboarding shows failure, not a hollow
  "connected".
- QR reappear: WhatsAppState gains a connected flag; broadcast_qr is a no-op
  once connected and the stale QR is cleared, re-enabled on reset.

Tests: wa_should_respond decision matrix (self-chat, contact, allow-list,
+ normalization) and the QR-locked-after-connect behavior.

fix(whatsapp): greet once per connection, not on every reconnect

Keepalive timeouts force frequent reconnects, each emitting Event::Connected.
The handler spawned send_connection_greeting on every one, so the owner was
spammed with the same confirmation repeatedly while it looked hardcoded. Guard
on the connected flag (set on connect, cleared only by a user reset) so the
greeting fires once per pairing/run. Also stop dictating the greeting wording:
the prompt now asks for a short natural first message in the agent's own voice
instead of a fixed 'online and ready' line.

fix(whatsapp): disconnect the live client before aborting on restart/stop

A pairing reset (or disabling the channel) aborted the agent's JoinHandle,
but aborting the task only drops the bot.run() future. whatsapp-rust runs
its keepalive and read loop on independent detached tasks, so the old socket
kept pinging and lingered as a second linked-device companion alongside the
freshly-paired one. Two companions on one session make WhatsApp drop a
socket, so inbound messages landed on an orphaned connection and never got a
reply (the keepalive 'dead socket' was the symptom, not the cause). Disconnect
the stored client first so the transport is torn down and auto-reconnect is
disabled before the task is aborted and a new agent spawned.

fix(whatsapp): resilient idempotent resend so a skipped device can't drop replies

wacore's parallel encrypt fan-out skips any recipient device whose Signal
session is not yet established (logs 'session ... not found. Skipping.'), and
the server then rejects the WHOLE stanza with error 400 — so a reply to a chat
that has a freshly-seen or stale linked device silently never arrives even
though the agent produced it. send_message does not surface that async 400, so
it cannot be retried reactively. Route the greeting and agent replies through
send_resilient: send, then resend once after a short delay reusing the SAME
message id. The first attempt's prekey fetch establishes the missing session as
a side effect, so the second lands; the shared id makes the pair idempotent
(recipients dedupe by id) so a first attempt that did deliver is never shown
twice.

fix(channels): never inherit a disabled or absent provider into new sessions

create_channel_session copied the most-recent session's provider/model
verbatim. A stale pick (a provider the user has since disabled, e.g. a custom
provider with enabled=false) then propagated onto every new channel session
along with its cross-provider model, surfacing as a 'stale model pin' each turn
and showing a disabled provider in the session list. Validate the inherited
provider against config (is_provider_usable); when it is disabled or absent,
drop it so the session falls through to the real config default instead.

fix(provider): exclude disabled providers from the fallback chain

A provider with enabled=false must never run, not even as a fallback. The
fallback builder created every listed provider regardless, so a sticky-fallback
could land on a disabled provider and pin its model onto the session. Skip any
chain entry that is not usable in config.

fix(whatsapp): collapse the owner self-chat to a single session

The bot pairs AS the owner, so the owner's own messages arrive addressed by LID
while the connection greeting and config use the PN. Keying the session by the
raw sender created a second owner session (wa-<LID>) separate from the
greeting's (wa-<PN>) on every connect. Key the owner self-chat by the
configured owner number so there is exactly one owner session.

fix(runtime): enlarge tokio worker stack to stop agent-turn stack overflow

The agent tool loop and the RSI digest are very deeply nested async state
machines; on the default 2MB worker stack a single poll could overflow and
abort the process ('thread tokio-rt-worker has overflowed its stack'). Build
the runtime by hand with a 16MB worker stack.

Confirmed from server acks: messages sent to the owner's LID JID
(<lid>@lid) are rejected with error 400 (the LID-form device session can't
be established, so the encrypt fan-out skips that device and the whole
stanza is refused), while messages sent to the owner's PN
(<num>@s.whatsapp.net) get a clean ack and deliver — the same target the
connection greeting already uses successfully. Route the owner self-chat
reply to the PN so the agent's response actually arrives instead of being
silently dropped. Non-owner chats keep their original chat JID.

fix(whatsapp): onboarding test confirms real delivery, not just transmission

test_whatsapp_connection returned Ok as soon as send_message transmitted the
stanza, so onboarding showed success even when the server later rejected the
message (error 400) and nothing arrived. Add a delivered-message broadcast on
WhatsAppState, populated from ReceiptType::Delivered receipts in the agent
event loop, and make the test wait for the greeting's own message id to be
delivered (20s timeout) before reporting success. Now the connection test only
confirms when a message actually reaches WhatsApp.

fix(telegram): #251 isolate /cd directory browser state per forum topic

dir_browsers was keyed by chat_id only, so two forum topics in the
same group overwrote each other's directory path. Now keyed by
(chat_id, topic_id) matching the same pattern as chat_sessions.

Changes:
- mod.rs: dir_browsers key i64 → (i64, Option<i32>)
- mod.rs: set/get/clear_dir_browser signatures accept topic_id

fix(whatsapp): route streamed reply text to the PN too, not just the final reply

The previous reply->PN fix only changed the FINAL reply target, but the agent's
response is usually delivered via the streamed intermediate-text path
(progress callback), and a streamed turn suppresses the final reply. That
streamed path still sent to the owner's LID chat, which the server 400s, so
replies kept getting dropped. Compute one reply_target (owner PN for the self
chat, original chat otherwise) and use it for BOTH the streamed text and the
final reply.

fix(whatsapp): serialize the session store to stop the encrypt race that drops replies

Confirmed from server acks: outgoing replies intermittently fail with error
400, always paired with 'session with <device> not found. Skipping.' The Signal
session store is read-modify-write and whatsapp-rust encrypts for a message's
recipient devices in parallel; with a 4-connection pool a session written for a
device on one connection wasn't always visible to the encrypt's read on another
in time, so that device got skipped, the participant list came out incomplete,
and the server rejected the whole stanza (only the race-winner delivered — the
'one reply then never' symptom). Use a single pooled connection so all session
reads/writes serialize. A personal bot's WhatsApp throughput makes the cost
negligible.

fix(whatsapp): accept Sender receipts as delivery confirmation for self-chat

The onboarding connection test waited for a Delivered receipt, but the bot is
paired AS the owner, so its messages go to the owner's own devices, which ack
with a 'sender' receipt (ReceiptType::Sender), never 'delivered'. The test
therefore timed out and reported failure even though the message landed, so
users kept hitting retry on a connection that actually worked. Treat Sender
receipts (in addition to Delivered) as confirmation that the message reached
WhatsApp.

fix(telegram): persist telegram_send posts so replies to them are recoverable

post, any telegram_send send/reply) got 'I can't see it': rich/cron messages
arrive in the reply with empty text, and the reply-context recovery looks the
replied-to message up in channel_messages by its Telegram message_id — but
telegram_send never persisted its outgoing messages, so the lookup found
nothing. (Normal agent replies already persist, which is why replying to those
works.)

for the rich path, the returned Message for plain chunks) and persist each as a

fix(telegram): exact-match dedup only, not substring replace — #252

The streaming dedup loop used String::replace() to strip each

placeholder. Since streaming sends DIFF chunks (each clearing

fix(whatsapp): migrate to upstream HEAD for LID/PN device registry

Replies to the owner self-chat were rejected by WhatsApp with error 400:
wacore 0.6.0 resolves a recipient's devices under both the phone-number
and LID identities and encrypts for each physical device twice. Once the
post-pair history sync teaches the client its LID device mappings, every
send is double-addressed and the server drops the whole stanza. The
connection greeting only landed because it raced ahead of that sync.

Pin whatsapp-rust/wacore to upstream HEAD (past published 0.6.0), which
replaces this with a device registry whose alias-aware LID<->PN lookup
collapses each physical device to one address, so a self-DM is addressed
once. Adapt to the API drift:
- generate_message_id() is no longer async
- bot.run() returns () and consumes self; the live client still arrives
  via the Connected event callback, so no handle is needed
- with_backend() takes the backend by value (the blanket Backend-for-Arc
  impl is gone) — pass the owned Store
- implement the new MsgSecretStore sub-trait (message-secret persistence
  for poll/edit handling) backed by a new wa_msg_secrets table
- implement the new SignalStore::mark_prekeys_uploaded and
  AppSyncStore::clear_mutation_macs methods

fix(utils): extract_react_marker only accepts real emoji, skips code spans

The extractor stripped ANY <<react:...>> occurrence and returned the raw
payload. A marker mentioned in prose (the agent discussing the feature
itself) was eaten out of the final text and its word payload fired a
reaction, so Telegram rejected it with REACTION_INVALID, and the mutated
final no longer matched the already-sent intermediate: exact-match dedup
failed and both copies of the message landed in the chat.

Now a directive is extracted only when the payload looks like an actual
emoji (non-empty, 8 chars max, no ASCII), and occurrences inside backtick
code spans are never treated as directives. Prose mentions stay in the
text verbatim.

Tests move from an inline mod to src/tests/react_marker_test.rs (project
rule) with new cases: word/placeholder payloads stay in prose, code-span
mentions untouched, compound emoji accepted, oversized payloads rejected.
The inline img_basic regression was already covered by image_util_test.

fix(telegram): strip react directives from intermediates + directive prompt rules

Intermediate chunks never ran extract_react_marker, so a directive
streamed mid-turn leaked raw into the chat (<<react:emoji>> before the
text) AND made the stored intermediate differ from the final text, whose
extraction runs before its dedup pass: exact-match found no match and
the same message delivered twice.

Apply extract_react_marker at all five intermediate send sites, matching
the <<IMG:path>> treatment those sites already have for the identical
marker-breaks-dedup incident class. The reaction itself still fires only
from the final-response path, which extracts from response.content, so a
dedup-suppressed final keeps its reaction.

Also tighten the reaction directive prompt: the value must be a literal
emoji character, never a word or placeholder, and mentioning the
directive in prose requires backticks so it is not executed.

fix(templates): group-chat rules never instruct self-silencing

The AGENTS.md template told the agent to decide on its own when to stay
silent in group chats and to answer with a sentinel token when doing so.
That fought the runtime permission gate (respond_to already decides which
messages reach the agent) and planting the token in every prompt is what
made a model emit it as a literal chat reply to a normal question.

Replace the section with reply/react/both guidance: every message that
reaches the agent gets handled (reply for questions/actions, react for
short acknowledgments, both when work plus tone deserve it), humor and
light roasting welcome per SOUL.md. Also drop the token mention from the
Heartbeats section: the poll prompt itself carries it, so it never needs
to sit in always-loaded context.

Two misleading-log fixes in the provider fallback path:

fix(telegram): fire intermediate reactions and strip directive from placeholder

Two reaction-directive issues in the Telegram streaming pipeline:

- Reactions only fired from the final-response path. The edit-loop and
  post-edit-loop intermediate sites in handle_message stripped the
  <<react:emoji>> directive but discarded the emoji, so a directive
  emitted during a thinking block never acknowledged the user until the
  whole turn finished. Add a small fire_reaction helper and fire
  immediately at both handle_message sites (on the user's message). The
  resume_session and flush_intermediates sites have no inbound user
  message to react to, so they strip only, now documented in place.
- The streaming placeholder edited the message with the raw snapshot

  placeholder-edit sites (reaction still fires from the intermediate or

fix(commands): strip @botname from the command token only, keep arguments (#265)

The fallback @handle strip in handle_command cut the input at the first
'@' in the whole line and discarded everything after it: a group command
like /respond_to@yourbot mention lost its argument and showed the current
mode instead of switching it, and any argument containing '@' (emails,
paths) was truncated.

Extract the strip into strip_command_handle: remove the handle from the
first token only, preserve arguments verbatim, leave non-command text
untouched. Covered by src/tests/command_handle_strip_test.

Also note in /respond_to usage output that multi-bot groups can
autocomplete the command to ANOTHER bot's handle, in which case this bot
never sees it (#264): that was why per-group respond_to never persisted,
not a wipe on restart.

fix(session): scope /new working directory to the same chat, not global-latest (#263)

`create_channel_session` sourced the new session's `working_directory` from
`get_most_recent_session()` — the global most-recent session across every
channel and profile. A TUI session in one directory therefore bled its cwd
into an unrelated channel chat: `/new` in a Telegram group could silently
adopt whatever directory the operator last used in the TUI.

Add an explicit `inherit_wd_from` parameter. The working directory now comes
only from the session that received the `/new` (or the idle-expired session
being replaced) in that same chat; brand-new chats and error-recovery paths
pass `None`. Provider/model inheritance is unchanged (still global-latest, the
documented TUI-provider pickup behaviour).

Threaded through every caller: Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp `/new`, the
shared idle-reset resolver, and Trello. Reworked the #258 tests to pin
same-chat inheritance and prove no cross-channel bleed.

fix(channels): stop channel commands from aborting the in-flight task (#266)

Every inbound message unconditionally cancelled the session's in-flight agent
before the command was parsed, so `/models`, `/help`, `/usage`, `/new` killed a
running tool loop mid-execution. Sending `/models` while the agent worked
dropped the whole task instead of just switching the model for the next run.

Remove the unconditional pre-command cancel in the Telegram, Discord, and
WhatsApp handlers. Genuine follow-up interrupts are still handled at dispatch
by `store_cancel_token`, which cancels the prior token before starting new
work, and `/stop` (bare `stop`) now cancels explicitly in its fast path. Slack
already cancelled only at dispatch, so it needed no change.

Result: a model switch applies to the next agent run or next user message and
never drops current work.

fix(providers): persist live-fetched models for custom providers, show real default (#267)

Two defects made a custom provider's Telegram `/models` list diverge from its
live catalogue and hide the configured default.

1. `apply_config` wrote the stale `config_models` (loaded from disk) back to
   `models = [...]`, discarding the freshly fetched `/v1/models` result held in
   `ps.models`. Selecting a model never updated the persisted list, so custom
   providers stayed frozen on whatever placeholder list was there first. Now it
   writes the live-fetched names first, with config-only names appended, and
   only skips the write when both are empty (no static-catalogue fallback, so
   providers that never fetched keep the prior behaviour).

2. `models_for_provider` picked the current model as `config_models.first()` — a
   stale placeholder — instead of the configured `default_model`. Now the
   default is the authoritative current model, surfaced on top and marked
   selected even when the stored list starts with a different (stale) entry.

Added a regression test pinning the default-on-top behaviour against a stale
stored list.

fix(resume): never age out in-flight turns, resume every surviving row (#268)

The startup resume scanner deleted every pending_requests row older than
10 minutes and only replayed the remainder. A pending row exists only
while a turn is in flight (completion deletes it, and the boot path
clears the table after reading), so the window purged exactly the turns
that most need resuming: long agentic runs. An interrupted 28-minute CLI
coding turn was dropped while a 5-minute-old turn on another provider
resumed.

Resume every surviving row. The only remaining age guard is a 24h
crash-debris cap keyed on updated_at (last interaction), and a new
touch() bumps updated_at so mid-turn persistence keeps multi-hour turns
inside the cap.

fix(agent): persist CLI turns to the DB as they stream, not at turn end (#269)

CLI providers run the whole agentic loop inside their subprocess, and the
assistant row was written once, atomically, when the turn ended. A restart
mid-turn therefore lost every intermediate message and tool result that
had been on screen: the TUI reloaded with nothing after the last user
message and a resume prompt had no context to continue from. API
providers never had this hole (per-iteration writes).

Add a live persister task for CLI turns: the wrapped progress callback
that already intercepts IntermediateText / ToolCompleted now also feeds
each segment to a writer that appends it to the assistant row in
streaming order (tool markers merged exactly as before) and touches the
session's pending-request row so multi-hour turns stay inside the resume
window (#268). The end-of-turn and Esc-cancel paths stop re-writing the
segments (the DB copy already exists), barrier the writer with a Flush,
and append only what streaming cannot know: the reasoning block and any
trailing response text. The writer targets the assistant row through a
shared cell so a queued-message injection retargets it at the fresh row.

Layout note: the reasoning block now lands after the streamed segments
in the row instead of before them.

fix(providers): by-name creation honours its ignore-enabled contract (#270)

create_provider_by_name documents that it ignores the enabled flag (it
restores session-pinned providers and builds explicitly-listed fallback
chains), but the CLI factories gate on cfg.enabled internally. A session
pinned to claude-cli whose config section was disabled at boot could
never be restored: the restore failed with a misleading 'missing API key'
error and the session silently landed on another provider, and claude_cli
was skipped from the fallback chain the user explicitly listed it in.

When the first creation attempt yields nothing, retry with the provider's
section force-enabled in a CLONED config (disk config untouched). The
keyless CLI providers (claude-cli, opencode-cli, codex-cli) also get a
default section synthesized when absent, since they authenticate through
their own login. Keyed providers without a section remain un-creatable
and the error now names the real possibilities instead of assuming a
missing API key.

feat(prompt): three-tier project directive-file discovery

Rewrites push_project_directives into a real discovery pass and fixes the
dead-code guard that shipped in 4e759c44.

The bug: working_directory arrives tilde-collapsed (`~/...`) per the
RuntimeInfo contract, and the old code ran `Path::is_dir()` on that literal
string. Rust never expands `~`, so the guard returned on the first check
every call and nothing was ever injected. Existing tests only passed
absolute paths, so they stayed green and masked it. The fix expands `~` via
the existing expand_tilde helper before any filesystem op.

New module `brain::directives` (pure, filesystem-only, testable) discovers
and classifies the directive/rule files of the major AI coding agents:

- Root single files: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, GEMINI.md,
  .cursorrules, .windsurfrules; nested .claude/CLAUDE.md,
  .github/copilot-instructions.md, .opencode/AGENTS.md.
- Recursively walked rule dirs: .cursor/rules/**/*.mdc,
  .claude/rules/**/*.md, .clinerules/**/*.{md,txt} (.clinerules may also be
  a single file).

Frontmatter classifies each rule into three tiers:

- Always: root files, Cursor `alwaysApply: true`, Claude/Cline rules with no
  `paths`.
- Conditional: Cursor `globs`, Claude/Cline `paths` (patterns shown).
- On-demand: Cursor .mdc with only a `description` (text shown so the agent
  can judge relevance).

Rendered as a tiered, filenames-only index (content read on demand via
read_file) that rebuilds every turn, so it survives compaction and stays
cheap. Only non-empty tiers are emitted.

Reuses split_frontmatter (now pub(crate)). 11 discovery/classification tests
plus a tilde-expansion regression under src/tests/.

fix(prompt): directive scan follows /cd and directive-file edits

Directive discovery was tied to frozen startup state. Two gaps, one root
cause: BrainRebuild read runtime_info.working_directory (baked at
construction) and only rebuilt when a ~/.opencrabs brain file's mtime
advanced.

Gap 1: /cd never took effect. set_working_directory mutates the shared
working_directory RwLock, but runtime_info stayed frozen, so the index
always reflected the startup directory. Now BrainRebuild holds the same
live working_directory Arc that tool execution uses; render reads the
current cwd and overrides working_directory (tilde-collapsed) before
assembling, so the scan follows /cd.

Gap 2: directive edits never refreshed the index. The rebuild trigger only
watched ~/.opencrabs/*.md. New directives::directives_mtime(root) returns
the newest mtime across the directive files/dirs under a root; render folds
it plus the live cwd into the trigger, so a directive add/edit or a /cd
invalidates the cache and nothing else does, preserving the warm
prompt-cache path when nothing changed.

Also fixes two em-dashes in the rendered directive section.

suite 4443/0, clippy --all-features clean.

fix(whatsapp): match allow list against the sender's PN twin for LID DMs (#276)

WhatsApp addresses most DMs by LID (the privacy id), whose digits never
equal a phone number, so the response gate matching only the raw sender
against allowed_phones silently dropped every allow-listed contact: the
bot answered nothing but the owner's own self-DM (which passes through
the number-agnostic self-chat rule).

The library already exposes the sender's other identity in sender_alt
(the PN JID for a LID-addressed sender, from the stanza's sender_pn).
wa_should_respond now matches the allow list AND the operator list
against both the sender digits and the alt digits, plus-normalized on
every side. Sender not on the list stays dropped under auto/allowlist
policies.

fix(config): normalize the plus prefix in is_owner comparisons (#277)

Every other allowed_phones consumer (response gate, owner fallback,
greeting, onboarding test, whatsapp_send) trims a leading plus on both
sides; is_owner compared raw strings. A config with
bot_owner = ["+15551234567"] (natural for pasted international numbers)
therefore broke owner gating for channel commands, since the digits
extracted from a JID never carry a plus. Trim both sides; the other
channels' ids never start with '+' so the trim is a no-op there.

feat(web_scrape): SSRF guard for the URL-to-markdown fetcher

A server-side URL fetcher is an SSRF primitive unless it refuses non-public
targets. Port insight_forge's url_validator as web_scrape/ssrf.rs: reject
non-http(s) schemes (file:// especially), localhost, private/loopback/
link-local/broadcast/multicast IPv4, the cloud metadata endpoint, and
loopback/multicast/unique-local IPv6.

Classify the host through url::Host instead of parsing host_str(), because
host_str() keeps the brackets on IPv6 literals ([::1]) which then fail
IpAddr parsing and slip past the filter. validate_url returns the parsed Url
so callers can reuse it as a base for resolving relative links.

feat(web_scrape): genericized structural HTML cleaner

Port insight_forge's html_content_cleaner as web_scrape/clean.rs, stripped of
every client-specific match. The original filtered lines containing FORMULARIO,
Nome:, Telefone:, Privacidade, Contact, and similar strings tuned for one
Portuguese SMB site; those would delete legitimate content on an arbitrary
page, so none survive. What remains is language-agnostic: strip_noise removes
script/style blocks, inline event handlers, and HTML comments; decode_html_
entities maps the common entities; collapse_blank_lines tidies spacing; and
to_plain_text reduces HTML to normalized text for the text output format.

Deliberately no URL-stripping phase: image and link URLs must survive into the
markdown so the agent can vision the specific images a task needs. Regexes are
LazyLock statics; no new dependency (regex + unicode-normalization already in
the tree).

feat(web_scrape): main-content extraction via scraper selectors

Port insight_forge's extract_main_content as web_scrape/extract.rs. A priority
cascade of container selectors (main, article, #content, [role=main], ...) is
tried first; the first match with substantial content wins. When none matches,
fall back to <body> with the structural junk elements (nav, footer, aside,
sidebar, forms, iframes, ads, social) stripped by selector-driven removal.
Pathological bodyless input returns the fragment unchanged so the caller always
has something to convert.

Extraction is fully synchronous and returns owned Strings: scraper's Html and
Selector hold Rc and are !Send, so keeping them off the async boundary is what
keeps the tool's execute() future Send. Adds the scraper dependency (0.27).

Port the HTML-to-markdown step as web_scrape/to_markdown.rs. absolutize_urls

are directly fetchable; already-absolute, anchor, data:, mailto:, tel:, and
javascript: URIs are left untouched, and protocol-relative //host/... URLs pick
up the page scheme. to_markdown wraps htmd, emitting images as ![alt](url) so
the agent visions only the specific images a task needs. Adds the htmd dep.

Chrome User-Agent and a bounded timeout, covering server-rendered pages at
near-zero cost. is_js_shell is a pure, network-free heuristic that flags pages
carrying script tags but almost no visible text (an unrendered SPA shell),
reusing clean::to_plain_text to measure content. When it fires, fetch_rendered
(behind the browser feature) drives headless Chrome, waiting for network idle so
client-side hydration completes before the HTML is read.

fix(reactions): tolerate escaped marker prefix so reaction fires

extract_react_marker gated on the exact literal prefix `<<react:`. Models
that escape sequences resembling markup emit `<\react:` or `<\\react:`
instead, escaping the second angle bracket. Those never matched, so the
reaction never fired and the mangled marker leaked into the chat as raw
text. The earlier hardening passes made the extractor stricter on the
payload side, which does not help when the prefix itself is malformed.

New match_react_open accepts a leading `<` followed by any run of `<` or
`\` characters, then `react:`, so `<<react:`, `<\react:`, `<\\react:`, and
`<react:` all normalize to the same extraction. The emoji-validation and
code-span guards are unchanged, so word payloads and code-span mentions
still do not extract, on a mangled prefix too.

mangled prefix with a word payload stays intact, and a mangled prefix
inside a code span is left untouched.

kept burning a deleteMessage + sendMessage pair per tick against

binary: two 429s within the first four minutes of a tool-heavy session.

the placeholder: a fresh tool-group message (append_tool_group's send
branch, shared by both handlers) and an intermediate text (its event arm
already flags it). Drop the unconditional flag from both ToolCompleted
arms. First-response latency is untouched (placeholder creation path
unchanged) and live feedback is unchanged (placeholder text edits and
group refresh edits keep their per-tick cadence).

feat(reactions): frame inbound reactions by sentiment and first name (#302)

Stage 1 of #302. The synthetic prompt handle_reaction built for an inbound
reaction only said "you may react back or reply" and referred to the user
as User "name". It gave the agent no read on what the reaction meant and
no steer to address the person naturally.

Add a small pure reaction_prompt module: classify_reaction maps the emoji
to a sentiment (positive 👍👌💪🫡🆗🔥💯 = approval / green light,
negative ⛔️🚫🛑👎 = pause and ask, else neutral) and build_reaction_prompt
frames the turn accordingly and addresses the user by first name. A
positive reaction now reads as a go-ahead to proceed, a negative one tells
the agent to pause and ask what to change.

Kept channel-agnostic and unit-tested (7 cases: classification of each
set, whitespace tolerance, and the by-name / sentiment framing). Stage 2
(surfacing a reaction into the in-flight tool loop) is separate.

feat(reactions): inject a mid-turn reaction into the running loop (#302)

Stage 2 of #302. A reaction that landed while a turn was already running
only ever fired a brand-new, separate agent turn after the fact, so it
could never steer work in progress, and two send_message calls could run
concurrently on one session (double charge, interleaved history).

Reuse the tool loop's existing per-session message_queue_callback rail
(the one the TUI uses for follow-up messages), which was never wired for
channels. Now:

- TelegramState carries a per-session pending-reaction queue (FIFO) and an
  active-turn set maintained by an RAII ActiveTurnGuard, so a crashed turn
  can't leave a session looking permanently busy. A dedicated set is used
  rather than cancel_tokens, whose completed tokens linger and would give
  false "busy" positives.
- handle_message marks the session active for the span of the turn and
  wires reaction_queue_callback into its AgentService (via a new
  factory create_agent_service_with_queue).
- handle_reaction, when a turn is active, enqueues a sentiment-framed
  "live feedback" message instead of firing a second turn; the loop drains
  it between rounds. When idle it keeps the existing standalone path.
- A drain-on-exit safeguard flushes any reaction that landed in the final
  round (after the loop's last between-rounds drain) as one short
  follow-up, so a mid-turn reaction is never silently stranded.

Positive reactions read as "keep going", negative as "pause and ask", and
the agent addresses the user by first name. Queue FIFO, guard lifecycle,
callback draining, and the mid-turn framing are unit-tested.

feat(goal): expose the goal system as a goal_manage tool (self-goaling) (#307)

The goal system was only reachable via the /goal slash command a human
types, so the model could not set a goal for itself and could not drive
its own multi-turn test/review/fix cycles.

Add a goal_manage tool wrapping GoalManager: action set/status/pause/
resume/clear, one action-dispatched tool matching the cron_manage /
task_manager / config_tool convention rather than five separate tools, so
it costs one schema entry, not five. Pure wrapper over the existing
GoalManager methods, constructed from ToolExecutionContext.service_context
exactly as the /goal slash handler already does.

No tool-loop changes: the post-turn judge hook (evaluate_after_turn) runs
unconditionally every turn and gates internally on an active goal_state
row, so a goal the model sets via the tool activates the judge identically
to one set by /goal. Registered in the shared core tool set; added to the
protected-builtin list, the utility tool_category, and KNOWN_TOOL_NAMES so
custom-OpenAI-compatible providers extract it reliably.

Tested: name / description / schema surface, no-approval and capability
guards, and clean error when service_context is absent.

feat(preamble): self-extract media frames when the vision tool is absent (#308)

Some harnesses expose analyze_image / analyze_video as tools; others (the
claude-cli -p provider, supports_vision() = false) give the underlying
model native vision but do not surface those tools. Asked to describe an
attached image or video there, the agent had no directive and would claim
blindness or describe the media from its filename (hallucination).

Add a VISION FALLBACK section to BRAIN_PREAMBLE: when analyze_image /
analyze_video is not in the toolset, read images directly with the file
tool and extract video frames with ffmpeg -vf fps=N, then read those
frames with native vision; only after both fail may the agent say it
cannot view the media. It reinforces, not overrides, the always-view-
before-describing rule. Lives in the compiled, versioned preamble rather
than a driftable brain file. Two regression tests lock the section header
and the concrete ffmpeg / no-filename-describing guidance.

fix(reactions): default reaction-triggered turns to react-only, not text (#309)

A reaction to a finished bot message fires a standalone agent turn, and
build_reaction_prompt biased it toward text: the positive branch said
"acknowledge by first name and keep the momentum", neutral said "respond
naturally", and the react-only option was a trailing afterthought. So the
bot answered nearly every reaction with prose. In a group where several
people react, that multiplied into a wall of near-duplicate acks.

Flip the default: a reaction is a lightweight acknowledgement, not a
request, so positive/neutral now steer to reacting back with a single
emoji and NO text, and "reply with ONLY <<react:EMOJI>>" is the stated
expected response. Thread is_group so a group hardens the react-only steer
(a text reply per reaction is noise for everyone else). Negative stays the
one case that warrants text: pause and ask what to change.

Mid-turn injection (#302 Stage 2) is unaffected: it rides the running turn
and never spawns a standalone turn, so it was never the spam source.
Regression tests updated for the react-only default and group hardening.

fix(telegram): dedup folded block against final answer by prefix, not exact match (#311)

On API providers the final answer rendered twice: once folded inside the
collapsed processing-log block (a copy cut off mid-sentence) and again as
the completion below. On claude-cli it did not, because there the answer
comes back empty in response.content and take_folded_final reclaims it out
of the block. On API providers the answer is in response.content, so the
delivery took the else branch, which only dropped the folded copy on an
EXACT match (norm_folded == norm_final). Streaming folds only a truncated
head of the answer, so the folded copy is a PREFIX of the final text, never
equal, and the exact check let the duplicate through.

Replace the exact-equality check with a pure helper folded_duplicates_final
that treats a substantial prefix overlap in either direction as a duplicate,
guarded by a minimum overlap (>= 20 chars) so a short distinct narration
line sharing an opening is not mistaken for the answer. Wired into both the
handle_message and resume_session delivery paths. Also log the refresh_flow
edit error instead of dropping it, so a failed block edit is traceable.

Tested: exact match, truncated prefix, whitespace-insensitivity, distinct
narration rejected, short shared opening rejected.

fix(telegram_send): apply markdown-to-HTML conversion for formatted output (#315)

The telegram_send tool was sending raw markdown text with no parse_mode,
causing formatting (bold, headers, code blocks) to render as literal
characters instead of styled text.

Fix: convert text through markdown_to_telegram_html() before sending,
and add .parse_mode(ParseMode::Html) to match the auto-delivery path
in handler.rs. This ensures telegram_send messages format identically
to normal agent responses.

Root cause: src/brain/tools/telegram_send.rs:612 called
.send_message() without parse_mode, unlike the handler delivery path
which always converts and sets ParseMode::Html.

Fixes #315

fix(lazy_tools): add analyze_image/analyze_video to CORE_TOOLS

Vision tools are fundamental capabilities that should be immediately
available when configured, not hidden behind tool_search discovery.
They're only registered by register_config_dependent_tools when a
vision backend exists (provider vision_model or Gemini image.vision),
so they won't appear in the active set if vision isn't configured.

This fixes the regression where lazy_tools=true caused analyze_image
to require a tool_search round-trip despite being a core capability.

fix(telegram): parse HTML in initial status messages

Both the draft fallback and standard paths were creating status
messages via message_in_thread() without parse_mode, so the <b>
tags added by build_status_message() rendered as raw text instead
of bold. The edit path already had .parse_mode(ParseMode::Html).

Fix: chain .parse_mode(ParseMode::Html) before .await on both
initial send sites (draft fallback + standard path).

Closes #312

fix(telegram): add parse_mode HTML to status message sends/edits (#312)

Status messages use <b> tags for bold formatting but were sent without
parse_mode, causing raw HTML tags to appear instead of rendered bold text.

Add .parse_mode(ParseMode::Html) to:
- Draft fallback path (line 3176)
- Edit existing message path (line 3191)
- Create new message path (line 3195)

This ensures <b> tags render correctly as bold in all three code paths.

fix(telegram): exact-match folded finals dedup at any length (#316)

A short final answer folded verbatim into the processing-log block
rendered twice: once inside the collapsed block and once as the real
completion. folded_duplicates_final guarded prefix matches with a
20-normalized-char minimum overlap (to avoid eating a narration line
that merely shares an opening with the answer), but the floor also
rejected EXACT matches below 20 chars, so short answers were never
recognized as duplicates.

Exact normalized equality now matches at any length (identical strings
carry no false-positive risk); the 20-char floor still applies to
partial prefix overlap, and empty sides never match. Covered by three
new cases in telegram_tool_group_test alongside the existing prefix and
rejection cases.

fix(telegram): map reactions to Telegram's allowed set, never go silent (#353)

Telegram message reactions only accept a fixed emoji list. The model
picks freely, so a reaction-only turn with an out-of-set emoji bounced
with REACTION_INVALID and the handler still skipped text delivery:
placeholder deleted, no reaction, no text. Four fully silent turns in
one day, and the directive prompt itself suggested an emoji that is not
in the allowed set.

Three-part fix:
- map_to_allowed_reaction: allowed emojis pass through (variation
  selector normalized, since the API list omits it), common out-of-set
  picks alias to close equivalents, everything else falls back to a
  thumbs up. Applied at all three send sites (final reaction-only,
  mid-turn intermediate, inbound-reaction reply).
- Never-silent guard: if a reaction-only turn's reaction send still
  fails, the emoji is delivered as a minimal text reply instead of
  skipping. A failed reaction degrades to text, never to nothing.
- The reaction directive now lists only allowed-set emojis and states
  that anything else gets remapped.

fix(telegram): never drop forwarded messages, tag forwards with provenance (#354)

Forwarding a message into the bot could leave the agent blind to content
fully visible in the chat. Two holes:

- A forward of a rich-formatted bot message arrives as a content type
  this Bot API client cannot decode. The handler classified it kind=other
  with empty text and hit the ancient non-text/voice/photo catch-all:
  silently ignored. The agent then denied the forward existed and went
  hunting for files on disk.
- Decodable forwards (text, photos, documents) entered the turn as if
  the user typed them, with no provenance, so the agent could not
  connect 'I just forwarded it' to the content.

Now: a message with forward metadata is NEVER ignored. Undecodable
forwards hand the agent an explicit placeholder naming the origin (so it
knows a forward arrived and can ask for a paste), readable forwards get
a [Forwarded from "origin"] tag before entering the turn, the session
context, and the display. Service messages without forward metadata are
ignored exactly as before.

fix(telegram): never delete the processing-log block on edit failure (#356)

refresh_flow deleted the entire blockquote message whenever an edit to
it failed, for ANY reason. The block carries folded intermediate content
since #300, so a transient 429 or the block outgrowing Telegram's
4096-char edit limit destroyed user-visible content: a fully rendered
report/table vanished from the chat over a 9-second throttle, and the
final response (a short stub pointing at a file) never restored it.
Three wipes in two minutes in today's log.

Error-class handling instead of delete-on-any-failure:
- proactive freeze before editing once the rendered block exceeds 4000
  chars (the edit could only fail)
- RetryAfter: sleep the indicated delay, retry once with re-rendered
  content; on a second failure keep the message, next tick retries
- MESSAGE_TOO_LONG: freeze — the message keeps its last render, the
  block closes, subsequent entries start a fresh one (entries rendered
  into the frozen message are dropped from state so the new block
  starts small)
- message is not modified: ignore
- message to edit not found: forget the id, nothing to delete
- anything else: keep the message and let the next tick retry

Deleting displayed content is never a failure mode anymore.

feat(telegram): raw-aware update intake — forwards of undecodable content reach the agent (#354)

Forwarding a rich-formatted message into the bot left the agent blind:
teloxide's typed parse discards content fields it does not know, for
this type together with the forward metadata, so the message arrived as
an empty kind and died in an ancient silent-ignore branch while sitting
fully rendered in the user's chat.

The intake now long-polls getUpdates as RAW JSON itself. Every message's
raw payload is stashed keyed by chat and message id, and a message
carrying none of the known content keys is rewritten in place into a
plain text message holding its raw content payload plus forward
provenance, so it flows through the ENTIRE normal pipeline (handler,
agent, session context, display). Readable forwards (text, photos,
documents) are tagged [Forwarded from ...] so the agent knows the
provenance instead of treating forwarded text as the user's own words.

Never-silent guarantees, live-verified: if no content and no raw payload
exist, the user gets an explicit error reply asking for a paste; an
update that fails the typed parse is error-logged with its payload.

Outage note, learned the hard way: teloxide's Update deserializer works
ONLY from string input. serde_json::from_value yields UpdateKind::Error
for every update including plain text, which no dispatch branch matches:
the first wiring of this listener consumed all updates and dispatched
none, taking the whole Telegram intake down. The typed parse goes
through from_str exclusively, and telegram_raw_update_parse_test pins
both behaviours so this cannot be reintroduced blind.

fix(telegram): single progress surface, status folds into block header (#360)

While a processing-log block is open, the rolling status now rides in
the block's own header ("N tool calls . read_file . 45s"), edited in
place, instead of running as a second standalone ticker message. The
standalone ticker remains only for blockless turns (pre-tool wait or
turns that never open a block), and is retired the moment a block
opens mid-turn.

When the final response lands the live status is cleared and one
settle refresh renders the plain "N tool calls" header. Sub-minute
elapsed values snap to 5s steps so header edits stay within the
per-chat edit budget. A lone tool line (no blockquote yet) carries
the status as a suffix so progress shows from the first call.

feat(telegram): decode rich content types natively, raw JSON stays the safety net (#359)

Two gaps closed in the rich-content intake:

1. KNOWN_CONTENT_KEYS was far behind what teloxide-core 0.13 actually
   parses. Checklists, paid media, giveaways, gifts, shared users/chats,
   refunded payments, boost/background/topic events and price-change
   events were being rewritten into the synthesized-JSON detour even
   though the typed parse handles them. The list now matches the
   client's real coverage (keys verified against its serde definitions).

2. New rich_decode module renders recognized content-carrying types as
   readable text for the agent: checklist (title plus checked/unchecked
   items), poll (question, options, votes), paid media, the giveaway
   family, gift and unique gift, story, users_shared and chat_shared,
   with message captions appended. Wired into both consumption points:
   the handler's no-content branch and synthesize_unknown_content.
   Anything unrecognized still falls back to the raw-JSON dump with
   provenance, so future Bot API types keep flowing losslessly.

Decoders bail to None on malformed shapes instead of panicking or
rendering half-empty output; 17 new tests cover each type, caption
append, id fallbacks, and the raw fallback path.

feat(tools): generate_document tool with native XLSX backend (#357)

parse_document could read documents but nothing could write them; the
agent had to improvise (CSV via write_file, ad hoc scripts). This adds
the write side as a built-in tool with structured input, dispatching
to native Rust backends so document creation ships inside the binary
with zero host dependencies.

First backend: XLSX via rust_xlsxwriter. Sheets are rows of JSON
cells; strings starting with "=" are written as live Excel formulas
so the workbook recalculates when the user edits it. Numbers and
booleans land as native cell types, nested JSON is stringified rather
than dropped, header row bolding and column widths are supported, and
invalid sheet names are sanitized (Excel's 31-char and character
rules) instead of failing the whole generation.

Round-trip tests read the generated workbooks back with calamine, the
same crate parse_document uses, proving our own read side can consume
what we write. Formula cells are verified via worksheet_formula.

DOCX, PDF, and a PPTX fallback land as follow-up commits.

fix(telegram): increase raw payload truncation limit to 4096

Rich message JSON payloads (verbose nested cell objects) were being
truncated at 3500 chars, cutting off mid-table. Telegram allows 4096.

Bump limit to match Telegram's max. Messages over 4096 still get split
by the existing send infrastructure.

feat(tools): native DOCX backend for generate_document (#357)

Second format for the document generation tool: Word documents via
docx-rs, generated natively in the binary. Input is an ordered list of
content blocks: heading (levels 1-3), paragraph (optional bold), list
(bulleted or numbered), and table (first row bolded as header by
default).

Headings register real Word paragraph styles so the document outline
and navigation pane work; lists register real numbering definitions
(bullet and decimal) so markers survive later editing in Word; tables
land as proper Word tables. Out-of-range heading levels clamp to 1-3
and non-string table cells are stringified as JSON, so sloppy model
input degrades gracefully instead of failing the generation.

Tests unzip the generated OOXML archive and assert document.xml and
numbering.xml contents directly.

feat(tools): native PDF backend for generate_document (#357)

Third format for the document generation tool: PDF via printpdf using
built-in Helvetica fonts, so no font files or host dependencies are
needed. Reuses the same content block model as the DOCX backend
(heading, paragraph, list, table), which means the agent can emit the
same blocks to either format.

Layout is a top-down A4 flow: greedy word wrap sized conservatively
against average glyph width so lines never overflow the right margin,
automatic page breaks, heading sizes by level, ordered/bulleted list
markers, and tables rendered as aligned columns with per-cell
wrapping. An optional title sets the PDF metadata title, defaulting
to the output file stem. printpdf save warnings are logged, never
swallowed.

Round-trip tests extract text back with pdf-extract, the same crate
the read side uses, and cover multi-page and wrapping behavior.

feat(tools): PPTX fallback backend for generate_document (#357)

Final format for the document generation tool. No mature Rust crate
exists for PowerPoint generation, so PPTX dispatches to the host's
python-pptx: slides (title, bullets, optional speaker notes) are sent
as JSON over stdin to a fixed generator script, with the output path
passed via argv. Slide content is never interpolated into code, so
quotes or code-looking text in titles cannot break out of the
generator.

When python3 or python-pptx is missing the tool returns an actionable
error naming the dependency and the install command, and pointing out
that XLSX, DOCX, and PDF still work natively. Never a silent failure.

The end-to-end test self-skips on hosts without python-pptx (the
dependency is environmental); the missing-module error path and the
JSON injection safety are always tested.

fix(telegram): remove standalone status message entirely (#360 follow-up)

The blockless-phase standalone ticker survived #360 and kept orphaning
duplicate "Working on" bubbles: its delete calls were silently dropped
while the tracking state cleared, so a failed delete (rate limit) left
the old message on screen and a fresh one was created next tick. The
draft path's real-message fallback fed the same orphan class.

The processing-log block, edited in place with the live status in its
header, is now the only real progress message. No standalone status
message is ever sent. Before a block opens, DMs with rich_messages
still show the auto-expiring draft preview, but a failed draft send
only logs; it never falls back to a persistent message. The
status_msg_id/status_shown_at state, all its create/edit/delete
paths, and the end-of-turn cleanup deletes are gone.

Also aligns the synthesized unknown-content truncation with the 4096
cap already applied to raw_content_for_agent, so rich forwarded
payloads are not cut earlier on the synthesize path.

fix(telegram): queue mid-turn messages instead of cancelling in-flight tools

A new message on a session with a running turn went through the normal
agent-call path, and store_cancel_token hard-cancelled the in-flight
call to prevent concurrent turns. That cancellation landed MID-TOOL:
a running vision analysis or long command was truncated and the model
came back through the truncated-tool-call recovery preamble.

Follow-up messages now ride the existing between-rounds injection rail
(the one mid-turn reactions already use): when a turn is active, the
message is queued with a steering preface and injected at the next
tool-round boundary; leftovers that miss the final round are flushed
by the existing drain-on-exit path. The user's message gets an
immediate reaction acknowledgment so it never looks silently eaten.
An explicit /stop still cancels immediately through the fast-cancel
path.

fix(doc_gen): PDF mojibake and table overlap (#357 follow-up)

Generated PDFs rendered non-ASCII text as mojibake and overlapping
table cells. Two causes, both in the PDF backend:

1. Built-in WinAnsi fonts get text bytes written through unre-encoded,
   so every non-ASCII character (curly quotes, em dashes, emoji)
   rendered as multi-byte garbage. All text is now transliterated to
   ASCII before layout: punctuation maps to close equivalents, status
   emoji map to readable tags ([OK], [X], [!]), and anything
   unmappable becomes '?' instead of being dropped silently.

2. Table rows advanced the baseline only when column 0 emitted a
   line, so whenever column 0 had fewer wrapped lines than a sibling
   cell, later cells stacked onto the previous line. The first
   emitted cell of each visual row-line now advances the baseline.
   Bold header rows also get extra wrap slack (wider glyphs), and
   words longer than a full line (paths, URLs) hard-split instead of
   running over the column or page edge.

Tests cover transliteration output, uneven cell heights, and the
long-word split.

fix(agent): synthetic prompts persist as compact system tags, not scaffolding

Reaction guidance and mid-turn steering prefaces were saved verbatim
as user messages, so the whole scaffolding text showed in the TUI
history and re-entered the model's context on every future turn.

Queued messages now carry a context/display split (QueuedUserMessage):
the LLM receives the full text for the live turn only, while the DB
and TUI persist either the user's actual words (mid-turn follow-ups)
or a compact tag like "[System: <name> reacted with <emoji>]"
(reactions). send_message gained a with_display variant so fresh-turn
reaction prompts and the drain-on-exit flush use the same split. TUI
follow-ups are unchanged: what the user typed is both context and
display. Queued-message persistence failures now log instead of being
silently dropped.

test(doc_gen): prove every wrapped table line gets its own baseline

Reproduces the audit-report table shape (4 columns, bold header, cells
wrapping to different heights) and simulates the PDF emitter's y
accounting, asserting that any two lines sharing a baseline are in
different columns. Layout internals are crate-visible so the invariant
is tested directly instead of parsing the serialized PDF back.

docs(doc_gen): tool description tells the agent to deliver files on channels

Generated documents were left as paths on disk; channel users cannot
open a server path. The generate_document description now instructs
the agent to send the file as a downloadable attachment in the same
turn via telegram_send send_document, whatsapp_send send_document, or
discord_send send_file, instead of pasting the path.

feat(doc_gen): PDF tables get content-sized columns, header separator, row rules

Tables previously split the page width evenly across columns and drew
no ruling, so a single-digit column wasted a fifth of the page while
verbose columns wrapped on every row, and the output read as loose
text columns rather than a table.

Column widths are now proportional to content: each column's natural
width comes from its longest cell (bounded by its longest single word,
since cells wrap), floored at a readable minimum, capped at 45% of the
body width so one verbose column cannot starve the rest, and scaled
with re-clamping passes to fit the body. A dark separator is drawn
under the header row and light rules between data rows, with breathing
room before, inside, and after the table. The layout flow is now typed
(text/rule/gap items) so spacing and ruling are explicit layout
outputs covered by tests: column sizing, cap enforcement, rule counts,
and the per-baseline invariant.

feat(doc_gen): PDF style layer with brand colors, page furniture, zebra rows (#362)

New optional `style` object on generate_document for pdf output:

- accent_color: colors headings, draws an underline bar below H1, and
  colors the table header separator
- text_color: body text color
- page_header {text}: brand line at the top of every page with an
  accent rule beneath it
- page_footer {text, page_numbers}: footer rule and text on every
  page, with exact "Page N of M" (pagination completes before saving)
- zebra_rows: alternating light fills behind table data rows

Everything defaults off, so unstyled documents render exactly as
before. Invalid hex colors fall back to defaults rather than failing
the generation. Content margins shrink automatically when header or
footer furniture is present. The tool schema documents every knob and
the description tells the agent to use styling for branded reports.

logo_path is accepted in the schema but rendered in the next change.

feat(doc_gen): render page-header logos in styled PDFs (#362)

page_header.logo_path now renders: the PNG/JPEG at the local path is
decoded, registered as an image XObject, scaled to the 8mm header
band via dpi mapping, and drawn on every page with the header text
shifted to sit beside it.

A missing or undecodable logo logs a warning and the document renders
without it; a bad logo never fails the whole generation. Covered by a
test embedding a real 1x1 PNG and asserting the XObject lands, plus
the missing-file path.

feat(doc_gen): bundle DejaVu Sans for real Unicode PDF text (#363)

PDF text previously rode the builtin WinAnsi Helvetica, so everything
non-ASCII was transliterated: em dashes became hyphens, accents and
Cyrillic were impossible, checkmarks turned into [OK] tags.

DejaVu Sans Book and Bold (2.37, free Bitstream Vera-derived license,
LICENSE vendored alongside) are now embedded via include_bytes and
registered per document; printpdf subsets them on save. Accents,
Cyrillic, Greek, arrows, and real checkmark glyphs render as typed.
Emoji still map to readable equivalents (no TTF carries color emoji):
checkmark/cross emoji become their text glyphs, warning becomes [!],
and unsupported emoji ranges become '?', never silently dropped. If
the bundled faces ever fail to parse, generation falls back to the
builtin font with full ASCII transliteration instead of failing.

Verified by extracting text back out of the generated PDF: the
embedded subset preserves "—", "✓", "naïve café →" through the
round trip.

feat(doc_gen): XLSX style layer with header fill, zebra, freeze, autofilter (#364)

The shared `style` input on generate_document is now format-generic
JSON, parsed by each backend into its own spec (invalid styles return
a clear error instead of being dropped).

XLSX styling knobs, all native via rust_xlsxwriter and all off by
default: header_fill and header_font_color (hex) color the header
row; zebra_rows alternates light fills behind data rows; freeze_header
pins the first row while scrolling; autofilter adds filter dropdowns
across the used range; tab_color colors the worksheet tab. Sheets
additionally take column_formats (currency, percent, date, integer,
number, or raw Excel format codes) applied per column, combined
correctly with zebra fills.

Styled workbooks are verified down to the OOXML parts (freeze pane,
autofilter, fill colors in styles.xml) and still round-trip through
calamine with formulas intact.

feat(doc_gen): DOCX style layer with accent headings, page furniture, shaded tables (#365)

Word output picks up the shared style object: accent_color colors the
real Heading 1-3 paragraph styles (the navigation pane keeps working),
page_header and page_footer render on every page via proper Word
header/footer parts, table_header_fill shades the header row, and
zebra_rows alternates light cell shading behind data rows.

Invalid hex colors degrade to the plain look instead of producing a
broken document. All knobs default off; unstyled documents are
byte-for-byte the same design as before. Verified by unzipping the
OOXML and asserting styles.xml, document.xml shading, and the header
and footer parts.

feat(doc_gen): PPTX style layer with brand templates and accent titles (#366)

PowerPoint output picks up the shared style object: template_path
builds the slides into an existing .pptx so they inherit the company
master (logos, fonts, backgrounds), accent_color colors slide titles,
and each slide can pick a layout index from the template's layout
list (out-of-range indices fall back safely).

The generator script now finds the body placeholder robustly instead
of assuming index 1 (templates vary), still receives everything as
JSON over stdin (no code injection surface), and a missing template
file errors out with an actionable message before python even spawns.
Invalid accent colors are logged and dropped rather than failing the
deck.

Template inheritance and the missing-template error are covered by
tests; the end-to-end ones self-skip on hosts without python-pptx.

docs(readme): document the generate_document tool and its styling surface (#367)

Adds a Document Generation feature row and a dedicated section
covering the four formats (native XLSX/DOCX/PDF, python-pptx PPTX),
live Excel formulas, the per-format styling knobs (brand colors, page
header/footer with logos and page numbers, zebra tables, freeze,
autofilter, number formats, PowerPoint brand templates, bundled
Unicode font), graceful degradation on bad style input, and channel
delivery as downloadable attachments.

feat(catalog): surface document tools in lazy-tools discovery (#368)

With lazy_tools on, the only always-injected tool-awareness surface is
the preamble hint; TOOLS.md is contextual there (it loads with the
prompt when lazy_tools is off, where full schemas already describe
every tool). The hint now names document creation and parsing (Excel
with live formulas, Word, PDF, PowerPoint) alongside browsing,
channels, and media, so lazy-mode turns know the capability exists
without loading anything.

tool_category() gains a "documents" bucket covering generate_document,
parse_document, and pdf_to_images so tool_search results and the
catalog group them properly. The workspace TOOLS.md template's
category table (scaffold for new users; personal live brain files are
untouched) gets the matching documents row.

feat(agent): run auto-approved tool batches concurrently (#361)

[agent] max_concurrent existed in config since the beginning but was
never enforced: every tool in a multi-tool response ran strictly
sequentially. Multi-tool batches where nothing needs interactive
approval now execute concurrently, capped by max_concurrent (clamped
to at least 1), in a new parallel_tools module.

Correctness contract preserved end to end: result blocks are yielded
via an order-preserving buffered stream so tool_result order always
matches the request order providers require; ToolStarted/ToolCompleted
progress events fire in real time as each tool starts and finishes;
all shared-state bookkeeping (feedback ledger, discovery-miss
bucketing, dashboard records, recent-path capture, phantom counters)
runs sequentially after the join. Cancellation aborts the batch and
keeps the completed prefix, mirroring the sequential break.

Batches containing any approval-gated tool, single-tool batches,
unknown tool names, and max_concurrent = 1 all take the existing
sequential path byte-identically, so the risk surface is confined to
genuinely parallel-safe batches. Known accepted seam: parallel bash
calls share the process working directory (last cd wins), the same
tradeoff every parallel-tool agent makes.

test(agent): cover parallel tool-batch eligibility, ordering, cancellation (#361)

Three contracts pinned: eligibility gating (single-tool batches,
approval-gated tools, and unknown tool names stay sequential; context
auto_approve neutralizes the gate), in-order result assembly proven
with slowest-first sleep tools (results ordered a/b/c despite reverse
completion, wall clock far under the sequential sum, proving real
overlap), and pre-cancelled tokens aborting the batch with no results.

docs(readme): document [agent] max_concurrent now that it is enforced (#361)

The setting existed since the AgentConfig section landed but was
never documented anywhere user-facing; with parallel tool execution
now live it changes real behavior, so the [agent] config example
gains the line with its semantics (auto-approved batches only,
1 = fully sequential).

fix(slack): migrate send_file to the external upload flow (#370)

Slack removed the files.upload API; send_file was still calling it
(behind allow(deprecated)) AND hardcoding image/png as the content
type for every file, so delivering a generated PDF or spreadsheet
failed twice over.

send_file now uses the supported three-step flow: get an upload URL
via files.getUploadURLExternal, POST the bytes to it, then finalize
with files.completeUploadExternal targeting the channel with the
caption as initial_comment. Content type is inferred from the file
extension (pdf, xlsx, docx, pptx, images, audio, video, text) with an
octet-stream fallback, paths get tilde expansion like the other
send tools, and each step failure returns its own actionable error
instead of one opaque upload failure.

feat(slack): group tool calls into one edited-in-place message (#371)

A multi-tool turn posted one Slack message per tool call (a gear line
edited to a check on completion), flooding the channel exactly the way
the Telegram side used to before its processing-log block.

The handler now keeps ONE grouped message per turn: an "N tool calls"
header with one status line per tool (gear while running, check/cross
when done). Tool starts append to the shared list and edit the same
message in place via chat.update, posting it only on the first tool;
completions flip the matching running entry's icon and re-render.
Failed posts and updates log loudly, never silently.

fix(tui): render live tool rounds on inactive panes (#369)

Tool events were already routed into background pane state
(ToolCallStarted/Completed write to the sidecar's active_tool_group),
but the inactive-pane renderer collapsed all of it into a single
"N tool calls" badge, so unfocused sessions looked frozen while their
tools ran.

The badge now carries the live tail of the group beneath it: up to
the last four tool calls render as individual rows with per-call
status (gear running, check done, cross failed) and an "... N
earlier" marker for longer turns, updating in real time exactly like
the focused pane's group. Multi-pane, multi-agent turns are now
visibly concurrent everywhere, not just on the selected pane.

feat(slack): reaction turns and react-back, Telegram parity (#372)

Inbound: a reaction_added on one of the bot's messages becomes an
agent turn, framed by the shared sentiment helpers (approval reads as
keep going, a stop-sign as pause and ask; react-only is the default
response). Slack reactions travel by name, so a name-to-glyph table
feeds the classifier. Session keying matches handle_message (DMs by
user, channels by id), the bot's own reactions and reactions on
non-bot messages are ignored, and history persists only a compact
"[System: name reacted with :emoji:]" tag via the display split
instead of the full prompt scaffolding.

Outbound: the agent's <<react:EMOJI>> marker previously leaked into
Slack message text verbatim; the final delivery pipeline now extracts
it and fires reactions.add on the triggering message, with the glyph
mapped to a valid Slack reaction name (unknowns degrade to thumbsup).
The reaction turn's own reply supports the same react-back.

Mapping tables and their sentiment alignment with Telegram are
covered by tests.

feat(slack): collapsible tool group with Expand/Collapse toggle

Slack has no native equivalent of Telegram's expandable blockquote, so
the grouped tool message now simulates it with Block Kit: collapsed by
default to a summary line ("N tool calls · X running"), with an Expand
button that flips to the full per-tool list and a Collapse button back.
Single-tool turns stay a plain line with no button.

Group state lives in SlackState keyed by the message ts (bounded to
the 20 most recent; older groups freeze at their last render, like
Telegram's frozen blocks), so the block_actions toggle re-renders the
same message long after the turn's closures are gone. Progress updates
preserve the user's expansion choice: a completing tool never snaps an
expanded group shut. Expansion is per-message, not per-viewer, since
the message is shared.

Covers render modes, toggle/preservation semantics, and retention
pruning with tests.

fix(slack): migrate image and TTS uploads to the external flow (#370 follow-up)

The send_file migration left two more deprecated files.upload callers
in the handler: generated-image delivery and TTS voice replies, both
broken the same way once Slack removed the legacy API (and the image
path hardcoded image/png regardless of actual format).

Both now go through a shared upload_external helper implementing the
supported three-step flow, with real MIME types (via the slack_send
content-type table) and per-step error messages. TTS keeps its
thread_ts threading.

docs(readme): document Slack grouped tool calls, reactions, external uploads

The Slack channel rows still described the removed files.upload API
and none of the recent upgrades. The feature row now covers the
grouped collapsible tool-call message (Block Kit Expand/Collapse,
edited in place), reaction turns with react-back, and the external
upload flow with real MIME types; the attachment matrix and TTS
normalization notes drop the stale files.upload references.
