docs(contributing): clarify atomic issues policy

Even if multiple bugs are related or share a root cause, each should be
a separate atomic issue. A single PR can reference and close multiple
atomic issues, but the issue tracker stays clean with one issue per bug.

This prevents mega-issues that bundle 5 bugs and become blockers when
only 3 are fixed.

fix(telegram): escape URL in convert_links href attribute (#373)

convert_links unescaped &/</> in URLs but inserted raw chars
into <a href>, producing invalid HTML. Telegram rejected it with
400 can't parse entities, falling back to plain text and losing ALL
formatting for the entire message.

Fix: re-escape clean_url via escape_html() before href insertion.
Rich path (render_html.rs) already did this correctly.

fix(telegram): reduce ctx footer visual weight (#374)

Non-technical users found the plain-text ctx: footer distracting.
HTML path wraps footer in <i> (italic) for lighter visual weight.
Rich path wraps footer in <sub> (subscript) for metadata styling.

Both handle_message and resume_session delivery paths updated
(4 locations total).

fix(config): default_provider/default_model only fallback on provider load failure (#379)

[agent] default_provider/default_model now only kick in when the session's
stored provider fails to load (missing API key, provider unavailable).

Previously they unconditionally overrode ALL sessions on config reload,
breaking split panes, different channels, and parallel provider testing.

Fixes #379

fix(telegram): split_message uses char count instead of byte length (#376)

split_message compared text.len() (bytes) against max_len, but Telegram
limits messages to 4096 characters (code points). For multi-byte UTF-8
(Cyrillic, emoji, CJK), this caused chunks to exceed the char limit and
get rejected with 'text is too long', cascading to plain-text fallback.

Switched to chars().count() for the boundary check and char_indices()
for the split point, so chunks are always measured in characters.

Regression tests: multi-byte text that fits in one chunk by char count
but exceeds byte limit, and multi-byte text that correctly splits.

fix(telegram): add RetryAfter handling to rich API post_rich (#377)

post_rich treated any non-ok response as unrecoverable, including 429
rate limits. When Telegram throttled the rich API, messages immediately
fell back to HTML instead of waiting for the retry window.

Added 429 detection with retry_after extraction from the response
parameters field. On rate limit, sleeps for the specified duration
(defaulting to 5s) and retries once before falling through to the
error path.

fix(telegram): strip_html_tags removes all HTML tags generically (#378)

The old strip_html_tags used a chain of .replace() calls that only
handled b, i, code, and pre tags. Surviving tags (a, u, s, blockquote)
rendered as literal text in the Telegram client when messages fell back
to plain text.

Replaced with a generic HTML tag stripper that removes anything between
< and > delimiters. Also added " entity unescaping. Made the
function pub(crate) so regression tests can call it directly.

Regression tests cover: all formatting tags, anchor tags with href
attributes, blockquote, and HTML entity unescaping.

feat(discord): reaction turns and react-back, channel parity (#381)

Inbound: reaction_add on a bot message becomes a sentiment-framed
agent turn via the shared reaction helpers (approval reads as keep
going with a silent react-back as the default, a stop-sign as pause
and ask). The allow list applies exactly as for messages, the bot's
own reactions and reactions on non-bot messages are ignored, session
keying matches handle_message, and history persists only the compact
"[System: name reacted with emoji]" tag via the display split.
Discord delivers unicode emoji directly, so glyphs feed the shared
classifier without a name mapping; custom guild emoji classify as
Neutral.

Outbound: the agent's <<react:EMOJI>> marker previously leaked into
Discord text verbatim; the final delivery path now extracts it and
fires a real reaction on the user's message, and reaction-turn
replies support the same react-back.

fix(telegram): stop status-draft loop rendering as endless typing

The rolling status draft path had two compounding bugs that made the
bot appear to be typing forever in rich-message chats:

1. sendRichMessageDraft's ok response legitimately carries no
   message_id (drafts are not messages), but the parser treated that
   as failure, so every 1.5s tick logged a phantom error and re-sent
   the draft from scratch instead of settling.
2. The tick re-sent unconditionally, so a long or concurrent turn
   hammered the rich API every 1.5s per session until Telegram
   returned 429s, with each re-send refreshing the client-side
   "composing" indicator indefinitely.

The ok response now counts as success regardless of message_id, and
draft refreshes are throttled to one per ~6 seconds per session via a
last-attempt timestamp on the streaming state.

security: deny access by default and gate all channel commands as owner-only

- is_owner() returns false when both allowed and bot_owner are empty
  (was true — open mode footgun on unconfigured installs)
- user_allowed() returns false when both allowed_users and bot_owner
  are empty (same secure-by-default behavior)
- All channel commands except /new are now owner-only:
  /compact, /doctor, /evolve, /help, /models, /rtk, /sessions,
  /stop, /usage, /profiles, /goal, /mission-control, /rename,
  /cd, /respond_to
- /new stays open for session recovery (bugged/hallucinated sessions)
- Updated 3 test files to reflect deny-by-default semantics

Closes #389, #390

fix(telegram): delete stale quip pool, restore dynamic pre-block status (#391)

The progress status was designed dynamic (model's thinking excerpt or
a preview of the user's ask, edited in place, folded into the grouping
block header as the single surface). A stale quip-pool module rotated
hardcoded lines into the long-elapsed bucket, and after the recent
single-surface restructuring its leftover draft path became the only
pre-block surface: long blockless turns showed canned text in a
separate bubble that also duplicated the block header.

Deleted outright: rolling_status_quips.rs, build_status_message,
pre_tool_rolling, the draft-status branch, and the now-unused
send_rich_message_draft. No canned status text remains.

Restored the intended design: a dynamic pre-block status message
(thinking excerpt, else "Working on: <user's ask>"), edited in place
only while no grouping block exists. When the block opens or the turn
ends it is deleted, and its id clears ONLY on successful delete so a
failed delete retries next tick instead of orphaning the bubble. The
block header remains the single status surface once a block exists.

feat(discord): collapsible grouped tool calls with Expand/Collapse (#380)

Multi-tool turns posted one Discord message per tool call. The handler
now keeps ONE grouped message per turn, collapsed by default to a live
summary ("N tool calls · X running") with an Expand button; the toggle
re-renders the same message via the component interaction response
(which also acks the click). Single-tool turns stay a plain line with
no button.

Group state lives in DiscordState keyed by message id, bounded to the
20 most recent (older groups freeze at their last render), and updates
preserve the user's expanded choice so a completing tool never snaps
an open group shut — the same contracts as the Slack port, pinned by
the same tests.

fix(discord): drop unread channel_id from tool group state (#380)

The Expand/Collapse toggle re-renders through the component
interaction response, which already targets the message, so the
stored channel was never read (unlike the Slack port, where
chat.update needs it). Deleted rather than suppressed.

feat(discord): media gallery - batch generated files into one message (#385)

Generated images/files were delivered one message per file, flooding
the channel on multi-image turns. All attachments now land in a single
multi-attachment message, chunked at Discord's 10-attachments-per-
message cap with the remainder rolling into follow-up batches.
Unreadable files log and are skipped without sinking the whole batch.

feat(discord): select menus, modal forms, component TTL, role access, forum threads

Four gap closures plus the shared interaction plumbing:

- send_select (#382): discord_send posts a string select menu (max 25
  options); the pick disables the menu, shows who chose what, and
  routes back into the channel's session as a new turn with only a
  compact [System: ...] tag persisted.
- send_form (#383): discord_send posts an "Open form" button that
  opens a modal (max 5 fields, short or paragraph); submissions are
  collected in field order and routed back the same way.
- Component TTL (#386): pending selects and forms expire lazily after
  [channels.discord] component_ttl_hours (default 24); stale clicks
  get an "expired" response and the dead components are stripped from
  the message instead of firing stale actions.
- Access groups (#387): new [channels.discord] allowed_roles grants
  guild members access when they carry ANY configured role id,
  evaluated per message alongside allowed_users.
- Forum channels (#384): threads and forum posts carry their own
  channel id, so the allowed_channels check now falls back to the
  PARENT channel; allow-listing a forum admits every post, each post
  keeping its own per-thread session via the existing keying.

Interaction-originated turns share one router (session resolution
mirroring handle_message, display-split persistence, chunked reply
delivery) in the new interactions module.

feat(doc_gen): image blocks embed visuals inline in PDF and DOCX (#392)

New {type:"image", path, width_mm?, caption?} block for generate_document:
local PNG/JPEG files render inline in the document flow between text
blocks, sized to width_mm (aspect preserved, clamped to the page body,
natural size downscaled to fit by default) with an optional italic
caption beneath. Charts, diagrams, and logos now live inside the
report instead of arriving as loose companion files.

PDF: the image registers as an XObject, placed via dpi mapping with
its own page-break check so a visual never straddles a page boundary;
a decode failure renders a visible note rather than silently dropping
the image. DOCX: embedded via a real drawing part with EMU sizing.
Both formats validate the file up front (docx-rs's Pic::new panics on
bad input), so a missing or corrupt path fails generation with an
error naming the path.

The image crate becomes an unconditional dependency (docx-rs already
pulls it into every build) with png+jpeg decoding for dimension
reading. Covered by tests: embedding round-trips in both formats,
captions render, media parts land in the OOXML archive, and missing
paths fail with the path in the message.

fix(provider): parse element-style <function><name> tool-call leaks (#398)

deepseek-v4-flash (opencode-go) emits tool calls as sibling XML
elements: a bare <function> wrapper, the tool in <name>, and every
parameter as its own child element. None of the seven existing
text-leak shapes anchor on this (no =name suffix, no JSON, no
<invoke>), so the block leaked verbatim into Telegram output and the
call never dispatched — the user saw raw protocol XML and a dropped
request.

New extraction pass handles the shape: gated on KNOWN_TOOL_NAMES so
prose discussing a <function> tag is never swallowed, optional closing
tag (models drop closers constantly, the block then ends at the next
<function> or end of text), parameters collected as typed values
(numbers/bools keep their JSON type so integer params validate),
matched ranges stripped from the visible text.

Tests cover the exact observed artifact, a dropped closer with typed
args, multiple blocks in one response, and prose immunity.
feat(telegram): flow logs via rich API (32K) with HTML fallback (#393)

chore(logs): stop per-frame and per-chunk debug spam (#400)

Daily logs ran 200-350MB, ~95% of it one source: the TUI renderer's
[SCROLL] start/end DEBUG pair fired on every frame (over a million
lines a day) carrying values identical frame after frame. The pair is
now ONE trace-level line emitted only when the scroll state actually
changed.

Also demoted to trace: per-chunk [TUI] ResponseChunk lines and the
per-turn context-budget line. whatsapp-rust's chatter under CUSTOM
targets (Client/Keepalive pings every 30s, UnifiedSession time-offset
lines) never matched the module-path directives, so the filter now
caps those targets at warn.

DEBUG keeps state transitions, errors, and decisions; steady-state
repetition is gone.

fix(telegram): delete leftover status bubble when the turn ends (#403)

The dynamic pre-block status deleted itself only when a grouping block
opened or final response text landed. React-only turns produce
neither: the <<react:emoji>> marker strips to empty text, so the
trigger never fired and the "Working on: ..." bubble persisted in the
chat forever after the loop shut down.

The end-of-turn path now takes any remaining status message id and
deletes it with three retries; state clears with the take so a
concurrent tick cannot resurrect it, and exhausted retries log an
error naming the chat instead of failing silently.

fix(telegram): flow block freezes and restarts below mid-turn follow-ups (#404)

A follow-up sent during a running turn is injected between tool rounds
via the steering rail, but the Telegram progress callback had no arm
for the QueuedUserMessage event: the open processing-log block never
learned about it, so later tools kept appending to the OLD block above
the user's message and activity appeared stuck between follow-ups.

Both edit loops now handle the event: the open block freezes in place
(content stays visible, same semantics as the size-limit freeze), the
response placeholder is marked for re-post, and the next tool round
opens a fresh block BELOW the follow-up so the chat keeps flowing
bottom-down. The user's own message is already visible in the chat, so
nothing is rendered for the event itself.

feat(vision): dedicated image.vision.provider override bypasses enabled gate (#401)

A vision-only provider (valid key + vision_model, enabled = false for
chat) could never serve analyze_image: the provider scan and the
fallback.vision chain both require enabled = true, so vision fell
through to the Gemini fallback or the setup hint.

New [image.vision] provider = "name" config resolves vision from that
provider regardless of its enabled flag — naming it is explicit
intent. An unresolvable name (no vision_model) logs a warning and
falls through to the normal scan. The implicit scan and the chain
keep their enabled gates untouched: those are pinned by existing
tests (skips_disabled_provider, chain_disabled_entry_skipped), and an
earlier draft that relaxed the chain instead was rejected exactly

fix(telegram): mid-turn guard before edit-loop spawn, preview from user text (#407)

Consecutive image/file drops filled chats with one eternal

gone when the block opens or the turn ends.

fix(cron): one scheduler per profile via lock, stop duplicate job execution (#453)

When a multi-profile `daemon` and a `-p <profile>` daemon (or the TUI) both
covered the same profile, each spawned its own scheduler polling the same
cron_jobs table with no coordination, so every due job fired twice or thrice
(runs 280ms apart, different LLM output, different cost).

Add a per-profile scheduler lock: an advisory flock on
~/.opencrabs/locks/scheduler/<profile>.lock in the GLOBAL locks dir, so the
multi-profile daemon, a profile-specific daemon, and the TUI all contend on
one file regardless of task-local profile home. Acquire it in both scheduler
spawn paths (the foreign-profile loop in cmd_daemon and the active-profile
scheduler in cmd_chat_inner); if another live process holds it, skip spawning
instead of running a second scheduler. The kernel releases the lock when the
fd closes on drop or process death, so a crashed daemon never wedges a
profile's scheduling. The owner PID is stamped into the file for observability.

Mirror of Alexey's #444. 4 regression tests pin the contract (acquire, deny
while held, per-profile isolation, retake after release) against a TempDir.

(fence-aware, a --- inside a code block stays literal), every section
capped at Slack's 3000-char limit with splits preferring paragraph
boundaries.

The plain text rides along as the notification fallback, and a rejected
blocks post retries text-only, so delivery never regresses on a Block
Kit error. New blocks module keeps the builders pure and unit-tested.

feat(slack): ctx footer as a small grey context block (#457)

The ctx budget footer rendered as plain body text, indistinguishable
from the conversation. It now rides the last message of every
completion as a Block Kit context block with italic mrkdwn inside:
Slack's small grey type, the native equivalent of Telegram's italic
footer.

The standalone footer posts from the intermediate-as-answer paths use
the same context block via a shared helper. Every path keeps a
plain-text fallback (footer appended to the fallback text, or a plain
retry when the blocks post is rejected) so the footer is never lost.

fix(agent): persist the closing iteration even when the phantom skip fired (#458)

The per-iteration DB persist skipped any text matching the phantom
tool-intent pattern, but the turn-end phantom detection uses a looser
rule: after successful tool calls, a text with no forward-looking
intent phrase is a completion acknowledgement, not a phantom. When the
two disagreed, the final completion streamed to the display and was
never written, so a restart or session reload lost it (the assistant
row ended at the last tool block).

Two layers:
- the persist-skip now applies the same exemption as the detector, so
  a completion ack after tool calls persists normally
- the skipped content is stashed instead of dropped, and if the turn
  closes on that very iteration it is flushed to the DB at turn close,
  so reloadable history always matches what the user saw on screen

fix(slack): ctx footer edits into the completion message, never posts below (#459)

The intermediate-as-answer paths posted the footer as its own message
under the completion. Owner spec: the footer belongs ON the completion,
display-only, exactly like Telegram appends it to the response text.

The intermediates list now carries the posted mrkdwn text alongside ts
and hash, and both paths append the footer via chat.update: the kept
message is rebuilt as Block Kit sections plus the small grey
context-block footer, which also retroactively enriches it. A rejected
blocks update retries as a plain-text update with the footer appended;
if that fails the footer is dropped with a warn. A standalone footer
post is never an option.

Unchanged: footer stays out of the DB record, session history and TTS;
the final-post path already carried it on the last message correctly.

fix(tui): session switch always syncs the agent working directory (#460)

Switching sessions could leave the agent on the PREVIOUS session's
working directory: the footer showed the new session's repo while the
system prompt and tools ran in the old one.

The agent's wd is a shared runtime value that tool-driven cd mutates
without updating the TUI-tracked path. load_session's restore compared
the session's persisted wd against the TUI-tracked value and skipped
the agent sync when they matched, which is exactly the case where the
agent sat on another session's directory.

Two changes:
- load_session pushes the session's persisted wd to the agent
  unconditionally, and pins the agent to the TUI-tracked directory
  when a session has no persisted wd, so a previous session's dir can
  never leak in
- complete_response resyncs the TUI-tracked wd from the agent, so a
  tool-driven cd during a turn shows in the footer instead of silently
  diverging

fix(phantom): close the anchor evasions and verb gaps behind live fake completions (#463, #464)

Three hallucinated completions shipped within an hour, all narration
with zero tool calls. Each escaped a different way:

- Inline directives broke every anchored pattern: the narration behind
  a react marker never matched. Detectors now strip inline directives
  before matching.
- The work-announcement regex was anchored to message start, so a lead
  clause or a whole sentence before the gerund evaded it. The matcher
  now tests every sentence start and tolerates a short comma clause.
- The post-success eligibility gate checked intent phrases only; a
  present-continuous announcement after a successful tool call closed
  the turn as a fake completion ack. The gate now also runs the
  work-announcement matcher: an announcement is a promise, never an
  ack.
- Verb gaps: the load family was missing everywhere, so 'Let me load
  both properly now.' matched nothing. Added load/sync/install/
  download/upload/register/enable/disable families to the English
  lists and load-family phrases to es/fr/pt/ru.
- New language-agnostic tell: a zero-tool iteration whose text names a
  registered tool (underscore names, word-boundary) is narrating usage
  it never executed, in any language. Wired into the nudge gate.
- New id.toml: Indonesian intent phrases scan alongside the other
  languages (char-set detection cannot route ASCII-Latin languages,
  but the intent scan checks every language at once).
- The past-tense claim checker gained a passive-voice guard so 'the
  config is loaded from disk' prose stays clean while 'Both loaded
  properly' claims fire.

All five live incident texts are pinned by regression tests on their
actual escape paths.

feat(cli): opencrabs session set-model for non-interactive switching (#465)

New subcommand sets provider/model on session rows without menus or raw
sqlite:

  opencrabs session set-model <provider/model> <id-or-prefix>
  opencrabs session set-model <provider/model> --name "<title match>"
  opencrabs session set-model <provider/model> --all

The pair splits on the FIRST slash so slashed model names survive.
Target resolution never guesses: an ambiguous id prefix or title match
errors with the candidate list, and --all covers non-archived sessions
only. The provider must name a configured section (new
factory::is_known_provider_name, reused by the upcoming direct-arg
channel switch). A running instance applies the pair on each session's
next message via the existing sync path.

Selection rules unit-tested in src/tests/cli_session_set_model_test.rs.

feat(config): force_default pushes the default pair to all sessions on reload (#466)

[providers.<name>] gains force_default. When the ACTIVE default
provider's section carries the flag, a config reload writes its default
pair to every non-archived session, overriding stored pairs. Absent or
false keeps the post-#379 isolation: defaults apply to new sessions
only.

The push never invents anything: it broadcasts exactly the section's
configured pair, skips rows already on it (no updated_at churn), never
touches archived sessions, and logs the count. Live sessions apply the
pair on their next message via the existing sync path. Implemented as
a small pure decision fn plus an apply fn wired into the ConfigWatcher
callbacks, both covered by tests (flag off, flag on, archived
exclusion, idempotence).

feat(channels): /models <provider/model> switches directly everywhere (#467)

/models with an argument applies the pair immediately to the CURRENT
session on every channel (the shared handle_command dispatch serves
Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp) and on the TUI — no inline keyboard
round trip. Bare /models keeps the interactive picker. /model works as
an alias.

The switch reuses the exact keyboard-flow path (switch_model:
per-session swap, manual pin, session + change-message persist) so
pinning semantics are identical. Unknown providers reply with an
explicit error instead of guessing; the pair parser (shared with the
CLI set-model through utils::provider_pair) splits on the FIRST slash
so slashed model names survive. The TUI reflects the switch in the
in-memory session immediately so the footer updates without a reload.

feat(channels): apply-to-scope selector for direct model switches (#468)

The direct /models <provider/model> switch gains scoping on every
surface: a trailing all token (/models minimax/MiniMax-M3 all) applies
the pair to every non-archived session after switching the current one.
Telegram additionally offers an inline Apply-to-all-sessions button on
the switch confirmation, riding the same pipe-separated callback
convention as the model picker (skipped when the payload would exceed
Telegram's 64-byte callback limit).

The bulk write lives on SessionService (set_provider_model_all_sessions,
shared semantics with the CLI --all path): rows already on the pair are
skipped, archived rows never touched, and live sessions pick the pair
up on their next message via the existing sync path. Session isolation
stays the default; all is always an explicit act. Writer covered by an
in-memory DB test.

docs(readme): document the #461 switching family

Covers opencrabs session set-model (CLI, id/title/--all targeting),
the direct /models <provider/model> switch on every channel and the
TUI with the all scope and Telegram's apply-to-all button, and the
force_default reload push.

refactor(telegram): one shared post-loop display drain for both handlers (#470)

The remaining-display-items drain (fold queued tools and intermediates
into the processing-log flow after the edit loop stops) was copy-pasted
between handle_message and resume_session, the drift risk called out in
the #462 analysis. Both now route through one drain_remaining_display,
with the only real difference expressed as a parameter: the inbound
message a folded react directive acknowledges, which resume does not
have.

feat(rsi): mission-control staleness indicator and provider creation fallback (#469)

RSI went dark for three days while the ledger kept recording, and
Mission Control showed it as healthy the whole time. Two fixes:

Staleness indicator: Mission Control (the report tool AND the TUI
analytics panel) now shows an RSI liveness line sourced from the last
self_improve / feedback_analyze / rsi_propose execution. Healthy reads
plain (RSI last run 2h 0m ago); older than 12h WITH tool events
recorded since warns loudly (RSI stale: last run 3d 2h ago, N tool
events since); never-ran states it. Old age with an idle ledger stays
calm: nothing happened for RSI to process. The threshold rules are a
pure function pinned by tests, including the exact incident shape.

Provider fallback: a dead self_improvement_provider (missing key,
typo, removed section) no longer kills the cycle — provider creation
falls back to the user's active provider with a loud warning, before
the existing [providers.fallback] chain wrap (which already covered
runtime failures since e39cd7c3).

refactor(telegram): move flow-block machinery to flow.rs, verbatim (#471 phase 1)

First mechanical cut of the 7.2k-line handler.rs: the processing-log
flow (streaming state types, the three renderers, and the flow
operations: open/refresh/append/restick/freeze/fold/dedup) moves to a
dedicated flow.rs.

Pure move: code is byte-identical except visibility widened to
pub(crate) on the moved items and two handler helpers the flow calls
(format_inline; send_html_or_plain was already crate-visible), plus a
glob re-export from handler so every existing call site and test
import path keeps working unchanged. handler.rs: 7221 → 6318 lines;
flow.rs: 924.

refactor(telegram): move markdown/HTML text transforms to markdown.rs, verbatim (#471 phase 1)

Second mechanical cut: md_to_html, command_md_to_html,
markdown_to_telegram_html, strip_html_tags, escape_html, format_inline,
convert_links, find_closing_marker and split_message move to a
dedicated markdown.rs. All are pure text transforms with no Bot API or
state dependency.

Pure move: byte-identical bodies, visibility widened to pub(crate) on
the two private helpers, glob re-export from handler keeps every call
site and test import stable.

refactor(telegram): move incoming-media helpers to media.rs, verbatim (#471 phase 1)

Third mechanical cut: caption merging, tmp file download/saving,
recent-tmp-file lookup and the size-capped getFile wrapper move to a
dedicated media.rs. Pure move, pub(crate) visibility bumps, glob
re-export keeps all paths stable.

refactor(telegram): move intermediate/outbound send helpers to intermediates.rs, verbatim (#471 phase 1)

Fourth mechanical cut: flush_intermediates, the last-intermediate
footer append, the rich-first intermediate send, the rate-limit
retrying wrapper and send_html_or_plain move to intermediates.rs.
Pure move, pub(crate) bumps, glob re-export keeps all paths stable.

refactor(telegram): move keyboard builders to keyboards.rs, verbatim (#471 phase 1)

Fifth mechanical cut: the tool-approval callback (Yes/Always/No
keyboard prompt), the /cd directory browser keyboard and the profile
picker keyboard move to keyboards.rs. Pure move, glob re-export keeps
all paths stable.

refactor(telegram): move crash-recovery resume to resume.rs, verbatim (#471 phase 1)

Sixth mechanical cut: resume_session (647 lines) moves to resume.rs.
Pure move; visibility widened on the handler internals it uses
(TypingGuard, tool_context, drain_remaining_display,
StreamingState::render), re-export keeps the ui.rs call path stable.

Phase 1 tally: handler.rs 7221 → 4547 lines; new modules flow (928),
markdown (367), media (319), intermediates (257), keyboards (243),
resume (656) — all under the 1k ceiling, most under 400. The remaining
4547 is dominated by the single handle_message function, which shrinks
further in phase 2 (delivery extraction, #471) and a follow-up front-
half split.

refactor(telegram): extract deliver_final_response from handle_message (#471 phase 2)

The 542-line final-response match moves out of handle_message into
deliver_final_response: marker extraction, sanitize, react directive,
dedup, reaction-only handling with the #439 work-turn guard,
folded-final reclaim, footer, rich-first send with HTML fallback,
chunked sends, history recording and TTS.

Body is verbatim except two deliberate mechanical edits, both
control-flow preserving:
- early 'return Ok(())' becomes 'return Ok(false)', and the call site
  returns from handle_message when false — the leftover-reaction flush
  still never runs on reaction-only/cleanup shapes, exactly as before
- clippy-driven needless-borrow removals on the now-reference params

streaming_msg_id ownership moves into the fn (it was only used by this
region and takes() internally).

refactor(telegram): resume rides the shared deliver_final_response (#471 phase 3)

deliver_final_response is now the ONE final-delivery path. The inbound
message becomes Option (reaction target and reply anchor): live turns
pass Some, resume passes None because the original message id is lost
across restarts — reactions strip without firing, exactly the old
resume behavior.

resume.rs drops its 250-line hand-maintained delivery copy for the
shared call. Deliberate unifications, previously drift between the
copies:
- the ctx footer renders in <i> like live turns (resume had <sub>)
- intermediate dedup uses the shared normalized matching
- group history now records the bot reply on resumed turns too

resume.rs: 656 → 476 lines; the two-path duplication called out in
the #462 analysis (item 1) is gone.

refactor(telegram): move the unified delivery path to delivery.rs (#471 phase 4)

deliver_final_response and drain_remaining_display move to a dedicated
delivery.rs (642 lines): the ONE path every Telegram turn ends on, for
live and resumed turns alike. Pure move with import/visibility plumbing
only (fire_reaction widened to pub(crate)).

handler.rs lands at 3983 lines — from 7221 at the start of #471.

fix(telegram): mid-turn follow-ups no longer shred the flow block (#475)

In a busy group every incoming message during a long turn queued as a
follow-up and froze the open flow block, so one turn fragmented into a
dozen tiny blocks (1 tool calls / 2 tool calls / 1 tool calls within a
minute) instead of one growing block at the bottom.

The freeze was #404's way of making the next round appear below the
user's follow-up. #451's restick now achieves that ordering by moving
the SAME block below the newest message on the next round, so the
freeze is obsolete: detach_flow_for_followup keeps the block open and
only re-posts the response placeholder. One block per turn, always at
the bottom — the original contract restored.

fix(telegram): code fences disqualify the native rich markdown path (#476)

A clean markdown message with a triple-backtick fence rendered in chat
with literal code-tag artifacts around the fenced block. The model's
output was verified clean in channel_messages; the mangling came from
Telegram's server-side rich markdown parser, which handles inline
formatting only and butchers fences. The path only opened yesterday
when rich_messages became the default (#425) — five prior weeks with
rich off never routed fenced messages there.

has_rich_structure now returns false whenever any line opens a fence,
so those messages ride the HTML pipeline, which renders fences
perfectly as pre blocks. Tables, headings, lists and math without
fences keep native rich. Applies to intermediates and final responses
alike. Regression test pins the exact incident shape.

fix(telegram): reclaim the folded answer before the reaction decision (#478)

A full completion rendered inside the collapsed Processing log block
while the visible final message was just the react emoji. The answer
had streamed as mid-turn narration and folded into the flow (#300);
the model closed with empty text plus a react directive, and the
reaction-only branch early-returned BEFORE the folded-final reclaim,
leaving the answer imprisoned in the block.

Two fixes:
- deliver_final_response reclaims the folded final BEFORE the reaction
  decision: an empty final with a folded answer delivers the answer as
  the completion, with the react landing as a reaction on top. The
  reaction-only skip now applies only when there is genuinely nothing
  to say.
- take_folded_final pops the whole trailing run of Text entries
  (joined in order) instead of only the last one: since #475 keeps ONE
  block across queued follow-ups, the answer can be multi-part, and
  popping one entry left earlier parts stuck. The pop is a pure
  function pinned by tests, including the exact incident shape.

feat(config): startup warnings for silent config drift (#477)

Two once-per-process diagnostics at startup, never on hot reload:

- an ignored working_directory key (top level or [agent]) is flagged:
  the schema has no such key and serde drops unknown keys silently,
  so the agent fell back to its own cwd with zero errors while the
  user believed the config applied. The warning also notes when the
  configured path does not exist on disk. Working directories are
  per-session.
- [agent] default_provider without force_default on the named section
  gets the escape-hatch hint: defaults apply to new sessions only,
  and force_default = true pushes the pair to all sessions on reload.
  An unknown default_provider name is flagged harder.

Pure decision function with tests covering clean config, both
warnings, the missing-path note, quiet-when-forced, and the unknown
provider case.

docs(readme): drop stale working_directory config key, note per-session cwd (#479)

working_directory was never a schema field; serde ignored it silently
since per-session working-directory isolation landed. Replace the
example line with a note that the working directory is per-session (set
via /cd or launch cwd).

fix(telegram): revert the fence disqualification, tables render rich again (#476 revert)

#476 made any message containing a code fence bypass rich and go HTML.
That was wrong: Claude CLI answers routinely carry a table AND a fence,
so those messages went fully HTML and the table unwrapped to raw pipes.
Rich is the default (#425) and nothing should be pulled out of it.

has_rich_structure counts a fence as rich structure again, so
structured messages render as native rich messages as before. Fence
mangling under Telegram's rich markdown parser is a separate cosmetic
issue whose correct fix is the native-block serializer (#420 path B),
not exclusion.

feat(telegram): status preview uses whole last human-readable text, no truncation (#487)

The collapsed block's ↳ activity line took the FIRST line of the LAST flow
entry and truncated it to 96 chars, so a raw-JSON last entry produced
`↳ {"model": ...}` and any narration was clipped.

latest_activity_preview now walks newest-first and returns the most recent
HUMAN-READABLE intermediary text — the whole thing, all paragraphs, newlines
preserved, no truncation (amendment) — after skipping entries that are JSON
(`{`/`[`), code blocks (triple backtick), or raw output (a bare path/number
with no internal whitespace). Narration is preferred over a following tool
line, since it usually describes the tool now running and reads better than
`⚙️ read_file src/agent.rs`. Falls back to the most recent tool label+context
when there is no human-readable text.

Mirror of Alexey's #481. Tests cover whole untruncated multi-line text, JSON
and code-block skip-back, marker stripping, one-word-sentence vs bare-path,
and the tool fallback; two prior tests that asserted truncation and
tool-line-over-narration are updated to the new contract.

feat(telegram): extract bash line-start comments as flow status (#488)

Bash commands often carry progress comments (`# --- Setup environment ---`,
`# Installing deps`) that are the most meaningful status a turn can show, but
they were only ever surfaced as raw command context.

Add extract_status_from_text and wire it into latest_activity_preview as the
second priority, between the whole-human-readable-text source (#487) and the
tool label+context fallback. When a turn has no narration, the preview pulls
line-start `#` comments from the most recent bash command: a comment is a line
whose first non-whitespace char is `#` (no shell-aware parsing of inline `#`),
the `#` and any `---`/`===` decoration are stripped (`# --- Setup ---` yields
`Setup`), shebangs are ignored, and multiple comments join by newlines,
untruncated. Narration still wins when present.

Mirror of Alexey's #482. Tests cover decoration stripping, multi-comment
newline join, shebang/inline-hash rejection, the no-comment fallthrough, and
both integration directions (bash-comments used with no narration, narration
beating bash comments).

feat(telegram): flow header wall-clock duration + finished/failed/timeout states (#486)

The block header showed coarse elapsed (`<1m`/`1m`, humanize_elapsed_coarse
from #452) during a turn and dropped it entirely on completion, with no visual
distinction between a successful, failed, or timed-out turn.

Header now reads:
- live: `⚙️ N tool calls · 45s` — precise wall-clock seconds anchored at turn
  start (new turn_started_at, never reset), then `1 min 30s`. The tool name
  left the header; the ↳ preview carries the activity now (#487/#488).
- settled: `✅ Finished (N tool calls, 45s)`, `❌ Failed (...)`, or
  `⏱ Timed out (...)`, dropping the count clause when no tools ran.

Add humanize_duration, a FlowOutcome enum, a FlowHeader header model, and a
shared flow_header_text so the classic HTML and rich-details headers can't
drift. The settled outcome is classified from the agent result (Ok → Finished;
Err → Timed out when the message names a timeout, else Failed), stamped on the
block and re-rendered once after deliver_final_response so it lands on the
block's final shape (post folded-answer promotion). No block means no settled
header, so plain tool-less turns stay a single clean response.

This reverts #452's coarse timer: live seconds restring the header each tick.
A manually expanded block collapsing on a header edit is a client-side
(Telegram Desktop) behavior with no server-side state to preserve, so it is out
of scope; precise progress time is worth more.

Mirror of Alexey's #480. Tests cover the duration format, live/settled header
strings, outcome icon/verb mapping, and the settled block render; the coarse
timer test is removed.

fix(telegram): cap folded narration length in the flow block (#489)

A Claude CLI turn split into 31 + 41 tool blocks with no user message
between: the split is the rich block's 30K char size freeze, and CLI
fills it fast because its whole answer streams as intermediate text
folded into the block (API keeps the answer in response.content, so
API blocks are compact tool lines and hold far more rounds).

Each folded narration entry is now capped at 300 displayed chars with
an ellipsis in both live renderers. Display-only: the renderers read
flow_entries without mutating them, so take_folded_final still reclaims
the full final answer. The block becomes a compact progress log that
holds far more rounds before the freeze. Tool lines and the
latest-activity preview are unchanged.

Split out of a concurrent-edit tangle where this landed bundled in the
#486 commit; recommitted here as its own change.

feat(telegram): send final responses as native rich blocks, fixing fence mangling (#476)

The rich markdown input mode is parsed server-side, and Telegram's
parser mangles code fences into literal <code> artifacts (the #476
complaint) while rendering tables. The HTML path renders fences but not
tables. Neither can do both, which is why disqualifying fenced messages
from rich (reverted earlier) only traded one ugliness for another.

Path B: final responses now serialize to native InputRichMessage
blocks via render_json (already built and tested) and send through the
new send_rich_blocks_id. The server does NO markdown re-parsing, so
tables AND code fences both render natively with nothing to mangle.

Safe rollout, zero regression risk: blocks are tried first, and on ANY
API rejection the send falls back to the markdown rich path (tables
good, fences mangle), then to HTML. Worst case is exactly today's
behavior. The ctx footer rides as an italic paragraph in the same
message. Intermediates and the flow block are unchanged for now; this
targets the final answer where tables and fenced code appear.

fix(telegram): fold mid-turn narration into flow block instead of a standalone bubble (#490)

While a processing-log block is open, the streaming edit loop opened a
separate `▋` placeholder for the model's mid-round narration, so
intermediate text like "fmt and clippy green. Running the test suite."
surfaced as its own Telegram message beneath the folded block, then got
deleted and folded on the next tool call (the "appears then vanishes").

Gate the standalone placeholder on `open_block.is_none()`: while a block
is open, narration folds into it via `append_intermediate_to_flow` and
the final answer is delivered once, complete, by `deliver_final_response`
at turn end. Turns with no tool calls keep the live streaming placeholder
unchanged. Stale-placeholder cleanup now runs unconditionally so a bubble
opened before the first tool call is still removed once a block opens.

fix(cli): run tool loop in headless run/agent so --auto-approve executes tools (#492)

`opencrabs run --auto-approve` and `opencrabs agent -m` called
`send_message`, a single `provider.complete()` that extracts and prints
the assistant text with no tool execution. So the model's tool calls
surfaced as plain text (markdown bash fences, XML) and exited 0 without
touching the filesystem. Every other surface (TUI, Telegram, Discord,
Slack, WhatsApp) routes through `run_tool_loop`; the headless CLI was the
only path that skipped it. The `--auto-approve` flag was discarded
outright in the REPL (`let _ = auto_approve`).

Route both paths through `send_message_with_tools_and_callback`:

- Build the service with `with_auto_approve_tools(auto_approve)` so the
  flag executes tools without an approval prompt.
- `run` (single-shot, no TTY when backgrounded) passes no approval
  callback: non-approval tools run, approval-gated ones are cleanly
  denied by the loop when the flag is absent.
- The interactive REPL prompts on stdin per approval-gated tool when the
  flag is absent.
- New `cli::headless_callbacks` module: stdout progress reporter plus the
  stdin approval prompt, with a pure `approval_from_answer` helper.

Regression tests cover the answer parsing and assert both handlers call
the tool-loop entry point and wire the flag.

fix(telegram): show latest-activity preview in the collapsed rich flow summary

The rich `<details>` flow block collapses to its summary alone, hiding the
body by default. #436 removed the `↳` latest-activity preview from that
summary on the reasoning that the body already lists every entry, but the
body is collapsed, so the summary was the only visible surface and it
carried no progress at all: a live rich block showed just
`⚙️ N tool calls · 45s` with no narration, no current step.

Render the preview in the summary (matching the classic HTML blockquote
path, which keeps it visible while collapsed). Narration wins as the
preview source, falling back to the most recent tool line. The minor
duplication when the block is expanded mirrors the classic path and is the
accepted trade for always-visible collapsed progress.

Tests updated to expect the preview in the summary; new regression asserts
folded intermediate narration surfaces in the collapsed summary.

fix(telegram): extract bash status comments from the raw command, not the decorated hint (#488)

The collapsed flow block's `↳` status preview pulls line-start `#` comments
from the most recent bash command (#482). It read `FlowLine::Tool.context`,
which is the DISPLAY hint from `tool_context_hint`: the command wrapped as
`` (`…`) `` and middle-truncated to 80 bytes. Two failures followed:

- A comment on the command's FIRST line was dropped. After decoration the
  line starts with `` ( `` not `#`, so the extractor's `starts_with('#')`
  never matched it. The issue's own example, `# --- Setup environment ---`
  on line 1, produced no status.
- The 80-byte middle-truncation elided or split comments in any longer
  command, violating the no-truncation amendment.

Carry the raw command separately: `ToolMsg`/`FlowLine::Tool` gain a
`raw_context` field populated from the redacted tool input at `ToolStarted`
(new `tool_status_source` helper), and `latest_activity_preview` extracts
from `raw_context`. Display still uses the decorated `context`.

The old tests passed a raw command as `context` via `tline`, so they tested
input the pipeline never produces. New `bash_line` helper builds a line the
real way (decorated context + raw command); regressions cover the first-line
comment and a >80-byte command.

fix(telegram): gate resume streaming placeholder on open block so narration folds (#490)

The #490 open-block guard landed in handle_message but not in resume_session,
which carries its own copy of the streaming edit loop. So a resumed turn
(crash-recovery replay) with an open processing-log block still opened a
standalone `▋` placeholder for mid-turn narration, leaking it as its own
message beneath the folded block: the exact bubble #490 fixed on the live path.

Mirror the guard here: compute open_block from open_group_msg_id, run the
stale-placeholder cleanup unconditionally, and only stream the standalone
placeholder when no block is open. While a block is open the narration folds
into it and the final answer is delivered by deliver_final_response at turn end.

feat(telegram): opt-in per-group open mode so a trusted group serves all members (#495)

Group members who were not individually listed hit "not authorized" when
they @mentioned or replied to the bot: the per-chat ACL only passes global
admins/owner or users named in `[channels.telegram.groups.<id>].allowed_users`,
so an ordinary member of an otherwise-trusted group was refused. Listing
every member by hand does not scale.

Add an opt-in `open` flag per group: `[channels.telegram.groups.<id>] open = true`
lets ANY member of THAT group pass the ACL without being individually listed.
DMs and every other group stay locked (a member of an open group is still
refused in DMs and in other groups unless separately allowed), so
secure-by-default holds everywhere else. Defaults to false, so existing
configs are unchanged.

This does NOT touch the empty-guard (`allowed_users` + `bot_owner` both empty
still denies, the #389/#390 secure-by-default fix); it only widens access
inside a group the owner has explicitly opted in.

Regression tests cover an open group serving an unlisted member, still
refusing that member in DMs and in other groups, and an unconfigured bot
denying even inside an open group.

docs(telegram): fix stale detach_flow_for_followup comment to match #475 behavior (#496)

The doc comment opened by describing a freeze-and-close: "keep the rendered
message on screen... close it... entries rendered into the frozen message are
dropped from state." The code does the opposite since #475: the block is NOT
closed or frozen and entries are NOT dropped; only the response placeholder
re-posts and #451's restick relocates the same block below the newest message.
The stale paragraph was copy-pasted from a freeze helper and contradicted the
implementation. Rewrite it to describe the #475 behavior the code implements.

fix(telegram): register /start in the command menu so onboarding is discoverable (#497)

`/start` was handled (handler.rs dispatches it before the ACL gate so even
unauthorized users get their user ID back) but never registered in the
command menu published via setMyCommands, so it never appeared in Telegram's
autocomplete in DMs or groups. The unauthorized-access reply tells users to
"Send /start to get your user ID", yet that command was the one the menu
never advertised: a self-defeating onboarding loop. `/new` was even
registered as "Start a new session", putting the word Start on the wrong
command while the real bootstrap command was invisible.

Add `start` as the first built-in command with a description reflecting its
job (get your user ID), distinct from `/new`. Default scope, so it publishes
to both DMs and groups. No handler change; the dispatch already exists.

fix(telegram): render the flow activity preview live-only, swap ↳ for • (#498)

The latest-activity preview (the mid-turn narration line under the flow
header) was appended unconditionally by both renderers, with no live-vs-
settled check. So when a turn settled, the stale narration stayed glued to
the `✅ Finished (N tool calls, D)` rollup instead of the rollup standing
alone. Introduced by f66806ed, which added the preview to the summary/header
but never gated it on turn state.

Gate the preview on `FlowHeader::Live(_)` in both render_flow_html_with
(classic blockquote) and render_flow_details_with (rich details): a settled
block is now just its outcome header, the narration remains only in the
collapsed body log. Also swap the `↳` carriage-return glyph for `•`: the
rich collapsed summary is inline-only (raw newlines ignored, the rich AST
has no line-break node), so the return glyph promised a break it could never
render; a bullet separates the preview honestly. The dead-code markdown
renderer gets the same glyph for consistency.

render_flow_details_with is now pub(crate) (matching render_flow_html_with)
so the settled path is directly testable. Regressions assert a settled block
carries no preview on both surfaces; existing preview tests updated to `•`.

fix(telegram): unify flow-block separator on the • bullet, drop the · middle-dot (#499)

The flow block mixed two separator glyphs: the header/status joins used the
`·` middle-dot while the latest-activity preview (#498) used the `•` bullet.
Unify on the bullet so the block reads with one consistent glyph.

Swap `·` to `•` at all five join sites in flow.rs: the entry+status joins in
render_flow_html_with, render_flow_details_with, and render_flow_rich, the
markdown header, and the flow_header_text Live header. `⚙️ 9 tool calls · 45s`
now reads `⚙️ 9 tool calls • 45s`, matching the preview. Doc comments in
flow.rs and handler.rs that quoted the old `·` header are updated to match,
and the render tests assert the bullet.

Scoped to the Telegram flow block. TUI, CLI, Discord/Slack tool-group
rollups, and usage-stat lines use `·` on their own surfaces and are left
untouched.

fix(telegram): lead the flow status header with the status message, bold it, italicize the count

Reorder the live status header so the status message comes first, then the
tool-call count, joined by the • bullet: ⚙️ status • count instead of
⚙️ count • status. The status message renders bold, the count italic.

Emphasis moves into the shared flow_header_text via a HeaderMarkup dialect
(<b>/<i> for HTML, **/_ for markdown) so all three renderers style the header
identically and can never drift. The plain-count and settled headers stay
fully bold. render_flow_rich now routes through flow_header_text instead of
rebuilding the header inline.

fix(telegram): answer a pending follow_up_question with a mid-turn text message (#500)

A follow_up_question that shows buttons blocks inside rx.await. Typing a
text answer instead of tapping a button did nothing: the handler saw an
active turn and queued the text for between-rounds injection, but the tool
never ends a round while suspended on the oneshot, so the text sat until a
button click or the 10-minute timeout.

Add a session -> question_id reverse map so a mid-turn text can resolve the
pending question directly: resolve_pending_question_with_text fires the
oneshot with the text, the tool unblocks and returns it as the answer. The
button-click path now also clears the reverse entry, and the tool clears
both maps on timeout or a closed channel so no dead entry lingers to
swallow the next message.

fix(telegram): atomically claim the turn to stop follow-ups forking a parallel turn (#501)

is_turn_active was checked ~600 lines before mark_turn_active ran, so a
follow-up arriving in that window (which includes a group-history DB
query) read the session as idle and started a SECOND concurrent agent
call. The new turn replied while the original was orphaned and kept
running as an unkillable zombie. The design intent (queue the follow-up
and inject it between the running turn's tool rounds) never fired: the
logs showed zero queued-for-injection events despite overlapping turns.

try_begin_turn does the check-and-set atomically under one lock: it
marks the session active and returns an RAII guard, or returns None when
a turn is already in flight (the caller then answers a pending
follow_up_question or enqueues for injection, exactly as before). The
guard is claimed at the mid-turn decision point and held through the
whole agent call, clearing on every exit path. The late mark is removed.

Atomicity pinned by tests (concurrent claim refused while active,
per-session independence, reclaim after the guard drops).

fix(rsi): stop re-proposing already applied/rejected skills and commands (#502)

Confirmed with live data: /standup was applied at 13:38 and re-proposed
identical at 15:01; github_workflow was applied twice (Jun 1, Jun 27)
and is pending again. The user re-approved the same suggestions dozens
of times because add_tool/command/skill_proposal deduped only against
PENDING proposals, never against the applied or rejected archives, so
RSI re-filed an identical proposal every cycle.

add_*_proposal now skips (returns an empty id, the tool reports 'already
applied or rejected, not re-proposed') when the name is in the applied/
or rejected/ archive. The list methods also filter handled names, so
stale duplicates filed before this landed self-heal out of the inbox
without touching the files. An applied skill already exists; a rejected
one the user said no to.

Tests: an applied command is not re-proposed, a rejected skill is not
re-proposed, and the archive round-trip test uses distinct names.

feat(rsi): propose slash commands from repeated user requests (#504)

RSI already promotes high-frequency bash subsystems the AGENT runs; this
adds the other half, codifying what the USER keeps typing (the /standup
case). A new detector groups recent user-message texts by a normalized
signature (lowercase, collapse whitespace, drop @mentions and
punctuation, exact significant-word sequence) and surfaces any signature
seen COMMAND_PATTERN_THRESHOLD+ times as a slash-command promotion
candidate. The RSI cycle queries recent_user_requests across all chats
and pushes each candidate as an opportunity the agent files via
rsi_propose kind=command.

Conservative by design: single words, existing slash commands, and long
prose are rejected so one-off chatter never proposes. Safe to suggest
freely now that #502 stops re-proposing already applied/rejected names.

The detector is a pure function with tests (recurring ask crosses the
threshold, mentions/punctuation normalize together, trivial and prose
rejected, most-frequent-first stable order). Remaining #504 scope
(tool-sequence to skill, workflow shortcuts) is a follow-up.

feat(rsi): detect recurring tool sequences as skill candidates (#504)

Where the command-pattern pass codifies what the user keeps typing, this
codifies what the agent keeps doing: an ordered tool run recurring across
many distinct sessions is a workflow worth a SKILL.md. Slide an n-gram
window over each session's tool sequence, count DISTINCT sessions per
n-gram, and surface any n-gram seen in enough sessions as a skill
candidate for the RSI agent to file via rsi_propose kind=skill.

Cross-session recurrence is the signal, so a within-session loop cannot
inflate it, and single-tool windows are skipped so a tight loop of one
tool never masquerades as a workflow. The detector is pure and unit
tested; a new recent_session_tool_sequences query feeds it ordered rows
grouped per session.

fix(provider): classify temporary model-unavailability 4xx as retryable (#505)

Some providers report an overloaded/at-capacity/temporarily-unavailable
model as a 4xx JSON API error instead of 429/5xx. The retry classifier
only retried 4xx bodies that were HTML infra pages or a 400 with an empty
error_type, so an overload arriving as a 400 with a real error_type, or as
any other 4xx, was treated as a hard client error: it surfaced with zero
retries, and only fell to the fallback chain if it happened to be a 400.

Add is_temporarily_unavailable(): it classifies a 4xx JSON body whose
error_type or message describes an overload/capacity/try-again condition,
while explicitly rejecting permanent model-unsupported and auth/validation
errors so an actionable config problem is never mistaken for a transient
blip. Wire it into is_retryable, which the fallback chain already consults
via should_try_next, so a transient unavailability now gets the retry
budget on the same provider and then rolls to the next provider — without
broadening auth or permanent-model handling.

Regression tests cover overload on 400-with-type and on 409, the
temporary-vs-permanent split, and the auth guard.

fix(telegram): reaction handler claims the turn atomically via try_begin_turn (#508)

The reaction handler checked is_turn_active and, on the fresh-turn path,
never marked the session active at all — so a reaction-fired turn was
invisible to a concurrent message or reaction and two turns could run on
one session, and it carried the same check-then-act TOCTOU window #501
fixed for handle_message.

Replace the check with try_begin_turn: on None a turn is already running,
so enqueue the reaction for mid-turn injection as before; on Some, hold the
guard across the send_message_with_display call so the reaction turn is
registered active for its whole duration and drops on completion. The
service-level message queue callback drains any reaction enqueued during
that turn, so a concurrent reaction is handled in-loop instead of forking.

Regression test models the handler flow: a reaction claims the turn, a
concurrent reaction is refused and enqueued, and the follow-up survives for
the running loop after the guard drops.

fix(agent): nudge before breaking identical tool-call loops, catch interleaved repeats (#507)

The exact-loop breaker only fired when the last N calls were strictly
consecutive and identical, and broke non-modification loops silently (only
browser loops got a user-facing nudge). A model re-issuing the same
successful call every other round slipped through, and when a general loop
was cut the user saw no signal.

Split the handling: modification tools (write/edit/bash) keep the strict
consecutive hard-break with no nudge. Non-modification tools now use a
windowed dominant-repeat check (pure repeat_loop_action helper) that counts
identical signatures in the recent window even when interleaved, nudges the
model once to use the results it already has or change course, and breaks
the turn only if the repeat persists after the nudge.

repeat_loop_action is a pure helper with unit tests for the below-threshold,
interleaved-nudge, nudge-once-then-break, and window-bound cases.

fix(telegram): lead the live flow header with the status message (#509)

The collapsed live header rendered as `duration • count • status` because the
status message was appended last by each renderer while flow_header_text only
ordered count and duration. The earlier reorder (2a5469dd) swapped the wrong
pair, so the real status message stayed pinned at the end.

Thread the activity preview into flow_header_text as an explicit status_msg
param and build the whole ordered live header there: status message first
(bold), then the tool-call count, then the duration (both italic), all
`•`-separated. Drop the separate trailing activity append from all three
renderers so the header is one ordered string that can never drift; each
renderer escapes/styles its own dialect before passing the activity in. The
settled Finished/Failed/Timed out header is unchanged.

Tests updated across all three renderers and the flow_header_text unit.

fix(telegram): inject a mid-turn slash command as its own directive, not a foldable follow-up

A slash command that resolves to a prompt (a skill or user command like
/drop_release) and lands while a turn is running was queued correctly, but
wrapped with the plain follow-up framing: 'factor it into the CURRENT task
now, do not restart from scratch'. For a deliberate command invocation that
wrapper neutralizes the directive — the model folds the skill body into
whatever unrelated work it was doing and the command never runs, so it
looks dropped. Verified in the logs: /drop_release arrived mid-turn, logged
'queued for injection', but the release workflow never started.

Capture the raw invocation from the UserPrompt arm and, when a mid-turn
message came from a slash command, inject it via a directive wrapper that
names the command and tells the model to carry out the instructions on
their own terms at the next safe stopping point. Its history entry shows
the command, not the resolved body. Plain follow-ups are unchanged.

The wrapper choice is a pure build_midturn_queued_message helper with tests
for both the slash-command and plain-follow-up cases.

fix(telegram): dedup the double gear when the live header status is the bare-tool fallback

The live flow header prints its own running gear, then the status message. When
narration and bash comments are both absent, the priority-3 fallback is the most
recent tool label, which for a still-running tool already leads with its own
running gear ("gear bash …"). The two gears collided, rendering a double gear in
the header.

Strip a leading running-gear (base plus its optional variation selector) from the
status message before bolding it, so the header's single live gear stands alone.
Settled outcome icons are left untouched: they read as the tool's own result, not
a duplicate of the header gear. Regression test asserts no double gear when a
running-tool fallback leads the header.

fix(telegram): preserve attachment names, store directed files durably, organize channel_attachments by platform (#513)

Three related fixes to the incoming-attachment storage path.

1. tmp naming leads with the original filename. Documents and audio were
   saved as {kind}-{chat_id}-{ts}.{ext}, discarding the real name, so a file
   like plan_mode_feature.plan.md landed as doc--1003-1783.md, unfindable.
   attachment_tmp_name now leads with the sanitized original stem and keeps
   the {chat_id}-{ts} suffix for origin detection and collision safety.
   Voice/photo/video_note keep the {kind}- prefix untouched: the tmp pickup
   scanner keys off it and never scans documents/audio.

2. Directed attachments reach channel_attachments. The passive (non-mention)
   branches already download and persist the file, but a message that
   @mentions the bot fell through to the directed store, which passed None
   for file data. So a mentioned file was stored as text only and lived
   solely as the ephemeral tmp copy. It now downloads the attachment and
   passes the bytes, so any attachment from anyone, mention or not, lands in
   the durable store.

3. channel_attachments organized per platform. Files now write to
   channel_attachments/telegram/ with the name-leading scheme
   ({stem}-{chat_id}-{msg_id}.{ext}, message id for per-chat uniqueness)
   instead of a flat {uuid}_{name} dump. A one-time startup migration sweeps
   pre-subdir flat files into telegram/, idempotent and clash-safe.

Tests cover the naming scheme and the migration (sweep, idempotency, name
clash).

Editing cannot persist a checklist), with advisory light-template-B
warnings logged and never blocking. The TUI reloads the plan document
after write_file and edit_file completions too, not only plan tool
calls, so Editing chrome follows the mirrored JSON. json-spec storage
table updated: single JSON store plus archive dir, shared loader in
utils/plan_files.rs, SQLite plan path documented as retired.

feat(plan): C3 plan tool contract, design/checklist tracks, goal wiring (#520)

init gains mode (design | checklist) with locked disambiguation: omitted
mode infers checklist from inline tasks and design from none;
mode=design with tasks, mode=checklist without tasks, design under tool
auto-approve (yolo never enters Editing), and empty imports are refused
with the allowed alternative. Design init creates the session .md
scaffold and returns its absolute path with a deterministic do-not-start
instruction; checklist init and import go Active immediately. init is
allowed from NoPlan or pre-init only: the first successful init upgrades
or replaces the pre-init sidecar, while a live post-init or Active plan
refuses with discard-first.

add_tasks lands as the primary append operation (array, at least one);
add_task stays as a single-task alias until the prompt switch. start and
complete are Active-only with deterministic Editing refusals, and the
auto-approve-on-first-start behavior is gone: approved_at is stamped
only by user Approve on the design track. A started task's acceptance
criteria now become the session goal via GoalManager and clear on
complete or skip (a failed task keeps its goal for the retry).

The tool loads and saves through the shared plan store (legacy map,
size guard, canonical status strings, atomic write) and completing the
last task archives both artifacts back to NoPlan. Tool description and
schema teach the two tracks and live operations.

Tests: new plan_tool_contract_test suite (12 cases across modes,
pre-init upgrade/replace, re-init refusal, Editing blocks, alias,
no-auto-approve, archive, import rules); flow tests moved to checklist

feat(plan): D1 commands, Approve validator, seed turn, design-track soft-nudge (#521)

New shared state machine utils/plan_mode.rs drives /plan, /show-plan,
/execute (Approve) and /discard identically on TUI and Telegram. The
Approve validator is a lightweight Rust scan of the session .md: empty
doc, missing Context labels (Problem, Target state, Intent), or zero
numbered Implementation steps refuse; any non-empty text after a label
passes (strictness locked, no placeholder heuristics).

Idle /execute has exactly two allowed paths: first approve (post-init
Editing with a valid .md) sets Active, stamps approved_at, and
dispatches one visible seed turn carrying the locked implement-turn
prompt (read the .md, one add_tasks with all steps 1:1, map Done-when
bullets to acceptance criteria, then start); and empty-tasks seed retry
re-dispatches the seed turn with no second approve. Everything else
refuses deterministically. While a turn is running, /execute and
Approve are refused immediately and never queued; /discard cancels the
in-flight turn first, then clears the pre-init flag or deletes both
plan artifacts.

The gate gains the locked seed tool policy: between Approve and a
successful start (design .md present, every task still Pending) only
reads and the plan tool flow; project writes, bash, spawn, sends, and
system mutators are blocked so a wandering seed turn cannot touch the
project before the checklist exists.

The shared PromptAnalyzer plan hint swaps from checklist shape to the
design track (init mode=design, write the SESSION PLAN .md, wait for
Approve) and plan-keyword matches now set the durable pre_init_editing
flag on both surfaces; keyword triggers are unchanged and slash and
skill expansions remain skipped. /plan and /execute and /discard are
owner-only on channels; /show-plan is open. Help and TUI autocomplete
list the four commands.

Tests: plan_mode_command_test suite (golden-fixture validator, both
approve paths, refusals, discard, show-plan, seed window) plus a
seed-window gate case; analyzer tests updated to the design-track hint.
Full suite 4855 green.

feat(plan): D2 dual-track prompts, state-branched compaction recovery (#521)

The preamble's CRITICAL: PLAN TOOL USAGE block and the NEVER-text-plans

Spawn and team agent-type enums accept architect (plan stays a valid
