fix(agent): resolve Runtime Info model/provider per session at prompt injection

The system brain renders from a RuntimeInfo snapshot frozen at startup, so
sessions that swapped providers (per-session /models pick, channel provider
sync, sticky fallback) kept telling the model it runs on the startup default
and it mis-reported itself when asked.

- new override_runtime_model_provider() rewrites the Model:/Provider: lines
  inside the Runtime Info section only; no-op when the section is absent
- live_system_brain_for_session() resolves the session pair the same way
  display surfaces already do (provider_model_for_session) and both prompt
  injection sites (context build, tool loop) now use it
- regression tests: section-scoped rewrite, no-op without the section

fix(react): accept </react> and bare > as reaction-marker terminators

The reaction directive extractor matched the opener tolerantly but the
closer strictly: only a literal >> closed the marker. A model that closed
with an XML-style </react> tag or a single > (Cursor/Cline muscle memory)
produced an unterminated marker, so the whole mangled directive leaked
into the chat as raw text instead of firing or being stripped.

- new find_react_close() finds the earliest of >>, </react>, or > and
  prefers the longest match at the same offset so >> is never mis-read
  as a bare >
- the emoji guard and backtick code-span protection are unchanged, so a
  word payload or an in-code mention still stays as prose
- regression tests: </react> fires, bare > fires, >> preferred over >,
  word payload with </react> stays, in-code bare > untouched

Closes #526

fix(telegram): show the 'Working on: <query>' header for claude-cli turns (#527)

Non-CLI providers stream reasoning/text before any tool runs, so the flow
header opens header-only with 'Working on: <query>' during that pre-tool
window. claude-cli runs tools inside the subprocess and emits a synthesized
ToolStarted+ToolCompleted at the first block close, so the flow block opens
with tool activity on the very first tick; latest-activity always leads the
header and the user-query preview is never shown. The turn then reads as
having no leading context, and the effect is worst during compaction (the
pre-block window is where that header lives).

Add a header_query_shown flag to StreamingState and render_flow_*_chrome_pref
variants that lead a live header with the query fallback even when activity
lines exist. render_flow / render_flow_details_state prefer the query on the
first tick (!header_query_shown && header_preview set); tick_flow_header flips
the flag once a block is open, so exactly the first tick leads with the query
and live activity leads after, matching non-CLI. Non-CLI output is unchanged:
its first render is header-only (no activity lines) so the query already led,
and the flag flips before tools arrive.

The 4s typing pinger already spans the whole turn including compaction, so no
extra compaction status is needed; this makes the query bubble reliably lead
that window too. Tests cover the query-lead, the shipped activity-lead, the
no-query fallthrough, the details summary, and wrapper/pref parity.

fix(react): accept keyword-less <<EMOJI>> reaction markers

Some models drop the react: tag entirely and just double-bracket the
emoji, <<✅>>. match_react_open hard-required the react: keyword after the
bracket run, so the keyword-less form never matched the opener and rode
into the chat as raw text.

- match_react_open now returns the offset past the bracket run for the
  keyword-less form too, gated on at least two < characters so a
  single-bracket <x> (HTML/emoticon noise, one char from a bare-> close)
  stays prose
- the is_reaction_emoji guard and backtick code-span protection are
  unchanged, so an ASCII word payload (<<word>>) and in-code mentions
  still stay prose; only a real emoji between double brackets fires
- regression tests: <<EMOJI>> fires, keyword-less bare-> close fires,
  single-bracket stays text, word payload stays text, in-code untouched,
  empty payload stays text

feat(telegram): make folded-narration cap provider-aware (#532, mirror of upstream #531)

The FOLDED_NARRATION_CAP=300 (#489) was a targeted fix for claude-cli, whose
whole model turn folds into the processing-log block as intermediate
narration and would fill the 30K rich-block budget. It was applied
unconditionally, so API providers — which keep their answer in
response.content and fold only brief interstitial narration — had that
reasoning truncated to 300 chars in the collapsed block for no benefit.

Make the per-entry cap provider-aware: CLI keeps 300; API providers pass
API_NARRATION_CAP (uncapped), so their folded reasoning shows in full. The
block-level 30K rich freeze still guards a pathological many-round turn, so
uncapping API entries cannot break the block. StreamingState carries an
is_cli flag (set from provider.cli_handles_tools() at construction in both
the handler and resume paths); render_flow / render_flow_details_state pick
the cap via narration_cap_for(is_cli) and thread it through the _chrome_pref
renderers. The cap remains display-only — flow_entries keep the full text and
take_folded_final reclaims the whole answer regardless.

Tests compare a capped vs uncapped render of the same lines (the header shows
the latest narration whole for both providers via latest_activity_preview, so
only the folded body differs), covering both the HTML and rich-details paths
plus the short-narration no-op.

feat(channels): include chat_id/thread_id in the [Channel: ...] prompt header (#533, mirror of upstream #510)

The per-turn [Channel: ...] header injected into the LLM context named the
platform but carried no chat/channel identifiers, so the agent had no way to
know which chat it was in — it had to guess or ask when configuring a cron
job that reports back to the current chat, or when sending across surfaces.

Add the identifiers to each handler's header:
- Telegram: chat_id, plus thread_id for forum topics (channel_id_hint helper).
- Discord: channel_id (msg.channel_id).
- Slack: channel_id.
- WhatsApp: chat JID.

The header stays per-turn and out of session history (display_text_override),
so this only adds the IDs to the LLM-facing context. channel_id_hint is a
pure helper with tests for the forum-topic and plain-chat cases.

feat(config): surface silent config.toml hot-reload recovery to the user (#534, mirror of upstream #517)

When config.toml became invalid, the hot-reload watcher recovered from
last-known-good (or kept the running config on a hard load failure) but
only tracing::warn'd it. An operator who saved a broken edit got no signal
that it was rejected and the process kept serving the previous provider
set — on a multi-profile daemon this silently ran profiles without their
intended custom providers.

Add a ReloadNotify hook to ConfigWatcher::spawn, fired on both the
recovered (was_recovered) and keep-current (load Err) branches with an
actionable message (what happened, the config path, and that on-disk edits
are inactive until it parses). cli/ui.rs wires it to a global TUI
SystemMessage AND a best-effort Telegram owner DM, so a headless daemon —
the real-world case — is no longer silent. The message names the profile
via profile_suffix so a multi-profile operator knows which one was rejected.

This is the notification piece (the report's low-complexity, high-value
core). The larger outcome-enum + policy-A (keep live config on hot-reload
parse failure instead of applying last-known-good) is left as a follow-up.

Tests cover ReloadNotify Send+Sync and profile_suffix_from's default/named
cases.

fix(telegram): strip @bot only as a command suffix, preserve standalone mentions (#528)

The handler stripped EVERY occurrence of @bot_username from the message
before the agent saw it. The intent was only to turn a command suffix
(/stop@opencrabsbot, which Telegram appends from menus) into /stop for
command matching, but replacing all occurrences also erased standalone
mentions — so in a multi-bot group the agent never saw it was addressed and
lost the context of who the message was for.

Strip @bot only when it immediately follows a /command token
(strip_command_mention_suffix), leaving standalone mentions intact so the
agent knows it was tagged and other bots' mentions survive. A trailing word
boundary keeps @opencrabsbot2 from matching @opencrabsbot. Mention DETECTION
(the respond/suppress checks) already runs on the raw pre-strip text, so it
is unaffected.

Note: the issue's proposed regex replaced the whole /cmd@bot match with an
empty string, which would have deleted the command too; this keeps the
command via the $1 capture. Pure helper with tests for the suffix strip,
standalone-mention preservation, the longer-username guard, and plain text.

chore(skills): remove unused opencli skill pointing at unbundled binary (#536)

The opencli SKILL.md advertised 25+ opencli-rs dynamic tools that require
a separate, uninstalled opencli-rs binary plus a daemon on port 19825.
Nothing shipped or provisioned that binary, so on a stock build the skill
loaded a doc describing tools that were never registered. Usage history
shows zero successful executions of any opencli-rs tool.

- Drop the opencli entry from BUILTIN_SKILLS in src/brain/skills.rs
- Delete the opencli template directory
- Remove README and BRAIN_CONSTITUTION references
- Add a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased

feat(telegram): retry telegram_send on 429 rate limits (#524)

The telegram_send tool bubbled a Telegram RetryAfter (429) straight back to
the agent as a failure — the reported ~14.5% failure rate (97/667) in
RSI-cycle data — instead of waiting out retry_after and retrying, which the
Telegram API requires clients to do.

Wrap every send/mutation arm (send, reply, edit, delete, pin, unpin,
forward, send_photo, send_document, send_location, send_poll, send_buttons,
ban_user, unban_user, set_reaction) with the existing, already-unit-tested
send_retrying_rate_limit helper (waits out RetryAfter up to 3 attempts, then
propagates; non-429 errors propagate immediately). Each closure rebuilds its
request per attempt (InputFile/markup/text cloned), since a teloxide request
is consumed on await. Pure read actions (get_chat*, get_member_count) are
left unwrapped. The rich-API send path already falls back to the retried
plain path on failure.

The retry semantics are covered by the existing telegram_send_retry_test
suite; this change routes the tool's sends through that helper.

fix(dynamic-tool): context-aware shell escaping so double-quoted params are safe (#523)

shell_escape_params only escaped single quotes (the '\''' idiom), which
assumes every {{param}} sits in a single-quoted argument. The command_code
template wraps the prompt in DOUBLE quotes (-p "{{prompt}}"), where $,
backtick and \ stay shell-interpreted — the 44% failure on complex prompts.
A single generic escaper cannot serve both quote styles, so escaping must be
context-aware.

Add render_shell_command: it resolves sections, then scans the template
tracking whether each {{param}} lands in a single-quoted, double-quoted, or
unquoted span and escapes for that context. Single-quoted and unquoted keep
the exact previous ' -> '\''' behavior (working templates are byte-for-byte
unchanged — full back-compat), while double-quoted spans backslash-escape \,
backtick, $ and ". The shell executor now renders via this instead of
shell_escape_params + render_template; the HTTP path is untouched.

shell_escape_params is retained (still tested). New tests cover the
double-quote fix, single/unquoted back-compat, embedded quotes, non-string
passthrough, unknown placeholders, sections, and an escaped quote inside a
double-quoted span; the existing shell_escape_params/execute tests still pass.

feat(web_search): rotate User-Agent and retry DuckDuckGo 403s (#525)

DuckDuckGo Lite 403s on IP/UA reputation and rate limits; web_search used a
single hardcoded User-Agent and returned an error on the first non-success,
with no retry, rotation, or fallback (a small but growing failure source).

Rotate through a pool of realistic browser User-Agents, retrying on a 403 /
transient failure with a short backoff before giving up. A hard failure now
returns an actionable error so the agent falls back to exa_search /
brave_search / http_request, exactly as the tool description already
instructs. The result parsing and formatting are factored into pure helpers.

Tests cover the UA pool (multiple distinct agents), the lite-result parser
(http/empty-title filtering, max_results), and the output formatter.

fix(telegram): register plan mode commands in bot menu (#537)

The plan mode commands (/plan, /show-plan, /execute, /discard) are
defined and handled in src/channels/commands.rs, but were not registered
in Telegram's bot command menu (set_my_commands in agent.rs). Users
couldn't see them in the command picker.

Add the four commands to the BotCommand list so they appear in the
Telegram menu. Discord, Slack, and WhatsApp use the same
commands::handle_command but don't have a separate command registration
system, so they already work when typed.

fix(telegram): re-attach plan keyboard after flow restick

The plan Approve/Discard keyboard rides the streaming flow message. When
a newer group message buries the block, restick_flow_if_buried re-posts
the flow lower and deletes the old copy that carried the keyboard, but
neither re-post path re-attaches it: the rich send API cannot carry
reply_markup, and the HTML re-post went out bare. applied_plan_kb was
also never reset, so the rich refresh path saw want == have and skipped
re-attaching, making the loss permanent.

After a relocation, reset applied_plan_kb to None and re-apply the
keyboard to the new message with editMessageReplyMarkup, so the buttons
survive burial on both the rich and HTML surfaces.

Closes #539

fix(plan): surface design prose in /show-plan and point chrome at it

show_plan read the .md body only to validate it, then returned just the
title, path, and ready-status. A reviewer on a chat channel has no file
access, so the design document under review was invisible without opening
it on disk.

- show_plan now echoes the design prose (truncated to 3000 chars to stay
  inside one Telegram message; the full text stays on disk)
- the Editing flow-chrome line points at /show-plan so the prose view is
  discoverable
- tests: prose body is surfaced, and a long body is truncated

Closes #540
style(telegram): rustfmt the /execute BotCommand registration

chore(db): drop orphaned plans/plan_tasks tables

Plan Mode originally persisted to SQLite (plans + plan_tasks, added in the
v0.1.0 initial release on 2026-02-14). The plan-lifecycle redesign moved
all plan state to per-session files (.opencrabs_plan_<session>.json for the
structured state, the sibling .md for design prose) and retired PlanService
and PlanRepository, so nothing has read or written these tables since. They
were dead schema that only confused anyone inspecting the database.

rusqlite_migration tracks schema version by position via user_version, so
deleting the mid-list add_plans migration would break every existing DB
(user_version would exceed the migration count). The safe removal is a new
trailing migration that drops both tables; the indexes go with them.

- new migration 20260713000001_drop_orphaned_plans_tables.sql
- MIGRATION_COUNT 29 to 30

refactor(plan): resolve session dir async, project/profile-aware

The plan store hardcoded ~/.opencrabs/agents/session/ for every session,
so plan artifacts ignored what the session was bound to. Resolving a
session's project is a DB lookup, so the path helpers could not stay sync.

- session_dir(session_id) is now async and resolves the destination:
  <project>/session/ when the session is bound to a project, else the
  profile-aware <home>/session/. It reads the process-global pool the same
  way the channel-send tools do, so no pool is threaded through call sites.
- reads fall back to the legacy flat agents/session/ dir, so plans written
  by an older binary are still found; writes always go to the resolved dir.
- the path helpers, load/save, state, gate, and lifecycle ops become async;
  callers await. plan_mode_state_of and format_active_checklist are split
  out as sync helpers so the TUI overlay renders from already-loaded state
  (plan_document + resolved path) without a per-frame DB lookup.
- set_plan_file_for_session no longer hardcodes agents/session under a raw
  $HOME; it resolves through the shared store and honors the active profile.

Closes #541

docs(plan): describe async project/profile-aware session dir resolution

- Storage sections now document session_dir(session_id): project-bound
  sessions resolve to projects/<slug>/session/, otherwise the
  profile-aware <home>/session/, with the legacy flat agents/session/
  kept as a read-only fallback via plan_json_read_path
- Path helpers documented as async (project branch is a DB lookup)
- SQLite plans/plan_tasks rows updated from dormant/retired to dropped
  (migration 20260713000001)

fix(telegram): clean up the header-only flow block on a react-only turn (#544)

When a turn resolved to react-only (the model returned just a <<react:EMOJI>>
marker, no text, no tools), delivery fired the reaction and deleted the
bottom streaming placeholder but LEFT the open processing-log flow block up.
That block had opened header-only from the model's thinking event and carries
the persistent plan chrome (Editing plan / show-plan / execute), so it
lingered as a 'Processing log' bubble with no answer — reading as if the bot
reacted and dropped the request (seen twice on the Qwen API provider replying
to praise while a plan was being edited).

On the react-only path, also delete the open flow block and clear its state
so only the reaction remains. The turn ran no tools here (the tools-with-no-
text case returns earlier via the #439 fallback), so the block is header-only
and safe to drop; the plan state persists independently, so /show-plan still
works.

No unit test: delivery is a Telegram I/O path with no pure seam; the fix is a
targeted message cleanup, verified green across the full suite.

fix(plan): assign order and default complexity on checklist import

The init file_path import path deserialized PlanTask directly, where
order and complexity are #[serde(default)] (both 0 when omitted). The
fresh-task reset loop rewrote id, status, and dependencies but never
touched order or complexity, so an imported plan using the schema's
recommended minimal shape (order and complexity omitted) left every
task at order 0. get_task_by_order then collided all tasks on order 0,
stalling complete-by-order past the first task, and every task rendered
at complexity 0 instead of the documented default of 3.

The reset loop now assigns order from 1-based array position and
defaults complexity to 3 when omitted (clamping provided values to the
1-5 scale), matching the add_task path. Regression test imports a
minimal three-task plan and asserts orders 1/2/3 and complexity 3 with
out-of-range clamping.

fix(plan): clear the session goal on plan discard

A started task with acceptance criteria pushes a goal into GoalManager;
complete and skip clear it, but discard only deleted the plan files and
left the goal behind, so stale goal chrome lingered until the session
ended. ADR 0003 groups discard with complete and skip for goal
clearing.

plan_mode::discard now takes the ServiceContext all three surfaces
already hold (TUI, Telegram command, Telegram plan:no callback) and
clears the goal in the post-init/Active arm, mirroring the complete and
skip paths. Regression test sets a goal, discards, and asserts it is
gone.

fix(telegram): surface a long no-tool react-only turn instead of silently dropping it (#546)

A react-only turn that ran no tools took the pure react-only path and
delivered nothing but the reaction. #439 only guards the tools-ran case, so
a turn where the model reasoned for minutes, ran no tools, and then bailed
with only a reaction was silently dropped — the reported 'executing a task
for 5m, it reacts and just stops'. A genuine ack (praise, 'got it')
completes in seconds, so gate on turn duration: when a no-tool react-only
turn took 60s or more it engaged with real work, so surface it as an
incomplete turn (delivery can't re-run the model) rather than dropping it
silently, so the user knows to re-send. Fast praise/ack react-onlys are
unchanged.

Scoped to delivery.rs; does not touch the concurrent work in commands.rs.

fix(channels): /models command shows session provider instead of global

The /models command was showing the global provider/model from config.toml
instead of the session's actual provider after per-session switches. This
was because format_providers() used agent.provider_name() and
agent.provider_model() which return the global values, not the session's.

Root cause: Channel model switches call swap_provider_for_session() which
updates the session's provider without touching the global config. But
format_providers() was reading from the global agent state, so it showed
stale data after a channel switch.

Fix: Updated format_providers() to accept session_id and use
provider_name_for_session() and provider_model_for_session() to get the
session's actual provider/model. All channel handlers (Telegram, Discord,
Slack, WhatsApp) already pass session_id to handle_command(), so no
changes needed at the call sites.

Added tests to verify:
- /models shows global provider when session has no override
- /models shows session provider after per-session override

Fixes #543

chore(plan): drop deprecated task_manager from the tool catalog

task_manager was superseded by the plan tool (mode=checklist) but was
still registered, so non-lazy mode advertised it to every model and
tool_search still surfaced it. ADR 0004 requires it gone from the
catalog and preamble.

Unregister TaskTool so it leaves the model-facing catalog and
tool_search discovery. The TaskTool code (brain::tools::task) and the
display-label and dispatch arms stay in place, so nothing is deleted and
the change is reversible; the tool is simply no longer advertised.

fix(cli): keep react-only marker so claude-cli turn ends cleanly

When a claude-cli turn streamed only a `<<react:EMOJI>>` marker, the
displayable text was flushed as an intermediate message and then every
text block was cleared before complete_response read them. That cleared
the react directive too, so delivery received empty response.content,
never took the react-only path, and settled a bare "Finished" flow block
that lingered after the reaction.

Reduce a flushed text block to its react directive instead of clearing
it outright: the marker survives into response.content, delivery treats

fix(telegram): resolve channel commands despite auto-injected media markers

In a group, when an incoming message has no photo of its own, the handler

prefix, and fell through to the agent as a prose prompt instead of opening
the picker. The failure looked tied to the session being busy, but the real
variable was whether a media marker had been appended.

handle_command, so command matching is immune no matter how the marker was
appended (attachment, reply, or recent-tmp pickup). The image still reaches
the agent via the handler's own text when the message is genuinely not a
command.

fix(plan): inject plan reminder in tool loop and gate Approve on readiness

Two causes of a plan that stays unapprovable while Approve spams refusals:

1. The plan-mode per-turn reminder (active_plan_reminder: Editing template
   rules or the Active incomplete-task nudge) was injected only in the simple
   send_message path (prepare_message_context). The tool-loop path, which drives
   Telegram and every channel that uses tools, built its own context and never
   injected it, so in plan mode the agent was never told the plan-template rules
   and wrote an empty template the approval gate refused forever. Inject it in
   run_tool_loop_inner where the user message is built, mirroring the simple
   path; the DB still stores the clean user message so it never accumulates.

fix(hashline_edit): widen hash to 4 chars and strip the real read prefix

hashline_edit was the worst tool by fail rate (reported 59%, ~93% locally),
with "edit mangled my file" even on successful calls. Two causes:

1. The line tag was a 2-char hash over a 16-letter alphabet: only 256 values,
   computed over line content alone. The collisions were overwhelmingly FALSE
   (distinct lines that happen to share a tag), not just identical lines: a
   20-line read had ~54% chance of a collision, 40 lines ~91%, 60 lines ~99.9%.
   read_file then marks colliding lines COLLISION| and validate_hash refuses the
   edit, so most reads left some line uneditable. Widen the tag to 4 chars
   (HASH_LEN, 65536 values), dropping a 20-line read to ~0.3% and 60 to ~4%.
   Identical-content lines still share a tag at any width and stay correctly
   deferred to edit_file.

2. read_file hashline=true prints lines as HASH|content, and models echo that
   exact form into the replacement. strip_hashline_prefixes only matched a
   legacy DIGITS#HASH| shape, never the real HASH| / COLLISION|, so an echoed
   prefix was written verbatim into the file. Strip a leading COLLISION|, a bare
   HASH| (HASH_LEN alphabet chars), or the legacy DIGITS#HASH| form, matching
   the hash alphabet precisely so real content with an early | (markdown tables)
   is untouched.

Tag width lives in one HASH_LEN constant; HashRef::parse and the model-facing
descriptions follow it. Added tests for the current-format prefix strip, the
markdown-pipe safety case, and a false-collision guard.

fix(http_request): a completed response is a successful invocation

existence probe, a 401/403 auth check, a 429 rate limit, and every 3xx/5xx

agent's error-recovery path for expected outcomes. The tool's job is to make
the request and return the response; the HTTP status is data for the model,
which already sees it in the output.

the status is impossible to miss, and keep status_code in metadata. Only real

fix(telegram): retry rich flow edit on 429 instead of splitting to HTML

fall back to the HTML edit path, whose limit is 4096 chars, which then froze the
block and started a new one. That is why blocks with 300+ tool calls never
split (they stay on rich) but this one did (a 429 bumped it to HTML).

lets the ~1.5s edit loop retry the rich edit, keeping the block on the 32K path
so it never splits; a not-modified response is a no-op; any other failure still
falls back to HTML. Extracted classify_rich_edit_error as a pure, tested helper.

trailing wrap-up showed, while the TUI rendered the full report inline. Nothing
prompts the wrap-up; it is just the tool loop returning the complete result and
the model closing out, and take_folded_final only rescues the trailing text.

record it in sent_intermediates for dedup, instead of only folding. Thin

fix(telegram): recover a leaked react marker on reaction turns

A smaller model replied to a reaction notification with its reasoning plus its
intended <<react:emoji>> wrapped in a code span. handle_reaction used the strict
extract_react_marker, which skips code-span markers (so agents discussing the
feature in docs don't fire spurious reactions) — so no reaction fired and the
whole meta-commentary was posted as a group message.

feature, so extract it leniently (ignore code spans) via new

is not a stop signal (the react-only default), drop the surrounding leaked
reasoning and deliver react-only. The strict extractor stays the default
everywhere else, and the payload guard still rejects word payloads so a real
doc mention never fires.

fix(phantom): catch narrated plans hidden behind a structured preamble (#589)

The zero-tool phantom retry gate consulted only the lead-in detector
(has_phantom_tool_intent_no_tools, which scans prose_lead_in — the text
before the first list/table/code line) plus the underscore-tool-name tell.
A reasoning-model turn that restates the task as a numbered list BEFORE its
"Let me .../Plan of attack:" narration defeats both: prose_lead_in truncates
at the numbered list, leaving only a benign description, and the narrated
actions are bare verbs that name no underscore tools. Such a monologue slipped
the gate and was delivered to the user instead of being retried into real
tool calls.

Wire the strict full-text detector has_phantom_tool_intent into the gate. It
scans the whole text and fires on >=2 "Let me" line-starts or >=2 numbered
action steps, so the buried narration is caught. Language-agnostic — applies
to every phantom_lang locale, not just the case observed.

monologue while the strict detector catches it.

fix(phantom): catch leading-imminence work announcements ('... Now downloading X') (#602)

A work announcement that LEADS with "Now <gerund>" and ends on a plain period
("Issue filed. Now downloading the font files as local assets.") slipped every
detector, so a model that narrated ongoing work it never did drew no self-heal
retry:
- work_announcement_re requires a TRAILING imminence marker (now / ... / :); a
  leading "Now" with a plain sentence end never matches.
- gerund_re (the "Now <gerund>" tell) was missing downloading and many verbs the
  work-announcement list already had.
- Post-success eligibility (has_forward_intent_post_success) only checked intent
  phrases + matches_work_announcement, so with a tool already run this turn,
  phantom detection was skipped entirely.

Fix: broaden gerund_re's verb list to match work_announcement_re (+ a re-? prefix),
add a matches_now_gerund helper (gerund_re across all languages), and consult it
in both has_forward_intent_post_success and has_phantom_tool_intent_no_tools.
Language-agnostic. Regression test asserts both paths now catch it.

perf(lazy-tools): LRU-bound the per-session active tool set (#603)

The session active-set was extend-only, so over a long session the request
tools array kept growing and never shrank — the per-turn schema cost drifted
back toward the full ~95-tool baseline, defeating lazy loading.

Track a monotonic last-touch sequence per activated tool (stamped on every
activate, and the JIT-on-execute path already re-activates a non-core tool
whenever it is actually called, so recency tracks real use). Once a session
exceeds MAX_ACTIVE_EXTENDED (24), evict the least-recently-used tools. Evicted
tools re-activate on next use, so nothing breaks — the working set just stays
small. Core tools are never counted (they always ship). Regression test covers
the cap and that a refreshed tool survives.

perf(lazy-tools): tool_search activates on use, not all 8 matches (#604)

tool_search pre-activated every match it returned (up to 8), injecting up to 8
tool schemas into subsequent requests even though the model calls one. Stop
pre-activating: tool_search now only returns the matched tools' full schemas as
text (so the model can call the one it needs with correct params), and
activation happens on actual use via the existing JIT-on-execute path. Only the
tool the model really calls gets its structured schema injected — a search no
longer balloons the request with unused schemas. Pairs with the LRU cap (#603).

fix(mission-control): window the Flakiest panel so fixed tools age out (#605)

The Flakiest panel computed fail rates from stats_with_failures(None) —
all-time cumulative over every tool_executions row ever — with no window and no
reset on an append-only table. So a tool that was flaky then fixed kept its
historical rate forever, and a fixed-but-idle tool never dropped (e.g.
http_request showed 33.3% all-time but 1 fail / 22 calls in the last 30d;
dependencies showed 100% with zero calls in 38 days).

Compute the Flakiest panel over a 30-day window (stats_with_failures(Some(...)),
requiring >=5 RECENT calls); keep Totals and Top-tools all-time. Fixed tools now
age out, idle tools drop off, and genuinely-still-failing tools stay flagged.
Header shows the window.

fix(rsi): prune already-handled entries from pending proposal files (#606)

The inbox filter (#502) hides pending proposals whose name is already
applied/rejected, so the Mission Control inbox is correct — but the pending
files were never cleaned, so legacy handled entries (filed before the add-time
check) linger forever. On a live install all 5 pending entries (docker_logs,
gh_issue_create, parse_json, /standup, github_workflow) were already applied,
so the files were non-empty while the inbox correctly showed 0.

Add ProposalsStore::prune_handled() — removes pending entries whose name is
already applied/rejected from all three files (only handled ones; a genuinely
pending proposal is untouched) — and call it once per RSI cycle where the store
is already opened for the dedup scan. Keeps the proposal store honest and
bounded.

Note: this is housekeeping, not the reason the inbox is empty — that is correct
(the obvious skill/command candidates were all applied and add-time dedup blocks
re-filing). Surfacing genuinely NEW suggestions is a separate concern (detection
thresholds), not a defect.

fix(phantom): make strict detector language-agnostic so accents can't disable it (#607)

detect_language flips to an accented-Latin language (FR/ES/PT) on a SINGLE
accented char (latin_accent > 0), unlike the Cyrillic branch which needs >20%.
So an English planning monologue containing one accented word ("Activité", plus
"Mes clients"/"Demandes") mis-detects as French, and has_phantom_tool_intent then
uses French patterns that cannot match the English "Let me ..." narration —
phantom slips, no retry fires (Kimi K3, repeatedly). Verified: strict=false on
the exact text, strict=true once the accent is stripped.

Make has_phantom_tool_intent scan EVERY language for its strong signals
(now_imperative, numbered_steps, past_tense, completion, gerund, trailing_colon,
and the intent+path corroboration) via max_lang_regex_count / any_lang_regex_match,
instead of only detect_language's single pick — mirroring lang_intent_match_any /
matches_work_announcement. A mis-detected language can no longer disable detection;
the per-language regexes carry distinctive tokens so the union is collision-free.
Regression test asserts the accented English monologue is caught.

feat(plan): scope yolo design refusal to /plan slash origin

The design track under auto-approve was refused unconditionally, so a

fix(compaction): honor the provider's configured window without a manual swap (#609)

context_limit_for_session returned session_context_limits[session] or the static
agent.context_limit (200K default). session_context_limits is only populated with
the provider's configured_context_window inside swap_provider_for_session (a manual
/models swap). So a session that just uses the configured provider compacted
against the 200K default while the flow header showed the provider's real window.

Observed: Kimi K3 configured for context_window = 1000000 showed "185K/1.0M 18%"
then auto-compacted to 105K — because the compaction budget was silently 200K
(185K is ~92% of 200K), not the 1M the header displayed.

Fix: fall back to the active session provider's configured_context_window() before
the static agent.context_limit default. provider_for_session already exists and
every provider carries configured_context_window(), so every session honors its
provider window, not just manually-swapped ones. Regression test covers an
un-swapped session honoring a 1M provider window.

no moonshot branch, so on load config.providers.moonshot.api_key stayed None and
the factory logged "Moonshot AI enabled but API key missing" and skipped the
provider — the key looked like it wasn't persisting.

Add the moonshot merge block, mirroring the other providers. Regression test

fix(config): config_for() resolves the moonshot provider (#611)

The /models dialog's detect_existing_key looks up the provider key via

arm, so it fell through to the `custom:` branch and returned None — the dialog
always showed an empty key even when the key was in config (and merged from
keys.toml via #610). configured_providers() and any other config_for-routed
moonshot lookup were broken the same way.

Add the moonshot arm. Regression test asserts config_for resolves the moonshot
slot for the id and its aliases (kimi, moonshotai).

eval(phase0): offline fixture-driven replay provider (#619)

Foundation for the offline eval harness (#618). ReplayProvider implements
the Provider trait by replaying an ordered sequence of scripted assistant
turns from a JSON fixture, advancing a cursor per call — deterministic, no
network. Turns carry optional narration text and/or a tool call; a tool
turn stops with ToolUse, otherwise the turn ends. Past the end it returns
a terminal empty end-turn so the loop never hangs.

Gated behind cfg(test) or the new 'eval' feature so it never ships in a
release binary. Tests cover ordering, tool turns, deterministic tool ids,
stream/complete parity, exhaustion, and the model default.

eval(phase0): context-manifest trace hook (#620)

ContextManifest::from_request analyzes a built LLMRequest into an
inspectable view of context composition: system-brain bytes/tokens, which
brain files are present, message count + token split, and the tool roster
with per-tool schema cost and CORE-vs-extended counts (cl100k tokenizer,
catalog::is_core). Purely derived from the request, so evals inspect
composition without touching any production path. Serialize-able for
scorecards. Tests cover brain-file detection, tool split, totals, the
empty case, and JSON output.

eval(phase1): compaction-fidelity harness + BinEval scorer (#621, #622)

Scorer (#622): BinEval-style decomposition — atomic yes/no BinaryQuestions
answered independently by a Judge, aggregated to per-dimension + overall
Scorecard with a threshold gate and stable render. Judging is abstracted
so evals run offline: SequenceJudge (preset verdicts) and ProviderJudge
over the fixture replay provider; a judge failure is a NO, never a silent
pass.

Compaction harness (#621): CompactionDataset pairs a synthetic
conversation with fact probes (user prefs, pending tasks, files, errors).
keyword_scorecard gives a deterministic offline fact-survival signal;
judge_scorecard grades semantically via a Judge. Bundled synthetic seed
dataset (no user identifiers). 22 eval tests green; fmt + clippy clean.

eval(phase2-4): recall metrics, regression baseline, RSI before/after (#623, #624, #625)

Phase 2 (#623): pure retrieval metrics — precision@k, recall@k, MRR,
nDCG@k over a ranked id list plus a relevant set — with a labeled query
dataset and a macro-averaged report. Offline: tests feed synthetic ranked
lists; a live run feeds real memory_search output through the same
functions.

Phase 3 (#624): Baseline captures a scorecard's overall + per-dimension
scores, serializes to JSON, save/load, and reports any score that dropped
beyond tolerance as a Regression (a missing dimension counts as a drop to
zero). Catches a change that quietly reduces fidelity/recall.

Phase 4 (#625): BeforeAfter compares targeted before/after with an
unrelated control; accepts only when the target improves by a margin AND
the control does not regress — the BinEval capability-vs-guidance guard.

fix(telegram): defer when a reply tags a different bot (#648)

In a group, a message that replies to our bot but explicitly @-tags a
DIFFERENT bot is addressed to that bot — yet the group gate fired on
replied_to_bot and we answered anyway (two bots both responded to one
request meant for the other). Telegram bot usernames must end in 'bot',
so mentions_other_bot() detects an @name ending in 'bot' that is not ours;
the mention + auto gates now require mentioned_us OR (replied_to_us AND
NOT tags_other_bot). Being tagged ourselves still always wins. Pure,
tested helper (synthetic handles only).

feat(plan-gate): read-only registry filter for subagents spawned in Editing (#649)

A subagent spawned while the parent session is in Plan-mode Editing runs
under a fresh child session that resolves to NoPlan, so the per-call plan
gate never fires for it, a hole in the write-freeze. Add
restrict_registry_to_read_only, which strips write, shell, system, and
Editing-denied tools from the child registry so the child can read,
search, and analyze to inform or review the design but cannot mutate the
project, run bash, or spawn further agents. spawn_agent itself carries
SystemModification, so a read-only child cannot mint a non-restricted
grandchild.

spawn_agent applies the filter when the parent session is Editing. This
path is reachable only after spawn_agent leaves EDITING_DENIED_NAMES
(staged separately); landing the safety net first keeps that removal safe.

The filter mirrors the post-init Editing deny set so the spawn-time
filter and the per-call gate cannot drift. Part of #649, step 1.

fix(telegram): harden md_to_html for **double** bold and fenced code (#650) The naive md_to_html only understood single-asterisk bold, so '**ask**' became 'ask' (empty bold pairs) and a language-tagged fence became 'rust'. That malformed HTML made Telegram reject the whole message under parse_mode HTML, dropping it to plain text with raw tags/entities showing — the garbage seen when a rich response fell back to this converter (used across ~10 agent.rs delivery paths). Now handles both '**double**' and '*single*' bold, and triple-backtick fenced blocks (language dropped) as 
, all HTML-escaped;
unbalanced spans (streaming cut-offs) still close cleanly. 7 tests.

fix(telegram): retire native rich-blocks for tables (#651)

Telegram's InputRichBlock rejects our table shape (render_json.rs sends
header/rows/align; Telegram wants cells/size), so every table 400'd the
native block send and burned a round-trip before falling back — the second
time this experimental, undocumented API's schema has bitten us (#476 was
first). Rather than chase a moving schema, skip the native path when a
table is present: delivery gates the rich send on !contains_table, and
display_html renders the table as a clean aligned monospace grid (handling
fences + bold correctly too, so mixed table+fence messages come out right).
Non-table rich content still uses native rich-blocks. Tests confirm the
table routes off-native and renders clean HTML (no empty-bold, no fence

fix(telegram): stop dropping in-flight turns on rapid resend (#652)

store_cancel_token cancelled any existing token for a session before
storing the new one. That behavior predates the atomic try_begin_turn
gate (#501), which is now the one-turn-per-session authority. With that
gate in place, a near-simultaneous resend reaching store_cancel_token
would hard-cancel the user's genuinely in-flight turn and drop the
running request instead of queuing it.

Overwrite the token without cancelling. Genuine cancellation (/stop,
provider swap) still goes through cancel_session. Regression test
asserts a second store does not cancel the first token and that
cancel_session still cancels.

fix(qwen): round-trip reasoning as reasoning_content, not content (#654)

Qwen preserve_thinking models (qwen3.8-max-preview and family, on the
built-in Qwen provider or a custom Model Studio / DashScope endpoint)
always think and return reasoning as a separate reasoning_content field.
Their contract requires that reasoning passed back as reasoning_content;
concatenating it into content is unsupported.

We persist reasoning as <!-- reasoning --> content markers. On reload for
API providers, strip_llm_artifacts removed only the marker tags via the
non-greedy HTML-comment regex, leaving the reasoning text behind in
content. That fed the model its own reasoning as content, breaking
preserve_thinking and making it spill fresh chain-of-thought into the
answer, which leaked to the TUI above the final response and posted as
standalone walls on Telegram while the clean final was missed.

Add a preserves_thinking(base_url, model) predicate covering the Qwen
family (via looks_like_qwen_target) and Moonshot kimi. At the context
load site, for those models hoist the reasoning out of content into the
in-memory thinking column via a new hoist_reasoning_blocks helper, so
from_db_messages rehydrates it as a leading ContentBlock::Thinking and
the encoder emits it as the separate reasoning_content field. Content is
left marker-free and reasoning-free. LLM-context only: no DB write, no
TUI replay change.

feat(tools): introduce MCP-style ToolHints risk model

Adopt the Model Context Protocol's orthogonal tool annotations as the
forward path for risk classification, replacing the flat ToolCapability
taxonomy as the source of truth for gating and approval decisions.

- Add `ToolHints` (read_only, destructive, idempotent, open_world) with
  pessimistic defaults matching MCP: an unannotated tool is assumed
  environment-modifying, destructive, non-idempotent, and open-world.
- Add `Tool::hints()` defaulting to `ToolHints::from_capabilities`, so
  every existing tool keeps its current behavior with no per-tool change.
- Add hint-based classifiers `is_destructive_hints` / `is_read_only_hints`
  in classify.rs; the cap-based helpers stay as a migration bridge.
- Move `requires_approval()` onto the hint-based classifier. Behavior is
  identical (hints derive from capabilities), but approval now runs on the
  MCP axes.

Non-breaking foundation. Follow-ups: override `hints()` per-tool (channel
sends destructive + open_world, pure reads read_only + idempotent), migrate
the plan gate and registry filter to hints, then delete the EDITING_ALLOWED
and EDITING_DENIED_NAMES name lists.
style(tools): sort classify module declaration into alphabetical order

refactor(tools): drive plan gate off MCP hints, delete both name lists

check_plan_gate now takes &ToolHints and gates purely on
hints.read_only. The name-based EDITING_ALLOWED and
EDITING_DENIED_NAMES constants are deleted entirely. The nine
tools they special-cased (six channel sends + three browser
mutators) are now caught by their MCP read_only hint overrides
from the prior commit.

restrict_registry_to_read_only filters on hints().read_only
instead of is_destructive(capabilities) + name list.

The gate logic collapsed to a single signal per state:
- NoPlan: allow
- Active seed window: read_only -> allow, else deny
- Active: read_only -> allow, !read_only && targets .md -> deny, else allow
- PreInitEditing: read_only -> allow, else RequireApproval
- PostInitEditing: read_only -> allow, targets .md -> allow, else RequireApproval

Tests rewritten to use hint constructors. spawn_agent and
resume_agent now require approval during Editing (they are
mutators); the old EDITING_ALLOWED override is gone.

feat(tools): add MCP hints overrides for sends and browser mutators

The six channel sends (telegram, discord, slack, whatsapp, trello,
a2a) and two browser mutators (click, type_text) carry only the
Network capability, which derives read_only = true by default.
Without explicit overrides they would pass freely during Editing
and never prompt under ask mode, despite being egress/mutation
tools.

Each now declares hints() with read_only = false, destructive =
true, open_world = true. This makes them caught by the plan gate
(RequireApproval during Editing) and the ask policy (prompts under
/ask). Under yolo, auto_approve stays true so no prompt fires.

feat(usage): fall back to last-known price for unknown models (#655)

Cost estimation matched models by substring against version-pinned
prefixes, so any new release (a future Opus/Sonnet revision, gpt-5.3,
qwen3.8-max-preview) matched nothing and was silently costed at $0.

Add a resolver ladder shared by estimate_cost and calculate_cost_with_cache,
most specific first: exact match, then a version-agnostic tier match that
strips version tokens from both sides so a new release inherits the
last-known price of its tier (qwen3.8-max-preview -> the qwen-max-preview
rate, claude-opus-4-9 -> the opus rate) while keeping max-vs-plus apart,
then a family-root flagship fallback. Matching is bidirectional so a
vendor-stripped short name (opus-4-9) still resolves, and a minimum
overlap guards against tiny coincidental hits. Only a genuinely
unrecognizable family returns None/$0.

fix(onboarding): send the real saved key on custom model fetch (#656)

A custom provider that already had a key stored EXISTING_KEY_SENTINEL in
api_key_input, not the real key. The model-fetch call sites sent that:
onboarding passed the sentinel as the bearer token, and the /models
dialog matched only built-in providers by display name and fell through
to no key for custom. Either way a remote custom endpoint (e.g. Model
Studio) got 401, while the chat path authenticated fine because it loads
the key from keys.toml.

Add ProviderSelectorState::effective_api_key(): a freshly typed key when
present, otherwise the saved key from config via load_api_key_from_config
(which already resolves custom providers through custom_by_name), and
never the sentinel. Use it at both fetch sites, replacing the onboarding
input-only logic and the dialog's display-name match. The key stays
optional, so a genuinely keyless local endpoint still sends no auth.
docs(agents): check current context (issue/PR + comments, git, code) before changing

perf(brain): date-granular runtime timestamp so the prompt cache can hit (#657)

Runtime Info rendered a per-second UTC timestamp inside the system brain,
and providers stamp cache_control on the whole system message. A prefix
that changed every second never matched a prior cache entry, so the
provider re-prefilled the full ~55K-token context on every turn — the
dominant cost of the 4-5s time-to-first-token, on every request, not
just new chats.

Coarsen the timestamp to date granularity (Current date: YYYY-MM-DD UTC)
in both render paths. The line is ambient context for the model only,
never parsed by code, so date keeps the load-bearing "what day is it"
signal while leaving the cached prefix byte-stable across turns and
same-model sessions. The brain then caches once and is reused via
cache-read, dropping first-token latency toward a warm-cache path during
active use. Applies to every cache-capable provider.

fix(preamble+eval): know channel attachments persist; don't fake a blocker (#659)

A user forwarded a file in a chat channel and the agent claimed it couldn't
read it ("other users' messages aren't stored", "never landed in my
searchable history"). False: forwarded/uploaded files persist to
~/.opencrabs/channel_attachments/<platform>/ and are readable regardless of
who sent them. Once told, the agent immediately ls'd the store, found the
file, and did the audit. Same self-awareness class as the STT/TTS case
(#635/#636): unaware of a runtime resource it already has.

Preamble: add a CHANNEL ATTACHMENTS directive next to VOICE/AUDIO and
VISION-FALLBACK — every sent/forwarded file persists to the attachments
store for the session; never claim a forwarded file isn't stored or can't
be read; list the store and read the most recent match.

Eval: add a second self-awareness scenario (forwarded-file-not-read) with
reads_persisted_attachment + no_false_blocker probes, expose
SelfAwarenessScenario::seeds(), and run both scenarios in the live eval.
Unit tests lock in that the aware response scores full and the real
false-blocker text fails both dimensions.

perf(cache): cache the stable brain independently of runtime info (#658)

Follow-up to #657. Even with a date-granular timestamp, the system brain
still carried per-session Runtime Info (model, provider, working dir),
and providers stamp cache_control on the whole system message — so
sessions on different models/channels/workdirs couldn't share the cached
brain.

Split the system prompt into a byte-stable cached prefix plus an uncached
runtime suffix:
- LLMRequest gains system_suffix + a system_full() helper. with_system now
  splits the Runtime Info block out of the brain (prompt_builder::
  split_runtime_suffix, keyed on a shared RUNTIME_INFO_HEADER const) into
  system_suffix; system stays the byte-stable brain. Additive: no suffix
  means system_full() == system, exactly the old behavior.
- Anthropic: system becomes two blocks — the stable brain with
  cache_control, then the suffix with none, so the breakpoint sits after
  the brain.
- custom/qwen: for a qwen/DashScope target the system message is a 2-part
  array [stable, suffix] and qwen_body_transform stamps cache_control on
  the FIRST (stable) part; other custom providers concatenate via
  system_full().
- All other providers (claude/codex/command/opencode CLI, gemini) use
  system_full() — byte-identical to before.

The ~107K brain now caches once and is reused across sessions regardless
of model/provider; runtime info rides uncached at the end (after AGENTS.md).

Tests: split_runtime_suffix / with_system / system_full, and the qwen
encoding (2-part system, cache_control on the stable part only). Existing
qwen (13), kimi (16), runtime-info (11) suites still pass.
test(cache): guard lazy-tools content stays in cached prefix, runtime in suffix (#662)

Fix bash grep-no-match counted as failure (#663)

grep/rg exit code 1 with empty stderr means 'no matches found' — a
successful empty search, not a failure. Previously this was counted
against bash success rate, inflating the failure rate with search noise.

Real grep errors (exit 2+) always populate stderr, so the fix is safe:
- Add is_search_no_match() helper that checks exit==1, stderr empty,
  and command invokes grep/rg/egrep/fgrep/git grep
- Treat as success with '(no matches found)' note
- Add 8 unit tests covering all variants

Root cause fix in bash.rs (not feedback_policy.rs) so the tool returns
success=true and never enters the failure ledger.

Fixes #663

Fix browser screenshot loop with hard auto-break (#664)

The identical-page detection existed but only warned. Models ignored the
warning and kept looping, burning tokens on duplicate screenshots.

Added consecutive-identical counter in BrowserManager:
- Increments on each identical full-page screenshot
- Resets on any page change (navigate, click, type)
- After 3 consecutive identical captures, returns hard error forcing
  the agent to stop screenshotting and take a different action

Reset calls added to:
- browser_navigate (after successful goto)
- browser_click (all 3 click paths: text=, xpath=, CSS)
- browser_type (after successful typing)

Fixes #664

Add retry logic and timeout guards to cron list queries (#665)

Cron list operations could fail under load due to brief DB contention
from scheduler updates. Added defensive measures:

- 5-second timeout on list_all and list_enabled queries
- Automatic retry after 100ms backoff on timeout
- Prevents hangs and improves resilience under concurrent load

WAL mode and 30s busy_timeout were already set in database.rs:48-51.
These guards add an extra layer of protection for transient contention.

fix(tools): correct CORE_TOOLS name drift dropping core tools in lazy mode (#669)

CORE_TOOLS listed context/http_client/config_tool, but the tools' real
name()s are session_context/http_request/config_manager. is_core() is an
exact match, so in lazy mode get_tool_definitions_filtered dropped all

as always-on core — the agent was told it had config_manager but never
got its schema until a blind tool_search. config_manager is exactly the
tool the self-awareness evals reward reaching for.

The same stale names appeared in two more tool-name lists with the same
effect: the custom_openai_compatible text-leak gate (a leaked
config_manager/session_context/http_request call was invisible to it) and

fix(brain): headless build_system_brain now surfaces compiled features + paths (#671)

fix(onboarding): let users type a model ID not in the fetched list (#676)

After the live model-fetch fix (#656) the custom-provider model step became

feat(redact): scope secret redaction to global/group/dm + /redact command (#677)

Redaction was a single global flag with no notion of where the bot speaks.
Separate it into scopes so secrets are scrubbed in shared group chats but
shown to the owner in DMs.

- Config: keep agent.redact_sensitive_data as the global master; add
  agent.redact_group and agent.redact_dm (Option<bool>). Resolver
  AgentConfig::redact_for(is_dm): DM defaults to NOT redacting
  (owner-private), group follows the global flag, explicit per-scope
  overrides win.
- sanitize: split redact_secrets into a core scrubber plus
  redact_secrets_scoped(text, is_dm) that gates on redact_for instead of
  the global flag.
- Telegram: StreamingState carries is_dm; the response render and the
  mid-turn intermediate fold now redact scope-aware.
- Command: /redact <global|group|dm> <on|off> (owner-only, mirrors
  /respond_to), persisted via write_key; bare /redact shows current scopes.
- The user-message -> DB persist redaction stays GLOBAL (secrets must never
  land in the DB regardless of scope); the TUI stays on the global flag.

Defaults: redact on globally + in groups, off in DMs. Tests for the
resolver.

feat(logging): config-driven debug_logs toggle with hot-reload on top of --debug (#678)

Debug file logging was only reachable via the --debug CLI flag, decided once
at process start. Non-technical users who run OpenCrabs as a service or via a
launcher could not turn detailed logs on when something misbehaved, or off
afterwards, without changing how the binary is launched and restarting.

Add agent.debug_logs (bool, default false, always serialized so it is visible
in config.toml and flippable by a user or the agent on request). Effective
state is `--debug OR debug_logs`, so the flag always wins and an operator who
launched with -d is never silenced by a config edit.

The tracing subscriber cannot re-init, so instead of two mutually exclusive
setups the subscriber now installs one file layer that is always attached but
gated per event by a process-global atomic. A pure effective-state helper
seeds the gate at startup (run(), after the profile resolves and config
loads) and a ConfigWatcher callback re-applies it on every hot-reload,
preserving the launch-time flag. The rolling file writer became lazy: it
builds the appender and log directory on first write only, so a disabled gate
never creates empty log files.

Tests: pure flag-or-config helper; AgentConfig default off; config.toml
round-trip on/off/absent.

fix(tui): document channel commands and /stop in the /help dialog

The TUI /help dialog is built from SLASH_COMMANDS, which only lists commands

they work in Telegram/Discord/Slack, and /stop was absent despite the TUI

Add /stop to SLASH_COMMANDS (it is TUI-executable), and add a CHANNEL_COMMANDS
list rendered under a dedicated "CHANNEL COMMANDS" heading in the /help dialog.
Channel commands are kept OUT of SLASH_COMMANDS on purpose so they do not show
in the TUI autocomplete (typing them in the TUI would fall through to unknown
command); /respond_to is per-chat and needs a chat context the TUI lacks.

fix(self-heal): catch zero-tool turns that claim high-stakes side-effects (#680)

A fabricated "vX shipped" release scoreboard with ZERO tool calls slipped every
phantom detector: prose_lead_in truncates at the first table row (so only the
`## vX shipped` heading was inspected), "shipped" was in no verb list, and the
line-anchored past_tense_standalone_re never matches table cells that start with
`|`. All detectors were tuned for narrated prose; a fabricated facts TABLE
matched none, so no nudge/retry/fallback fired and the fake release reached the
user as if real.

Fix by verification, not more patterns: a turn that executed zero tool calls but
claims 2+ distinct high-stakes side-effects (ship/release, git push, tag,
version bump, changelog write, external post) is fabricating by construction —
those cannot happen without a tool call. claims_unbacked_side_effects scans the
full text incl. table cells, so output shape is irrelevant; it is gated on
tool_calls_completed_this_turn == 0 so a real release turn (which ran git/bash)
is never touched. The 2+ threshold keeps a lone "I pushed it earlier" from
tripping. Belt-and-suspenders: added "shipped" to action_verbs.

identifiers): scoreboard flagged; short acks / single mention / prose not

fix(preamble): spell out table-rendering mechanics so Telegram renders them (#689)

Telegram responses rendered tables as raw pipes. Rich messages are on by
default; the cause is model OUTPUT — a weaker model (qwen3.8-max-preview)
emits a table collapsed onto one line or inlined after a label
(`Pricing: | a | b | ...`), which table::try_parse can't detect, so the
message falls to the plain HTML path and the table shows as literal pipes.

The RESPONSE FORMATTING section said to use tables but never stated HOW to
write one that renders. Add explicit mechanics: a table must start on its own
line (blank line before), header row, `|---|---|` separator row, then each data
row on its own line; never put the header on a label's line and never collapse
rows onto one line. Applies to every response, vision-derived ones included.

Sentinel test asserts the guidance is present in the built brain.

fix(telegram): re-expand collapsed inline tables so they render (#690)

Robustness complement to #689. When the model emits a table collapsed onto one
line (header, |---| separator, and rows jammed together with no row-newlines),
table::try_parse can't detect it, so it renders as raw pipes.

reflow_collapsed_tables re-expands such a line: a line is treated as collapsed
only when it carries BOTH a dash-only separator cell AND ordinary content cells
(a state a well-formed multi-line table never has on one line), then the
empty-gap boundaries (| | / ||) between rows are broken into newlines so the
result parses as a proper table. Idempotent; prose, a lone separator row, and
already-expanded tables are untouched.

Applied to the response text once in deliver_final_response before the
rich-vs-HTML branching (so both the native-rich detection and the HTML render
see it), and inside markdown_to_telegram_html as a catch-all for the other
render paths (intermediates, resume).

Tests: collapsed 2-col table expands and parses; label-prefixed collapsed table
expands; already-multiline and lone-separator and prose (incl. pipes and stray
dashes) untouched; surrounding non-table lines survive.

fix(provider): send reasoning_effort for non-Kimi custom providers (qwen/modelstudio) (#691)

A custom provider with reasoning_effort = "xhigh" (modelstudio / DashScope
qwen3.8-max-preview) never sent it. from_generic_request resolved the configured
setting only via kimi_reasoning::resolve_fields, whose classify() recognizes only
Kimi families — a qwen model returned (None, None), so the request's
reasoning_effort field stayed None and the model ran shallow (and narrated).

Branch on kimi_reasoning::is_kimi_model: Kimi models keep the family-specific
resolver (effort for K3, thinking on/off for K2.x); any other custom-provider
model passes the configured reasoning_effort straight through as the request's
reasoning_effort field. So a user can set effort on any custom provider.

Tests: qwen passes xhigh through; no setting sends nothing; Kimi K3 max still
routes through the family resolver; Kimi on/off maps to thinking, never leaks
into reasoning_effort.

fix(agent): preserve reasoning on the empty-reasoning nudge so preserve_thinking models stop re-reasoning (#692)

qwen3.8-max-preview (Model Studio) looped reasoning for 200s+/20k+ tokens
non-stop. Per Alibaba's notes for this model: thinking is ALWAYS on,
reasoning_effort defaults to xhigh, and preserve_thinking is on — the COMPLETE
reasoning_content must be echoed back in history; concatenating it into content
is unsupported.

The tool-call path already preserves reasoning as a Thinking block, but the
empty-reasoning nudge path added Message::assistant(String::new()) — an empty
message that DROPPED the reasoning (its comment even claimed to preserve it). So
when qwen produced a reasoning-only turn, we threw its reasoning away and nudged;
the model saw its reasoning missing from history and re-reasoned ~20k tokens from
scratch, up to 5 nudges — the runaway loop.

Extract assistant_reasoning_stub: carry the reasoning as a leading Thinking block
(encoded back as reasoning_content) so the model builds on it instead of
re-deriving it; empty only when there is genuinely no reasoning. reasoning_effort
xhigh (my earlier #691) is not the cause — xhigh is this model's default.

Tests: stub carries reasoning as a Thinking block when present; empty when the
reasoning is absent/blank.

fix(provider): disable #658 cache split — 2-part array system broke tool-calling (#693)

After #658, with_system split the system brain into a stable prefix + runtime
suffix, and for qwen/DashScope targets the request sent the system as a 2-part
content ARRAY so cache_control could mark only the stable part. OpenAI-compatible
endpoints (qwen Model Studio, modelscope, zhipu, and the fallbacks) mishandle an
array-shaped system prompt and stop emitting tool calls — the agent narrated
endlessly and never acted for 10+ requests. Worked fine before #658.

Disable the split: with_system stores the whole system as a single string and
sets system_suffix = None, so every provider takes its single-string path (qwen:
Value::String, then qwen_body_transform stamps a 1-element cache_control array =
the pre-#658 shape the model reliably called tools with; other OpenAI-compatible:
plain string; Anthropic: single cached block). Prompt-cache hit is sacrificed for
a working agent.

Tests updated: with_system keeps the whole system with no suffix; qwen request
encodes the system as a single string, not a 2-part array.

fix(agent): make the empty-reasoning nudge tool-aware so it stops suppressing tool calls (#692)

The empty-reasoning self-heal nudge (added Apr 17, 05ab425a) assumed the model
had already run tools and just needed to write the answer: "The tool results
above are sufficient — write the answer now... do not call more tools." When the
model reasoned but had NOT run a single tool yet, that text told it not to call
the tool it needed, so it narrated instead — never executing a tool for many
turns in a row.

Extract empty_reasoning_nudge(no_tools_yet, attempt): when no tool has executed
this turn, the nudge now ENCOURAGES calling the required tool via the structured
tool-call API (or writing the answer if genuinely done); only once a tool HAS run
do we steer toward "write the answer from the results above".

Tests: no-tools nudges reference calling a tool and never suppress tool calls;
the tools-ran nudge steers to writing the answer.

fix(provider): default stop_reason to EndTurn on stream terminal chunk (#694)

qwen3.8-max-preview ends some text turns without a finish_reason our SSE parser
captures (tool-call turns get finish_reason=tool_calls and work). At the terminal
chunk ([DONE] or the final usage-only chunk) pending_stop_reason was still None,
so the MessageDelta carried stop_reason=None. The tool loop reads None as a
dropped/unfinished stream and retries the SAME turn — even though the response is
fully complete on screen. The turn never ends, keeps "thinking", qwen isn't
streaming (0 activity), and can't be cancelled.

A stream that reached its terminal marker is COMPLETE by definition, so default
stop_reason to EndTurn when no finish_reason set one, at both terminal sites
([DONE] fallback and the usage-only final chunk). Tool turns are unaffected (they
set ToolUse before the terminal chunk); the idle-timeout path for genuinely
dropped streams is unchanged.
