provider isolation:
- session-keyed Arc<RwLock<PathBuf>> map, seeded from the global on first use;
  a cd in one session's tool loop mutates only that session's handle.
- live_system_brain_for_session overrides the Runtime Info working-dir line for
  the session (like Model/Provider) via override_runtime_working_directory.
- tool context, recent-paths, compaction, and the request cwd resolve the
  session's handle instead of the global.
- session switch, /cd, and resume seed the session's handle; the footer syncs
  from it. The global is retained only as a seed for brand-new sessions.

Cache-safe: the working-dir line sits in the already-uncached per-session
Runtime Info tail; within a session the cwd is stable and across sessions the
prefix already diverges at Model/Provider above it.

fix(provider): restore a session's saved provider before its turn so it never runs on the global default (#704)

After a restart the in-memory session_providers map is empty, so
provider_for_session fell back to the global default for any session not yet
explicitly restored (resume path, channel turns, sessions not switched-to). The
turn then ran on the wrong provider and guard_cross_provider_model_leak silently
remapped the saved model to that provider's default — a switch the user never
made.

Add ensure_session_provider_restored: before the tool loop resolves the
provider, if the session has a saved provider_name that isn't registered and
differs from the global default, create and register it paired with the saved
model. No-op when already registered, when no provider is saved, or when the
saved provider is already the global default. Fixes every entry point at once.

fix(session): don't persist an involuntary provider/model remap over a session's saved pair (#705)

complete_response persisted response.provider_name/model back to the session
row whenever they differed, with no check that the change was intended. Combined
with a turn that ran on the wrong provider after a restart, this silently
rewrote a session's saved pair and the corruption survived every restart.

Thread a started_on_session_provider signal (provider_matches_session) from the
tool loop into AgentResponse: true when the turn began on the session's own
saved provider (or the session had none). complete_response now skips the
persist when the pair changed but the turn did NOT start on the session's
provider — an involuntary remap. Genuine fallbacks start matched and still
persist here and via the ProviderSwitched handler.

fix(followups): make suggest_followups description channel-accurate so the model invokes it instead of writing plain-text suggestions (#706)

The tool description and module doc were TUI-only ("appear in the input area,
gray ghost text to accept with Tab"), which reads as irrelevant on a chat
channel. Steered that way, the model narrates the suggestions as prose instead
of calling the tool — so on Telegram they arrive as dead gray text with no
button to tap, exactly the reported symptom, and the render/callback path is
never reached (no suggest_followups execution and no followup callbacks in the
logs).

Rewrite the tool description, input-schema description, module doc, and the
preamble guidance to be channel-agnostic: the tool renders INTERACTIVE UI on
every surface (tap-to-send buttons under the reply on chat channels, a pick-list
or ghost-text accept in the TUI), and the model MUST call the tool to make the
options tappable — plain-text suggestions are dead text. No change to the
already-correct Telegram render_suggestions / callback wiring.

feat(telegram): greet the group with an onboarding nudge when the bot joins (#707)

Added to a group the bot posted nothing, so members had no idea it was there or
how to onboard. When the joining bot is us (member id matches the cached
bot_user_id), post a short high-energy welcome that tells new members to send
/start so their id lands in the per-group allowlist, then @mention to chat, plus
a tip to grant admin and disable privacy mode so it hears non-mention messages.

fix(telegram): group /start registers the member per-group instead of the stale config.toml lecture (#708)

In a group, /start hit the generic branch and replied with the sender's id and
"add this to config.toml under [channels.telegram] allowed_users" — the global
allowlist, requiring manual editing, and it fired even for the owner who is
already allowed. Nobody was ever registered.

Group /start now writes the sender into channels.telegram.groups.<chat_id>.
allowed_users (via auto_register_to_group) and confirms with a short message;
the owner and already-registered members get their own variant. The config.toml
message is gone from the group path. DM /start keeps its self-host onboarding.

feat(telegram): /cowork deep link requests admin rights so the bot joins already-promoted (#709)

The Add-to-Group deep link was ?startgroup=cowork_<id> with no admin request, so
the bot landed as a plain member and the flow relied on the user promoting it by
hand. Telegram supports requesting rights inline via &admin=<rights>; the
Add-to-Group UI then adds the bot already promoted.

build_cowork_deep_link now appends &admin=invite_users+delete_messages+pin_messages+manage_chat.
invite_users is what create_chat_invite_link needs; admin also lets the bot read
every message regardless of privacy mode. Tests assert the admin param and that
invite_users is present.

fix(telegram): refine group onboarding UX (#707, #708)

- Welcome-on-join copy is high-energy, and the "make me admin" nudge only shows
  when the bot actually isn't admin (the cowork deep link usually lands it
  promoted, so the line is redundant then).
- Owner's /start in a group is silent: Telegram auto-fires it when the bot is
  added and the owner is already allowed everywhere, so a reply is just noise.
- DM /start NEVER auto-registers (invite-only): it returns the sender's id to
  share with the bot owner, or to add to config.toml when self-hosting.
- New members' /start in a group registers them per-group and confirms.

docs(telegram): update /cowork flow for admin-on-add and /start registration (#707, #708, #709)

Document that the /cowork deep link requests admin so the bot joins already
promoted (recommend always keeping it admin), that members register by sending
/start in the group (writing the per-group allowlist), and that DM /start never
auto-registers but returns the sender's id to share with the owner.

fix(telegram): auto-register any member who joins a bot group, not just flagged cowork groups (#710)

Auto-register on join was gated on is_cowork_group, a flag only set by
handle_cowork_group_join, which runs on /start cowork_<id> — a message Telegram
does not deliver when the bot is added via a startgroup deep link. So joiners
were silently never written to the per-group allowlist (verified: a member who
joined after the bot got no allowlist entry).

Drop the gate: any non-bot member joining a group the bot is in is registered
into that group's own allowlist (group-scoped, never DM). /start stays as the
fallback for members already present before the bot joined.

feat(preamble): verify every scene before declaring motion-graphics work done (#711)

The agent declared animation/motion-graphics work complete off a code read or a
single full render and missed per-scene errors it could have caught. Add a hard
rule to BRAIN_PREAMBLE (after FINISHING A TURN): read the composition/timeline
file for the scene list and frame ranges, probe EACH scene individually with the
project's own tooling (remotion still --frame=N, still/probe scripts, screenshot
at timestamp) watching for render/page errors, actually LOOK at each probe frame
with vision rather than trusting "it didn't throw", and only then report done. A
lone full-timeline render is explicitly not a substitute.

fix(config): validate keys.toml before saving the last-good snapshot (#712)

save_last_good_config validated config.toml before snapshotting it but copied
keys.toml unconditionally, so a broken keys.toml was faithfully copied into
keys.last_good.toml — recovery then failed exactly when needed and every API key
and the bot token became unloadable (observed: both files broken at the same
line). Guard the keys copy with a parse check mirroring the config guard.

Adds src/config/guard.rs: shared parse-guards (protected_file, parses,
deny_if_would_break) for the OpenCrabs config.toml/keys.toml, reused by the write
paths in the follow-up commits.

fix(config): deny edit_file/write_file writes that would break config.toml/keys.toml (#713)

The file-write tools had no validation when targeting the OpenCrabs config or
secrets file, so a raw agent edit that produced invalid TOML silently corrupted
it and took the agent down (no keys, no bot token) — the actual vector behind
the broken keys.toml. Both tools now run the new config guard before writing:
when the target resolves to the profile's real config.toml/keys.toml and the new
content wouldn't parse, the write is denied, the parse error is returned to the
agent, and it is logged. A project's own config.toml (elsewhere) is untouched.

fix(config): re-validate before fs::write in the config_manager write paths (#714)

Defense in depth: write_key/write_array (config.toml) and write_keys_key
(keys.toml) serialized the toml_edit document straight to disk with no re-parse.
Each now validates the serialized output against its schema (Config / KeysFile)
before writing; on failure it logs and returns an explanatory error, leaving the
file unchanged, so the config_manager path can never corrupt the file either.

feat(preamble): edit config/keys only via config_manager, never raw file edits (#715)

Add a hard rule to BRAIN_PREAMBLE: change config.toml/keys.toml only through the
config_manager tool, never edit_file/write_file/bash. Raw edits can corrupt the
file and lose every API key and the bot token; config_manager validates and
refuses breaking writes. If a raw edit is denied with a parse error, read it and
switch to config_manager rather than retrying.

feat(tools): follow_up_question degrades to plain text on non-interactive surfaces (#716)

On cron/webhook/A2A sessions there's no question_callback, so the tool
hard-errored and the agent burned a call it then had to work around every time.
When no interactive callback is present it now returns a SUCCESS whose output is
the question plus numbered options as plain text (via render_plaintext_question),
so the agent relays it in its reply instead of erroring. Interactive surfaces
keep the blocking button flow unchanged.

fix(telegram): gate member auto-registration to open=true groups (secure by default) (#717)

#710 auto-registered any joiner in any group and #708 let /start self-register
anywhere, which broke secure-by-default: a group the owner never opened silently
admitted members. Both paths are now gated on [channels.telegram.groups.<chat_id>].open:
- join-based auto-register fires only when the group is open;
- group /start registers only in an open group; in a non-open group it returns
  the sender's id and points them to ask the owner to run /cowork or add them,
  never a silent self-add.
Non-open groups stay secure by default; open=true (via /cowork or config) is the
explicit opt-in.

feat(telegram): /cowork opens the target group (open=true, persisted) (#718)

Make /cowork the explicit, owner-initiated action that opens a group so its
members are allowed (and tracked via the open-gated auto-register from #717),
persisting until the owner changes it. Two triggers, both via the guarded
write_key:
- bot self-join where the adder has a pending /cowork session -> set the group
  open=true and clear the session (the cowork deep-link path);
- /cowork run inside a group by the owner -> open THIS group (covers a group the
  bot was already added to before).
Adds cowork::set_group_open. The welcome message reflects whether the group was
opened as a cowork group.

docs(telegram): document per-group open field and the /cowork opens-group model (#719)

Document [channels.telegram.groups.<chat_id>].open (per-group blanket allow,
default off, never global), correct the stale group /start line (it now registers
in open groups and returns the id otherwise, not "silently ignored"), and
describe that /cowork is the owner-initiated action that sets a group open=true
with auto-registration gated to open groups. Secure by default everywhere else.

fix(vision): expand ~ in provider_vision and analyze_video paths (#720)

analyze_image was fixed to resolve tilde paths (493c1358) but the provider-vision
image path and analyze_video still read the RAW path. Since the prompt renders
paths tilde-collapsed, the model passes ~/… and, when a vision provider is
configured (that path runs before the Gemini fallback), the read failed on a
literal ~ dir — the agent then retried with an absolute path, a regression from
going right first try. Both paths now resolve via resolve_tool_path(&src,
&context.working_dir()) before reading.

feat(agent): add symmetric message-enqueue plumbing for background-task resume (#722)

Phase 1 of the long-task session-callback: today the message queue only has a
DRAIN callback (MessageQueueCallback) the tool loop calls between iterations.
Add the symmetric producer so a background-task watcher can push a completion
into a session's queue on any surface:
- MessageEnqueueCallback type + QueuedUserMessage::system(context, display);
- AgentService.message_enqueue_callback field + with_message_enqueue_callback
  builder + enqueue_session_message(session_id, msg) (no-op with a warn when no
  surface wired it).
Inert until the watcher, bash auto-promote, and per-surface producers land in
later phases. Round-trip covered by session_enqueue_callback_test. Design spec:
~/.opencrabs/research/long-task-session-callback.md.

feat(agent): background-task manager + bash auto-promote of known-long commands (#722)

Phases 2-3. The manager (background_tasks.rs) runs a command detached and, on
completion, enqueues a system QueuedUserMessage into the originating session via
the enqueue producer — so the tool loop resumes it at the next iteration
boundary (mid-turn) or as a fresh turn.

bash now auto-promotes known-long commands (cargo test/build/run/clippy, npm/
pnpm/yarn test|build, npx remotion render, gh run watch, …): when a background
manager is wired it hands the command off, returns "running in the background,
I'll continue when it finishes", and frees the 600s budget. sudo is excluded
(needs the inline password flow). Fully inert until a surface wires the enqueue
producer (phase 5), so no behavior change yet — bash runs inline as before.

AgentService.background_manager (built from the enqueue callback) flows to the
tool context. Tests cover the allowlist, label, completion framing, tail, and a
real detached-command -> enqueue round-trip.

feat(tui): activate background-task resume on the TUI (#722)

Wire the TUI enqueue producer and the idle-resume trigger so the background
feature actually fires. On a detached long command finishing, the manager's
enqueue callback sends TuiEvent::BackgroundTaskDone; the TUI handler injects the
completion mid-turn (via the message queue) if the session is still processing,
or spawns a fresh resume turn (resume_background_turn) if it's idle. The resume
uses send_message_with_tools_and_display with the service-level callbacks, so
streaming, tool calls, and the final response route to the TUI like any turn,
and history shows the compact display tag while the LLM sees the full result.

End-to-end on the TUI now: bash auto-promotes cargo test / renders / gh run
watch, frees the 600s budget, and the session resumes itself when the task
finishes. Channels + preamble land next.

feat(preamble): tell the agent long tasks run in the background and resume the session (#722)

Add a preamble block: genuinely long commands (cargo test/build, npx remotion
render, gh run watch, …) run detached automatically — bash returns immediately
and the session resumes itself when the task finishes (mid-turn at the next
tool-call boundary, or a fresh turn if idle). So run the command normally, don't
block-wait, don't re-run to "check", don't hand-roll polling; the result comes
back explicitly. Ordinary quick commands still run inline. Accurate on the TUI
now; channel resume wiring is the remaining piece.

feat(telegram): activate background-task resume on Telegram (#722)

Wire the Telegram enqueue producer so the feature works on Telegram, not just the
TUI. ChannelFactory gains create_agent_service_full(queue, enqueue); the Telegram
agent supplies an enqueue callback (resume::build_enqueue_callback) that, on a
detached long command finishing, resolves session→chat (TelegramState), grabs the
bot, and calls resume_session to deliver a full-streaming turn to the chat. The
agent handle is filled via a weak holder after the service is built (it can't be
captured at creation), breaking the cycle.

Now on Telegram: cargo test / renders / gh run watch auto-background, free the
600s budget, and the chat gets the result when the task finishes. Discord/Slack/
WhatsApp still run inline (same pattern applies; follow-up).

fix(telegram): render suggest_followups last and fix taps doing nothing (#723, #724)

The suggested-next buttons fired mid-turn (before the final message) because the
SuggestedFollowups event rendered immediately when the model called the tool.
And a tap did nothing because the stash was set mid-turn, so any re-entry into
handle_message for that session ran clear_pending_followups and wiped it before
the tap.

Buffer the options in StreamingState.pending_suggestions and render_suggestions
ONCE at the very end of handle_message, after all delivery — so the buttons are
always the last message AND the stash is set fresh at turn end, with no window
for it to be cleared before a tap. Add tap-path logging (callback data, empty
stash, unparseable data) so the routing is diagnosable.

fix(qwen): apply the reasoning_content missing-safety to qwen, not just Moonshot (#725)

preserve_thinking providers 400 when an assistant tool_call message omits
reasoning_content while thinking is on ("reasoning_content is missing in
assistant tool call message at index N"). The resume-side hoisting gate
(preserves_thinking) already covers qwen (aliyuncs/dashscope, model starts with
qwen), but the encode-side placeholder safety was gated on the Moonshot-only
needs_reasoning_content_for — so a qwen assistant tool_call message without a
captured Thinking block (legacy DB row, or a turn that yielded no reasoning)
sent reasoning_content=null and qwen 400'd, causing turn failures and retry/
fallback churn.

Gate the encode-side placeholder on the same qwen-aware preserves_thinking,
symmetric with the resume side. Real reasoning is always preferred; the
placeholder is only a fallback when reasoning is genuinely absent. Covered by
the existing preserves_thinking_matches_qwen_family test.

fix(tui): decide click-vs-drag on mouse-up so click-drag selects text instead of expanding (#726)

MouseClick (mouse-down) called handle_click_select, which toggled the expand
state of the collapsible tool-group / reasoning block under the cursor. So
starting a drag-to-select over such a block fired the expand on mouse-down before
the drag began, and the drag-to-copy path in handle_mouse_up never ran.

Mouse-down now only starts the gesture (resets the drag anchor). The click-vs-
drag decision happens on mouse-up: handle_mouse_up click-selects (expand) when no
drag occurred and extracts+copies when a drag did. A plain click still expands;
a click-drag now selects text to copy.

feat(tui): 3-state expand cycle for reasoning, capped so it never floods the view (#727, #726)

Expanding a reasoning/thinking block dumped the entire (often 2+ page) thinking
into the viewport, burying everything. Reasoning now cycles through three states
on each click or ctrl+o: collapsed -> capped (first 10 lines + a "… N more
(click / ctrl+o for full)" hint) -> full -> collapsed. Tool-call groups are
unaffected (they aren't bloated).

Also map tool-group lines to their own message in chat_line_to_msg (they mapped
to None, so a click didn't reliably toggle the group under the cursor and could
hit an adjacent block) — completes the #726 click-to-expand fixes.

Adds DisplayMessage.expanded_full + cycle_details_expand(); click ToggleDetails
and ctrl+o both cycle. Covered by details_cycle_is_collapsed_capped_full_collapsed.

docs(readme): document the click/ctrl+o 3-state expand cycle and drag-to-copy (#727, #726)

Add a Terminal UI row: reasoning expands collapsed -> capped -> full ->
collapsed via click or ctrl+o so a long thought never floods the view; tool
groups toggle; a click toggles the block under the cursor while a click-drag
selects text to copy instead of expanding.

fix(resume): stop perpetual re-resume of completed sessions on restart

A resume turn went through run_tool_loop, which re-inserted a fresh
pending_requests row for the recovery itself. When the resume was then
interrupted (cancelled by a new message, process killed on another
restart, or a crash before the cleanup delete), that row survived and
resumed the same already-done session on every subsequent startup, with
rows piling up.

Thread a track_pending flag through run_tool_loop (true for genuine user
turns) and add resume_interrupted_turn, which passes false. Point both
resume entry points at it: TUI/Discord/WhatsApp/Slack in cli/ui.rs and
Telegram in channels/telegram/resume.rs. Only genuine user-initiated
turns remain recoverable.

Closes #729

fix(tui): drop the cancelled query and its empty assistant placeholder as a pair

A turn persists the user row and an empty assistant placeholder up front, then
streams content into the placeholder. If the user double-escapes to cancel
before the agent produces anything, the placeholder stays empty and the query
is left unanswered. #698 cleaned up the display but its DB delete only fired
when the trailing row was a user row — after the placeholder insert the trailing
row is the empty assistant, so the query was never deleted and survived into the
next turn's LLM context, duplicating on resend.

Add MessageRepository::delete_trailing_unanswered_pair, which removes the empty
assistant placeholder and its preceding user query together, and only when the
trailing assistant row is genuinely empty so an answered turn is never touched.
The cancel-restore path calls it instead of the single-row delete. Only the
freshly-created trailing rows are affected, so earlier context is never shifted.

Closes #730

fix(telegram): dedup outbound media so the agent can't upload the same file twice

A model can repeat a send_photo/send_document call, and a large upload can time
out client-side after Telegram already delivered it and get re-sent — both land
the identical file+caption twice back-to-back.

Add MediaSendDedup (per-chat, TTL-windowed) and claim the send signature
(action + chat + file reference + caption) before uploading in send_photo and
send_document. A duplicate within the window is skipped with a note instead of
re-uploading; a deliberate re-send after the window still goes through.

Closes #721

fix(tui): anchor the clicked block's header when it expands or collapses

Clicking a tool group or reasoning block to expand it changed the transcript
height while scroll_offset stayed fixed-from-bottom, so the viewport jumped
pages and threw the clicked block off-screen — worst near the bottom, where the
streaming compensation is skipped and the view snaps to the bottom.

On a click toggle, pin the clicked message's header to the screen row it sits on
(chat_expand_anchor), and in render_chat restore it there via the pure
anchored_scroll_offset helper after the height change. The block now grows or
shrinks in place; at the very bottom auto-scroll re-arms so streaming still
sticks. Ctrl+O stays a global toggle-all and is unaffected.

Closes #728

fix(rsi): dedup scanner ignores fenced code and table rows

The brain-file dedup scanner flagged legitimately-repeated lines, producing
false-positive removal proposals that would break teaching gates and tables:
- teaching-gate examples repeat common code lines across the WRONG/CORRECT
  fenced blocks; the scan had no fenced-code-block tracking
- identical table header rows like a two-column header recur across unrelated
  tables; is_structural_line only skipped separator rows (those with a --- run)

Add a fence-aware eligible_dedup_lines extractor that skips lines inside code
fences, and treat any table row (starts and ends with a pipe) as structural.

Tests: table rows structural, fenced code excluded, and a full scan over
repeated headers + fenced code produces zero clusters.

Closes #736

fix(browser): larger viewport and maximized headed window

viewport and start the headed window maximized so the live view matches.

Closes #738

fix(browser): validate tab close with a truthful outcome

close_page removed the page from the map and issued a best-effort CDP close but
returned true whenever an entry existed, so browser_close could not tell a
confirmed close from a silent failure, and tabs piled up across automations.

Return a CloseOutcome (Closed / NothingOpen / Failed): browser_close now reports
each truthfully. The handle is always dropped from the map, so the next browser
action gets a fresh tab even when the OS tab lingered — smooth transitions
between many automations.

Closes #739

fix(plan): auto-complete the trailing delivery task at turn settle

A plan whose only remaining task is the trailing deliver-the-result step never
reached is_complete() on its own: delivering the final answer is exactly what
leaves that box unchecked, so the plan never archived and its card lingered with
1/N done.

Add PlanDocument::complete_trailing_delivery_task, which completes the last task
only when every earlier task is already Completed/Skipped and the last is
Pending (a Pending task earlier in the list, or a Failed/Blocked last task, is a
genuine gap and left untouched). The turn-settle hook calls it only when the
turn actually delivered a final response, persists, then archives.

Closes #737

fix(tui): label the live token counter as a turn total and show ctx budget

The spinner showed '(8s · 31872 tok)' next to 'is thinking...', but
streaming_output_tokens is the whole turn's output (reasoning + completion text
across every tool iteration, reset only at turn start) — not the size of the
current thought. Pairing the bare number with 'is thinking...' made a normal
multi-tool turn read as one 31k-token thought.

Extract format_turn_spinner_meta (pure, tested): renders 'N tok this turn' and
appends the ctx budget (ctx: X/Y Z%, same helper as the Telegram flow footer).
All three spinner sites (responding / thinking / inline) use it.

Closes #741

fix(tui): live thinking shows a short excerpt, not a scrolling wall

During the thinking-only phase the TUI rendered the last 12 reasoning lines plus
a '⋯ N more lines' tally, which made a normal turn look like one giant thought.

Show a single latest-sentence excerpt (🧠 …) instead, mirroring the Telegram
flow header. The excerpt logic moves to utils::string::thinking_excerpt (one
shared impl); Telegram's thinking_status_excerpt now delegates to it. The full
reasoning stays available on the finalized message's 3-state expand.

Closes #742

fix(tui): drop ctx from the live spinner, it already shows under the input

#741 added the ctx budget to the thinking/responding spinner, but the TUI footer
under the input already shows ctx: X/Y Z% — so it was duplicated on screen. Keep
the spinner to live turn info only (elapsed + N tok this turn); ctx stays in the
footer where it belongs.

Closes #744

fix(tui): strip discarded phantom self-heal narration from the live buffer

When the phantom detector fires (model narrates actions without calling a tool),
the iteration is discarded server-side (skipped for DB persist) and a self-heal
nudge is injected. But that text was already streamed to the TUI and was never
removed, so every discarded narration piled up on screen across retries — a
30k-token wall that read like leaked thinking.

Emit ProgressEvent::StripStreamedContent (usize::MAX, clamped to the buffer
length by the TUI) when a phantom iteration is discarded, mirroring the
gaslight-refusal strip. The whole streamed buffer is discardable on a phantom
iteration (nothing was committed), so it is wiped before the retry.

Closes #745

fix(agent): bound the phantom self-heal loop instead of re-nudging forever

Once the phantom retry budget was exhausted, the code reset the counter and kept
nudging the same provider indefinitely (comment: 'user presses Stop if they want
out'). A model stuck narrating instead of calling tools re-narrated forever, each
iteration burning a full response — a runaway.

Bound it: the budget may roll MAX_PHANTOM_ROLLS times (each roll strips the
discarded narration from the TUI like #745), after which the turn gives up and
ends with the model's narration as the answer, persisted so it survives reload.
Total phantom attempts are now ~MAX_PHANTOM_RETRIES * (MAX_PHANTOM_ROLLS + 1)
instead of unbounded.

Closes #746

fix(phantom): catch image-generation hallucination (media claim, no marker, 0 tools)

The model claimed it generated/edited and delivered an image ('There it is.
Seamless background, better brightness/exposure contrast...') with zero tool
calls and no image attached, repeatedly across turns — and phantom detection
exonerated it as Finished. generate_image delivers via <<IMG:>> markers, so the
hallucinated text (no marker, no ship/push/tag words, no 'Let me' intent phrase)
matched none of the existing tells.

Add claims_unbacked_media_result: a turn asserting a produced/delivered image or
media result (there it is / generated it / the edited image, about a visual
subject) with no <<IMG:>>/<<VID:>> marker is fabricating. Wired into the
mid-turn phantom trigger, gated on zero tool calls so a real generation turn
(which ran the tool and emitted a marker) is never flagged.

Closes #747

fix(provider): retry a flaky-provider 404 instead of treating it as permanent

A bare HTTP 404 (ApiError) was not retryable — only 5xx, HTML-body 4xx, and
temporarily-unavailable-signal 4xx retried. Flaky providers throw transient 404s
on a valid endpoint mid-run, so the turn bailed (and on a single-provider setup,
stopped) instead of retrying with backoff.

Classify a 404 that is NOT model-unsupported as retryable, so it enters the
bounded backoff retry chain. Genuine model-not-found 404s are still caught by
is_model_unsupported and stay permanent (route to the model-mismatch UX).

Closes #748

fix(agent): make mid-stream retry more patient (5 attempts, exponential backoff)

The mid-stream error / stream-drop retry was hardcoded to 3 attempts. A user on
a flaky provider (frequent transient 404s mid-run) reported the run 'stops after
three retries' and asked for more patient backoff resumption.

Bump MAX_STREAM_RETRIES to 5 and route both mid-stream retry loops through it
with exponential backoff (500ms, 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s ≈ 15s of patience), so a flaky
provider recovers and the run continues where it stopped instead of dying. Pairs
with #748 (flaky 404s are now retryable).

Closes #749

fix(agent): auto-recover from a repetitive-tool-call poisoned session

When an agent makes the same tool call (identical name + args) across many
consecutive rounds — e.g. polling a down endpoint — the history fills with
identical tool_use/tool_result pairs. Some providers then reject EVERY request
with a 500 (Repetitive tool calls detected), permanently bricking the session:
each new message re-sends the poison and 500s again, recoverable only by a
manual DB delete.

Add a repetition module (pure, tested) that detects the guardrail error and
collapses consecutive identical tool rounds to one, keeping the first and
preserving text-bearing or non-consecutive rounds. Classify that 500 as
NON-retryable so it surfaces immediately (no wasted provider retries), and add a
tool-loop recovery arm that prunes the duplicates and retries once with a healed
history — so the session self-heals instead of dying. Also lower the per-turn
identical-call breaker (nudge 5->3, break 7->4) so a turn poisons far less
before the loop is stopped.

Closes #740

fix(phantom): make image-generation hallucination detection multilingual

claims_unbacked_media_result (#747) used hardcoded English phrases. Like every
other phantom tell, it must work across languages. Move the media delivery
phrases and visual context words into the phantom_lang TOMLs (en/es/fr/id/pt/ru)
via two new LangConfig fields, and scan the union across all languages so a
Spanish/French/Portuguese/Indonesian/Russian 'here's your image' narration is
caught too, immune to language mis-detection.

Tests: the exact reported English narration plus es/pt/fr/id narrations are
flagged; a <<IMG:>> marker still exonerates in any language.

Closes #750

fix(agent): don't deliver an image hallucination when self-heal gives up

With multilingual media-phantom detection (#750) and the bounded self-heal loop
(#746): when the model narrates a fake image result and never calls
generate_image, the phantom retries exhaust and the give-up delivered the
model's narration ('Actually generated this time...') as the answer — so the lie
still reached the user.

On give-up, when the narration is a media hallucination
(claims_unbacked_media_result), strip the false streamed text and deliver a
truthful message (no image tool ran, nothing was produced) instead of the
model's false claim. Non-media give-ups still deliver the narration as before.

Closes #751

fix(agent): turn-end phantom verdict catches narration delivered via recovery paths

A zero-tool turn where the model reasons without answering triggers the
empty-reasoning nudges, then on exhaustion walks the fallback chain. The
fallback provider's narration ('On it. Filing the issue and starting the work
now. Let me check the repo first.') is produced AFTER the per-iteration phantom
check already ran on the earlier empty text, so it was never re-checked and
reached the user as Finished with 0 tools executed.

Add a path-independent turn-end phantom verdict on the final answer: when the
turn ran ZERO tools and the answer is a phantom narration (intent-to-act,
unbacked side effects, or a fabricated image), strip the streamed lie and
deliver a truthful message instead. Multilingual by construction — reuses the
phantom_lang detectors (verified: the union scan is immune to mis-detection).

Closes #752

feat(claude-cli): discover the model list from the CLI instead of hardcoding

The /models menu for claude-cli read a hardcoded const, so a model released
after build time (Opus 5) never appeared even though Claude Code's own /model
menu listed it on the same machine.

Discover the list at menu time instead: parse the aliases the installed binary
documents in `claude --help` (--model: "an alias for the latest model"), union
with the built-in const as a floor so nothing disappears if the CLI is missing
or its help text changes shape, and append the versions learned_alias observed
the CLI actually resolve — which is how a brand-new release surfaces by name
with no code change. The --help subprocess is cached per process; learned
versions are re-read each call so the menu tracks the latest resolution.

Both the menu and Provider::supported_models now read that discovery, so a
newly discovered model can't be rejected downstream as not in the catalogue.

A shared shape filter guards both sources: it keeps prose out of the parse (the
apostrophe in the help text shifts naive quote pairing) and keeps non-model
sentinels out of the menu (a real learned cache held a synthetic placeholder
value for an alias).

Closes #753

fix(claude-cli): surface Opus 5 in the model picker (third parallel list + state discovery)

The /models (onboard:provider) dialog still showed no Opus 5 after the previous
change, because the TUI onboarding picker had its OWN copy of the list:
tui/onboarding/fetch.rs read claude_cli::SUPPORTED_MODELS directly, bypassing
the discovery the menu and provider were switched to. That is exactly the
parallel-list drift this repo's tests warn about. It now calls available_models().

Discovery also could not name a brand-new release: `claude --help` only
advertises the family aliases, and the learned-alias cache lags until the CLI
resolves one in a real run. Add a third, best-effort source: the model ids the
CLI itself records on this machine in ~/.claude.json —
additionalModelOptionsCache[].value (its option catalogue) and
clientDataCacheSlots.*.model (models actually run). Read-only and fail-safe: a
missing file, changed schema, or parse error yields nothing and the built-in
const floor still applies.

Ids are normalized on the way in (claude- prefix and bracketed variant suffix
stripped), so the help example claude-fable-5 and the recorded fable-5 collapse
to one entry instead of appearing twice.

Verified live on this machine: the picker now offers opus-5 alongside the
aliases, with no duplicates and no un-normalized spellings.

Refs #753

fix(tui): format every claude-cli model row consistently in the picker

The picker rendered a half-formatted list: "opus-5" appeared as its raw id
directly below a properly formatted "Opus 4.8", "Fable 5" appeared on two rows,
and the bare aliases showed as lower-case ids next to prettified versions.

Three causes:
  * prettify_claude_cli_model required a two-part version (rest.split_once('-')),
    so a major-only release like opus-5 returned None and fell through raw. It
    now accepts both shapes (4-8 -> 4.8, 5 -> 5) and the fable family.
  * model_display_label mapped BOTH the alias `fable` and the version `fable-5`
    to "Fable 5", so discovery surfacing both produced two identical rows.
  * the bare aliases had no label at all, so they rendered as raw ids.

The bare aliases are a moving pointer to the newest release of a family (the CLI
documents them as "an alias for the latest model"), so they are now labelled
"Opus (latest)" / "Fable (latest)" / etc. rather than a fixed version — that
removes the duplicate and makes it obvious that picking `opus` gets the newest
Opus.

Tests pin both whole-picker invariants, so this cannot regress as models ship:
no two models may share a label, and no row may render un-formatted.

Closes #754

fix(tui): order the model picker newest-first instead of by merge order

available_models() returned models in the order they were discovered (help
parse, then the CLI state file, then the const floor), so the picker read as
nonsense: Opus 5 rendered BELOW Opus 4.8 and ABOVE Opus 4.7, making the newest
release look older than its neighbour.

Sort semantically instead: bare aliases first (they are the moving 'latest'
pointer and the safest pick), then versioned models grouped by family with the
newest version first. Major-only and major-minor versions compare correctly
because both parse to a (major, minor) pair, so 5 -> (5,0) outranks
4.8 -> (4,8).

Test pins the ordering so it cannot regress as new models ship.

Closes #755

refactor(tui): extract the tool-group scan from render_chat behind a tested seam

Groundwork for the unified per-turn block (#743 step 1). No behavior change: the
renderer produces exactly the same output, the loop just moved.

render_chat inlined the look-ahead that walks a run of consecutive tool groups
(stepping over the thinking-only messages that sit between them). Because it was
inline, the only coverage was a hand-maintained COPY of the same loop in
tui_tool_stack_test, which could drift from the real renderer without any test
failing.

Extract it as the pure scan_tool_stack(messages, start) -> ToolStack {count,
total_calls, end}. The renderer calls it, and the test helper now delegates to it
too, so the existing six stacking tests exercise production logic instead of a
lookalike.

That also exposes something the copy could never test: `end`, the index the
renderer turns into skip_count. Get it wrong and the chat either repeats rows or
silently drops the assistant's reply. Four new tests pin it — interleaved
thinking is consumed, visible text is NOT consumed, a lone group advances by
one, and a mid-list offset only walks forward.

Remaining for #743 (the block itself) is unchanged and still needs a live TUI to
verify: a turn has no identity on DisplayMessage (it must be inferred from user
message boundaries), expand state is per-message rather than per-turn, there is
no per-turn header, and click/scroll/drag route through line->message rather
than line->block.

Refs #743

feat(tui): infer turn boundaries so a turn can be grouped

DisplayMessage carries no turn marker, so nothing in the renderer knew which
messages belonged to the same turn — the foundation every per-turn feature (one
collapsible block, a per-turn header, a single expand state) needs.

Add the pure turn_ranges(&[DisplayMessage]) -> Vec<TurnRange>: a turn opens at a
user message and runs to the next one, absorbing the assistant text,
thinking-only messages, tool groups and any system/error rows in between. Rows
preceding the first user message (history-paging markers, a restored
transcript's leading rows) form their own leading range so nothing is dropped.
turn_of() resolves a row back to its turn for click/anchor use.

No behavior change — nothing renders differently yet.

Tests pin the shape, including that turns cover every message with no gaps or
overlap, and that back-to-back user messages split into one turn each.

Closes #757

feat(tui): per-turn header summarising the work a turn did

A turn rendered as loose rows with no summary, unlike the Telegram flow block
whose header reads status, tool count and duration.

Add a header line above each turn's first non-user row: a status glyph, the
tool-call count across the WHOLE turn (not per group), the failed count when
any call failed, and the humanised duration. Built on the turn grouping from
#757 via the pure turn_summary + format_turn_header, so both are unit-tested.

Only turns that actually ran tools get a header — a plain question-and-answer
turn would just gain noise, so format_turn_header returns None there. ctx is
deliberately absent: it lives in the footer under the input and duplicating it
was #744.

Header lines map to no message, so click, drag-select and the #728 scroll
anchor are untouched; wiring the header to a turn-level toggle is the follow-up.

Closes #759

feat(tui): fold a turn's working-out into its header

The per-turn header (#759) summarised a turn but folded nothing, so a turn still
rendered as the same wall of loose rows with one more line on top — worse, not
better. This makes the header actually collapse the turn.

A folded turn hides its working-out — thinking, tool groups, and the
intermediate narration between them — and keeps what still matters: the user's
question, the final answer, error rows, and anything interactive (an approval
prompt or menu, which would otherwise become unreachable). Same shape as the
Telegram flow block, where the log folds and the answer stays a clean bubble.

Defaults are chosen so live work is never hidden: the newest turn stays open,
older turns fold. Clicking a turn header overrides that for that turn, in either
direction, and the header says which action a click performs.

State is keyed by the turn's ANCHOR MESSAGE UUID rather than an index, because
indices shift as messages arrive and mean nothing across sessions — so this
stays correct with split panes, where each pane renders its own session's list.

Header rows map to no message: click, drag-select and the #728 scroll anchor
keep routing through line->message exactly as before. The turn toggle rides a
separate line->turn map consulted first.

Tests: the final answer is the last visible assistant text; a folded turn keeps
only the question and the answer; errors and interactive rows are never hidden;
newest-open / older-folded defaults; and an explicit click overriding either way.

Closes #758

fix(tui): fold a turn as soon as it settles, not only older turns

The fold defaulted to keeping the NEWEST turn open. In practice the turn on
screen is always the newest, so while working nothing ever appeared to collapse
— the whole point of the feature was invisible.

Keep a turn open only while it is still RUNNING; the moment it settles it folds
to its header. Older turns stay folded as before, and an explicit click still
overrides either way.

Closes #758 follow-up

fix(tui): fold every turn by default, running or settled

Folding only after a turn settled still left the running turn rendering its
whole working-out — so the wall was still there while you worked, which is
exactly when it hurts. Grouped-and-collapsed has to mean always.

Every turn now folds to its header by default; a click on the header opens one.
Live progress is unaffected: in-flight streaming text and the active tool group
render from their own state after the message loop, not from the finalized rows
being folded — so you still watch work happen, you just do not get the wall of
finalized thinking, tool groups and intermediate narration behind it.

Closes #758 follow-up

fix(qwen): stop sending a blank reasoning chain, it made qwen leak and repeat

Qwen requires the COMPLETE reasoning_content passed back and cannot concatenate
reasoning into content. #725 extended the reasoning_content gate to qwen, but
the only thing that gate controls is the FALLBACK: real reasoning is already
sent for every provider by the branch above it. So its sole effect on qwen was
substituting a blank placeholder (a single space) whenever no Thinking block
was available.

That fired constantly: the DB thinking column is currently never written (47
assistant rows in the last day, 0 with thinking), so every historical assistant
tool_call message reached qwen with an empty thinking chain. Qwen then
re-derived its reasoning and, unable to put it in content, spilled it into the
visible answer — the reasoning-only turns, leaked thinking, and repeating
paragraphs of #760.

Restrict the blank-chain fallback to Moonshot, which only validates that the
field is present and non-empty. Qwen keeps receiving real reasoning whenever we
have it; it just never receives a blank one. Omitting beats corrupting.

Refs #760

fix(tui): keep the tool-call summary at full visibility when a turn is folded

Folding replaced the cyan bold tool-group header with a dim grey line, so a
folded turn read as LESS important than the rows it stood in for. That was an
accidental side effect of the fold, not a deliberate change.

Render the turn header's summary in the same cyan bold the tool-group header
used, keeping only the click hint dim.

Refs #758

feat(telegram): scope owner-gated command replies to the invoker

Bot API 10.2 added `receiver_user_id` to sendMessage: a group message
only the named member can see. Every slash command is owner-gated, so
the whole group has been watching replies addressed to one person.

Terminal command replies now go ephemeral in groups: /help, /usage,
/doctor, /evolve, /mission-control, /rtk, /respond_to, /redact, /plan,
/show_plan, the /new, /stop, /compact and /discard acks, the /execute
busy refusal, and the "not authorized" notice.

Left public on purpose:
- Replies carrying an inline keyboard (/models, /sessions, /cd,
  /profiles). Their buttons drive callback edits, which need the
  editEphemeralMessage* methods this path does not implement.
- Commands resolving to a prompt (/goal, /cowork, skills). Those run a
  full agent turn with streaming edits and plan cards.
- Every reply in a DM, which is already private.

teloxide 0.17 has no binding for the parameter, so the new module calls
sendMessage over raw HTTP, mirroring the sendRichMessage client. The
send never errors: a rejected or unreachable call falls back to the
existing public path, so a pre-10.2 Bot API server behaves as before.
sendRichMessage did not gain the parameter, so a scoped reply renders as
HTML rather than native rich.

Closes #756

feat(telegram): ask the server whether rich messages can be scoped

The 10.2 changelog enumerates the methods that gained `receiver_user_id`
and sendRichMessage is not among them, but that method's own parameter
table was never available to confirm the omission. Assuming it either
way is a guess baked into the binary.

A scoped command reply with rich structure now attempts sendRichMessage
with the parameter first and remembers what the server said. If it is
accepted, group command replies keep native rich rendering and stay
private. If it is refused, the answer is cached for the process and the
HTML path takes over, costing exactly one wasted call.

A transport error deliberately leaves the answer unknown: a dropped
connection is not the server declining the parameter, and caching it as
one would forfeit native rich for the rest of the process over a blip.

The POST helper now reports Sent/Rejected/Transport instead of a bool so
the two failure kinds cannot be conflated, and build_rich_body is split
out so the scoped request is the public one plus the scoping field, with
a test pinning them together.

fix(channels): reconcile the /models picker against the live inventory

A `models = [...]` array in config.toml short-circuited the live fetch
entirely, so the chat-channel picker froze at whatever was written to
config. A model the provider released later was unreachable from
Telegram, Discord and Slack even though the TUI could select it, and a
model the provider dropped still showed until a turn actually failed.
The comment already claimed "config models first, then live fetch"; the
code was an either/or.

Config is now a seed and an ordering preference: the configured entries
render first, the live list is unioned in behind them. The wait is
budgeted on what there is to fall back to, 3s when a config list can
carry the menu and 10s when nothing else can, and a timeout still
renders the configured list rather than failing.

That breaks an assumption in the button path. callback_data is capped at
64 bytes, so a model whose name does not fit is encoded as its position
in the list, and model_at_index reconstructed those positions from
config. With live entries past the end of the config array it no longer
can, and a miss does not fail safe: the caller falls back to the raw
token and would select a model literally named "#7". So the picker now
records what it rendered, per provider, and positions resolve against
that first. This also closes the same latent hole for CLI providers,
whose canonical list was never in config either.

OpenRouter and custom providers still skip the live fetch, which is
deliberate: a 300+ entry inline keyboard is its own design problem.

Closes #761

fix(tui): make a folded turn readable and keep it in place when toggled

The per-turn fold shipped without ever being run, and four things were
wrong in use.

Expanding jumped the viewport pages away from the click. Every other
expandable path pins a scroll anchor before toggling; the turn header
branch did not, so unfolding inserted the whole working-out above a
fixed-from-bottom offset. A header line belongs to no message, so it
cannot use the existing message-keyed anchor: it needs one resolved
through the turn map, which is what chat_expand_anchor_turn adds.

The header sat flush against the answer below it and read as part of
that text. It now ends with a blank line like every other block.

Folding a turn lost information. A collapsed tool group still shows its
last call, so a folded turn showing only "39 tool calls" was strictly
worse than what it replaced. The header now carries the same preview
line, styled identically, red when that call failed.

Ctrl+O looked broken while a turn was folded: it expanded tool groups
that the fold was still hiding. It now drives the fold itself, scoped to
the newest turn so a long transcript does not reflow underneath the
user, and only that turn's header advertises the key.

The comment claiming the newest turn stays open was stale since the
change that made everything fold; corrected rather than reinstated.

folded_turn_preview is a pure seam with tests covering last-call-wins,
the failure flag, a turn that ran no tools, turn isolation, and a range
past the end of the list.

feat(tui): show what a detached background command is doing

A genuinely long command runs detached so it does not churn toward the
bash 600s cap, and the turn ends the moment it is spawned. That left the
footer with nothing to draw: no spinner, because no turn is active, and
a five minute build looked exactly like a hang. The agent would say it
was waiting on the test suite and the UI showed no sign anything was
running at all.

The manager already tracked a per-session count but threw away what was
running, so no surface could say more than "a task exists". It now keeps
the label and start time, and exposes them through running_tasks.

The footer renders the oldest task with its elapsed time, plus a count
when others are running behind it: "cargo test 1m 30s +2". Oldest,
because that is the one the wait is actually about and the one whose
elapsed time answers whether it is stuck.

Reading straight from the manager each frame avoids a second source of
truth for which tasks are live. The runner already redraws on a 10ms
poll, so the elapsed time ticks without any new event plumbing.

fix: report background tasks a restart killed instead of waiting forever

A long command runs detached and the turn ends immediately, on the
promise that the session resumes when it finishes. That promise lived
entirely in an in-memory map: killing the process dropped the child AND
every record of it, so the session sat waiting on a resume that could
never arrive and nothing said why. The bash tool still told the model
"I'll continue this session automatically when it finishes", which was
simply false across a restart.

In-flight commands are now persisted before they run. Startup treats
every surviving row as interrupted, because the process that owned the
child is gone with it, and reports it into its own session: the command
did not complete, here is what it was, decide whether to run it again.
Deciding is left to the agent rather than re-running something expensive
on its behalf.

Rows are keyed by task id, not label, so two identical commands in
flight clear independently and finishing one does not retire the other.
Persisting before the command starts is what makes a mid-run restart
visible; clearing on completion is what stops the next startup reporting
a phantom interruption, so both failures are logged loudly even though
the command itself is unaffected.

fix(tui): split a reloaded turn back into its iterations

After a restart, a reasoning-heavy turn rendered as a wall of thinking
that the live view had folded away.

The tool loop persists a turn one iteration at a time: a reasoning block
wrapped in markers, then that iteration's visible text appended raw.
Reload split only on TOOL markers, so a turn that ran no tools fused
every iteration into ONE assistant message holding all the text and one
merged reasoning blob. That single message is the turn's last non-empty
assistant row, which makes it the final answer, and the per-turn fold
must always show the final answer. So the whole turn stayed on screen no
matter what the fold did.

Splitting each text region on its reasoning-block boundaries restores
the chronological think-text-think-text layout the live view had, so
only the last text segment is the final answer and the rest fold away.
No storage format changes, so rows already written are fixed too.

Measured against the row that prompted this, 25457 chars with 3 wrapped
blocks: reload produced 1 row with 18704 visible chars, and now produces
6 rows with a 566-char answer and 18130 chars folded behind the header.

This does not address the storage side. Only the provider's separate
reasoning channel is ever wrapped, so reasoning the model emits as
ordinary content is persisted as ordinary content and stays
indistinguishable from the answer. Those 18130 chars are still reasoning
prose living in the content column; they are merely folded now instead
of shown. Tracked separately.

fix(tui): collapse narration the model kept thinking past

A restart still showed a wall: the model restates its reasoning through
the content channel, where it is persisted unwrapped and is
indistinguishable from an answer. Splitting on reasoning markers was not
enough, because one of those unwrapped restatements sat between two
reasoning blocks and rendered as ordinary text.

Position is the one exact signal available. A text segment with reasoning
after it is one the model carried on thinking past, so it cannot be the
answer however much it reads like one. Those render collapsed; only text
with no further reasoning behind it stays visible. No guessing at which
prose looks like thinking, which would corrupt real answers.

Measured on the two rows that produced the reports:

  17090 chars -> 571 visible, 16433 collapsed
  25457 chars -> 566 visible, 24761 collapsed

Both now show their actual answer and nothing else.

This is still a rendering fix. The unwrapped reasoning remains in the
content column and is still fed back as assistant content on the next
turn, which is what makes the model repeat itself. That root cause is
#760 and is not addressed here.

fix(tui): stop an expand from scrolling the view up by its own size

Opening any block jumped the viewport several pages up.

The from-bottom scroll offset absorbs lines that arrive at the bottom
while the user is scrolled up, so streaming output does not push what
they are reading off screen. Expanding a block also grows the
transcript, and that growth was being absorbed the same way: the offset
gained exactly the number of lines the block added, scrolling the view
up by the size of the thing just opened. A large tool group is a few
hundred lines, hence four pages.

The anchor restore was supposed to overwrite the offset and pin the
clicked row, and it does, but only when the anchored row still has lines
in the frame. A row hidden by the turn fold resolves to nothing, the
restore is skipped, and the compensation is left as the last word. That
is why the jump survived the anchor work.

A user-opened block is not content appended below them, so it is now
excluded from the compensation outright rather than relying on the
restore to undo it afterwards. Streaming growth still compensates
exactly as before.

The predicate is pure and covers the cases that matter: streaming still
absorbed, an expand never absorbed however large, collapse and
first-render and already-at-bottom all unchanged.

fix(tui): keep a turn's header after it is expanded

Expanding a "N steps" turn erased the only control that could collapse
it again. The turn opened, the header vanished, and there was nothing on
screen showing where to click to put it back.

A turn that ran no tool calls gets no header from format_turn_header, so
the step-count fallback was its only one, and that fallback required the
turn to be folded. One click flipped folded to false, the fallback
stopped applying, and the header disappeared along with any way back.
Turns with real tool calls were unaffected, which is why this only
showed on the step-count ones.

Whether a turn has working-out behind its header is now derived from the
messages rather than from the current fold state, so the header is
present in both and the hint reads "click to expand" or "click to fold"
against a control that is actually there.

A bare question and answer still gets no header: nothing folds away, so
there is nothing to strand the user with.

fix(tui): stop a background task's system scaffolding reaching the chat

A finished background task published its entire injection into the
transcript as a user turn: the "[System: ...]" preface, the full shell
command, exit status and fifty lines of output.

QueuedUserMessage exists precisely to prevent that. It carries
context_text for the model and display_text for the DB and the UI, and
the mid-turn path threw the second one away: the TUI queue was a
Vec<String>, so only the context could be queued, and the drain then
wrapped whatever it found in ::plain, promoting that context into the
display text. The idle path never had the bug because it passes both
halves straight to the agent service, which is why this only appeared
when a task finished while a turn was still running.

The queue now holds QueuedUserMessage, and draining joins the two halves
separately instead of collapsing them. Typed follow-ups are unaffected:
their halves are identical, so joining either way gives the same result.

Sites that only clear the queue are untouched. The input restore and the
queued-message preview both read display_text now, so a system entry
cannot spill its context into the input chrome either.

feat(tui): give the live reasoning summary room to finish a thought

The thinking line was capped at 80 characters and rendered as a single
line, so a multi-step chain was cut off exactly where it got useful:
"#766 tests running in background -> wait for them -> commit #766 ->
comment+close #...".

The cap is now 300 characters and the excerpt wraps across at most three
lines, continuations aligned under the first past the emoji. Three is a
hard ceiling, not a window: a longer excerpt truncates with an ellipsis
on the last line. The one-line form existed to replace a scrolling
12-line wall and that property is kept, only the budget widens.

The cap is a parameter rather than a new constant in the shared helper.
Telegram renders the same excerpt into a status message it edits
repeatedly, where length is noise, so it keeps the 80-character budget
and only the TUI asks for 300.

fix(deps): clear the quick-xml DoS advisories from the dependency tree

cargo audit reported 7 vulnerabilities, six of them quick-xml across three
versions: RUSTSEC-2026-0194 (quadratic run time on duplicate attribute
names) and RUSTSEC-2026-0195 (unbounded namespace-declaration allocation),
both 7.5, both denial of service reachable from parsing untrusted XML.
The document parser reads XLSX and DOCX from whatever the agent is handed,
so that input is not trusted.

Three separate paths, each fixed at its source:

  quick-xml 0.37 -> 0.41            direct dependency
  calamine  0.26 -> 0.36            pulled quick-xml 0.31
  pprof removed                     pulled inferno 0.11, then quick-xml 0.26

pprof was dead weight. It was declared optional and Unix-only, but the
`profiling` feature is a bare flag read by one `cfg!` check and never
activated the dependency, and no module referenced pprof. It only ever
existed in the lockfile, where it dragged in a vulnerable quick-xml with
no fixed release reachable from pprof 0.15. Removing it beats pinning a
transitive dep for a feature that was never wired up.

0.41 dropped `BytesText::unescape`, splitting decode and entity handling
into two calls. `decoded_text` restores the single-call shape for the
three extraction sites rather than spreading the dance through each, and
keeps the previous skip-on-error behaviour so an undecodable run of text
does not fail the whole document.

Remaining: protobuf 2.28 (RUSTSEC-2024-0437) via crabrace 0.1.0, which
pins prometheus 0.13 as a hard dependency with no feature gate. Not
fixable here; needs crabrace to move to prometheus 0.14.

fix(deps): drop crabrace, keep the two GETs it existed for

cargo audit is now clean. The last vulnerability, protobuf 2.28
(RUSTSEC-2024-0437), came in through crabrace -> prometheus 0.13, and
could not be fixed from here: prometheus only pulls protobuf as a default
feature it never uses, but Cargo features are additive so a consumer
cannot turn one off.

Removing the dependency was the better answer, because protobuf was a
symptom. crabrace ships the registry SERVER in the same package as its
client with no feature gate, so importing it for two GETs also compiled
axum, tower, tower-http, config, dotenvy, prometheus and
tracing-subscriber, and forced a second reqwest and a second axum into a
tree that already had both. The client itself was reqwest with three
lines of glue, and reqwest is already a direct dependency.

Everything used is now in src/config/registry_client.rs: GET /providers,
GET /health, and the Provider and Model structs. Field names, renames and
serde defaults are copied exactly, so an existing registry is unaffected.
Two small changes to the original behaviour, both deliberate: the base
URL tolerates a trailing slash, and health_check reports an unreachable
server as false rather than an error, since callers use it to decide
whether to try at all.

  vulnerabilities  1 -> 0
  axum             0.7.9 + 0.8.9 -> 0.8.9
  gone from lock   crabrace, prometheus, protobuf

reqwest 0.11 survives via kalosm-common through rwhisper, unrelated to
this path.

CrabraceConfig, CrabraceIntegration and ProviderUpdater keep their names
and signatures, so both existing test files pass untouched. Note for
whoever finishes provider auto-discovery: nothing calls update_once or
start_auto_update_loop today, and the default base_url is plaintext
http://localhost:8080, which needs changing before that path goes live.

refactor(config): rename the provider-registry surface off the vendor name

The removed dependency's name was still all over the config surface:
a [crabrace] section, crabrace.enabled, OPENCRABS_CRABRACE_URL and
friends, CrabraceConfig and CrabraceIntegration. Nothing by that name
exists in the tree any more, so every one of those was an invitation to
go looking for something that isn't there.

  [crabrace]                  -> [provider_registry]
  OPENCRABS_CRABRACE_*        -> OPENCRABS_PROVIDER_REGISTRY_*
  CrabraceConfig              -> ProviderRegistryConfig
  CrabraceIntegration         -> ProviderRegistry
  src/config/crabrace.rs      -> src/config/provider_registry.rs
  config_crabrace_test.rs     -> config_provider_registry_test.rs

Behaviour is unchanged: same fields, same defaults, same validation,
same HTTP contract. The old section name was never load-bearing because
the code behind it has never been called, and unknown top-level keys are
ignored on load, so an existing config.toml carrying [crabrace] keeps
working exactly as before, which is to say it does nothing.

Three CI audit ignores are now obsolete and removed: RUSTSEC-2024-0437
(protobuf, which came through the removed dependency) and
RUSTSEC-2026-0194 / -0195 (quick-xml, fixed by the bump to 0.41). The
lru advisory's comment blamed the same dependency and was wrong; it
arrives via kalosm-language-model through rwhisper, corrected in place.

The remaining ignores are all unmaintained-crate warnings.

style(tui): quiet inline code so it stops out-shouting the prose

Inline code rendered in full-saturation brand orange AND bold. It is the
most repeated accent in an answer, often several times per paragraph, so
at that intensity it pulled the eye off the text it was embedded in and
beat every other colour on screen: the failure red, the highlighted code
block, the cyan language label. Those all read comfortably; this did not.

Now a muted amber with the bold dropped. The weight was doing as much of
the damage as the hue, since nothing else in body text is bold by
default. Code still has to be identifiable, not loud.

Kept local to markdown rendering rather than changing palette::ORANGE.
The brand colour still belongs to titles, spinners and selections, which
appear once each and are meant to draw attention.

fix(agent): let approval_policy reach the tool gate on every surface

With approval_policy = "auto-always", a tool call could still fail before
execution with "Tool requires approval but no approval mechanism
configured". The policy was read only inside approval callbacks, via
check_approval_policy, so a surface with no callback never consulted it.
The one-shot `run` command is exactly that: it passes no callback and
derived auto_approve_tools from the --auto-approve flag alone, so a
configured auto-always was ignored and every gated tool was denied.

The policy now resolves once in AgentService::new, from the config that
constructor already receives, and all four call sites inherit one answer
instead of each deriving their own. Resolving there rather than in the
gate is deliberate: the existing check loads config from disk, and the
gate runs for every tool call.

with_auto_approve_tools now widens instead of assigning. An absent CLI
flag means "nothing to add", not "revoke the policy", which is what
turned a configured auto-always back off. Passing true still forces the
grant for callers that have their own, such as subagents whose spawn the
parent already approved.

The denial message named only the missing mechanism, which read as a
wiring bug and sent people looking in the wrong place. It now says the
policy does not auto-approve and names both ways out. Reaching that
branch is now proof the policy really gates, since an auto policy clears
the gate above it.

Two test premises moved with the behaviour rather than being worked
around. The shipped default policy is auto-always, so new_for_test and
the parallel-eligibility helper now pin a gating policy: inheriting the
default would auto-approve every test service and stop the approval tests
from reaching the machinery they exist to cover.

Closes #769

docs(readme): say approval_policy governs headless runs too

Follow-up to the policy resolution fix. Two spots read wrong once the
policy actually reaches every surface.

The `run` row presented --auto-approve as the way to run unattended,
which sounds like a requirement. Under the shipped default it is not:
`run` is already unattended, and the flag only matters when the policy
gates. Someone adding --yolo to a cron entry was working around a
problem they did not have.

The config block documented the setting accurately but said nothing
about scope. Setting `ask` for safety now also governs cron, CI and
`run`, which are exactly the contexts with nothing to prompt on, so the
note spells out what happens there and how to keep those working.

Closes #772

style(tui): make inline code the footer's slate blue, not a brown

The desaturated amber read as brown, which is worse than the loud orange
it replaced. Desaturating a warm colour to quiet it only muddies it.

Inline code now borrows the slate blue the footer already uses for
recessive text, so the palette gains no new hue. It sits a step brighter
than the footer's own value: chrome can recede because nobody reads it
closely, but inline code carries the identifiers inside a sentence and
has to stay legible against body text. It is also less saturated than the
link blue, so the two remain distinguishable beyond the link's underline.

Still not bold. That was half of why the original drew the eye.

fix(tui): fold intermediate text while the turn is still running

A turn mid-flight left exactly one block of narration exposed while the
tool groups and thinking on either side of it folded away.

The fold exempts one row per turn, the final answer, and that row was
picked as the last non-empty assistant message. Mid-turn the last such
message is not the answer, it is the latest step, so every fresh
intermediate text was promoted into the exempt slot as it arrived. The
previous one folded the moment a newer one replaced it, which is why
there was always exactly one showing.

A running turn now has no exempt row at all: settled_final_answer_idx
returns None for the newest turn while processing, so every step sits
behind the header until the turn finishes and its real answer appears.
Only the newest turn can be unsettled, so scrollback keeps every earlier
reply visible.

Nothing becomes invisible that was not already shown twice: in-flight
text renders from the streaming buffer, with the reasoning excerpt and
the spinner beside it. The folded copy was the duplicate.

feat(tui): move the background-task indicator onto the input border

A detached command ends its turn the instant it spawns, so nothing else
on screen says work is still happening. The indicator lived in the status
bar, which is the last place the eye goes, and it sat behind the model
name and token rate.

It now attaches to the input box's top border, left side, opposite the
ctx budget on the bottom border. Same treatment, same box, and it lands
where the user is already looking while they wait.

The label is capped at 28 characters. The stored label allows 60, which
is fine for a log line and far too long for a border title: a real
command like "cargo test --locked --profile ci --lib 2>&1 | tail -40"
crowded out everything beside it. Leading words identify a command, so
the tail is what goes.

The budget applies to the command only. Elapsed time and the overflow
count are short, fixed-width, and the entire reason the indicator exists,

fix(phantom): count issue-tracker actions as completion claims

A turn with zero tool calls announced "Closed #767 as completed with
remarks" and the detector let it through, twice in a row. The sentence
cleared every structural gate: prose lead present, 37 characters so well
inside the 80-char sentence limit, active rather than passive. It failed
on vocabulary alone.

action_verbs held twenty words, all git and deploy shaped: pushed,
deployed, merged, committed, tagged, released. No form of close, comment,
file, open or assign appeared in any of the six language files. Those are
side-effecting actions the agent performs constantly, and a fabricated
one was indistinguishable from prose.

That gate is what enables the entire self-heal path, so a miss there is
not a smaller warning, it is silence: no retry, no provider nudge, no
narration strip. The fabrication reached the user as fact.

Verbs added across all six languages, not just English, since the list is
per-language and the gap was identical in each.

The passive guard covers the new entries as it did the old ones, so "the
issue is closed" stays prose about state. Past-tense claims only reach
this branch when the whole turn ran zero tools, so a real close followed
by an accurate "Closed #767" is still exonerated by the post-success path.
