* fix(phantom): catch marker-less bare-participle announcements in en/pt/es (#1694)

"Reading them, with mtimes so I know each postdates the tree it claims to
cover." ended a turn that called nothing. It is an announcement of unfinished
work carrying none of the tokens the existing arms key on: work_announcement_re
and gerund_re want a trailing now / … / :, plan_announcement_re wants then /
before / after. All three missed it, so it shipped as a finished answer.

The construction is not the hard part; separating it from a participial SUBJECT
is, because the surface form is identical: "Reading them is straightforward."
and "Getting them took a while." No copula list can do the split: the second
statement carries no copula, and neither does French "En les lisant, on
comprend vite." What separates them is the word class the pronoun is followed
by: an announcement takes nothing, a clause introducer, or a closed-class
modifier, while a statement takes the finite verb its subject governs. So
announcement_tail_words is a closed class (prepositions, conjunctions,
numerals, ordinals, modals, fixed adverbials) and deliberately not a verb list,
which is the open class that never converges (#1122).

Two additive LangConfig fields, both #[serde(default)]. The en stem filter is
closed-set too: >=3 chars and not ending in a/h/r, which drops bring, string,
ring, cling, fling, spring, during, king, sing, wing, sting, thing and the
some/any/every/no-thing family while keeping reading, checking, verifying,
getting and loading.

Group 1 must be rest-of-clause ([^.!?\n]*), not the punctuation class
([.!?:\n]*): the latter matches only punctuation, so every tail comes back
empty and every statement fires. Seven false positives before that was caught.
The optional adverb group is what makes "Reading them carefully." an
announcement while "Reading them carefully takes a while." stays a statement:
the adverb is absorbed only when the clause ends there.

Clitic position differs per language, so the pattern is written per language
rather than transplanted: en and ru separate, pt enclitic behind a hyphen
(Lendo = l + endo, hence {1,}), es fused with an accent shift (Leyéndolos
carries é, so a flat endo alternation matches neither it nor Corriéndolos nor
Siguiéndolos), fr proclitic, id fused on -nya.

fr, id and ru ship INERT, and that is stated rather than hidden: the French
gérondif is idiomatically an adverbial of means, and id/ru have no present
tense copula for a tail rule to bite on, so the announcement/statement split
needs a discriminator nobody has found yet. A guessed arm there would nag
legitimate replies, which is the #1506 harm and worse than missing one
phantom. Every consumer guards is_empty(), so an absent arm is inert, not
broken; a test asserts the emptiness so enabling one is a deliberate change.

fix(shell): run command strings under a real bash, with honest sh fallback

The bash tool is named bash and its description teaches bash idioms, but
shell_pair() answered ("sh", "-c") on every non-Windows host. On Debian and
Ubuntu /bin/sh is dash, where most bashisms do not error: IFS=$'\t' assigns
the three literal characters $, \, t and exits 0, so every later field split
chops at the letter t and the caller gets corrupt data dressed as success.
Measured on this host against /bin/dash: the reporter's tab-separated split
yields |h|op||a|op| (6 fields) where bash yields htop|atop| (2), exit code 0
both times. echo -e leaks its flag the same silent way.

Probe for a real bash once per process, behind the same choke point, so all
five consumers of shell_pair() move together: the bash tool, the detached
background runner, dynamic tools, the Ralph plan verification gate and the
TUI bang operator. Candidates are tried in a fixed absolute-path order and a
candidate is believed on behaviour rather than filename: it must answer the
ANSI-C probe with exactly one tab byte and carry BASH_VERSION, which rejects
dash and busybox ash alike. Where no bash exists the pair still falls back to
("sh", "-c") but announces it once, so the dialect in force is discoverable
instead of inferred from a silent misparse.

The tool description now states the dialect and the fallback, so the model
can adapt when bash is genuinely absent.

The previous shell_pair_matches_platform test pinned ("sh", "-c") on Unix and
would have blocked this fix rather than caught it; it is replaced by
assertions on the contract (a spawnable shell, bash preferred, sh only where
no bash exists) plus byte-exact regression guards for the misparse, including
two that run dash directly to prove the probe rejects it and that the
corruption was real.

fix(a2a): notify transport retry with reserve-before-deliver idempotency (#199)

An A2A `session/notify` retry could deliver twice. The caller mints the
notify id, the transport times out, and the retry carries the same id — but
nothing server-side remembered the first attempt, so the message went out a
second time. A timeout is ambiguous, never a verdict.

The receipt store now doubles as the idempotency ledger: `reserve()` claims
an id before any delivery, so a known id reports the prior outcome instead of
delivering a second copy. The caller-supplied id is threaded end to end, and
an absent or malformed id still gets a server-side mint, so every pre-#199
caller behaves exactly as before. A non-delivery (refused_in_flight, no_route)
banks nothing, so it releases the id and a retry stays free to deliver — the
id is worth keeping only where an attempt actually accepted the notify.

fix(telegram): carry an excerpt in the pruned reply pointer and de-gate reply recovery (#548)

The pruned pointer said "[Replying to X's message above]" — a contentless
reference. The history block renders as [HH:MM] sender: text with no message
ids and the compaction summary preserves none either, so the text is the only
resolvable key the model has; "message above" named nothing. It now carries a
bounded 120-char excerpt.

Recovery and the honesty marker were both gated on the replied-to sender being
a bot. A human's photo, sticker or voice note arrives with empty text exactly
as a rich bot message does, so a user-to-user reply to media produced ctx=None
— the model was not told a reply had happened at all. Both are now
sender-agnostic, with the topic-creation service message excluded so ordinary
forum messages do not each gain a spurious marker.

Adds topic_root/unrecoverable/in_context to the INFO line: the field reports
behind #548 could only be read as "ctx=None, reason unknown".

fix(telegram): do not chase the topic root in reply recovery (#548)

De-gating the recovery lookup made it fire for every message in a forum
topic, where reply_to_message is always the topic-creation service message.
That id belongs to a service message, so the query can only waste work — and a
store hit on it would inject the topic's own metadata as though it were the
content the user replied to. The guard is hoisted so the lookup and the
honesty marker both respect it.

feat(acp): live model catalog in session/new + pair-aware set_model

session/new now answers models.availableModels built from the configured
providers (same provider_registry walk the factory uses — enabled and
usable sections only), with modelIds in the provider/model pair form the
CLI already parses. session/set_model routes a pair through
create_provider_by_name + swap_provider_for_session + mark_manual_switch,
so the picker drives a real provider switch instead of a name override;
a bare model name still just re-serves on the current provider.

feat(acp): native session/set_mode with server-side approval policy

Modes advertised in session/new (supervised/auto-accept-edits/auto/
full-access/plan) and validated on set_mode — unknown ids are a hard
error, never a silent mismatch about who approves what. The turn's
approval callback consults the mode: plan denies mutating tools before
the client is asked so the agent learns the boundary from the denial,
auto/full-access approve without a round-trip, auto-accept-edits
auto-approves edit kinds only, supervised forwards to the client as
before.

feat(acp): session/compact + available_commands push

session/compact drives the loop's own manual-compaction marker turn — the
same string the TUI and channels use — so client compaction is the
production path, not a reimplementation. After session/new answers, the
server pushes available_commands_update with the built-in table, installed
skills, and the user's commands.toml entries (names normalised to ACP
shape, deduped), giving clients real command discovery instead of the
filesystem scraping other harnesses do.

feat(cli): add --quiet to run for machine-pure stdout

Gates the processing banner, progress callback, and stats footers so
stdout carries only the answer payload in every format. One-shot
callers (MonoCode text harness, scripts) can parse --format json
without filtering spinner noise.

feat(acp): replay transcript + restore per-session model on session/load

An agent advertising loadSession re-sends the stored conversation as
session/update notifications before answering the load. Stored rows map
to live-turn chunk shapes: user -> user_message_chunk; assistant ->
thought chunks (persisted thinking plus inline reasoning segments via
the TUI splitter) and message chunks. Replay mapping lives in
protocol::replay_updates with tests split to src/tests/ to keep
protocol.rs under the 500-line ceiling.

Also rehydrates the per-session model/provider override from the
session row on load: the agent service's per-session maps are
in-memory, so a fresh acp process used to forget the user's pick.
Provider restore falls back to a bare model pin when the provider no
longer exists in config. session/set_model now stores the pair form so
models_payload can mark the current selection correctly.

feat(acp): include context window size in usage updates

The usage session/update carried only used tokens; clients with a
context meter (MonoCode's context display) need the window total.
Sourced per-session via context_limit_for_session so swapped providers
report their own window.

refactor(acp): ext-prefix the steer method

session/steer is not in the ACP method set; custom methods get an
underscore prefix (same convention as cursor's _session/steer). The old
spelling stays accepted as an alias so older adapters keep working.
feat(acp): persist set_model pick on the session row for cross-process restore
fix(acp): cover Segment::Blocked in replay and align fixtures with line-start marker contract

fix(acp): stop doubling streamed answers as round aggregates

The loop emits live deltas via StreamingChunk and then the round's
full text again via IntermediateText; the ACP bridge mapped both to
agent_message_chunk, so every streamed answer rendered twice on the
client (wire-proven in the four-phase smoke: two identical frames).

Track text streamed since the last round boundary and skip the
aggregate when it repeats it — the same dedup rule the WhatsApp
handler applies pre-send. Aggregates that carry unstreamed text
(CLI providers stream nothing) still emit; tool events reset the
boundary so round 2 dedups against its own chunks.

fix(acp): route session/set_mode to the mode handler

The rebase composition folded SESSION_SET_MODE into the
SESSION_SET_MODEL dispatch arm, so every set_mode request was answered
as a bogus model switch (the mode id parsed as a model name) and the
real mode-vocabulary handler was dead code. The only symptom was a
clippy unreachable-pattern warning — unit tests stayed green because
they test handlers, not routing.

Two changes: dispatch arms are separate again, and set_model no longer
accepts modeId as a param fallback — a mode id reaching the model
handler is a routing accident and should fail loud, not silently
switch models to 'supervised'. The four-phase smoke now pins routing:
valid set_mode must return a result, bogus mode ids must get
INVALID_PARAMS (-32602).

feat(acp): restore context meter on session load

Replay now emits a final usage update built from the provider's own
last measurement (Message.input_tokens on the last assistant row),
falling back to the session's lifetime token_count, with the window
size from context_limit_for_session. No estimates: real numbers or
nothing.

fix(acp): per-call approval override beats config auto-approve policy

The tool-context seed mirrored auto_approve_tools from the config policy,
so approval_policy=auto-always silently suppressed the ask even when a
per-call override callback was present — the loop gate's third condition
(!tool_context.auto_approve) un-did the override precedence the loop
promises. ACP supervised mode never consulted the client.

The seed now honours the override: context_auto_approve =
auto_approve_tools && !has_override_approval. Post-approval flips are
untouched, so tools still see approval once granted.

Regression test: override callback + auto_approve_tools(true) must be
consulted (the ACP dogfood setup, config auto-always).
